summary: Foundations of adic spaces, Part II: analytic and formal geometry. The packet plans, at declaration granularity, everything the Tau Ceti roadmap Foundations of adic spaces leaves to a successor: completed tensor products of Huber pairs with their topology, plus ring, universal property and uniformisation; fibre products of adic spaces under Huber's noetherian hypotheses, with sheafiness for rings with a noetherian ring of definition (Huber 1994, Theorem 2.2, Case I); the morphism theory of Huber's book (adic morphisms, the finite-type classes, separated, proper and partially proper morphisms with the valuative criteria, finite and quasi-finite morphisms, continuous differentials, unramified, smooth and étale morphisms, the Jacobian criterion and standard étale presentations); the classical affinoid algebras; analytification of schemes locally of finite type (Huber 1994, Proposition 3.8), Tate's rigid spaces and Huber's rigid–adic comparison, analytic groups and invariant differentials; noetherian formal geometry after EGA I §10 and EGA III §§4–5 (Spf, completion, coherent formal modules, formal functions, Grothendieck existence and algebraisation); admissible formal schemes, admissible blow-ups, flattening by admissible blow-up (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II after Raynaud–Gruson), Raynaud's theorem, Huber's generic fibre of type-(S) formal schemes, the good-reduction locus, residue discs and Hasse domains with fractional valuation bounds; coherent sheaves (Tate and Kiehl for finite modules, quasi-Stein spaces, Čech acyclicity on sheafy Tate affinoids, Kiehl gluing of vector bundles, the proper mapping theorem, base change, proper GAGA) and traces along finite locally free morphisms with pull–identify–trace; AdicEtaleGeometry A1's étale and pro-étale sites on these carriers, smooth pairs and boundary complements; sousperfectoid rings and spaces, perfectoid-times-smooth products and the coefficient algebras and sheaves of CHJ; and dagger geometry after Grosse-Klönne (overconvergent Tate algebras, dagger algebras, Monsky–Washnitzer weak completions, dagger spaces, strict neighbourhoods, the comparison with rigid spaces, and the overconvergent, logarithmic and compactly supported de Rham complexes). It keeps every identifier of the reviewed decomposition and follows the accepted restructuring RS-05. Sources are public: Huber's 1994 Math. Z. paper and Kiehl's and Bosch–Lütkebohmert's papers through the Göttingen digitisation centre, EGA I and III through Numdam, and arXiv or author copies of the rest; Huber's 1996 book is cited only through excerpts the reviewed decomposition verified, and every excerpt was checked against the text read. Every stage is source-decomposed: all its targets are realised by nodes; the anchor's Layers 0–5, which the pinned Tau Ceti tree does not yet contain in full, and the inputs owned by other roadmaps are recorded as requests; unread proof sources (Bosch–Güntzer–Remmert, Huber's habilitation, Temkin, Elkik and others) are recorded as gaps.

nodes.title: Noether normalisation for K-affinoid algebras
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one and let A ≠ 0 be a K-affinoid algebra. Then there are d ≥ 0 and an injective homomorphism of K-algebras ι : K⟨T₁,…,T_d⟩ → A making A a finite K⟨T₁,…,T_d⟩-module. Every such ι is continuous and strict (a homeomorphism onto its image, which is closed). Lean name: Huber.Affinoid.exists_finite_injective_tateAlgebra.
hypotheses: K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one

A is a K-affinoid algebra: a commutative K-algebra with a complete Hausdorff first-countable ring topology for which K → A is strictly topologically of finite type (Tau Ceti IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType (algebraMap K A): a continuous open surjection of K-algebras K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ = restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n K → A; Wedhorn Definition 5.57)
proofSteps: Choose a continuous open surjection π : K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ → A (Tau Ceti IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType) and induct on n. If ker π = 0 take d = n and ι = π.

If 0 ≠ f ∈ ker π: a K-algebra automorphism σ of K⟨X⟩ of the form X_i ↦ X_i + X_n^{c_i} (i < n, c_i ≫ 0) makes σ(f) X_n-distinguished, and Weierstrass division by σ(f) makes K⟨X⟩/(σ(f)) a finite module over K⟨X₁,…,X_{n−1}⟩ (Weierstrass division and preparation, anchor Layer 0.5 item 3, requested from the anchor).

Hence K⟨X₁,…,X_{n−1}⟩ → A is finite. Its image is K⟨X₁,…,X_{n−1}⟩/J, again a K-affinoid algebra because every ideal of the noetherian complete Tate ring K⟨X₁,…,X_{n−1}⟩ is closed (strong noetherianness of K, anchor Layer 0.5; Tau Ceti isNoetherianRing_of_isStronglyNoetherian and isClosed_of_isNoetherian). The induction hypothesis gives a finite injection K⟨T₁,…,T_d⟩ → K⟨X₁,…,X_{n−1}⟩/J; compose finite maps (Mathlib Module.Finite is transitive).

Continuity and strictness: A is a finite module over the complete noetherian Tate ring K⟨T⟩, so its given complete metrisable topology is the module topology (Tau Ceti IsTateRing.isModuleTopology), and the K⟨T⟩-linear map ι from the finite module K⟨T⟩ into the noetherian module A is strict (Tau Ceti LinearMap.isStrictMap_of_module_finite, which also gives continuity); its image is closed (Tau Ceti isClosed_of_isNoetherian).
acceptance: For the annulus A = K⟨X, Y⟩/(XY − 1), T ↦ X + Y is a finite injection K⟨T⟩ → A (X is a root of Z² − TZ + 1), whereas K⟨X⟩ → A, X ↦ X, is injective but not finite (X⁻¹ is not integral over K⟨X⟩).
For a finite field extension L/K (with its unique absolute value) d = 0 and ι is K → L.

nodes.title: Residue fields of K-affinoid algebras at maximal ideals are finite over K
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one and A a K-affinoid algebra. For every maximal ideal m ⊆ A the field A/m is a finite extension of K; consequently m is closed, the absolute value of K extends uniquely to a power-multiplicative (indeed multiplicative) norm on A/m (the spectral norm), and for every homomorphism of K-algebras φ : A → B into a K-affinoid algebra B and every maximal ideal n ⊆ B the ideal φ⁻¹(n) is maximal, so φ induces Max(φ) : Max B → Max A. Lean name: Huber.Affinoid.finiteDimensional_residueField.
hypotheses: K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one

A is a K-affinoid algebra: a commutative K-algebra with a complete Hausdorff first-countable ring topology for which K → A is strictly topologically of finite type (Tau Ceti IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType (algebraMap K A): a continuous open surjection of K-algebras K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ = restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n K → A; Wedhorn Definition 5.57)
m a maximal ideal of A
proofSteps: A/m is a K-affinoid algebra: m is closed because every ideal of the noetherian complete Tate ring A is closed (Tau Ceti IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType.isStronglyNoetherian, isNoetherianRing_of_isStronglyNoetherian, isClosed_of_isNoetherian), so the quotient presentation K⟨X⟩ → A → A/m is again a continuous open surjection.

Noether normalisation (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-noether-normalisation) gives a finite injection K⟨T₁,…,T_d⟩ → A/m. A field that is integral over a subring forces the subring to be a field (Mathlib isField_of_isIntegral_of_isField); K⟨T₁,…,T_d⟩ is not a field for d ≥ 1 because T₁ is a nonzero non-unit (it lies in the kernel of the evaluation at the origin). Hence d = 0 and A/m is finite over K.
The absolute value of the complete field K extends uniquely to a power-multiplicative K-algebra norm on the finite extension A/m (Mathlib spectralNorm_unique).
For φ : A → B and n ∈ Max B, A/φ⁻¹(n) embeds into the finite extension B/n of K, so it is a domain finite-dimensional over K, hence a field.
acceptance: For c ∈ K° not a square in K, the maximal ideal (T² − c) of K⟨T⟩ has residue field K(√c) of degree 2, not K: points of Max K⟨T⟩ need not be K-rational.
For A = K⟨T⟩ and c ∈ K°, the maximal ideal (T − c) has residue field K.

sources.excerpt: Proposition 5.61. Let A be a k-algebra topologically of finite type. Then for every maximal ideal m the quotient A/m is a finite extension of k.
sources.match: The main statement.

sources.excerpt: (a) Every maximal ideal of A has residue field finite over K.

nodes.title: K-affinoid algebras are Jacobson rings
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one and A a K-affinoid algebra. Then A is a Jacobson ring (Mathlib IsJacobsonRing A): every prime ideal is the intersection of the maximal ideals containing it. Consequently the nilradical of A is the intersection of all maximal ideals, so f ∈ A is nilpotent iff f(x) = 0 for all x ∈ Max A, and f is a unit iff f(x) ≠ 0 for all x ∈ Max A. Lean name: Huber.Affinoid.isJacobsonRing.
hypotheses: K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one

A is a K-affinoid algebra: a commutative K-algebra with a complete Hausdorff first-countable ring topology for which K → A is strictly topologically of finite type (Tau Ceti IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType (algebraMap K A): a continuous open surjection of K-algebras K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ = restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n K → A; Wedhorn Definition 5.57)
proofSteps: The Tate algebra K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ is a Jacobson ring (BGR 5.2.6/3; stated in Conrad, Several approaches, Theorem 1.1.5(2)). Proof source: BGR, not public; recorded as a gap on this node.
A is a quotient of a Tate algebra and quotients of Jacobson rings are Jacobson (Mathlib isJacobsonRing_of_surjective).
The nilradical (Mathlib nilradical) is the intersection of the primes, each an intersection of maximal ideals; an element outside every maximal ideal is a unit.
acceptance: In K⟨T⟩/(T²) the class of T vanishes at the unique point and is nilpotent but nonzero; in K⟨T⟩ an element with no zero on Max K⟨T⟩, such as 1 + ϖT, is a unit.
Non-example outside the hypothesis: the valuation ring K° (not a K-affinoid algebra) is local with Jacobson radical K°° ≠ 0 while its nilradical is 0, so K° is not a Jacobson ring.

sources.excerpt: (2) The ring Tn is Jacobson: every prime ideal p of Tn is the intersection of the maximal ideals containing it.
sources.match: The Jacobson property of Tate algebras.

sources.excerpt: By Theorem 1.1.5, every k-affinoid algebra A is noetherian and Jacobson with finite Krull dimension, and A/m is a finite extension of k for every m ∈ M (A).
sources.match: Passage to quotients.

sources.excerpt: By the Jacobson property of A, a ∈ A is nilpotent if and only if a(x) = 0 for all x ∈ M (A).
sources.match: The nilradical consequence.

nodes.title: Maximal ideals of Tate algebras are generated by polynomials
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one, n ≥ 0 and m ⊆ K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ a maximal ideal. Then m₀ = m ∩ K[X₁,…,X_n] is a maximal ideal of the polynomial ring, K[X]/m₀ → K⟨X⟩/m is an isomorphism, and m = m₀·K⟨X⟩; more precisely there are polynomials p_i ∈ K[X₁,…,X_i] monic in X_i (1 ≤ i ≤ n) with m = (p₁,…,p_n). nodes.title: The supremum seminorm of a K-affinoid algebra
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one and A a K-affinoid algebra. Max A is the set of maximal ideals of A (Mathlib MaximalSpectrum A); for x ∈ Max A with ideal m_x and f ∈ A, |f(x)| is the absolute value of f mod m_x in the finite extension A/m_x of K (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-residue-fields-finite), for the unique extension of |·|. The supremum seminorm of f ∈ A is |f|_sup = sup_{x ∈ Max A} |f(x)| (and |f|_sup = 0 when A = 0). It is finite: |f|_sup ≤ |f|_π for the residue norm |f|_π = inf{‖g‖ : π(g) = f} of every presentation π : K⟨X⟩ → A (‖·‖ the Gauss norm). It is a power-multiplicative K-algebra seminorm (|f + g|_sup ≤ max(|f|_sup, |g|_sup), |fg|_sup ≤ |f|_sup|g|_sup, |λf|_sup = |λ||f|_sup for λ ∈ K, |fⁿ|_sup = |f|_supⁿ), it is contracted by every K-algebra homomorphism φ : A → B of K-affinoid algebras (|φ(f)|_sup ≤ |f|_sup), it is a norm iff A is reduced, and on a Tate algebra K⟨X⟩ it is the Gauss norm. Lean name: Huber.Affinoid.supNorm : A → ℝ≥0.
hypotheses: K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one

A is a K-affinoid algebra: a commutative K-algebra with a complete Hausdorff first-countable ring topology for which K → A is strictly topologically of finite type (Tau Ceti IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType (algebraMap K A): a continuous open surjection of K-algebras K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ = restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n K → A; Wedhorn Definition 5.57)
proofSteps: Well defined: |f(x)| uses the unique extension of |·| to the finite extension A/m_x (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-residue-fields-finite).

Finite: for a lift g = Σ a_ν X^ν of f and x ∈ Max A the images x_i of X_i in A/m_x satisfy |x_i| ≤ 1 (m_x is closed and the images of power-bounded elements are power-bounded), so |f(x)| ≤ max_ν |a_ν| = ‖g‖; take the infimum over lifts.

Seminorm, multiplicativity bounds and power-multiplicativity hold pointwise because each |·(x)| is a multiplicative absolute value on A/m_x; contraction because Max(φ) maps Max B into Max A with (φ f)(y) = f(Max(φ)(y)) in the common finite extension.
Norm iff reduced: |f|_sup = 0 iff f lies in every maximal ideal iff f is nilpotent (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-jacobson, Mathlib nilradical).
acceptance: For A = K⟨T⟩/(T − c) with c ∈ K°, |f|_sup = |f(c)|.
For A = K[ε]/(ε²), |ε|_sup = 0 although every residue norm of ε is positive.

nodes.title: Power-bounded elements of K-affinoid algebras are those of supremum seminorm at most one
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one and A a K-affinoid algebra. For f ∈ A: f is power-bounded (f ∈ A°, Tau Ceti powerBoundedSubring) iff |f|_sup ≤ 1; and f is topologically nilpotent iff |f|_sup < 1. Hence A° = {|f|_sup ≤ 1} and A°° = {|f|_sup < 1}. nodes.title: On a reduced K-affinoid algebra the supremum norm defines the topology
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one and A a reduced K-affinoid algebra. Then |·|_sup is a norm on A equivalent to the residue norm |·|_π of every presentation π : K⟨X⟩ → A: there is C > 0 with |f|_sup ≤ |f|_π ≤ C·|f|_sup for all f. Consequently A° = {|f|_sup ≤ 1} is bounded, i.e. A is uniform. Conversely, if A° is bounded then A is reduced. Lean name: Huber.Affinoid.supNorm_equivalent_of_isReduced.

A is a K-affinoid algebra: a commutative K-algebra with a complete Hausdorff first-countable ring topology for which K → A is strictly topologically of finite type (Tau Ceti IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType (algebraMap K A): a continuous open surjection of K-algebras K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ = restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n K → A; Wedhorn Definition 5.57)
A reduced (Mathlib IsReduced A) for the main statement

The reverse bound |f|_π ≤ C|f|_sup is BGR 6.2.4/1 (Kedlaya–Liu Corollary 2.5.6): via Noether normalisation (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-noether-normalisation) and the open mapping theorem for the finite K⟨T⟩-module A. Proof source BGR, not public; recorded as a gap on this node.
A° = {|f|_sup ≤ 1} (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-power-bounded-iff-sup) is then contained in {|f|_π ≤ C}, which is bounded.

nodes.title: Homomorphisms of K-affinoid algebras are continuous
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one. Every homomorphism of K-algebras φ : A → B between K-affinoid algebras is continuous. Consequently the topology of a K-affinoid algebra is determined by its K-algebra structure: the residue norms of any two presentations are equivalent. Lean name: Huber.Affinoid.continuous_of_algHom.

A, B K-affinoid algebras

proofSteps: Reduce to A = K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩: a presentation π : K⟨X⟩ → A is a quotient map, so φ is continuous iff φ ∘ π is.

|φ(X_i)|_sup ≤ |X_i|_sup ≤ 1 (contraction, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-supremum-seminorm), so each φ(X_i) is power-bounded (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-power-bounded-iff-sup), and the universal property of the Tate algebra (Wedhorn 5.50, anchor Layer 0.4, requested) gives a continuous K-algebra map ψ : K⟨X⟩ → B with ψ(X_i) = φ(X_i).

⋂_{n,k} nᵏ = 0 in the noetherian ring B (Krull's intersection theorem in each local ring B_n, Mathlib Ideal.iInf_pow_eq_bot_of_isLocalRing), so φ = ψ is continuous.

nodes.title: A ring of definition with reduced reduction is the ring of power-bounded elements
nodes.statement: Let A be a Tate ring, A₀ ⊆ A a ring of definition and ϖ ∈ A₀ a pseudo-uniformizer of A (a topologically nilpotent unit, Tau Ceti IsPseudoUniformizer). If A₀/ϖA₀ is a reduced ring, then A₀ = A° (Tau Ceti powerBoundedSubring). In particular, for K complete rank-one with pseudo-uniformizer ϖ and a K-affinoid algebra A = B[1/ϖ] with B ⊆ A an open bounded K°-subalgebra (for instance B = K°⟨X⟩/I flat over K°), B/ϖB reduced implies B = A° = {|f|_sup ≤ 1}. Lean name: Huber.PairOfDefinition.ringOfDefinition_eq_powerBoundedSubring_of_isReduced.
hypotheses: A Tate ring
A₀ a ring of definition containing a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ
A₀/ϖA₀ reduced
proofSteps: A₀ ⊆ A°: a ring of definition is bounded (Tau Ceti PairOfDefinition.le_powerBoundedSubring).

Let a ∈ A°. A₀[a] is a ring of definition (Tau Ceti PairOfDefinition.adjoin), hence bounded (PairOfDefinition.isBounded_ringOfDefinition); since the ϖⁿA₀ form a neighbourhood basis of 0 (Tau Ceti IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero), there is c ≥ 0 with ϖ^c aᴺ ∈ A₀ for all N ≥ 0.

A₀ is open, so ϖᵐa → 0 and some ϖᵐa lies in A₀; let m ≥ 0 be minimal. If m ≥ 1 put b = ϖᵐa ∈ A₀; then b ∉ ϖA₀ (otherwise ϖ^{m−1}a ∈ A₀, ϖ being a unit of A). For N with mN > c, bᴺ = ϖ^{mN−c}·(ϖ^c aᴺ) ∈ ϖA₀, so b is nilpotent in A₀/ϖA₀, hence zero there by reducedness — a contradiction. So m = 0 and a ∈ A₀.
For the K-affinoid case, B is a ring of definition (open and bounded) containing ϖ, and A° = {|f|_sup ≤ 1} (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-power-bounded-iff-sup).
acceptance: For K = ℚ_p and B = ℤ_p⟨T⟩, B/pB = 𝔽_p[T] is reduced and B = ℚ_p⟨T⟩°.

The reducedness hypothesis cannot be dropped: for B = ℤ_p⟨T⟩[S]/(S² − p²T) ⊂ A = B[1/p], B/pB = 𝔽_p[T, S]/(S²) is not reduced, and S/p satisfies (S/p)² = T, so S/p is integral over B, hence power-bounded, but S/p ∉ B (B is free over ℤ_p⟨T⟩ with basis 1, S); thus B ⊊ A°.

nodes.title: Huber rings of noetherian type (Huber's noetherian hypothesis)
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative topological ring which is a Huber ring (Tau Ceti `IsHuberRing A`). A is *of noetherian type* if (i) A admits a pair of definition (A₀, I) (Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition A`) whose ring of definition A₀ is a noetherian ring, or (ii) A is a Tate ring (`IsTateRing A`) and strongly noetherian in Tau Ceti's sense (`IsStronglyNoetherian A`: every completed restricted power-series ring A⟨X₁,…,X_k⟩, k ≥ 0, is a noetherian ring). This is the hypothesis Huber places on affinoid rings in Theorem 2.2 and Propositions 3.6–3.8 of the 1994 paper ('has a noetherian ring of definition or is a strongly noetherian Tate ring'). Conventions: the predicate concerns the topological ring only (no plus ring); completeness is not part of it, and every result that needs a complete ring assumes completeness and the Hausdorff property separately. Clause (i) does not say that A is a noetherian ring: every discrete ring is of noetherian type because its prime subring (the image of ℤ) is an open noetherian subring with ideal of definition 0. For a Tate ring clause (i) implies clause (ii) (a Tate ring with a noetherian ring of definition is strongly noetherian), so for Tate rings the predicate is exactly strong noetherianness; the converse implication fails: ℂ_p is strongly noetherian but has no noetherian ring of definition (a ring of definition A₀ ⊆ O_{ℂ_p} contains some p^N·O_{ℂ_p}, and the A₀-ideal p^N·𝔪_{ℂ_p} is not finitely generated). Lean name: `Huber.IsNoetherianType A` (a Prop-valued class).
hypotheses: A is a commutative ring with a topology making it a topological ring and a Huber ring (`IsHuberRing A`).
proofSteps: The definition is the disjunction of (i) and (ii); no choice of pair of definition is part of the data.

The discrete case: for discrete A the image R of ℤ → A is a subring, open because A is discrete, and (R, 0) is a pair of definition since the subspace topology on R is discrete, which is the 0-adic topology; R is a quotient of ℤ, hence noetherian.

Clause (i) implies clause (ii) for Tate rings: if A is Tate with noetherian ring of definition A₀, the completed rings A⟨X₁,…,X_k⟩ have the ring of definition Â₀⟨X₁,…,X_k⟩, the completion of the finitely generated A₀-algebra A₀[X], which is noetherian by R0/noetherian-adic-completion; inverting a pseudouniformiser gives A⟨X⟩ noetherian (Wedhorn Remark 6.37(3)).
acceptance: ℤ_p⟦T⟧ with the (p, T)-adic topology is of noetherian type by (i) and is not a Tate ring.
ℚ_p⟨T⟩ is of noetherian type by (i) (ring of definition ℤ_p⟨T⟩) and by (ii).
K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ for a perfectoid field K is not of noetherian type.

nodes.title: Adic homomorphisms of Huber rings
nodes.statement: Let A and B be Huber rings. A ring homomorphism φ : A → B is *adic* if there exist a pair of definition (A₀, I) of A and a ring of definition B₀ of B such that φ(A₀) ⊆ B₀ and the ideal φ(I)·B₀ of B₀ is an ideal of definition of B₀ (it is finitely generated, and the subspace topology of B₀ is the φ(I)B₀-adic topology); equivalently, there is a Tau Ceti pair of definition Q of B with φ(P.ringOfDefinition) ⊆ Q.ringOfDefinition and Q.idealOfDefinition equal to the ideal of Q.ringOfDefinition generated by φ(P.idealOfDefinition). Every adic homomorphism is continuous. Lean name: `Huber.IsAdicHom φ` (a Prop). Huber 1994 recalls this definition from his 1993 paper; Wedhorn records it as Definition 6.23.

proofSteps: Definition by existence of the pairs of definition; continuity: φ(Iⁿ A₀) ⊆ (φ(I)B₀)ⁿ, and the latter form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0 in B.

More precisely, for every pair of definition (A₀, I) of A, B₀ := π(closure of A₀⟨X⟩_T) is a ring of definition of B and φ(I)·B₀ is an ideal of definition of B₀.

nodes.title: Rings topologically of finite type over a ring of noetherian type are of noetherian type
nodes.statement: Let A be a complete Hausdorff Huber ring of noetherian type (R0/noetherian-type-huber-ring) and φ : A → B a ring homomorphism to a complete Hausdorff Huber ring B with `IsTopologicallyFiniteType φ` (Tau Ceti). Then B is of noetherian type. More precisely: (i) if A has a noetherian ring of definition A₀, then B has the noetherian ring of definition π(Â₀⟨X⟩_T) (Huber 1994 Corollary 3.4(iii), Wedhorn Proposition 6.35); (ii) if A is a strongly noetherian Tate ring, then B is a strongly noetherian Tate ring (Huber 1994 Corollary 3.4(ii), Wedhorn Remark 6.37(1)).
hypotheses: A complete Hausdorff Huber ring of noetherian type.
B complete Hausdorff Huber ring.
φ : A → B with Tau Ceti `IsTopologicallyFiniteType φ`.
proofSteps: (i) The presenting ring Â⟨X⟩_T has the ring of definition Â₀⟨X⟩_T, the completion of A₀[t·X_i : t ∈ T_i] (Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.weighted` and `PairOfDefinition.completion`). A₀[t·X_i] is a finitely generated A₀-algebra (the T_i are finite), hence noetherian (Hilbert basis theorem), and its completion is noetherian by R0/noetherian-adic-completion.
(i) cont.: π is an open quotient map, so π(Â₀⟨X⟩_T) is a ring of definition of B (proof of R0/topologically-finite-type-is-adic), and a quotient of a noetherian ring is noetherian.

(ii) B is Tate: a continuous homomorphism from a Tate ring has Tate target (Wedhorn Proposition 6.25, `Huber.IsAdicHom.of_isTateRing` in R0/adic-ring-homomorphism). Over a Tate base, topologically finite type equals strictly topologically finite type (Wedhorn Proposition 6.34), and a ring strictly topologically of finite type over a strongly noetherian ring is strongly noetherian (Tau Ceti `IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType.isStronglyNoetherian`). The weighted-to-strict step is the step of the anchor's Corollary 8.35 (every Tate ring topologically of finite type over a strongly noetherian Tate ring is strongly noetherian), imported from anchor Layer 4.

nodes.title: Ideals of complete rings of noetherian type are closed
nodes.statement: Let A be a complete Hausdorff Huber ring of noetherian type. Then every ideal J ⊆ A is closed, and A/J with the quotient topology is a complete Hausdorff Huber ring of noetherian type; the quotient pair (A/J, integral closure of the image of A⁺) (Tau Ceti `Pair.quotient`) is a complete Huber pair and the quotient map is a quotient mapping in Huber's sense.
hypotheses: A complete Hausdorff Huber ring of noetherian type.
J an ideal of A; A⁺ a ring of integral elements for the quotient-pair statement.
proofSteps: Tate case: A is a noetherian ring (R0/noetherian-type-huber-ring), complete and first countable; Tau Ceti `isClosed_of_isNoetherian` (every submodule of a noetherian complete metrisable module over a complete Tate ring is closed) applied to A as a module over itself.

Noetherian ring of definition case: let (A₀, I) be a pair of definition with A₀ noetherian; A₀ is I-adically complete because A is complete and A₀ is open (closed); J ∩ A₀ is an ideal of A₀ and A₀/(J ∩ A₀) is I-adically Hausdorff by Krull's intersection theorem (Mathlib `IsHausdorff.of_le_jacobson`, with I ⊆ Jac(A₀) by `IsAdicComplete.le_jacobson_bot`), so J ∩ A₀ = ⋂ₙ (J ∩ A₀ + Iⁿ) is closed in A₀; since A₀ is open, J is closed in A (an additive subgroup whose intersection with an open subgroup is closed is closed).

A/J is Hausdorff because J is closed, complete because a quotient of a complete metrisable group by a closed subgroup is complete, and Huber with pair of definition the image of (A₀, I); A → A/J is an open quotient map, hence topologically of finite type, so A/J is of noetherian type (R0/topologically-finite-type-noetherian-type).
The plus ring of the quotient pair is Tau Ceti's `Pair.quotient` construction.
acceptance: In ℚ_p⟨T⟩ every ideal, e.g. (T), is closed; in ℤ_p⟦T⟧ every ideal is closed.

Non-example outside the hypothesis: in the Tate ring C(ℤ_p, ℚ_p) of continuous functions with the supremum norm, the ideal of functions vanishing on a neighbourhood of 0 is not closed (its closure is the ideal of functions vanishing at 0, which contains x ↦ x).

nodes.title: Completion of a strict exact complex is strict exact
nodes.statement: Let C⁰ → C¹ → ⋯ be a complex of Hausdorff abelian topological groups whose topologies are defined by a countable fundamental system of open subgroups, with continuous differentials. If the complex is exact and every differential is strict (continuous and open onto its image with the subspace topology), then the completed complex Ĉ⁰ → Ĉ¹ → ⋯ is exact and its differentials are strict.
hypotheses: each Cⁱ is linearly topologised with a countable basis of open subgroups
exactness and strictness of every differential
proofSteps: Uniform structures: each Cⁱ is a Hausdorff abelian group with a countable basis (Uⁱ_k) of open subgroups, so it is metrisable and its completion Ĉⁱ (Mathlib UniformSpace.Completion) has the closures of the Uⁱ_k as a basis of open subgroups; every continuous homomorphism extends uniquely to a continuous homomorphism of completions.

Strict maps complete to strict maps: for a strict d : C → D with image E ⊆ D, openness gives for every k an l with d(U_l) ⊇ E ∩ V_k. The closure Ē of E in D̂ is the completion of E; given y ∈ Ē ∩ V̄_k choose a sequence e_j ∈ E converging to y with e_{j+1} − e_j ∈ V_{k_j} for a rapidly increasing sequence k_j, lift each difference to U_{l_j} and sum the lifts: the series converges in Ĉ (the U_{l_j} shrink) to x ∈ Ū_l with d̂(x) = y. Hence d̂(Ĉ) = Ē and d̂ : Ĉ → Ē is open.

Exactness at Ĉⁱ: im(d̂ⁱ⁻¹) is the closure of im(dⁱ⁻¹) by the previous step; ker(d̂ⁱ) is the closure of ker(dⁱ), because for x ∈ ker(d̂ⁱ) approximated by x_j ∈ Cⁱ the elements dⁱ(x_j) → 0 lift, by strictness of dⁱ, to elements z_j → 0 with dⁱ(z_j) = dⁱ(x_j), and x_j − z_j ∈ ker(dⁱ) converges to x. Since ker(dⁱ) = im(dⁱ⁻¹), the two closures agree.

nodes.title: Linear maps of finite modules over a Huber ring with a noetherian ring of definition are strict (Huber Lemma 2.3(i))
nodes.statement: Let A be a Huber ring with a pair of definition (A₀, I) (Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition A`) such that A₀ is a noetherian ring. For a finitely generated A-module M, the natural topology of M is the module topology (Mathlib `IsModuleTopology A M`: the finest topology making M a topological A-module); for every finitely generated A₀-submodule M₀ ⊆ M generating M over A, the subgroups IⁿM₀ (n ≥ 0) form a fundamental system of open neighbourhoods of 0. Then for finitely generated A-modules M and N with their natural topologies, every A-linear map u : M → N is strict: it is continuous, and u : M → u(M) is open for the subspace topology on u(M) ⊆ N.
hypotheses: A Huber ring with a pair of definition (A₀, I), A₀ noetherian (completeness is not assumed).
M, N finitely generated A-modules with their natural (module) topologies.
proofSteps: Natural topology: if m₁, …, m_s generate M₀ over A₀ and M over A, then (x₁, …, x_s) ↦ ∑ x_j m_j is a continuous open surjection Aˢ → M for the module topology, and it maps (IⁿA₀)ˢ onto IⁿM₀; hence the IⁿM₀ form a basis of open neighbourhoods of 0 (Huber 1994, before Lemma 2.3). A-linear maps between modules with module topologies are continuous (Mathlib IsModuleTopology.continuous_of_linearMap).

Choose a finitely generated A₀-submodule N₀ ⊆ N generating N with u(M₀) ⊆ N₀ (add the finitely many u(m_j) to generators of N). Q := u(M) ∩ N₀ is an A₀-submodule of the finite A₀-module N₀, hence finitely generated (A₀ noetherian).
Artin–Rees (Mathlib Ideal.exists_pow_inf_eq_pow_smul; EGA 0_I 7.3.2): there is c with Q ∩ IⁿN₀ = Iⁿ⁻ᶜ(Q ∩ IᶜN₀) ⊆ Iⁿ⁻ᶜQ for n ≥ c, so the subspace topology on Q ⊆ N₀ is its I-adic topology.
Each of the finitely many generators q of Q lies in u(M) = A·u(M₀); for a ∈ A there is k with Iᵏa ⊆ A₀ (a·x → 0 as x → 0 and A₀ is open), so IᵏQ ⊆ A₀·u(M₀) = u(M₀) for some k.
Hence u(IⁿM₀) = Iⁿu(M₀) ⊇ Iⁿ⁺ᵏQ ⊇ u(M) ∩ Iⁿ⁺ᵏ⁺ᶜN₀, which is a neighbourhood of 0 in u(M) for the subspace topology: u is open onto its image.
acceptance: For A = ℤ_p⟨T⟩ (ring of definition itself, ideal (p)) the inclusion of the ideal (T) into A is strict: the subspace topology on (T) is the p-adic topology of (T) ≅ A.

Outside the hypothesis the statement fails: for the Tate ring A = C(ℤ_p, ℚ_p) (supremum norm, ring of definition the functions with values in ℤ_p, not noetherian), multiplication by the function x ↦ x is an A-linear map A → A with non-closed image, hence not strict (a strict map of complete metrisable groups has complete, hence closed, image).

nodes.title: Finite modules over a complete Huber ring with a noetherian ring of definition are complete, with closed submodules (Huber Lemma 2.3(ii))
nodes.statement: Let A be a complete Hausdorff Huber ring with a pair of definition (A₀, I) such that A₀ is noetherian, and let M be a finitely generated A-module with its natural topology (R0/noetherian-rod-module-topology-strict). Then M is complete and Hausdorff, and every A-submodule of M is closed in M. For every finitely generated A₀-submodule M₀ ⊆ M generating M, M₀ is open in M and I-adically complete and separated.
hypotheses: A complete Hausdorff Huber ring with a pair of definition (A₀, I), A₀ noetherian.
M a finitely generated A-module with its natural topology.
proofSteps: A₀ is open, hence closed, in the complete ring A, so A₀ is complete for its I-adic topology; being noetherian with I ⊆ Jac(A₀) (Mathlib IsAdicComplete.le_jacobson_bot), every finite A₀-module M₀ is I-adically Hausdorff (Mathlib IsHausdorff.of_le_jacobson) and the canonical map Â₀ ⊗ M₀ → M̂₀ is bijective (Mathlib AdicCompletion.ofTensorProduct_bijective_of_finite_of_isNoetherian), so M₀ = M̂₀ is I-adically complete (EGA 0_I 7.3.6).

M₀ is open in M with the I-adic topology as subspace topology (R0/noetherian-rod-module-topology-strict); an abelian topological group with a complete Hausdorff open subgroup is complete and Hausdorff, so M is.

For a submodule M' ⊆ M, M' ∩ M₀ is an A₀-submodule of M₀, finite (A₀ noetherian), hence I-adically complete by the first step; by Artin–Rees (Mathlib Ideal.exists_pow_inf_eq_pow_smul) its I-adic topology is the subspace topology, so M' ∩ M₀ is a complete subgroup of the Hausdorff group M₀, hence closed in M₀. A subgroup whose intersection with an open subgroup is closed is closed, so M' is closed in M.
acceptance: For A = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ ((p, T)-adic) every ideal is closed and A/(pT) is complete.
M = ℤ_p⟨T⟩/(T − p) ≅ ℤ_p over A = ℤ_p⟨T⟩ is complete, and its submodule pM is closed.

nodes.title: Completion of a finite module over a Huber ring with a noetherian ring of definition is base change to Â (Huber Lemma 2.3(iii))
nodes.statement: Let A be a Huber ring with a pair of definition (A₀, I) such that A₀ is noetherian, Â its completion (Tau Ceti `IsHuberRing.completion`), and M a finitely generated A-module with its natural topology. Then the canonical map M ⊗_A Â → M̂ to the Hausdorff completion of M is an isomorphism of topological Â-modules, where M ⊗_A Â carries its natural Â-module topology. In particular M ⊗_A Â is complete and Hausdorff.
hypotheses: A Huber ring with a pair of definition (A₀, I), A₀ noetherian.
M a finitely generated A-module.
proofSteps: Â has the pair of definition (Â₀, I·Â₀) with Â₀ noetherian (R0/noetherian-adic-completion), so R0/noetherian-rod-module-topology-strict and R0/noetherian-rod-module-complete apply over Â.

Choose a surjection π : Aⁿ → M with kernel K (an A-submodule, not necessarily finitely generated). The natural topology of M is the quotient topology of Aⁿ (module topology), so π is open, and K ⊆ Aⁿ carries the subspace topology: 0 → K → Aⁿ → M → 0 is exact with strict maps, and its completion 0 → K̂ → Âⁿ → M̂ → 0 is exact, with K̂ the closure of K in Âⁿ (R0/strict-complex-completion-exact).

By right exactness of ⊗_A Â, M ⊗_A Â = Âⁿ / Â·K. The Â-submodule Â·K ⊆ Âⁿ is closed (R0/noetherian-rod-module-complete over the complete ring Â) and contains K, so Â·K ⊇ K̂; conversely K̂ is an Â-submodule (closure of an A-submodule, by continuity of the Â-action) containing K, so Â·K ⊆ K̂. Hence M ⊗_A Â = Âⁿ/K̂ ≅ M̂ as Â-modules, compatibly with the canonical maps.

Topologies: both sides are finite Â-modules; M̂ is complete Hausdorff with the natural Â-topology (R0/noetherian-rod-module-complete) and the bijection is Â-linear, hence a homeomorphism for the natural topologies (R0/noetherian-rod-module-topology-strict over Â).
acceptance: For A = ℤ_p[T] with the p-adic topology and M = A/(T), M ⊗_A Â = ℤ_p⟨T⟩/(T) = ℤ_p = M̂.

nodes.title: Spec of a Huber ring and of an open subring agree away from the open primes (Huber 1993 Lemma 3.7)
nodes.statement: Let A be a Huber ring and B ⊆ A an open subring. Let T ⊆ Spec B be the set of open prime ideals of B (a closed subset) and f : Spec A → Spec B the morphism induced by the inclusion. Then f⁻¹(T) is the set of open prime ideals of A, and f restricts to an isomorphism of schemes Spec A ∖ f⁻¹(T) → Spec B ∖ T. Concretely, for every topologically nilpotent s ∈ B the map of localisations B_s → A_s is bijective, and the open sets D(s) ⊆ Spec B for such s cover Spec B ∖ T. For B = A₀ a ring of definition with ideal of definition I this reads Spec A ∖ V(I·A) ≅ Spec A₀ ∖ V(I).
hypotheses: A Huber ring; B ⊆ A an open subring.
proofSteps: For s ∈ B topologically nilpotent and a ∈ A, sⁿa → 0, so sⁿa ∈ B for n large because B is open; hence every a/sᵐ ∈ A_s equals sⁿa/sⁿ⁺ᵐ with sⁿa ∈ B, and B_s → A_s is surjective. It is injective because localisation is exact and B → A is injective (Mathlib IsLocalization.Away).

A prime 𝔭 of B is open iff it contains every topologically nilpotent element of B: if 𝔭 is open, sⁿ ∈ 𝔭 for topologically nilpotent s; conversely B ∩ A°° is open (A°° is open in the Huber ring A), so 𝔭 ⊇ B ∩ A°° is open (for B = A₀ this reads I ⊆ 𝔭). So every 𝔭 ∉ T misses some topologically nilpotent s ∈ B, i.e. the D(s) cover Spec B ∖ T, and their preimages D(s) ⊆ Spec A cover Spec A ∖ f⁻¹(T).
A prime 𝔮 of A is open iff 𝔮 ∩ B is open in B (B is open in A), so f⁻¹(T) is the set of open primes of A.
The isomorphisms Spec A_s ≅ Spec B_s are compatible on overlaps D(ss'), so they glue to the isomorphism Spec A ∖ f⁻¹(T) ≅ Spec B ∖ T.
acceptance: For A = ℚ_p⟨T⟩ and B = A₀ = ℤ_p⟨T⟩: T = V(p), f⁻¹(T) = ∅ and Spec ℚ_p⟨T⟩ ≅ Spec ℤ_p⟨T⟩ ∖ V(p), i.e. A = A₀[1/p].
For a discrete ring A and B its prime subring every prime is open and both complements are empty.

nodes.title: The blow-up scheme Proj(⊕ Jⁿ) of a finitely generated submodule (Huber 1994 (1.1)–(1.2))
nodes.statement: Let φ : C → B be a ring homomorphism, F = {f₀, …, fₙ} ⊆ B a finite subset generating the unit ideal of B, and J ⊆ B the C-submodule generated by F. Let R(J) := ⊕_{n≥0} Jⁿ·Tⁿ ⊆ B[T] (J⁰ := φ(C); for n ≥ 1, Jⁿ is the additive subgroup generated by the products j₁⋯jₙ, j_i ∈ J), an ℕ-graded ring (Mathlib `GradedAlgebra`) generated over R(J)₀ = φ(C) by the degree-one elements f·T, f ∈ F. Put Y := Proj R(J) with g : Y → Spec C the composite of Mathlib's `Proj.toSpecZero` and Spec(C → φ(C)). The evaluation R(J) → B, T ↦ 1, maps the irrelevant ideal onto an ideal containing F, hence onto B, and so defines s : X := Spec B → Y (Mathlib `Proj.fromOfGlobalSections`) with g ∘ s = Spec φ; this is Huber's diagram (1.1) in the case I := J·B = B, where X = Proj(⊕ Iⁿ) = Spec B. Properties (Huber (1.2)(i),(ii)): (a) the opens D₊(f·T), f ∈ F, cover Y and s⁻¹(D₊(f·T)) = D(f), so s is affine; (b) for a nonempty S ⊆ F with product t = ∏_{f∈S} f, the open U = D₊(t·T^{|S|}) is affine with O_Y(U) = C[f/f' : f ∈ F, f' ∈ S] ⊆ B_t (the φ(C)-subalgebra of the localisation B_t generated by these fractions) and O_X(s⁻¹U) = B_t; (c) g is projective, hence proper and separated, and Y is noetherian when C is. Lean name: `AlgebraicGeometry.submoduleBlowup φ F`.
hypotheses: C, B commutative rings, φ : C → B a ring homomorphism.
F ⊆ B finite with F·B = B; J the C-submodule generated by F.
proofSteps: R(J) is a graded subring of B[T]; since J is generated by F as a C-module, Jⁿ is generated by the monomials of degree n in F, so R(J) is generated in degree one by F·T and is of finite type over φ(C) (Mathlib GradedAlgebra, Submodule powers).

The irrelevant ideal is generated by F·T, so the D₊(f·T) cover Y (Mathlib Proj.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top). Its image under T ↦ 1 contains F, which generates B, so Mathlib Proj.fromOfGlobalSections gives s, with s⁻¹(D₊(r)) = D(r(1)) for homogeneous r of positive degree (Proj.fromOfGlobalSections_preimage_basicOpen) and g ∘ s = Spec φ (Proj.fromOfGlobalSections_toSpecZero).

(b): D₊(t·T^{|S|}) ≅ Spec of the degree-zero part of R(J)_{tT^{|S|}} (Mathlib Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec, HomogeneousLocalization.Away). Its elements are a·T^{k|S|}/(t·T^{|S|})ᵏ with a ∈ J^{k|S|}; writing a as a sum of products of k|S| elements of F and tᵏ as a product of k|S| elements of S shows that the map to B_t, a·T^{k|S|}/(tT^{|S|})ᵏ ↦ a/tᵏ, has image C[f/f']. It is injective: if a/tᵏ = 0 in B_t then tᴺa = 0 in B, so (tT^{|S|})ᴺ·aT^{k|S|} = 0 in R(J) ⊆ B[T].

(c): R(J) is of finite type over φ(C), so Proj.toSpecZero is proper (Mathlib: separated by Proj.isSeparated, universally closed by Proj.valuativeCriterion_existence, the IsProper instance for finite type graded algebras); Spec φ(C) → Spec C is a closed immersion, hence proper.
acceptance: For C = ℤ_p⟨T⟩ ⊆ B = ℚ_p⟨T⟩ and F = {p, T} (p is a unit of B), J = (p, T) is an ideal of C, R(J) is the Rees algebra of (p, T) and Y is the blow-up of Spec ℤ_p⟨T⟩ in (p, T), with the two charts Spec ℤ_p⟨T⟩[T/p] and Spec ℤ_p⟨T⟩[p/T]; s maps Spec ℚ_p⟨T⟩ into the complement of the exceptional divisor.
Huber's construction is recovered: the charts C[F/f] are the rings of definition of the rational localisations B(F/f) used in (1.3.1)(ii).

nodes.title: The submodule blow-up is an isomorphism away from the centre (Huber 1994 (1.2)(iii))
nodes.statement: In the situation of R0/submodule-blow-up (φ : C → B, F ⊆ B finite with F·B = B, J = ∑_{f∈F} C·f, Y = Proj R(J), g : Y → Spec C), let H ⊆ C be an ideal such that Spec φ restricts to an isomorphism Spec B ∖ V(H·B) → Spec C ∖ V(H). Then g restricts to an isomorphism g⁻¹(Spec C ∖ V(H)) → Spec C ∖ V(H). In particular, if B is a Huber ring, C ⊆ B a ring of definition with ideal of definition I and φ the inclusion, then g is an isomorphism over Spec C ∖ V(I).
hypotheses: φ, F, J, Y, g as in R0/submodule-blow-up (F·B = B).
H ⊆ C an ideal with Spec B ∖ V(H·B) ≅ Spec C ∖ V(H) via Spec φ.
proofSteps: Let h ∈ H. Localisation is exact, so R(J) ⊗_C C_h = ⊕ (J_h)ⁿTⁿ ⊆ B_h[T] with J_h the C_h-submodule of B_h generated by F, and g⁻¹(D(h)) = Proj R(J_h) (Mathlib Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec on the charts D₊(f·T), whose rings C[F/f] localise to C_h[F/f]).

By hypothesis C_h → B_h is an isomorphism, so J_h is an ideal of C_h ≅ B_h containing F, hence J_h = C_h (F generates the unit ideal), and R(J_h) = C_h[T]; each chart C_h[F/f] equals (C_h)_f because 1/f = ∑ c_i f_i/f for a relation 1 = ∑ c_i f_i.

The charts D₊(f·T) ∩ g⁻¹(D(h)) ≅ D(f) ⊆ Spec C_h cover g⁻¹(D(h)) and map isomorphically onto the cover {D(f)} of D(h) (F generates the unit ideal), compatibly on overlaps; so g⁻¹(D(h)) → D(h) is an isomorphism, and these glue over h ∈ H.
For a ring of definition C ⊆ B with ideal of definition I, Spec B ∖ V(I·B) ≅ Spec C ∖ V(I) by R0/open-subring-spec-isomorphism, so H = I satisfies the hypothesis.

nodes.title: Deep Čech cocycles are coboundaries from a fixed level (Huber 1994 (1.3.1)(i))
nodes.statement: Let B be a Huber ring with a pair of definition (C, I) such that C is noetherian, let F = {f₀, …, fₙ} ⊆ B generate the unit ideal, J = ∑ C·f_i, and let g : Y = Proj R(J) → Spec C and s : Spec B → Y be as in R0/submodule-blow-up. Let P be a finitely generated B-module and N ⊆ P a finitely generated C-submodule generating P over B; let 𝒢 ⊆ s_*(P̃) be the image of the morphism σ : g*(Ñ) → s_*(P̃) adjoint to Ñ → g_*s_*(P̃) = (P as a C-module)~ induced by N ⊆ P, a coherent O_Y-module. For i ≥ 1 let K_i^• be the augmented Čech complex of Iⁱ𝒢 for the affine open covering 𝔘 = {D₊(f₀T), …, D₊(fₙT)} of Y (degree −1: global sections), and let K_0^• be that of s_*(P̃); since s_*(P̃) ⊇ 𝒢 ⊇ I𝒢 ⊇ I²𝒢 ⊇ ⋯ these are subcomplexes K_0 ⊇ K_1 ⊇ K_2 ⊇ ⋯, and K_0^• is the augmented Čech complex (**) 0 → P → ∏ P_{f_{i₀}} → ∏ P_{f_{i₀}f_{i₁}} → ⋯ of P̃ for the covering D(f₀), …, D(fₙ) of Spec B (s⁻¹D₊(f_iT) = D(f_i)). Write d_i^p : K_i^p → K_i^{p+1} for the differentials. Then for every p ∈ ℤ and every u ≥ 1 there is v ≥ u with ker(d_v^{p+1}) ⊆ im(d_u^p) = d^p(K_u^p).
hypotheses: B Huber with noetherian ring of definition C, ideal of definition I (finitely generated).
F ⊆ B finite generating the unit ideal; P a finite B-module; N ⊆ P a finite C-submodule generating P.
proofSteps: Y is noetherian and proper over Spec C (R0/submodule-blow-up (c)); 𝒢 is coherent as the image of the coherent g*(Ñ) in the quasi-coherent s_*(P̃) (s affine), and so is every Iⁱ𝒢 (coherent sheaves on noetherian schemes: supplier JacobianChallenge Layer B).
For p ≤ −2 the claim is empty; for p = −1, ker(d_v^0) = d^{−1}(K_v^{−1}) ⊆ d^{−1}(K_u^{−1}) for v ≥ u. Fix p ≥ 0.

Čech cohomology computes sheaf cohomology: 𝔘 is a finite affine open covering of the separated scheme Y and Iⁱ𝒢 is quasi-coherent, so Hⁿ(K_i^•) = Hⁿ(Y, Iⁱ𝒢) (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.Cohomology) for n ≥ 1 (supplier JacobianChallenge Layer B: Čech ≃ derived on a separated scheme).

Artin–Rees in cohomology (EGA III 3.3.2; AdicSpacesPartII:F0/graded-cohomology-finiteness (i) applied to the proper C-scheme Y, the ideal I and 𝒢): ⊕_u H^{p+1}(Y, I^u𝒢) is a finite module over the Rees algebra ⊕ I^u, so there is k with H^{p+1}(Y, I^{u+r}𝒢) = I^r ⊙ H^{p+1}(Y, I^u𝒢) for all u ≥ k, r ≥ 0, where x ⊙ y is the image of y under multiplication by x : I^u𝒢 → I^{u+r}𝒢 (Huber (1)). In particular each H^{p+1}(Y, I^u𝒢) is a finite C-module.

Torsion: for c ∈ I, localisation at c is exact and commutes with the Čech complex of a quasi-coherent sheaf on an affine covering (Mathlib IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_basicOpen), so H^{p+1}(Y, I^u𝒢)_c = H^{p+1}(g⁻¹D(c), I^u𝒢); g⁻¹(D(c)) ≅ D(c) is affine (R0/submodule-blow-up-isomorphism-away with H = I), so this vanishes (acyclicity of affines, supplier JacobianChallenge Layer B). Hence Supp H^{p+1}(Y, I^u𝒢) ⊆ V(I), I ⊆ √Ann (Mathlib Module.support_eq_zeroLocus), and since I is finitely generated there is t with I^t·H^{p+1}(Y, I^u𝒢) = 0 (Mathlib Ideal.exists_pow_le_of_le_radical_of_fg) — Huber (2), replacing his reference to EGA I (1971) 1.6.8.4.

Conclusion (Huber): it suffices to treat u ≥ k, since im(d_u^p) ⊇ im(d_k^p) for u ≤ k. Put v = u + t. For a ∈ ker(d_v^{p+1}) with class ā ∈ H^{p+1}(Y, I^{u+t}𝒢) write ā = ∑ x_j ⊙ ȳ_j with x_j ∈ I^t and y_j ∈ ker(d_u^{p+1}); then a − ∑ x_j y_j ∈ im(d_v^p) ⊆ im(d_u^p), and each x_j y_j ∈ im(d_u^p) because x_j ȳ_j = 0 in H^{p+1}(Y, I^u𝒢). Hence a ∈ im(d_u^p).

nodes.title: The Čech complexes of Iⁱ𝒢 form a neighbourhood basis in the natural topology (Huber 1994 (1.3.1)(ii))
nodes.statement: Let B be a Huber ring with a pair of definition (C, I) such that C is noetherian, let F = {f₀, …, fₙ} ⊆ B generate the unit ideal, J = ∑ C·f_i, and let g : Y = Proj R(J) → Spec C and s : Spec B → Y be as in R0/submodule-blow-up. Let P be a finitely generated B-module and N ⊆ P a finitely generated C-submodule generating P over B; let 𝒢 ⊆ s_*(P̃) be the image of the morphism σ : g*(Ñ) → s_*(P̃) adjoint to Ñ → g_*s_*(P̃) = (P as a C-module)~ induced by N ⊆ P, a coherent O_Y-module. For i ≥ 1 let K_i^• be the augmented Čech complex of Iⁱ𝒢 for the affine open covering 𝔘 = {D₊(f₀T), …, D₊(fₙT)} of Y (degree −1: global sections), and let K_0^• be that of s_*(P̃); since s_*(P̃) ⊇ 𝒢 ⊇ I𝒢 ⊇ I²𝒢 ⊇ ⋯ these are subcomplexes K_0 ⊇ K_1 ⊇ K_2 ⊇ ⋯, and K_0^• is the augmented Čech complex (**) 0 → P → ∏ P_{f_{i₀}} → ∏ P_{f_{i₀}f_{i₁}} → ⋯ of P̃ for the covering D(f₀), …, D(fₙ) of Spec B (s⁻¹D₊(f_iT) = D(f_i)). Write d_i^p : K_i^p → K_i^{p+1} for the differentials. Give P its natural topology as a B-module and, for S = {f_{i₀}, …, f_{i_p}} ⊆ F with product t, give P_t = P ⊗_B B_t its natural topology over the Huber ring B(F/S) (the uncompleted rational localisation: the ring B_t with ring of definition C[f/f' : f ∈ F, f' ∈ S] and ideal of definition I·C[f/f'], Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.locSubring`, `PairOfDefinition.locIdeal`), and K_0^p the product topology. Then for every p ∈ ℤ the subgroups K_i^p (i ≥ 1) form a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of 0 in K_0^p.
hypotheses: As in R0/blow-up-cech-artin-rees.
proofSteps: p ≥ 0: by R0/submodule-blow-up (b), D₊(t·T^{|S|}) is affine with ring C[F/S] ⊆ B_t and s⁻¹ of it is D(t), so Γ(D₊(tT^{|S|}), s_*P̃) = P_t and Γ(D₊(tT^{|S|}), Iⁱ𝒢) = Lⁱ·G_S, where G_S is the image of N ⊗_C C[F/S] in P_t and L = I·C[F/S]. G_S is a finitely generated C[F/S]-submodule generating P_t over B_t, and C[F/S] is noetherian (Mathlib Algebra.FiniteType.isNoetherianRing), so {Lⁱ·G_S} is a basis of neighbourhoods of 0 for the natural topology (R0/noetherian-rod-module-topology-strict applied to the Huber ring B(F/S)); K_i^p is the finite product of these.
p = −1: K_i^{−1} = Γ(Y, Iⁱ𝒢) and K_0^{−1} = P. By construction IⁱN ⊆ Γ(Y, Iⁱ𝒢), and IⁱN is open in P (R0/noetherian-rod-module-topology-strict), so every K_i^{−1} is a neighbourhood of 0.

Conversely fix k. By EGA III 3.3.2 (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/graded-cohomology-finiteness (i) with p = 0) there is r with Γ(Y, I^{r+j}𝒢) = I^j·Γ(Y, I^r𝒢) for all j ≥ 0. Γ(Y, I^r𝒢) ⊆ P is a finitely generated C-submodule and IᵏN is an open C-submodule, so I^j·Γ(Y, I^r𝒢) ⊆ IᵏN for some j (finitely many generators, I^j·x → 0); hence K_{r+j}^{−1} ⊆ IᵏN.

nodes.title: Strict Čech exactness for standard rational coverings when B has a noetherian ring of definition (Huber 1994 (1.3))
nodes.statement: Let B be a complete Hausdorff Huber ring with a noetherian ring of definition C (ideal of definition I), B⁺ a ring of integral elements, f₀, …, fₙ ∈ B elements generating the unit ideal, and P a finitely generated B-module. Put U_i = R(f₀, …, fₙ / f_i) ⊆ Spa(B, B⁺) and, for i₀ < ⋯ < i_p, U_{i₀…i_p} = U_{i₀} ∩ ⋯ ∩ U_{i_p} (rational, with 𝒪(U_{i₀…i_p}) the completion B⟨F/f_{i₀}, …, F/f_{i_p}⟩ of the uncompleted rational localisation B(F/f_{i₀}, …, F/f_{i_p}), whose ring is B_{f_{i₀}⋯f_{i_p}}). Give each P ⊗_B 𝒪(U_{i₀…i_p}) its natural topology. Then the augmented Čech complex (*) 0 → P → ∏_{i₀} P ⊗_B 𝒪(U_{i₀}) → ∏_{i₀<i₁} P ⊗_B 𝒪(U_{i₀i₁}) → ⋯ is exact and all its differentials are strict. This is Huber's (1.3) for 𝓕 = P ⊗ 𝒪_B, stated with the terms written out; the case P = B is the structure sheaf.
hypotheses: B complete Hausdorff with a noetherian ring of definition C and ideal of definition I ⊆ C.
f₀, …, fₙ ∈ B generate the unit ideal.
P a finitely generated B-module.
proofSteps: The algebraic Čech complex (**) 0 → P → ∏ P_{f_{i₀}} → ∏ P_{f_{i₀}f_{i₁}} → ⋯ of P̃ for the covering D(f₀), …, D(fₙ) of Spec B is exact (R0/localization-cech-complex-exact).

Give P_{f_{i₀}⋯f_{i_p}} = P ⊗_B B(F/f_{i₀}, …) its natural topology over the uncompleted rational localisation (ring of definition C[F/f_{i₀}, …], noetherian, Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.locSubring`); the differentials are linear, hence continuous (Mathlib IsModuleTopology.continuous_of_linearMap). Each term has a countable basis of neighbourhoods of 0, and its completion is P ⊗_B 𝒪(U_{i₀…i_p}) (R0/noetherian-rod-module-completion-tensor, with 𝒪(U) the completion of B(F/f), Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.completionLocObj`), so the completion (**)^ of (**) is (*).

Strictness of (**): with Y, g, s, 𝒢 and the subcomplexes K_0 = (**) ⊇ K_1 ⊇ ⋯ of R0/submodule-blow-up and R0/blow-up-cech-artin-rees, fix p and u ≥ 1 and take v as in R0/blow-up-cech-artin-rees; then im(d_0^p) ∩ K_v^{p+1} ⊆ ker(d_v^{p+1}) ⊆ im(d_u^p) = d_0^p(K_u^p).

By R0/blow-up-cech-filtration-neighbourhoods for K^{p+1}, im(d_0^p) ∩ K_v^{p+1} is a neighbourhood of 0 in im(d_0^p); so d_0^p(K_u^p) is a neighbourhood of 0 in the image for every u, and since the K_u^p form a neighbourhood basis of K_0^p (R0/blow-up-cech-filtration-neighbourhoods), d_0^p : K_0^p → im(d_0^p) is open.
(**) is exact with strict differentials between Hausdorff groups with countable neighbourhood bases, so its completion (*) is exact with strict differentials (R0/strict-complex-completion-exact).
acceptance: For B = ℤ_p⟨T⟩ with ring of definition ℤ_p⟨T⟩ (p-adic) and f₀ = 1, f₁ = T the covering {|T| ≤ 1}, {|T| ≥ 1} of Spa(B, B) gives an exact strict complex 0 → B → B × ℤ_p⟨T, T⁻¹⟩ → ℤ_p⟨T, T⁻¹⟩ → 0.

nodes.title: Huber pairs with a noetherian ring of definition are sheafy (Huber 1994 Theorem 2.2, Case I)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair with A complete and Hausdorff and having a noetherian ring of definition, and X = Spa(A, A⁺). Then: (a) for every rational subset U ⊆ X the complete ring 𝒪_X(U) has a noetherian ring of definition; (b) for every finitely generated A-module M, every rational subset U and every g₀, …, g_m ∈ 𝒪_X(U) generating the unit ideal, the augmented Čech complex of the standard rational covering {V_j = U ∩ R(g/g_j)} of U with terms M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(V_{j₀} ∩ ⋯ ∩ V_{j_p}) (natural topologies) is exact with strict differentials; (c) every open covering of a rational subset U has a refinement by such a standard rational covering; (d) the structure presheaf 𝒪_X is a sheaf of complete topological rings, i.e. (A, A⁺) is sheafy (the anchor's `Huber.IsSheafyPair`). Sheaf-cohomology vanishing is AdicSpacesPartII:R3/noetherian-rod-acyclicity-finite-modules.
hypotheses: A complete Hausdorff Huber ring with a noetherian ring of definition (A is not assumed Tate).
A⁺ a ring of integral elements; M a finitely generated A-module (for (b)).
proofSteps: (a) For U = R(T/s), 𝒪_X(U) is the completion of A(T/s), whose ring of definition A₀[T/s] (Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.locSubring`) is a finitely generated A₀-algebra, hence noetherian (Mathlib Algebra.FiniteType.isNoetherianRing); its completion is noetherian (R0/noetherian-adic-completion) and is a ring of definition of 𝒪_X(U) (Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.completionLocObj`). Huber: 'for every rational subset U, F_A(U)^ is complete and has a noetherian ring of definition'.

(b) Spa(𝒪_X(U), 𝒪_X⁺(U)) ≅ U matching rational subsets and their rings (Huber 1994 Lemma 1.5, (1.4); anchor Layer 3), so the covering {V_j} is the standard covering {R(g/g_j)} of Spa 𝒪_X(U); apply R0/noetherian-rod-laurent-cech-strict to B = 𝒪_X(U) (noetherian ring of definition by (a)) and P = M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U), using M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(V) = P ⊗_B 𝒪_X(V).
(c) Huber Lemma 2.6 = Wedhorn Lemma 7.54 for the complete affinoid ring 𝒪_X(U) (anchor Layer 2), transported to U by (b)'s identification.

(d) Rational subsets form a basis closed under finite intersections (anchor Layer 2), so by Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.isSheaf_iff_isSheafFor_rationalCover` and EGA 0_I 3.2.2 it suffices to treat coverings 𝔙 of rational U by rational subsets. Choose a standard refinement 𝔘 (c). Exactness of 0 → 𝒪(U) → ∏_𝔘 𝒪 → ∏ 𝒪 ((b), M = A) gives injectivity and gluing for 𝔘; 𝔘 restricted to each V ∈ 𝔙 is a standard covering of V (images of the g_j), so injectivity on V gives the sheaf condition for 𝔙 (Huber: a refinement suffices).

Topology: 𝒪(U) → ∏_𝔙 𝒪(V) → ∏_𝔘 𝒪(W) is injective and strict by (b), so the first map is a topological embedding; each 𝒪(U) is complete (R0/noetherian-rod-module-complete with M = A). Hence 𝒪_X is a sheaf of complete topological rings on the basis and on X (EGA 0_I 3.2.2).

nodes.title: Discrete Huber pairs are sheafy with Čech-acyclic rational coverings (Wedhorn Theorem 8.28(c))
nodes.statement: Let A be a ring with the discrete topology and A⁺ ⊆ A an integrally closed subring, so that (A, A⁺) is a complete Huber pair (pair of definition (A, 0)) and Spa(A, A⁺) = {v ∈ Spv A : v(a) ≤ 1 for all a ∈ A⁺}. Then: (a) for every rational subset U = R(T/s), 𝒪(U) = A_s with the discrete topology; (b) for every finite covering (U_j = R(T_j/s_j)) of a rational subset U = R(T/s) by rational subsets and every A-module M, the augmented Čech complex 0 → M_s → ∏ M_{s_{j₀}} → ∏ M_{s_{j₀}s_{j₁}} → ⋯ of the covering with coefficients M ⊗_A 𝒪 is exact in all degrees; (c) 𝒪 is a sheaf of complete (discrete) topological rings on Spa(A, A⁺), i.e. (A, A⁺) is sheafy. No noetherian hypothesis is made.
hypotheses: A a discrete ring (any commutative ring); A⁺ ⊆ A integrally closed.
M an arbitrary A-module (for (b)).
proofSteps: (a) With the pair of definition (A, 0), the uncompleted rational localisation A(T/s) is A_s with ring of definition A[T/s] and ideal of definition 0 (Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.locSubring`, `PairOfDefinition.locIdeal`), so its topology is discrete and it is complete: 𝒪(R(T/s)) = A_s (anchor Layer 3).

Covering: U_j ⊆ U gives a restriction A_s → A_{s_j}, so D(s_j) ⊆ D(s) in Spec A. For 𝔭 ∈ D(s) the trivial valuation v_𝔭 (value 0 on 𝔭, 1 elsewhere) lies in Spa(A, A⁺) (every valuation is continuous on a discrete ring) and in U, hence in some U_j, so s_j ∉ 𝔭: the D(s_j) cover D(s) = Spec A_s (anchor Layer 2).
Intersections: U_{j₀} ∩ ⋯ ∩ U_{j_p} is rational with ring A_{s_{j₀}⋯s_{j_p}} (anchor Layer 2, Wedhorn Remark 7.30(5)), and M ⊗_A A_{s_{j₀}⋯} = (M_s)_{s_{j₀}⋯} because s is a unit there.
(b) The complex is the extended Čech complex of the A_s-module M_s for the elements s_j of A_s, which generate the unit ideal; it is exact by R0/localization-cech-complex-exact.

(c) Every open covering of a rational subset is refined by a finite rational covering (rational subsets are a quasi-compact basis, anchor Layer 2); (b) with M = A in degrees −1, 0 gives the sheaf condition on rational coverings, which suffices by Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.isSheaf_iff_isSheafFor_rationalCover`; all rings are discrete, so the topological condition is automatic.
acceptance: The discrete ring ℤ[T₁, T₂, …] (not noetherian) with A⁺ = A gives a sheafy Spa(A, A).
For A = k[T] discrete and A⁺ = k, the covering R(1, T / T) ∪ R(T, 1 / 1) of Spa(A, A⁺) gives the exact complex 0 → k[T] → k[T, T⁻¹] × k[T] → k[T, T⁻¹] → 0.

nodes.title: Complete rings of noetherian type are stably sheafy
nodes.statement: Let A be a complete Hausdorff Huber ring of noetherian type. Then A is stably sheafy in the anchor's sense (`Huber.IsStablySheafyRing A`, Wedhorn Definition 8.26): for every complete Hausdorff Huber ring B topologically of finite type over A (Tau Ceti `IsTopologicallyFiniteType`) and every ring of integral elements B⁺ of B, the structure presheaf of Spa(B, B⁺) is a sheaf of complete topological rings. Three cases occur: (T) B Tate — B is strongly noetherian and the anchor's Layer 4.1 theorem applies, with all-degree exactness of augmented Čech complexes on finite rational covers of rational subsets; (N) B has a noetherian ring of definition (for instance ℤ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟦T⟧) — Huber 1994 Theorem 2.2, Case I (R0/noetherian-rod-sheafy), with exact strict Čech complexes on standard rational covers of rational subsets, which refine every open cover; (D) B discrete — R0/discrete-huber-pair-sheafy, with all-degree Čech exactness on finite rational covers (a special case of (N), since the prime subring of a discrete ring is a noetherian ring of definition, with an elementary proof).
hypotheses: A complete Hausdorff Huber ring of noetherian type.
proofSteps: Every complete B topologically of finite type over A is of noetherian type (R0/topologically-finite-type-noetherian-type): it has a noetherian ring of definition or is a strongly noetherian Tate ring (R0/noetherian-type-huber-ring).
Case (T): the anchor's Layer 4.1 proves `Huber.IsSheafyPair B B⁺` and all-degree Čech exactness for complete strongly noetherian Tate B (Wedhorn Theorem 8.28(b), Corollary 8.35).
Case (N): R0/noetherian-rod-sheafy (d) applied to (B, B⁺) (Huber 1994 Theorem 2.2, Case I: the blow-up construction (1.1)–(1.2), strictness (1.3.1), (1.3), refinement (1.5) with Lemma 2.6).
Case (D): R0/discrete-huber-pair-sheafy (c) applied to (B, B⁺).
acceptance: Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩) and all its rational localisations are sheafy (case T).
Spa(ℤ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩) and Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧⟨X⟩, ℤ_p⟦T⟧⟨X⟩) are sheafy (case N).
Spa(𝔽_p[T], 𝔽_p) is sheafy (case D).

nodes.title: The completed tensor product of Huber pairs along adic homomorphisms
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) be Huber pairs (Tau Ceti `Pair`) and f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) morphisms of Huber pairs (Tau Ceti `Pair.Hom`) whose underlying ring homomorphisms are adic (R0/adic-ring-homomorphism). Choose a pair of definition (A₀, I) of A and rings of definition B₀ ⊆ B⁺, C₀ ⊆ C⁺ with f(A₀) ⊆ B₀, g(A₀) ⊆ C₀ such that f(I)B₀ and g(I)C₀ are ideals of definition. Let E := B ⊗_A C (Mathlib `Algebra.TensorProduct`, B and C being A-algebras through f and g), let F ⊆ E be the image of B₀ ⊗_{A₀} C₀ (a subring), and give E the group topology for which {Iⁿ·F : n ≥ 0} is a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of 0, where Iⁿ·F is the additive subgroup generated by the products of images of elements of Iⁿ with elements of F. Then E is a Huber ring with pair of definition (F, I·F), the maps inl : b ↦ b ⊗ 1 and inr : c ↦ 1 ⊗ c are adic, the topology does not depend on the choice of (A₀, I, B₀, C₀), and E⁺ := the integral closure in E of the image of B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺ is a ring of integral elements of E. The *completed tensor product* is the complete Hausdorff Huber pair B ⊗̂_A C := (Ê, Ê⁺), where Ê is the Hausdorff completion of E (Tau Ceti `IsHuberRing.completion`) and Ê⁺ is the closure of the image of E⁺; it carries the morphisms of Huber pairs inl : (B, B⁺) → B ⊗̂_A C, inr : (C, C⁺) → B ⊗̂_A C with inl ∘ f = inr ∘ g. It is a Tate ring whenever B or C is. Pinned conventions: B ⊗̂_A C always means this completed pair; the plus ring is the integral closure of the image of B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺ (not the image itself), then closed up in the completion; no uniformisation is performed; the construction is not defined unless both f and g are adic. Lean name: `Huber.Pair.completedTensor f g hf hg`.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) Huber pairs; B and C need not be complete.
f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) and g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) morphisms of Huber pairs.
The ring homomorphisms underlying f and g are adic.
proofSteps: Common choice of rings of definition: adicness of f gives (A₀¹, I¹, B₀) and of g gives (A₀², I², C₀). Let A₀ ⊆ A₀¹ ∩ A₀² ∩ A⁺ be a ring of definition with ideal of definition I (intersections of rings of definition and of a ring of definition with the open subring A⁺ are rings of definition, anchor Layer 0.2, Wedhorn Corollary 6.4). Since I is open in A, (I¹)ᴺ ⊆ I for large N, so f(I)B₀ ⊇ (f(I¹)B₀)ᴺ is open in B₀; it is finitely generated by topologically nilpotent elements, so a power of it lies in f(I¹)B₀; hence f(I)B₀ is an ideal of definition; likewise for g. Replace B₀, C₀ by B₀ ∩ B⁺, C₀ ∩ C⁺ (still rings of definition containing the images of A₀ ⊆ A⁺).

Ring topology (Morel Proposition II.3.2.1): multiplication is continuous at 0 because F is a subring and Iᵃ F · Iᵇ F ⊆ I^{a+b} F; for a pure tensor b ⊗ c choose k with b·f(I)ᵏB₀ ⊆ B₀ and c·g(I)ᵏC₀ ⊆ C₀ (B₀, C₀ open and multiplication by b, c continuous), then (b ⊗ c)·I^{2k}F ⊆ F, so every x ↦ ax is continuous; Bourbaki's criterion (Topologie générale III §6 no. 3) gives a ring topology.

Pair of definition: F is open, I·F is generated by the finitely many images of generators of I, and Iⁿ·F = (I·F)ⁿ, so (F, I·F) is a pair of definition (Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition`); inl(B₀) ⊆ F and inl(f(I))·F = I·F, so inl (and likewise inr) is adic.

Independence of choices: for two admissible choices take a third inside both (intersections as in step 1); the neighbourhood bases are mutually cofinal because each ideal of definition is open in A and each ring of definition of B (resp. C) contains a power of the other's ideal of definition times it.

Plus ring: E⁺ contains F (B₀ ⊆ B⁺, C₀ ⊆ C⁺), so it is open; images of b ⊗ 1 with b ∈ B⁺ ⊆ B° are power-bounded because f(I)ᵏ·{bⁿ} ⊆ B₀ gives Iᵏ·{(b ⊗ 1)ⁿ}·F ⊆ F; E° is an integrally closed subring (anchor Layer 0.2), so the integral closure of the image of B⁺ ⊗ C⁺ lies in E°; Tau Ceti `Pair.isRingOfIntegralElements_integralClosure` concludes.

Completion: Ê is a Huber ring (Tau Ceti `IsHuberRing.completion`, `PairOfDefinition.completion`), and the closure of the image of E⁺ is a ring of integral elements of Ê with Spa(Ê, Ê⁺) ≅ Spa(E, E⁺) (completion of Huber pairs, anchor Layer 0.3; Wedhorn Lemma 7.47(4), Proposition 7.48).
Tate: the image of a pseudouniformiser of B under inl is a topologically nilpotent unit of Ê (Tau Ceti `IsTateRing.completion`).

nodes.title: Universal property of the completed tensor product
nodes.statement: Let f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) and g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) be morphisms of Huber pairs with adic underlying ring homomorphisms, and let D = B ⊗̂_A C with inl, inr (R0/completed-tensor-product). Let R be a complete Hausdorff nonarchimedean topological commutative ring and R⁺ ⊆ R a closed subring integrally closed in R (for instance a complete Huber pair, or (O_X(X), O_X⁺(X)) for an adic space X). For all continuous ring homomorphisms φ : B → R, ψ : C → R with φ(B⁺) ⊆ R⁺, ψ(C⁺) ⊆ R⁺ and φ ∘ f = ψ ∘ g, there is exactly one continuous ring homomorphism χ : D → R with χ(D⁺) ⊆ R⁺, χ ∘ inl = φ and χ ∘ inr = ψ. In particular the square of f, g, inl, inr is cocartesian in the category of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs. If moreover R is Huber and φ is adic, then χ is adic. No adicness of φ or ψ is needed.
hypotheses: f, g morphisms of Huber pairs whose underlying ring homomorphisms are adic.
R complete Hausdorff, nonarchimedean (open additive subgroups form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0).
R⁺ ⊆ R a closed subring, integrally closed in R.
φ, ψ continuous, φ(B⁺) ⊆ R⁺, ψ(C⁺) ⊆ R⁺, φ ∘ f = ψ ∘ g.
proofSteps: Algebraic factorisation: Mathlib `Algebra.TensorProduct.lift` gives the unique ring homomorphism χ₀ : B ⊗_A C → R with χ₀(b ⊗ c) = φ(b)ψ(c) (R is commutative, so the commutation hypothesis is automatic).

Continuity of χ₀ for the topology {Iⁿ·F}: given an open subgroup U of R choose an open subgroup V with V·V ⊆ U (continuity of multiplication at (0, 0)), then k with φ(f(I)ᵏB₀) ⊆ V and ψ(g(I)ᵏC₀) ⊆ V (continuity of φ, ψ and f(I)B₀, g(I)C₀ ideals of definition — this is where adicness of f and g is used); I^{2k}·F is generated by images of (f(I)ᵏB₀) ⊗ (g(I)ᵏC₀), so χ₀(I^{2k}·F) ⊆ V·V ⊆ U.
Extension: Mathlib `UniformSpace.Completion.extensionHom` extends χ₀ to the completion D, with `UniformSpace.Completion.extensionHom_coe` giving χ ∘ inl = φ, χ ∘ inr = ψ.
Plus rings: χ maps the image of B⁺ ⊗ C⁺ into R⁺, hence its integral closure into the integral closure of R⁺ in R, which is R⁺; by continuity and closedness of R⁺ the closure D⁺ maps into R⁺.
Uniqueness: two such χ agree on the image of B ⊗_A C (Mathlib `Algebra.TensorProduct.ext`), which is dense (`Huber.Pair.completedTensor.denseRange_tmul`), and R is Hausdorff.
Adicness of χ when φ is adic: χ(F) lies in a ring of definition R₀ ⊇ φ(B₀)ψ(C₀) and χ(I·F) = φ(f(I))·χ(F) generates an ideal of definition of R₀ because φ(f(I)B₀)R₀ does.

nodes.title: Base change of weighted restricted power series and of their quotients
nodes.statement: Let λ : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) be a morphism of Huber pairs whose ring homomorphism is adic, and let M = (M₁,…,M_n) be finite subsets of A with every M_i·A open in A. Then (a) every λ(M_i)·B is open in B, so the weighted restricted power-series pair B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)} = B⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩_{λ(M₁),…,λ(M_n)} is defined (Huber's plus ring: the integral closure of {∑ b_ν X^ν : b_ν ∈ λ(M)^ν·(B⁺)^ for all ν}); (b) the morphism A⟨X⟩_M ⊗̂_A B → B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)} induced by the natural extension λ' : A⟨X⟩_M → B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)} of λ (X_i ↦ X_i) and by the structure map B → B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)} is an isomorphism of complete Huber pairs; (c) if σ : A⟨X⟩_M → (C, C⁺) is a quotient mapping of complete Huber pairs (surjective, continuous and open, C⁺ the integral closure of σ(A⟨X⟩_M⁺)) with kernel 𝔞, then C ⊗̂_A B ≅ B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}/𝔟 with 𝔟 the closure of λ'(𝔞)·B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}, quotient topology and plus ring the integral closure of the image of B⟨X⟩⁺_{λ(M)}; if B is complete of noetherian type then 𝔟 = λ'(𝔞)·B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}. Consequently B → C ⊗̂_A B is topologically of finite type as a morphism of Huber pairs (a quotient mapping out of B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}) and as a ring homomorphism (Tau Ceti `IsTopologicallyFiniteType`).
hypotheses: λ : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) a morphism of Huber pairs with adic ring homomorphism.
M₁,…,M_n finite subsets of A with each M_i·A open.
For (c): σ a quotient mapping of complete Huber pairs out of A⟨X⟩_M.
proofSteps: (a) An open ideal of A contains Iᵏ·A for a pair of definition (A₀, I) (Wedhorn Lemma 6.6, anchor Layer 0.2), so λ(M_i)·B ⊇ λ(I)ᵏ·B ⊇ (λ(I)B₀)ᵏ, which is open because λ is adic. The weight-family hypothesis of Tau Ceti's `weightedRestrictedSubring` (λ(M_i)ᵐ·U a neighbourhood of 0 for all m and all neighbourhoods U) follows from openness of λ(M_i)·B by Wedhorn Lemma 6.20 = Huber Lemma 1.1, which the anchor's Layer 0.4 states as the equivalent form of its standing hypothesis (imported).

(b) The pair-level universal property of A⟨X⟩_M (Huber 1994 Lemma 3.5(i): morphisms A⟨X⟩_M → (R, R⁺) to complete pairs correspond to morphisms φ : A → R together with r_i ∈ R such that φ(m)·r_i ∈ R⁺ for m ∈ M_i), imported with the plus ring of A⟨X⟩_M from the anchor's Layer 5.2; its ring-level part is Tau Ceti `existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_completion_weightedRestrictedSubring_of_isWeightedVarPowerBounded` (elements of R⁺ are power-bounded), and λ' is Tau Ceti `weightedMapCompletion` (λ(M_i) ⊆ λ(M_i)).

(b) cont.: by R0/completed-tensor-product-universal-property, morphisms A⟨X⟩_M ⊗̂_A B → (R, R⁺) correspond to pairs (A⟨X⟩_M → R, B → R) agreeing on A, hence to (ψ : B → R, r_i with ψ(λ(m))·r_i ∈ R⁺), which by Lemma 3.5(i) for B are the morphisms B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)} → (R, R⁺). Both objects represent the same functor on complete Hausdorff Huber pairs, and the comparison morphism is the one of the statement; so it is an isomorphism (Yoneda).

(c) C ⊗̂_A B represents pairs (C → R, B → R) agreeing on A; C → R is a morphism A⟨X⟩_M → R killing 𝔞 (universal property of the quotient pair, Tau Ceti `Pair.quotient` and `Pair.Hom.quotientLift`, plus continuity: a continuous map to a Hausdorff R killing 𝔞 kills its closure); so C ⊗̂_A B represents morphisms B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)} → R killing λ'(𝔞), which B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}/𝔟 represents. The noetherian case: 𝔟 is closed by R0/noetherian-type-ideals-closed applied to B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}, which is of noetherian type by R0/topologically-finite-type-noetherian-type.
Topologically finite type: B → B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}/𝔟 is the composite of the presenting map with an open quotient map (Tau Ceti `IsTopologicallyFiniteType.comp_isOpenQuotientMap`).

nodes.title: Completed base change along a topologically-finite-type map preserves noetherian type and sheafiness
nodes.statement: Let λ : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) and μ : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) be morphisms of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with λ adic and μ topologically of finite type as a ring homomorphism (Tau Ceti `IsTopologicallyFiniteType`; then μ is adic by R0/topologically-finite-type-is-adic). If B is of noetherian type, then inl : B → B ⊗̂_A C is topologically of finite type, B ⊗̂_A C is a complete Hausdorff Huber ring of noetherian type, and B ⊗̂_A C (with its plus ring, or with any other ring of integral elements) is sheafy — indeed stably sheafy (R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy). If μ is topologically of finite type as a morphism of pairs, inl is so as a morphism of pairs.

nodes.title: Rational localisation commutes with completed tensor products
nodes.statement: Let f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) be morphisms of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with adic ring homomorphisms, D = B ⊗̂_A C, and p_B = Spa(inl) : Spa D → Spa B, p_C = Spa(inr) (Tau Ceti `Pair.Hom.spaComap`). Let U = R(T/s) ⊆ Spa B, V = R(T'/s') ⊆ Spa C, W = R(T''/s'') ⊆ Spa A be rational subsets with Spa(f)(U) ⊆ W and Spa(g)(V) ⊆ W, and let O(U) = B⟨T/s⟩ etc. denote the rational localisations as complete Huber pairs (anchor Layer 3.1; Tau Ceti `completionLocalization`). Then: (1) p_B⁻¹(U) = R(inl(T)/inl(s)) and p_C⁻¹(V) = R(inr(T')/inr(s')) are rational, and p_B⁻¹(U) ∩ p_C⁻¹(V) is the rational subset R(inl(T ∪ {s})·inr(T' ∪ {s'}) / inl(s)inr(s')); (2) the maps O(W) → O(U), O(W) → O(V) are adic and the canonical morphism O(U) ⊗̂_{O(W)} O(V) → O_D(p_B⁻¹(U) ∩ p_C⁻¹(V)) is an isomorphism of complete Huber pairs; (3) consequently Spa(O(U) ⊗̂_{O(W)} O(V)) → Spa D is a homeomorphism onto p_B⁻¹(U) ∩ p_C⁻¹(V) matching rational subsets.
hypotheses: f, g morphisms of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with adic ring homomorphisms.
U, V, W rational subsets (T·B open, etc.) with Spa(f)(U) ⊆ W, Spa(g)(V) ⊆ W.
proofSteps: (1) Preimages: Tau Ceti `Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset` computes p_B⁻¹(R(T/s)) = R(inl(T)/inl(s)) as sets; since inl is adic, inl(T)·D is open (T·B ⊇ power of an ideal of definition, Wedhorn Lemma 6.6), so this is a rational subset in Huber's sense (Wedhorn Lemma 7.46(3)). Finite intersections of rational subsets are rational with the product presentation (anchor Layer 2.2, Wedhorn Remark 7.30(5)).

(2) Adicness: B → O(U) is topologically of finite type (Wedhorn Example 6.38, Huber 1994 Corollary 3.4(i)) hence adic (R0/topologically-finite-type-is-adic); O(W) → O(U) is adic by cancellation (`Huber.IsAdicHom.of_comp`, R0/adic-ring-homomorphism) since A → O(W) → O(U) equals A → B → O(U).

(2) cont.: morphisms O(U) ⊗̂_{O(W)} O(V) → (R, R⁺) (complete Huber pairs) correspond (R0/completed-tensor-product-universal-property) to pairs (O(U) → R, O(V) → R) agreeing on O(W); by the universal property of rational localisation (Tau Ceti `existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`, Huber 1994 Proposition 1.3) these are pairs (B → R with Spa R → U, C → R with Spa R → V) agreeing on A (agreement on O(W) follows from agreement on A by uniqueness in O(W)'s universal property), i.e. morphisms D → R whose Spa-image lies in p_B⁻¹(U) ∩ p_C⁻¹(V), i.e. morphisms O_D(p_B⁻¹(U) ∩ p_C⁻¹(V)) → R. Yoneda gives the isomorphism.

(3) The adic spectrum of a rational localisation is homeomorphic to the rational subset with rational subsets matched (Tau Ceti `spaLocalizationHomeomorph`, anchor Layer 3.1; Huber 1994 Lemma 1.5(ii)).

nodes.title: Valuations agreeing on a common subring extend jointly to the tensor product
nodes.statement: Let A → B and A → C be ring homomorphisms and let y ∈ Spv B, x ∈ Spv C be valuations whose pullbacks to A agree as points of Spv A (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.comap`). Then there is a valuation v on B ⊗_A C whose pullbacks along inl : B → B ⊗_A C and inr : C → B ⊗_A C are y and x. Field form: for field extensions K₁, K₂ of K₀ and valuation rings V_i ⊆ K_i with V₁ ∩ K₀ = V₂ ∩ K₀, there are a field L, K₀-embeddings K₁ → L, K₂ → L (L a residue field of K₁ ⊗_{K₀} K₂) and a valuation ring W ⊆ L with W ∩ K₁ = V₁ and W ∩ K₂ = V₂.
hypotheses: A → B, A → C commutative ring homomorphisms.
y, x valuations (points of Spv) with equal pullbacks to A.
proofSteps: Reduction to fields: equal pullbacks give equal supports 𝔯 = supp(y) ∩ A = supp(x) ∩ A; put K₁ = κ(supp y), K₂ = κ(supp x), K₀ = κ(𝔯), V₁, V₂ the valuation rings of y, x, V₀ = V₁ ∩ K₀ = V₂ ∩ K₀ (equal pullbacks).

Flatness: V₁ and V₂ are torsion-free over the valuation ring V₀, hence flat (Mathlib `Module.Flat.flat_iff_torsion_eq_bot_of_isBezout`; valuation rings are Bézout domains). Hence R := V₁ ⊗_{V₀} V₂ is flat over V₁ and over V₂, so nonzero elements of V₁ and V₂ are non-zero-divisors on R, and R embeds in K₁ ⊗_{K₀} K₂.

A prime over both maximal ideals: R/(𝔪₁R + 𝔪₂R) ≅ k₁ ⊗_{k₀} k₂ ≠ 0 (a tensor product of nonzero vector spaces over the field k₀), so some prime P of R contains 𝔪₁R + 𝔪₂R (Mathlib `Ideal.exists_le_maximal`).

A minimal prime Q ⊆ P (Mathlib `Ideal.exists_minimalPrimes_le`) consists of zero-divisors (Mathlib `Ideal.disjoint_nonZeroDivisors_of_mem_minimalPrimes`), so Q ∩ V₁ = 0 = Q ∩ V₂ and L := Frac(R/Q) contains K₁ and K₂ over K₀.

The local ring (R/Q)_{P/Q} is a local subring of L, dominated by a valuation subring W of L (Mathlib `LocalSubring.exists_le_valuationSubring`, Stacks 00IA). W ∩ K₁ is a valuation ring dominating V₁ (𝔪₁ ⊆ P), hence equal to V₁ (valuation rings are maximal for domination, Mathlib `ValuationSubring.isMax_toLocalSubring`); likewise W ∩ K₂ = V₂.
Ring form: v is the valuation of W composed with B ⊗_A C → K₁ ⊗_{K₀} K₂ → L.

nodes.title: Spa of a sheafy completed tensor product is the fibre product
nodes.statement: Let f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) and g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) be morphisms of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with adic ring homomorphisms, such that Spa A, Spa B, Spa C are adic spaces (their pairs are sheafy), and let D = B ⊗̂_A C (R0/completed-tensor-product). If D is sheafy (the anchor's `Huber.IsSheafyPair`), then Spa D with the morphisms Spa(inl) : Spa D → Spa B and Spa(inr) : Spa D → Spa C is a fibre product of Spa B → Spa A ← Spa C in the category of adic spaces: for every adic space X and morphisms a : X → Spa B, b : X → Spa C with Spa(f) ∘ a = Spa(g) ∘ b there is a unique morphism X → Spa D composing to a and b. Sheafiness of D is a hypothesis, not a conclusion: it is supplied by R0/completed-tensor-noetherian-stability in the noetherian case and by other stages in other cases (perfectoid: PerfectoidSpaces:P2; sousperfectoid: AdicSpacesPartII:R5).
hypotheses: f, g morphisms of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with adic ring homomorphisms.
(A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) sheafy.
D = B ⊗̂_A C sheafy.
proofSteps: Morphisms into an affinoid: for an adic space X and a complete Hausdorff sheafy pair (R, R⁺), morphisms X → Spa R correspond bijectively and naturally to morphisms of pairs (R, R⁺) → (O_X(X), O_X⁺(X)) (Huber 1994 Proposition 2.1(ii), Wedhorn Proposition 8.25; imported from the anchor's Layer 5).

(O_X(X), O_X⁺(X)) is a complete Hausdorff nonarchimedean topological ring with a closed integrally closed subring (the sheaf condition in complete topological rings, anchor Layer 3.2–3.4; O_X⁺ is defined by v_x ≤ 1).

Compatible pairs (a, b) correspond to morphisms φ : B → O_X(X), ψ : C → O_X(X) of pairs with φ ∘ f = ψ ∘ g; R0/completed-tensor-product-universal-property gives a unique χ : D → O_X(X) with χ ∘ inl = φ, χ ∘ inr = ψ; translate back by the first step (naturality gives the compositions).
