nodes.title: Fibre products along a finite-type morphism over an arbitrary affinoid base change
nodes.statement: Let S = Spa(A, A⁺), X = Spa(C, C⁺), Y = Spa(B, B⁺) be affinoid adic spaces with complete Hausdorff pairs, B stably sheafy, f : X → S given by a morphism μ : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) topologically of finite type (presented by a quotient mapping σ : A⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩_M → (C, C⁺) with kernel 𝔞), and g : Y → S given by an arbitrary morphism of pairs λ : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) (not assumed adic). Let L ⊆ B be a finite set generating an ideal of definition of a ring of definition of B. For m ≥ 1 put M_{L,m} := (λ(M₁) ∪ Lᵐ, …, λ(M_n) ∪ Lᵐ) (each λ(M_i) ∪ Lᵐ generates an open ideal of B), and W_m := Spa(B⟨X⟩_{M_{L,m}}/J_m) with J_m the closure of the ideal generated by λ'(𝔞) and the integral-closure plus ring. Then: (1) each W_m is an affinoid adic space topologically of finite type over Y; (2) for m ≤ m' the restriction B⟨X⟩_{M_{L,m'}}/J_{m'} → B⟨X⟩_{M_{L,m}}/J_m identifies W_m with the rational subset {w ∈ W_{m'} : w(ℓ·X_i) ≤ 1 for all ℓ ∈ Lᵐ and all i} of W_{m'}; (3) the adic space W := ⋃_m W_m obtained by gluing along these open embeddings, with its maps to X and Y, is a fibre product X ×_S Y in the category of adic spaces; (4) if λ is adic then W = W_∞ := Spa(B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}/J) = Spa(C ⊗̂_A B) is affinoid; in general W is not quasi-compact.
hypotheses: S, X, Y affinoid with complete Hausdorff pairs; B stably sheafy (anchor `Huber.IsStablySheafyRing`).
μ topologically of finite type as a morphism of pairs (anchor Layer 5.2), presented by σ.
λ an arbitrary morphism of Huber pairs; L generates an ideal of definition of a ring of definition of B.
proofSteps: Openness: Lᵐ·B contains a power of an ideal of definition, so each λ(M_i) ∪ Lᵐ generates an open ideal and B⟨X⟩_{M_{L,m}} is defined (with Tau Ceti's weight-family hypothesis via anchor Layer 0.4, as in R0/completed-tensor-restricted-power-series (a)).

(1) B → B⟨X⟩_{M_{L,m}}/J_m is a quotient-mapping presentation, so it is topologically of finite type and its ring is sheafy because B is stably sheafy (anchor Layer 3.4 definition of `IsStablySheafyRing`).

(2) The pair-level universal property of weighted restricted series (Huber 1994 Lemma 3.5(i), anchor Layer 5.2) gives the restriction maps; they present the target as the rational localisation of the source at {ℓX_i ≤ 1 : ℓ ∈ Lᵐ} (both represent the same functor; Tau Ceti `existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`), so W_m is a rational, hence open affinoid, subspace of W_{m'} (Huber 1994 proof of Proposition 3.8, the same argument with E(k)).

(3) Gluing the W_m along these open embeddings (anchor Layer 5.3) gives W with compatible maps to X (through C → B⟨X⟩_{M_{L,m}}/J_m) and to Y. Universal property: for an affinoid test object V = Spa(R, R⁺) with morphisms to X and Y over S, the images r_i ∈ R of X_i satisfy μ(m)·r_i ∈ R⁺, and for each ℓ ∈ L the image of ℓ is topologically nilpotent, so ℓᵐ·r_i ∈ R⁺ for m large (R⁺ is open and ℓᵐ r_i → 0); hence the pair of maps factors uniquely through W_m for m large (Lemma 3.5(i) and the quotient universal property, Tau Ceti `Pair.Hom.quotientLift`), compatibly in m. For general V, glue over an affinoid cover (morphisms of adic spaces form a sheaf, anchor Layer 5).

(4) If λ is adic, λ(M_i)·B is already open (R0/completed-tensor-restricted-power-series (a)), the weights Lᵐ are redundant for m large, and W = Spa(B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}/J) ≅ Spa(C ⊗̂_A B) (R0/completed-tensor-restricted-power-series (c)).
Non-quasi-compactness: in the example of the acceptance list W is the open unit disc, which is an increasing union of closed discs with no finite subcover.
acceptance: S = Spa(ℤ_p, ℤ_p), X = Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) = Spa(ℤ_p⟨X⟩_{p}/(pX − 1)), Y = Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧, ℤ_p⟦T⟧) with the (p, T)-adic topology, L = {p, T}: W_m = {|T|ᵐ ≤ |p| ≠ 0} and X ×_S Y = ⋃_m W_m is the open unit disc over ℚ_p, which is not affinoid (Hübner Example 9.4; Scholze–Weinstein, Berkeley lectures, the open unit disc example).
If Y = Spa(ℤ_p⟨T⟩) (λ adic) then X ×_S Y = Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩) is affinoid.

nodes.title: Existence of fibre products of adic spaces
nodes.statement: Let f : X → S and g : Y → S be morphisms of adic spaces (the anchor's category, Layer 5). Assume that Y is covered by open affinoids Spa(B, B⁺) with B complete and stably sheafy (anchor `Huber.IsStablySheafyRing`) — for instance Y locally noetherian (R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space, by R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy) — and that one of the following holds: (a) f is locally of finite type (anchor Layer 5.2, which is Huber's notion); (b) f is locally of weakly finite type (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes) and g is adic (R0/adic-morphism). Then the fibre product X ×_S Y exists in the category of adic spaces (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Limits.HasPullback f g` for that category). Its projections p : X ×_S Y → X and q : X ×_S Y → Y satisfy: q is locally of finite type in case (a), and locally of weakly finite type (locally of finite type if f is) in case (b); p is adic whenever g is adic. X ×_S Y is covered by stably sheafy affinoids, and is locally noetherian if Y is. Local form: over affinoid S = Spa A, X = Spa C, Y = Spa B with g adic, X ×_S Y = Spa(C ⊗̂_A B) (R0/affinoid-fibre-product); with g not adic, X ×_S Y is the ascending union of affinoids of R0/fibre-product-along-finite-type and need not be affinoid. Nothing is asserted outside these hypotheses: fibre products of adic spaces do not exist in general.
hypotheses: f : X → S, g : Y → S morphisms of adic spaces.
Y covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings (e.g. Y locally noetherian).
(a) f locally of finite type, or (b) f locally of weakly finite type and g adic.
proofSteps: Gluing reduction (Wedhorn proof of Theorem 8.56(i)): if S = ⋃ S_i, f⁻¹(S_i) = ⋃ X_ij, g⁻¹(S_i) = ⋃ Y_ik are open covers such that all X_ij ×_{S_i} Y_ik exist, then X ×_S Y exists: open subspaces of a fibre product are fibre products of the corresponding opens, and adic spaces and their morphisms glue (anchor Layer 5.3; morphisms of adic spaces form a sheaf). Rational subsets of stably sheafy affinoids are stably sheafy (they are topologically of finite type over them, Huber 1994 Corollary 3.4(i) and composition of tft maps, Wedhorn Proposition 6.33(1)), so the affinoid Y_ik can be chosen stably sheafy and inside a given affinoid.

Case (b), affinoid: choose affinoid X_ij = Spa C, S_i = Spa A with A → C topologically of finite type (definition of lwft), hence adic (R0/topologically-finite-type-is-adic); A → B is adic because g is adic (R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus (i)). B → C ⊗̂_A B is topologically of finite type (R0/completed-tensor-restricted-power-series), so C ⊗̂_A B is sheafy (stable sheafiness of B), and R0/affinoid-fibre-product gives X_ij ×_{S_i} Y_ik = Spa(C ⊗̂_A B).
Case (a), affinoid: R0/fibre-product-along-finite-type (no adicness of g needed).

Projections: locally q is B → B⟨X⟩_{M'}/𝔟, topologically of finite type (as pairs in case (a), and as pairs in case (b) when f is lft, as rings otherwise); p is locally C → C ⊗̂_A B = inl, which is adic (R0/completed-tensor-product) when g is adic.

Stability: the affinoid pieces are topologically of finite type over stably sheafy B, hence stably sheafy (composition of tft maps); if B is of noetherian type they are of noetherian type (R0/topologically-finite-type-noetherian-type).
acceptance: For S analytic every morphism is adic (R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus), so fibre products over an analytic base exist as soon as f is locally of weakly finite type and Y is locally noetherian (Huber 1996 remark recorded in the decomposition).
Huber 1994 Proposition 3.7 is the special case (a) with g adic.
Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧) ×_{Spa ℤ_p} Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) exists and is the (non-affinoid) open unit disc over ℚ_p.
Non-example outside the hypotheses: Spa(ℤ[T₁, T₂, …], ℤ) × Spa K is not representable (Scholze–Weinstein, Berkeley Lecture 3); there f is not locally of finite type.

nodes.title: Points of a fibre product surject onto compatible pairs, not injectively
nodes.statement: In the situation of R0/fibre-products-existence, let Z = X ×_S Y with projections p : Z → X, q : Z → Y. For all x ∈ X and y ∈ Y with f(x) = g(y) there is z ∈ Z with p(z) = x and q(z) = y; that is, the map |Z| → |X| ×_{|S|} |Y| of underlying sets is surjective. It is not injective in general: for L = ℚ_p(√p), X = Y = Spa(L, O_L) and S = Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p), |X|, |Y|, |S| are single points and |Z| = |Spa(L × L, O_L × O_L)| has two points; and over the pair of Gauss points of two closed unit discs over ℚ_p there are infinitely many points of the bidisc (the Gauss point and, for every 0 < r < 1, the point f ↦ sup{|f(T, S)| : |T| ≤ 1, |T − S| ≤ r}).
hypotheses: The hypotheses of R0/fibre-products-existence (either case).
proofSteps: Reduce to affinoid S = Spa A, X = Spa C, Y = Spa B (points lie in affinoid opens; open subspaces of fibre products are fibre products).

Case g adic (Z = Spa D, D = C ⊗̂_A B): regard x, y as continuous valuations of C, B with equal pullbacks to A. R0/valuation-amalgamation gives a valuation v of E = C ⊗_A B over x and y. Let H be the larger of the convex hulls of Γ_x and Γ_y in Γ_v; H contains the characteristic subgroup cΓ_v (every v(e) is bounded by products of values of x and y), so w := v|H is a valuation (restriction to a convex subgroup containing cΓ_v, Huber 1993 §2, anchor Layer 1.4) still over x and y.

w ∈ Spa(E, E⁺): w ≤ 1 on the image of C⁺ ⊗ B⁺ and hence on its integral closure E⁺; w is continuous because for the ideal of definition I·F the values w(I) are cofinal (x(I), y(I) are cofinal in Γ_x, Γ_y and w(i) < 1 on I) (Wedhorn Theorem 7.10 = anchor Layer 1.5 criterion for Cont); Spa(E, E⁺) = Spa(D, D⁺) (anchor Layer 0.3 / Wedhorn 7.48).

Case (a) with g not adic: apply the same construction to C ⊗_A B → O(W_m) (R0/fibre-product-along-finite-type); the value w(X_i) is fixed and w(ℓ)ᵐ → 0 for ℓ ∈ L (y continuous), so w(ℓᵐ X_i) ≤ 1 for m large and w extends by continuity to a point of W_m.

Non-injectivity: L ⊗_{ℚ_p} L ≅ L × L (as √p ∈ L), the completed tensor product needs no completion, and Spa(L × L, O_L × O_L) is the disjoint union of two copies of Spa(L, O_L) (R0/affinoid-fibre-product); the bidisc points are sup-norms over the polydiscs {|T| ≤ 1, |T − S| ≤ r}, which differ for different r and project to the Gauss points.

nodes.title: Stability of adicness and of the finite-type classes under base change
nodes.statement: Let the cartesian square Z = X ×_S Y (p : Z → X, q : Z → Y) be as in R0/fibre-products-existence, q being the base change of f along g and p the base change of g along f. Then: (i) if f is locally of finite type (anchor), so is q; (ii) if f is locally of weakly finite type and g is adic, q is locally of weakly finite type and p is adic; (iii) if f is locally of +weakly finite type (R0/plus-weakly-finite-type) and g is adic, q is locally of +weakly finite type; (iv) if f is locally of finite presentation (R0/locally-finite-presentation), so is q; (v) if g is adic, p is adic (R0/adic-morphism); (vi) if g is adic and f is quasi-compact, q is quasi-compact; if g is adic and f is quasi-separated, q is quasi-separated. Quasi-compactness is not preserved by base change along a non-adic g: the base change of the quasi-compact morphism Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) → Spa(ℤ_p, ℤ_p) along Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧) → Spa(ℤ_p) is the open unit disc over ℚ_p → Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧), which is not quasi-compact. The base-change properties of separated, proper, finite, étale and smooth morphisms are stated with those notions (R0b/R0c nodes) and are not part of this lemma.
hypotheses: The hypotheses of R0/fibre-products-existence for f and g.
proofSteps: All assertions are affinoid-local on Z (the classes are defined affinoid-locally and open subspaces of fibre products are fibre products); compute with the local forms.

(i), (ii): locally q is B → B⟨X⟩_{M'}/𝔟 (R0/completed-tensor-restricted-power-series, R0/fibre-product-along-finite-type), topologically of finite type as pairs, resp. as rings; p is locally inl : C → C ⊗̂_A B, adic when g is (R0/completed-tensor-product), i.e. (v).

(iii): if C⁺ is the integral closure of A⁺[E ∪ C°°] (E finite), then the plus ring of C ⊗̂_A B is the closure of the integral closure of the image of C⁺ ⊗ B⁺, which lies in the integral closure of B⁺[inl(E) ∪ D°°] because inl(C°°) consists of topologically nilpotent elements; so q is +wft with the finite set inl(E) (R0/plus-weakly-finite-type).

(iv): in the discrete case B ⊗_A C is a finitely presented B-algebra when C is a finitely presented A-algebra (base change of finite presentation, Mathlib `Algebra.FinitePresentation.baseChange`), and otherwise (iv) is (i).

(vi): with g adic the fibre product over affinoids is affinoid (R0/affinoid-fibre-product), so preimages of quasi-compact opens covered by finitely many affinoids are covered by finitely many affinoids (Wedhorn Remark 8.57(2)); quasi-separatedness likewise from intersections of affinoids. The counterexample for non-adic g is R0/fibre-product-along-finite-type's open disc.
acceptance: The base change of the closed unit disc Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩) → Spa ℚ_p along Spa ℂ_p → Spa ℚ_p is the closed unit disc over ℂ_p, locally of finite type over Spa ℂ_p.
Non-example: quasi-compactness fails for the open-disc base change above.

nodes.title: Adic morphisms of adic spaces
nodes.statement: A morphism f : X → Y of adic spaces (the anchor's category, Layer 5) is *adic* if every x ∈ X has an open affinoid neighbourhood U and there is an open affinoid V ⊆ Y with f(U) ⊆ V such that the ring homomorphism O_Y(V) → O_X(U) induced by f is adic (R0/adic-ring-homomorphism). Equivalently (R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus) f maps analytic points to analytic points, and then the ring maps O_Y(V) → O_X(U) are adic for all open affinoids with f(U) ⊆ V. Here a point is analytic if it has an open neighbourhood U whose ring O_X(U) contains a topologically nilpotent unit; on Spa(A, A⁺) this means that its support is not open (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.IsAnalyticPoint`). Every morphism into an analytic adic space is adic. Lean name: `AdicSpace.IsAdic f` (a `MorphismProperty` of the anchor's category).
hypotheses: f : X → Y a morphism of adic spaces.
proofSteps: Definition by an affinoid-local condition; independence of the chosen affinoids and the analytic-locus characterisation are R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus.
acceptance: Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩) → Spa(ℚ_p) is adic; Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧) → Spa(ℤ_p) is not.

nodes.title: A morphism is adic exactly when it preserves analytic points
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of adic spaces. (i) If f is adic, then for all open affinoid U ⊆ X and V ⊆ Y with f(U) ⊆ V the ring homomorphism O_Y(V) → O_X(U) is adic. (ii) f is adic iff f(X_a) ⊆ Y_a. (iii) f(X_na) ⊆ Y_na. In particular every morphism to an analytic adic space is adic.
hypotheses: f : X → Y a morphism of adic spaces.
proofSteps: Analytic points are local: for an open subspace U, U_a = X_a ∩ U (Wedhorn Remark 8.37(2)), and on Spa(A, A⁺) a point is analytic iff its support is not open (Huber 1994 Remark 3.1; Tau Ceti `IsAnalyticPoint`; anchor Layer 2.3).

Affinoid statement (Wedhorn Lemma 7.46(1),(2)): for a continuous φ : A → B of affinoid rings with B complete and g = Spa(φ): g(X_na) ⊆ Y_na (supports pull back to supports; open ideals pull back to open ideals); if φ is adic then g(X_a) ⊆ Y_a (a topologically nilpotent element with nonzero value maps to one); if g(X_a) ⊆ Y_a then φ is adic — otherwise, for pairs of definition with φ(A₀) ⊆ B₀, φ(I) ⊆ J, the radicals of φ(I)B₀ and J differ (`Huber.IsAdicHom.of_radical_eq` in R0/adic-ring-homomorphism), giving a non-open prime 𝔭 ⊇ φ(I)B₀, and Wedhorn Lemma 7.45 (a complete affinoid ring has an analytic point whose support meets B₀ in a prime containing 𝔭; anchor Layer 2.3 analytic-point theory) produces x ∈ X_a with g(x) ∉ Y_a.

(ii) ⇒: cover X by affinoids U with adic O_Y(V) → O_X(U) and apply the affinoid statement; ⇐ and (i): for any affinoids U, V with f(U) ⊆ V, f(U_a) ⊆ V_a, so O_Y(V) → O_X(U) is adic by the affinoid statement.
(iii) from the affinoid statement; the analytic-target case is (ii) with Y_a = Y.
acceptance: For Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧) → Spa(ℤ_p) the analytic point with support (p) maps to a non-analytic point, so the morphism is not adic.
Every morphism of analytic adic spaces is adic.

nodes.title: Morphisms locally of weakly finite type and the finite-type hierarchy
nodes.statement: A morphism f : X → Y of adic spaces is *locally of weakly finite type* if every x ∈ X has an open affinoid neighbourhood U and there is an open affinoid V ⊆ Y with f(U) ⊆ V such that the ring homomorphism O_Y(V) → O_X(U) is topologically of finite type (Tau Ceti `IsTopologicallyFiniteType`, which is Huber 1994's and Wedhorn 6.29(i)'s notion; no condition on the plus rings); f is *of weakly finite type* if moreover f is quasi-compact. Hierarchy (Huber 1996 after 1.2.1): locally of finite presentation (R0/locally-finite-presentation) ⇒ locally of finite type ⇒ locally of +weakly finite type (R0/plus-weakly-finite-type) ⇒ locally of weakly finite type ⇒ adic (R0/adic-morphism). Here 'locally of finite type' is the anchor's Layer 5.2 notion — the ring map (O_Y(V), O_Y⁺(V)) → (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) is topologically of finite type as a map of pairs, i.e. presented by a quotient mapping out of a weighted restricted power-series pair A⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩_M — which is exactly Huber 1994's Definition following Lemma 3.5; this node does not redefine it. Comparison with Tau Ceti: the ring-level condition is Tau Ceti's `IsTopologicallyFiniteType`, whose weight families satisfy `IsWeightFamily`, equivalent for Huber rings to Huber's 'M_i·A open' by Huber 1994 Lemma 1.1 = Wedhorn Lemma 6.20 (the anchor's Layer 0.4 equivalence), and whose completeness hypothesis on the target is automatic here since O_X(U) is complete. Lean names: `AdicSpace.LocallyOfWeaklyFiniteType f`, `AdicSpace.IsWeaklyFiniteType f`.
hypotheses: f : X → Y a morphism of adic spaces.
proofSteps: Definition affinoid-locally; the hierarchy: lft ⇒ l+wft is R0/plus-weakly-finite-type's relation, l+wft ⇒ lwft by definition, lwft ⇒ adic by R0/topologically-finite-type-is-adic, lfp ⇒ lft by definition.

Composition and cancellation from Wedhorn Proposition 6.33 (tft maps compose; if ψ ∘ φ is tft then ψ is), restriction to open subspaces from Wedhorn Proposition 8.50 (rational localisations are tft, Huber 1994 Corollary 3.4(i)).
acceptance: Every open immersion is locally of finite type; the closed unit disc over ℚ_p is of finite type over Spa ℚ_p.
An affinoid morphism of weakly finite type need not have a topologically-finite-type global ring map (Wedhorn Remark 8.52).

nodes.title: Morphisms locally of +weakly finite type
nodes.statement: A morphism f : X → Y of adic spaces is *locally of +weakly finite type* if every x ∈ X has an open affinoid neighbourhood U and there is an open affinoid V ⊆ Y with f(U) ⊆ V such that O_Y(V) → O_X(U) is topologically of finite type (Tau Ceti `IsTopologicallyFiniteType`) and there is a finite set E ⊆ O_X⁺(U) with O_X⁺(U) equal to the integral closure in O_X(U) of the subring generated by the image of O_Y⁺(V), E and the topologically nilpotent elements O_X(U)°°. It is *of +weakly finite type* if moreover quasi-compact. This is the finiteness condition in Huber's definition of proper morphisms (proper = +weakly finite type, separated, universally closed). nodes.title: Morphisms locally of finite presentation
nodes.statement: A morphism f : X → Y of adic spaces is *locally of finite presentation* if every x ∈ X has an open affinoid neighbourhood U and there is an open affinoid V ⊆ Y with f(U) ⊆ V such that (O_Y(V), O_Y⁺(V)) → (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) is topologically of finite type as a morphism of pairs (anchor Layer 5.2) and, whenever O_Y(V) carries the discrete topology, O_X(U) is a finitely presented O_Y(V)-algebra (Mathlib `RingHom.FinitePresentation`). (The discrete case is the only one in which the condition adds anything; this follows the description of Huber 1996 Definition 1.2.1 recorded in the reviewed decomposition.) Consequences: over an analytic Y, locally of finite presentation = locally of finite type; over Y whose discrete affinoid rings are noetherian rings (for instance t(𝔜) for a locally noetherian formal scheme 𝔜) the two notions agree as well; they differ over discrete non-noetherian affinoids. Lean name: `AdicSpace.LocallyOfFinitePresentation f`.
hypotheses: f : X → Y a morphism of adic spaces.
proofSteps: Definition affinoid-locally; agreement with lft: an analytic affinoid has no discrete ring of functions unless empty (a point of Spa of a discrete ring has open support), and over a discrete noetherian ring finite type equals finite presentation (Mathlib `Algebra.FinitePresentation.of_finiteType`).

nodes.title: Locally noetherian adic spaces (Huber's noetherian hypothesis)
nodes.statement: An adic space X (the anchor's category, Layer 5) is *locally noetherian* if every x ∈ X has an open affinoid neighbourhood U whose complete Hausdorff ring O_X(U) is of noetherian type (R0/noetherian-type-huber-ring): it has a noetherian ring of definition, or it is a strongly noetherian Tate ring. This is the hypothesis of Huber 1994 Propositions 3.6–3.8 ('every point has an open affinoid neighbourhood U such that O(U) has a noetherian ring of definition or is a strongly noetherian Tate ring'). The condition places no restriction on plus rings. Conventions: a locally noetherian analytic adic space is one locally of the form Spa(A, A⁺) with A a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring (the setting of Zavyalov's foundational results); because every discrete ring is of noetherian type, every discretely ringed adic space is locally noetherian in this sense, and results that need honest noetherian rings (for instance on coherent sheaves) must add that hypothesis. Lean name: `AdicSpace.IsLocallyNoetherian X` (a class).
hypotheses: X an adic space.
proofSteps: Definition by the local condition on affinoid neighbourhoods; stability properties from R0/topologically-finite-type-noetherian-type (rational localisations and quotients are topologically of finite type).
acceptance: Closed discs and polydiscs over ℚ_p, Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧), and all rigid-analytic varieties over a complete nonarchimedean field (viewed as adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(k, k°)) are locally noetherian.

nodes.title: Closed adic subspaces cut out by ideal sheaves; closed, open and locally closed embeddings
nodes.statement: Let X be an adic space (the anchor's category). (1) Affinoid model: for a complete Hausdorff sheafy Huber pair (A, A⁺) and a closed ideal J ⊆ A with A/J sheafy, the quotient pair A/J := (A/J, integral closure of the image of A⁺) (Tau Ceti `Pair.quotient`; Huber's (A^▷/J, (A⁺/(J ∩ A⁺))^c)) gives Spa(A/J) → Spa(A), a homeomorphism onto the closed set {v : J ⊆ supp v} (Tau Ceti `Pair.Hom.isClosedEmbedding_spaComap_quotientHom`, `range_spaComap_quotientHom`). (2) An ideal sheaf 𝓘 ⊆ O_X (a sheaf of ideals of the underlying sheaf of rings) is *admissible* if X has a cover by open affinoids U = Spa(A, A⁺) such that J_U := 𝓘(U) is a closed ideal of A, A/J_U is sheafy, and for every rational W ⊆ U the ideal 𝓘(W) is the kernel of O_X(W) → O_{Spa(A/J_U)}(W ∩ V(J_U)). The *closed adic subspace* V(𝓘) is (Z, O_Z, (v_z)) with Z = {x ∈ X : 𝓘_x ≠ O_{X,x}}, O_Z = (O_X/𝓘)|_Z topologised on each such U as the structure sheaf of Spa(A/J_U) (so O_X(U) → O_Z(U ∩ Z) is continuous and open), and v_z induced through O_{X,z} → O_{X,z}/𝓘_z; it is an adic space with V(𝓘) ∩ U ≅ Spa(A/J_U) over U, and the inclusion ι : V(𝓘) → X is a morphism of adic spaces. V(𝓘) is retained as an adic space (a ringed space with valuations), never replaced by the closed subset Z. (3) A morphism h : T → X is a *closed embedding* if it is isomorphic over X to ι : V(𝓘) → X for an admissible 𝓘; an *open embedding* if it is an isomorphism onto an open subspace; a *locally closed embedding* if it factors as a closed embedding into an open subspace U ⊆ X followed by the inclusion of U. Comparison with the anchor (Layer 5.1): closed embeddings are exactly the anchor's closed immersions (affinoid-locally Spa(A/J) → Spa(A) with J closed and A/J sheafy), with 𝓘 = ker(O_X → h_*O_T); this node adds the ideal-sheaf description, the universal property and locally closed embeddings, and does not redefine closed immersions. On a locally noetherian X every ideal of an affinoid ring of noetherian type is closed and A/J is of noetherian type, hence sheafy (R0/noetherian-type-ideals-closed, R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy); the identification of admissible ideals with coherent ideals is AdicSpacesPartII:R3/coherent-ideal-closed-subspace. Lean names: `AdicSpace.closedSubspace 𝓘`, `AdicSpace.IsLocallyClosedImmersion`.
hypotheses: X an adic space; 𝓘 an admissible ideal sheaf.
proofSteps: Affinoid model from Tau Ceti `Pair.quotient` and Proposition 7.38 in Tau Ceti (`Pair.Hom.isClosedEmbedding_spaComap_quotientHom`).

Gluing: on overlaps of two admissible affinoids U, U' the subspaces Spa(A/J_U) and Spa(A'/J_{U'}) agree on common rational subsets W, because both are the closed subspace of Spa O(W) defined by the closed ideal 𝓘(W) (admissibility and the quotient universal property, Tau Ceti `Pair.Hom.quotientLift`); glue (anchor Layer 5.3).
Valuations and local rings: O_{Z,z} = O_{X,z}/𝓘_z is local and v_z factors through it because 𝓘_z ⊆ supp(v_z) for z ∈ Z (points of Spa(A/J) have support containing J).

Comparison with the anchor's closed immersions: V(𝓘) → X is affinoid-locally Spa(A/J) → Spa A; conversely for an anchor closed immersion h the kernel ideal sheaf is admissible (on the given affinoid cover it is J·(completed localisations) by the anchor's independence of the cover) and h ≅ V(ker h♯) over X by the universal property below.
Universal property: a morphism g : T → X factors through ι iff g♯(𝓘)·O_T = 0, and then uniquely (affinoid-locally the quotient universal property; morphisms of adic spaces form a sheaf).
acceptance: V(T·O) ⊆ Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩) is the origin Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p); V(T²·O) has the same underlying point and ring ℚ_p[T]/(T²).

For an affinoid algebra A over k and any ideal J, A/J = (A/J, (A/J)°) (Huber 1996 (1.4.1) with BGR 6.3.4/1; the plus-ring identity is AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor via Huber 1994 Lemma 4.4).

nodes.title: The diagonal of a morphism locally of weakly finite type is a locally closed embedding
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of adic spaces that is locally of weakly finite type, with X covered by open affinoids whose rings are complete and stably sheafy (for instance X locally noetherian). Then X ×_Y X exists (R0/fibre-products-existence, case (b), f being adic) and the diagonal Δ_f : X → X ×_Y X is a locally closed embedding (R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings): with W the union of the open subspaces U ×_V U ⊆ X ×_Y X over all open affinoids U ⊆ X, V ⊆ Y with f(U) ⊆ V and O_Y(V) → O_X(U) topologically of finite type, W is open, contains Δ_f(X), and Δ_f : X → W is a closed embedding; over U ×_V U = Spa(O_X(U) ⊗̂_{O_Y(V)} O_X(U)) it is Spa of the multiplication map m : O_X(U) ⊗̂_{O_Y(V)} O_X(U) → O_X(U), a quotient mapping with closed kernel. Separatedness (R0b: AdicSpacesPartII:R0/separated-morphism) is the condition that Δ_f be a closed embedding into all of X ×_Y X.
hypotheses: f locally of weakly finite type (hence adic).
X covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings.
proofSteps: Existence and affinoid charts: f is adic (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes), so X ×_Y X exists and, for U, V as in the statement with C = O_X(U), A = O_Y(V), U ×_V U = p₁⁻¹(U) ∩ p₂⁻¹(U) = Spa(C ⊗̂_A C) (R0/fibre-products-existence, R0/affinoid-fibre-product; C ⊗̂_A C is topologically of finite type over the stably sheafy C, hence sheafy, R0/completed-tensor-restricted-power-series); these are open in X ×_Y X, so W is open.
Δ_f⁻¹(U ×_V U) = U because p₁ ∘ Δ_f = p₂ ∘ Δ_f = id_X; and Δ_f(x) ∈ U ×_V U for x ∈ U, so Δ_f(X) ⊆ W.

On U ×_V U, Δ_f corresponds to m : C ⊗̂_A C → C with m ∘ inl = m ∘ inr = id (R0/completed-tensor-product-universal-property). m is surjective and continuous; it is open because inl is a continuous section: for an open subgroup G, m(G) ⊇ inl⁻¹(G), which is open. ker m is closed (C Hausdorff). m(D⁺) ⊆ C⁺ and C⁺ = m(inl(C⁺)) ⊆ m(D⁺), so C⁺ is the integral closure of m(D⁺): m is a quotient mapping and (C, C⁺) ≅ (C ⊗̂_A C)/ker m as quotient pairs (Tau Ceti `Pair.quotient`, `Pair.Hom.quotientLift`); Spa(C) → Spa(C ⊗̂_A C) is a closed embedding (Tau Ceti `Pair.Hom.isClosedEmbedding_spaComap_quotientHom`).

Hence Δ_f : X → W is affinoid-locally over W the closed immersion Spa((C ⊗̂_A C)/ker m) → Spa(C ⊗̂_A C) with closed kernel and sheafy quotient C; closed immersions are local on the target (anchor Layer 5.1, independence of the affinoid cover), so Δ_f is a closed embedding into W and a locally closed embedding into X ×_Y X (R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings).

For the line obtained by gluing two closed discs along the identity of an open subdisc (a non-separated space), Δ is a closed embedding into the open W ⊊ X ×_{ℚ_p} X but not a closed embedding into X ×_{ℚ_p} X.

nodes.title: The norm of a Tate ring attached to a ring of definition, a pseudouniformiser and a radius
nodes.statement: Let A be a Tate ring (Tau Ceti `IsTateRing A`). A *norm datum* d = (A₀, ϖ, r) on A consists of a ring of definition A₀ (the `ringOfDefinition` of a Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition A`), a pseudouniformiser ϖ of A lying in A₀ (Tau Ceti `IsPseudoUniformizer ϖ`: a topologically nilpotent unit; A₀ contains one by Wedhorn Proposition 6.14) and a real number r with 0 < r < 1. The *norm of A attached to d* is α_d : A → ℝ≥0, α_d(x) := inf{ rⁿ : n ∈ ℤ, ϖ⁻ⁿx ∈ A₀ } (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.4.4). The exponent set is nonempty and downward closed, so α_d(x) = r^{N(x)} with N(x) = sup{ n ∈ ℤ : x ∈ ϖⁿA₀ } ∈ ℤ ∪ {+∞} (r^{+∞} := 0). Then α_d is a nonarchimedean ring seminorm (Mathlib `RingSeminorm A` with `IsNonarchimedean`), α_d(1) ≤ 1 and α_d(ϖx) = r·α_d(x); its closed balls are {α_d ≤ rⁿ} = ϖⁿA₀ (n ∈ ℤ), so it defines the topology of A; it vanishes exactly on the closure of {0} = ⋂ₙ ϖⁿA₀, so it is a norm iff A is Hausdorff, and (A, α_d) is a Banach ring in Kedlaya–Liu's sense iff A is moreover complete. Pinned conventions: ϖ must lie in A₀; the function depends on d, and only its equivalence class (for fixed ϖ and r) and the topology it defines are canonical. Lean names: `Huber.TateNormDatum A` for d and `Huber.tateNorm d` for α_d.
hypotheses: A is a Tate ring (Tau Ceti `IsTateRing`).
A₀ is the ring of definition of a Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition A`, and ϖ ∈ A₀ is a pseudouniformiser of A.
r is a real number with 0 < r < 1.
proofSteps: Nonempty exponent set: A₀ is an open neighbourhood of 0 and ϖ is topologically nilpotent, so ϖᵏx → 0 and ϖᵏx ∈ A₀ for k ≫ 0; downward closed: ϖ⁻ⁿx ∈ A₀ implies ϖ⁻⁽ⁿ⁻¹⁾x = ϖ·(ϖ⁻ⁿx) ∈ A₀ because ϖ ∈ A₀.

Seminorm axioms: A₀ is a subring, so ϖ⁻ⁿx, ϖ⁻ᵐy ∈ A₀ give ϖ⁻ⁿ⁻ᵐxy ∈ A₀ and, for m = n, ϖ⁻ⁿ(x ± y) ∈ A₀; hence α_d(xy) ≤ α_d(x)α_d(y), α_d(x + y) ≤ max(α_d(x), α_d(y)), α_d(−x) = α_d(x); 1 ∈ A₀ gives α_d(1) ≤ 1 and every n is allowed for x = 0. These are the fields of Mathlib `RingSeminorm` and the inequality `IsNonarchimedean`.
Balls and topology: α_d(x) ≤ rⁿ iff ϖ⁻ⁿx ∈ A₀ iff x ∈ ϖⁿA₀, and the sets ϖⁿA₀ (n ≥ 0) form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0 in A (Tau Ceti `IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero`).
Kernel: α_d(x) = 0 iff x ∈ ⋂ₙ ϖⁿA₀, the closure of {0} because the ϖⁿA₀ are a basis of open subgroups.

Change of datum: rings of definition A₀, A₀' both containing ϖ satisfy ϖᵏA₀ ⊆ A₀' and ϖᵏA₀' ⊆ A₀ for some k ≥ 0 (each is bounded, the other open), so α' ≤ r⁻ᵏα and α ≤ r⁻ᵏα'; replacing r by r' replaces α_d by α_d^{log r'/log r} because α_d takes values in r^ℤ ∪ {0}.
acceptance: For A = ℚ_p, A₀ = ℤ_p, ϖ = p and r = 1/p the norm is the p-adic absolute value.

For a Banach algebra (A, ‖·‖) over a complete nonarchimedean field K with ‖cy‖ = |c|·‖y‖ (c ∈ K), A₀ the unit ball, ϖ ∈ K with 0 < |ϖ| < 1 and r = |ϖ|: ‖x‖ ≤ α_d(x) < r⁻¹‖x‖ for all x, so α_d is equivalent to ‖·‖.

uses.how: a Tate f-adic ring is given the structure of a Banach ring by this norm, so the Banach-ring statements of Kedlaya–Liu §§2.3–2.8 apply to complete Tate Huber rings

nodes.title: The spectral seminorm of a Tate ring
nodes.statement: Let A be a Tate ring with a norm datum d = (A₀, ϖ, r) and norm α_d (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-ring-norm). The *spectral seminorm* of (A, d) is |x|_sp := lim_{n→∞} α_d(xⁿ)^{1/n} = inf_{n≥1} α_d(xⁿ)^{1/n} (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.1.9; the limit exists by Fekete's lemma), which is Mathlib's `smoothingSeminorm α_d` (defined because α_d(1) ≤ 1 and α_d is nonarchimedean). It is a power-multiplicative nonarchimedean ring seminorm (Mathlib `IsPowMul`: |xⁿ|_sp = |x|_spⁿ for n ≥ 1) with |x|_sp ≤ α_d(x). It does not change when A₀ is replaced by another ring of definition containing ϖ (equivalent norms have the same spectral seminorm), and replacing r by r' raises it to the power log r'/log r. Intrinsic properties: |x|_sp < 1 iff x is topologically nilpotent; |x|_sp ≤ 1 for every power-bounded x; the kernel {x : |x|_sp = 0} is the ideal ⋂ₙ ϖⁿ·A°° (A°° the topologically nilpotent elements), it contains the nilradical and the closure of {0}; |1|_sp = 1 if A is Hausdorff and nonzero. Functoriality: if φ : A → B is a continuous ring homomorphism of Tate rings and B carries a datum (B₀, φ(ϖ), r) with φ(A₀) ⊆ B₀ (such B₀ exists because φ is adic), then |φ(x)|_sp ≤ |x|_sp. Pinned convention: the Gel'fand-spectrum formula |x|_sp = max_{β ∈ M(A)} β(x) (Berkovich) is not part of this node; it is the input of AdicSpacesPartII:R3/uniform-spectral-seminorm. Lean name: `Huber.spectralSeminorm d`.
hypotheses: A is a Tate ring with a norm datum d = (A₀, ϖ, r) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-ring-norm).
proofSteps: Definition: `smoothingSeminorm α_d` with the hypotheses α_d(1) ≤ 1 and `IsNonarchimedean α_d` (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-ring-norm, API tateNorm_one_le, isNonarchimedean_tateNorm); the limit formula is Mathlib `tendsto_smoothingFun_of_map_one_le_one`, power-multiplicativity is `isPowMul_smoothingFun`, and |x|_sp ≤ α_d(x) is `smoothingFun_le_self`.
Independence of A₀: if α' ≤ Cα then α'(xⁿ)^{1/n} ≤ C^{1/n}α(xⁿ)^{1/n}, and C^{1/n} → 1 (tate-ring-norm, API tateNorm_equiv_of_ringOfDefinition); the r-dependence follows from tateNorm_rpow.

|x|_sp < 1 iff x ∈ A°°: if |x|_sp < 1 then α_d(x^N) < 1 for some N, so α_d(x^{Nk+j}) ≤ α_d(x^N)^k α_d(x^j) → 0 and xⁿ → 0 (α_d defines the topology); conversely xⁿ → 0 gives α_d(x^N) ≤ r for some N and |x|_sp ≤ α_d(x^N)^{1/N} < 1 (Mathlib `smoothingFun_le`). Power-bounded x have bounded α_d(xⁿ), so |x|_sp ≤ 1.

Kernel: |x|_sp = 0 implies |ϖ⁻ⁿx|_sp ≤ |ϖ⁻¹|_spⁿ·|x|_sp = 0 < 1, so ϖ⁻ⁿx ∈ A°° for all n; conversely x ∈ ϖⁿA°° gives |x|_sp ≤ |ϖ|_spⁿ < rⁿ. Nilpotents and the closure of {0} (where α_d = 0) lie in the kernel. If A is Hausdorff and nonzero, α_d(1) > 0 and α_d(1ⁿ) = α_d(1), so |1|_sp = 1.

Functoriality: φ is adic because A is Tate (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-ring-homomorphism, API IsAdicHom.of_isTateRing), giving a ring of definition B₀ ⊇ φ(A₀); φ(ϖ) is a pseudouniformiser of B; α_{d'}(φ x) ≤ α_d(x) (tate-ring-norm, API tateNorm_map_le), and smoothing is monotone.
acceptance: For A = K⟨T⟩, A₀ = K°⟨T⟩, ϖ ∈ K° with 0 < |ϖ| < 1 and r = |ϖ|, |f|_sp is the Gauss norm sup |aₙ|.
For A = K[ε]/(ε²) (finite free over K, A₀ = K° ⊕ K°ε) |ε|_sp = 0 while α_d(ε) = 1.

nodes.title: The spectral topology of a Tate ring
nodes.statement: Let A be a Tate ring. The *spectral topology* on A is the topology defined by a spectral seminorm |·|_sp (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-seminorm): the ring topology whose neighbourhoods of 0 are generated by the balls {x : |x|_sp < ε}, ε > 0. For every pseudouniformiser ϖ of A the sets ϖⁿ·A°° (n ≥ 0; A°° the ideal of topologically nilpotent elements) form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0 for it; in particular it does not depend on the norm datum. Write A_sp for A with this topology (Lean: the type synonym `Huber.SpectralTop A`, with the ring equivalence `toSpectralTop : A ≃+* SpectralTop A`). Then: (i) the identity A → A_sp is continuous; (ii) A_sp is a Tate ring with pseudouniformiser ϖ and pair of definition (A_sp,≤1, ϖ·A_sp,≤1), where A_sp,≤1 = {x : |x|_sp ≤ 1}; (iii) the topologically nilpotent elements of A_sp are those of A, and A_sp° = {x : |x|_sp ≤ 1} is bounded, so A_sp is uniform (Hansen–Kedlaya Definition 2.3, the anchor's Layer 4.2 predicate); (iv) every ring of integral elements A⁺ of A is a ring of integral elements of A_sp, giving a Tau Ceti `Pair` on A_sp and a morphism of Huber pairs (A, A⁺) → (A_sp, A⁺); (v) every continuous ring homomorphism φ : A → B of Tate rings is continuous as a map A_sp → B_sp; (vi) the identity A → A_sp is a homeomorphism iff A° is bounded, i.e. iff A is uniform. Lean name: `Huber.SpectralTop A`.
hypotheses: A is a Tate ring (Tau Ceti `IsTateRing`).
proofSteps: Basis: ϖⁿ·A°° ⊆ {|x|_sp < rⁿ} because |ϖⁿy|_sp ≤ |ϖ|_spⁿ|y|_sp ≤ rⁿ|y|_sp and |y|_sp < 1 for y ∈ A°°; and {|x|_sp < rⁿ·|ϖ⁻¹|_sp⁻ⁿ} ⊆ ϖⁿ·A°° because |ϖ⁻ⁿx|_sp ≤ |ϖ⁻¹|_spⁿ|x|_sp < 1 (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-seminorm, API spectralSeminorm_lt_one_iff). A°° is an additive subgroup (Tau Ceti `topologicallyNilpotentIdeal`, an ideal of A°). Changing ϖ to ϖ' gives the same filter since ϖ'^m ∈ ϖ·A° and ϖ^m ∈ ϖ'·A° for m ≫ 0.
(i): A°° ⊇ ϖ·A₀ is open in A, so each ϖⁿA°° is an open subgroup of A.

(ii),(iii): A_sp,≤1 is a subring (|·|_sp is a nonarchimedean submultiplicative seminorm with |1|_sp ≤ 1), open (it contains A°°) and bounded (ϖⁿ⁺¹·A_sp,≤1 ⊆ ϖⁿA°°); ϖ is a unit with ϖⁿ ∈ ϖⁿ⁻¹A°°; so (A_sp,≤1, ϖ) is a pair of definition. If x is power-bounded in A_sp then |x|_spⁿ = |xⁿ|_sp is bounded, so |x|_sp ≤ 1; conversely |x|_sp ≤ 1 puts all powers in the bounded set A_sp,≤1.
(iv): A⁺ ⊆ A° ⊆ A_sp,≤1 = A_sp°; A⁺ contains A°° (Tau Ceti `IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`), which is open in A_sp; integral closedness does not involve the topology.
(v): φ maps A°° into B°° and ϖ to a pseudouniformiser φ(ϖ) of B (φ is adic, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-ring-homomorphism), so φ(ϖⁿA°°) ⊆ φ(ϖ)ⁿB°°, a basic neighbourhood of B_sp.

(vi): if A° is bounded it is a ring of definition, the sets ϖⁿA° are a basis of A (Tau Ceti `IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero`) and ϖⁿ⁺¹A° ⊆ ϖⁿA°° ⊆ ϖⁿA°; conversely equal topologies give A° = A_sp°, which is bounded by (iii).

nodes.title: The spectral topology has the same continuous valuations, adic spectrum and rational subsets
nodes.statement: Let A be a Tate ring and A_sp = `Huber.SpectralTop A` (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology). A valuation on A is continuous for the topology of A iff it is continuous for the spectral topology: Cont(A_sp) = Cont(A) as subsets of Spv(A) (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.cont`). Consequently, for every ring of integral elements A⁺ of A, Spa(A_sp, A⁺) = Spa(A, A⁺) as subspaces of Spv(A) (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spa A⁺` for the two topologies), and for every finite T ⊆ A and s ∈ A the rational subsets R(T/s) (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset A⁺ T s`) of the two spectra are equal; a finite subset generates an open ideal of A iff it generates an open ideal of A_sp (in both Tate rings: iff it generates the unit ideal).
hypotheses: A is a Tate ring; A⁺ is a ring of integral elements of A.
proofSteps: Cont(A_sp) ⊆ Cont(A): the identity A → A_sp is continuous (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology (i)), and a valuation all of whose sets {x : v(x) < γ} are open for the coarser topology has them open for the finer one.

Cont(A) ⊆ Cont(A_sp): let v ∈ Cont(A) and γ ≠ 0 in its value group; for a pseudouniformiser ϖ some power satisfies v(ϖ)ⁿ < γ (Tau Ceti `Valuation.exists_pow_lt_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`, {v < γ} being a neighbourhood of 0), and v(y) < 1 for every topologically nilpotent y (Tau Ceti `Valuation.IsContinuous.lt_one_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`); so the subgroup {x : v(x) < γ} contains ϖⁿ·A°°, a neighbourhood of 0 in A_sp (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology, basis), and is open in A_sp.

Spa and rational subsets are defined inside Spv(A) from Cont, the plus ring and the elements T, s only (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spa_def`, `ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`), and the subspace topology comes from Spv(A), which does not depend on the topology of A; so they coincide. In a Tate ring an ideal is open iff it is the unit ideal (Tau Ceti `IsTateRing.isOpen_iff_eq_top`), for both topologies.
acceptance: For A = K[ε]/(ε²) with A⁺ = K° + Kε and K = ℚ_p, Spa(A_sp, A⁺) = Spa(A, A⁺) is a single point, the valuation a + bε ↦ |a|_p.
For uniform A the statement is the identity (A_sp = A by AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology (vi)).

nodes.title: The uniformization of a Tate Huber pair
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair (Tau Ceti `Pair`) with A a Tate ring. Its *uniformization* is the Huber pair (A^u, A^{u+}) where A^u is the Hausdorff completion of A_sp = `Huber.SpectralTop A` (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology; Tau Ceti `IsHuberRing.completion`, `IsTateRing.completion`), i.e. the separated completion of A for its spectral seminorm (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.8.13), and A^{u+} is the closure of the image of A⁺ in A^u. It comes with the morphism of Huber pairs ι : (A, A⁺) → (A^u, A^{u+}), the composite of the continuous identity A → A_sp and the completion map. Properties: (a) (A^u, A^{u+}) is a complete Hausdorff Huber pair, A^u is a Tate ring, and A^u is uniform (A^{u°} is bounded; the continuous extension of |·|_sp to A^u is a power-multiplicative norm defining its topology); (b) ι has dense image and kernel {x : |x|_sp = 0}; (c) for every complete Hausdorff Huber pair (B, B⁺) with B° bounded and every morphism of Huber pairs φ : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) there is exactly one morphism φ^u : (A^u, A^{u+}) → (B, B⁺) with φ^u ∘ ι = φ, so uniformization is left adjoint to the inclusion of complete Hausdorff uniform Tate Huber pairs into Tate Huber pairs; (d) Spa(ι) : Spa(A^u, A^{u+}) → Spa(A, A⁺) is a homeomorphism under which rational subsets correspond to rational subsets; (e) if A is complete, Hausdorff and uniform, ι is an isomorphism. Pinned conventions: morphisms are Tau Ceti `Pair.Hom` (continuous, plus rings respected), which for Banach rings are the bounded morphisms (Hansen–Kedlaya Remark 2.11); the plus ring is the closure of the image of A⁺, not the image. Lean name: `Huber.Pair.uniformization`.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) is a Huber pair and A is a Tate ring.
For the universal property: (B, B⁺) is a complete Hausdorff Huber pair with B° bounded.
proofSteps: A_sp is a uniform Tate ring, A⁺ is a ring of integral elements of A_sp and the identity is a morphism of Huber pairs (A, A⁺) → (A_sp, A⁺) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology).

Completion: Completion(A_sp) is a complete Hausdorff Tate ring with the completed pair of definition (Tau Ceti `IsHuberRing.completion`, `IsTateRing.completion`, `PairOfDefinition.completion`); the closure of the image of A⁺ is a ring of integral elements (anchor Layer 0: completion of Huber pairs, Wedhorn Lemma 7.47).

Uniformity: |·|_sp is uniformly continuous on A_sp and extends to a seminorm β on A^u; β is power-multiplicative (β(xⁿ) = β(x)ⁿ passes to limits), a norm (A^u is separated for it) and defines the topology of A^u; a power-bounded x has β(x)ⁿ = β(xⁿ) bounded, so A^{u°} ⊆ {β ≤ 1}, which is bounded.

Dense image and kernel: Mathlib `UniformSpace.Completion.denseRange_coe`; the kernel of A_sp → Completion(A_sp) is the closure of {0} in A_sp, which is {x : |x|_sp = 0} (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-seminorm, API spectralSeminorm_eq_zero_iff).

Universal property: φ is continuous as a map A_sp → B_sp (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology (v)) and B_sp = B because B° is bounded (spectral-topology (vi)); B being complete and Hausdorff, φ extends uniquely to a continuous ring homomorphism A^u → B (Mathlib `UniformSpace.Completion.extensionHom`, `extensionHom_coe`); it maps A^{u+} into B⁺ since B⁺ is an open, hence closed, subgroup containing φ(A⁺). Uniqueness: two continuous extensions agree on the dense image of ι. B is Tate because it receives a continuous map from a Tate ring (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-ring-homomorphism, API IsAdicHom.of_isTateRing).

Spa: the completion morphism induces a homeomorphism Spa(A^u, A^{u+}) → Spa(A_sp, A⁺) identifying rational subsets (anchor Layer 0: Spa of the completion, Wedhorn Proposition 7.48), and Spa(A_sp, A⁺) = Spa(A, A⁺) with the same rational subsets (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology-cont-eq); preimages of rational subsets are Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`.
(e): for complete Hausdorff uniform A, A_sp = A (spectral-topology (vi)) and the completion map of a complete Hausdorff ring is an isomorphism.
acceptance: (K[ε]/(ε²), K° + Kε)^u = (K, K°) with ι the reduction map ε ↦ 0.
For A = {Σ aₙTⁿ ∈ K⟦T⟧ : |aₙ|(n+1) → 0} with ‖f‖ = sup |aₙ|(n+1), A^u = K⟨T⟩ and ι is the inclusion.
For a complete Hausdorff uniform (A, A⁺), for instance (K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩), ι is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: The uniform completed tensor product of Tate Huber pairs
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) be complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with A a Tate ring, and f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) morphisms of Huber pairs (Tau Ceti `Pair.Hom`; f and g are adic and B, C are Tate by Wedhorn Proposition 6.25). The *uniform completed tensor product* is B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C := (B ⊗̂_A C)^u, the uniformization (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization) of the completed tensor product (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product), with inlᵘ := ι ∘ inl and inrᵘ := ι ∘ inr. Properties: (a) it is a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate Huber pair and inlᵘ ∘ f = inrᵘ ∘ g; (b) it is a pushout of (f, g) in the category of complete Hausdorff uniform Tate Huber pairs: for every such (R, R⁺) and morphisms φ : (B, B⁺) → (R, R⁺), ψ : (C, C⁺) → (R, R⁺) with φ ∘ f = ψ ∘ g there is exactly one morphism χ : B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C → (R, R⁺) with χ ∘ inlᵘ = φ and χ ∘ inrᵘ = ψ; (c) the canonical morphism ι : B ⊗̂_A C → B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C induces a homeomorphism of adic spectra identifying rational subsets; (d) ι is an isomorphism iff B ⊗̂_A C is uniform (for instance K⟨T⟩ ⊗̂_K K⟨S⟩ = K⟨T, S⟩), and it is not an isomorphism in general: ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p is not uniform (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.8.5). No sheafiness of B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C and no fibre-product property of its Spa is claimed. Lean name: `Huber.Pair.uniformCompletedTensor f g`.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) complete Hausdorff Huber pairs, A a Tate ring.
f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) morphisms of Huber pairs.
proofSteps: f and g are adic and B, C are Tate (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-ring-homomorphism, API IsAdicHom.of_isTateRing), so B ⊗̂_A C is defined and is a complete Hausdorff Tate Huber pair (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product, API completedTensor.isTateRing).
(a), (c): uniformize (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization: uniformity, completeness, Spa homeomorphism).

(b): given φ, ψ into a complete Hausdorff uniform (R, R⁺) — R⁺ is closed and integrally closed — the universal property of the completed tensor product (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product-universal-property) gives a unique χ₀ : B ⊗̂_A C → (R, R⁺), and the universal property of the uniformization (R0/uniformization, lift) factors χ₀ uniquely through ι; uniqueness of χ follows from hom_ext of both constructions.
(d): R0/uniformization (isIso_of_isUniform) for ⇐; for ⇒ an isomorphic copy of a uniform pair is uniform. The non-example is Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.8.5.
acceptance: K⟨T⟩ ⊗̂ᵘ_K K⟨S⟩ ≅ K⟨T, S⟩ for a complete nonarchimedean field K.
ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p → ℂ_p ⊗̂ᵘ_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p is not an isomorphism (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.8.5).

nodes.title: Separated morphism of adic spaces
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of adic spaces (the category of the AdicSpaces anchor, Layer 5) that is locally of weakly finite type (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes). Such an f is adic, so the fibre product X ×_Y X exists in the category of adic spaces (R0/fibre-products-existence, case (b)) and the diagonal Δ_f: X → X ×_Y X is the morphism with both projections equal to the identity. The morphism f is separated if the image Δ_f(|X|) is a closed subset of the underlying space |X ×_Y X| of the adic fibre product (Huber 1996, 1.3.1). Conventions: (1) X ×_Y X is the fibre product of adic spaces, never the topological fibre product |X| ×_{|Y|} |X|; the comparison map |X ×_Y X| → |X| ×_{|Y|} |X| is surjective and in general not injective (R0/fibre-product-points). (2) Separatedness is only defined for morphisms locally of weakly finite type; no separatedness predicate is attached to a morphism outside that class. (3) By R0/diagonal-locally-closed the diagonal is a locally closed embedding, so a separated f has Δ_f a closed embedding (closed adic subspace in the sense of R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings) whenever X, Y are locally strongly noetherian analytic adic spaces and f is locally of finite type (Zavyalov, Quotients, Corollary B.7.4).
hypotheses: f: X → Y is a morphism of adic spaces, locally of weakly finite type
Closedness is tested in the underlying topological space of the adic fibre product X ×_Y X
proofSteps: Existence of X ×_Y X: f locally of weakly finite type implies f adic (inclusion chain of R0/finite-type-morphism-classes), so case (b) of R0/fibre-products-existence applies with g = f.
The diagonal is the morphism given by the universal property of the fibre product (R0/fibre-products-existence); being separated is the property 'range of |Δ_f| is closed'.

Characterisation (3): Δ_f is a locally closed embedding (R0/diagonal-locally-closed); a locally closed embedding with closed image is a closed embedding (R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings; Zavyalov, Quotients, Lemma B.6.14 in the locally strongly noetherian analytic case).
acceptance: The structure morphism of the closed unit disc Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) → Spa(K, K°) is separated: its diagonal is the closed subspace V(T₁ − T₂) of the closed bidisc.
The unit disc with doubled origin is not separated over Spa(K, K°).

uses.how: separatedness is a defining condition of proper and of partially proper morphisms (R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism, R0/partially-proper-morphism)
separatedness is characterised by uniqueness of centres of valuation rings

over a strongly noetherian Tate affinoid base, the intersection of two affinoid opens of a separated X is affinoid; this is what Čech computations of coherent cohomology (AdicSpacesPartII:R3, Kiehl proper mapping theorem) use
a section of a separated smooth morphism is a Zariski-closed (lci) immersion, via the diagonal

The structure morphism D → Spa(K, K°) is separated: D ×_K D is the closed bidisc Spa(K⟨T₁,T₂⟩, K°⟨T₁,T₂⟩) and Δ(D) = V(T₁ − T₂) is closed. At the same time the diagonal of |D| is not closed in the product of topological spaces |D| × |D|, because |D| is not Hausdorff (the Gauss point has proper specialisations); a definition testing closedness in |X| ×_{|Y|} |X| would wrongly declare D non-separated.

nodes.title: Universally closed morphism of adic spaces
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of adic spaces that is locally of weakly finite type. For every adic morphism g: Y' → Y the fibre product X' = X ×_Y Y' exists (R0/fibre-products-existence, case (b)); let f': X' → Y' be the base change. The morphism f is universally closed if, for every adic morphism g: Y' → Y, the continuous map |f'|: |X'| → |Y'| is a closed map (Huber 1996, 1.3.2(i)). Conventions: base change is only taken along adic morphisms, which is the class along which Huber's fibre product (b) exists; over an analytic Y every morphism is adic (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes), so there the condition is 'closed after every base change'.
hypotheses: f: X → Y locally of weakly finite type
Test morphisms g: Y' → Y range over all adic morphisms of adic spaces
proofSteps: The base changes exist by R0/fibre-products-existence (b); the property is the conjunction over all adic g of IsClosedMap |f'|.

Relation to specialisation: a closed continuous map is specializing (Mathlib IsClosedMap.specializingMap), so universally closed implies universally specializing (R0/universally-specializing-morphism); the converse for quasi-compact f is R0/proper-iff-partially-proper-quasi-compact.
acceptance: Every finite morphism to an analytic adic space is universally closed (R0/finite-morphisms).
The closed unit disc D → Spa(K, K°) is not universally closed.

The morphism D → Spa(K, K°) is quasi-compact, separated and of +weakly finite type but not universally closed: it is not universally specializing, since for the Gauss point x ∈ D and the valuation ring A ⊊ k(x)⁺ of k(x) that is the preimage of the valuation ring of the residue field k(T) at T = ∞, the pair (x, A) has a centre on Spa(K, K°) but none on D (T ∈ K°⟨T⟩ would have to lie in A). A definition requiring only that |f| itself be closed would accept D, since |D| → |Spa(K, K°)| (a point) is trivially closed.

nodes.title: Proper morphism of adic spaces
nodes.statement: A morphism f: X → Y of adic spaces is proper if it is of +weakly finite type (quasi-compact and locally of +weakly finite type, R0/finite-type-morphism-classes), separated (R0/separated-morphism) and universally closed (R0/universally-closed-morphism) (Huber 1996, 1.3.2(ii)). Conventions: (1) the finiteness condition is '+weakly finite type', which includes quasi-compactness and the plus-ring condition O_X⁺(U) = integral closure of O_Y⁺(V)[E ∪ O_X(U)°°] for a finite E; it is neither 'locally of finite type' (Mathlib's IsProper for schemes) nor 'weakly finite type'. (2) Properness of rigid analytic varieties in Kiehl's sense (Conrad AWS, Definition 3.2.3) is a different definition; the comparison is AdicSpacesPartII:R1/proper-separated-comparisons.
hypotheses: f: X → Y morphism of adic spaces
proofSteps: Conjunction of three predicates; the finiteness predicate comes from R0/finite-type-morphism-classes (of +weakly finite type = quasi-compact and locally of +weakly finite type).
acceptance: Every finite morphism to an analytic adic space is proper (R0/finite-morphisms).
Proper equals partially proper and quasi-compact (R0/proper-iff-partially-proper-quasi-compact).
The projective line over K is proper over Spa(K, K°); the closed unit disc is not.

uses.how: proper = partially proper + quasi-compact (R0/proper-iff-partially-proper-quasi-compact)
valuative criterion for properness of analytic adic spaces
finite = proper and quasi-finite; proper with proper fibre is finite nearby (R0/finite-morphisms, R0/finite-from-proper-fibre, R0/quasi-finite-and-finiteness-criteria)
finiteness and base change of coherent cohomology are stated for proper morphisms
finiteness of étale cohomology is proved for proper smooth adic spaces over Spa(K, O_K)

A2 imports properness from R0

nodes.title: Universally specializing morphism of adic spaces
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of adic spaces. For x ∈ X, f is specializing at x if for every specialization y' of f(x) (that is, y' ∈ closure{f(x)} in |Y|) there is a specialization x' of x with f(x') = y'. If f is locally of weakly finite type, f is universally specializing at x₀ ∈ X if for every adic morphism g: Y' → Y and every point x₀' of X' = X ×_Y Y' lying over x₀, the base change f': X' → Y' is specializing at x₀'; f is universally specializing if it is so at every point (Huber 1996, 1.3.3, as recorded in the reviewed decomposition). Convention: 'f specializing at every point' is exactly Mathlib's SpecializingMap for the continuous map |f|.
hypotheses: f locally of weakly finite type for the 'universally' version
Base change along adic morphisms only
proofSteps: Pointwise definition, then quantified over all adic base changes (which exist by R0/fibre-products-existence (b)) and all points over x₀.
acceptance: Closed maps are specializing, so universally closed morphisms are universally specializing.
For the inclusion D ⊆ P¹ of the closed disc into the projective line, the specialization of the Gauss point in the direction |T| > 1 does not lift, so this open embedding is not specializing.

Being an open embedding therefore does not imply being universally specializing.

nodes.title: Partially proper morphism of adic spaces

Conventions: partial properness is a relative notion for morphisms; an open subspace U ⊆ X is partially proper over X only in special cases (the inclusion of the open unit disc into the closed disc is, the inclusion of the closed disc into P¹ is not). The Kedlaya-Liu notion of a partially proper open subset (inverse image of an open subset of the real quotient) is a different definition, compared only through its uses.

nodes.title: Valuation rings of an analytic adic space and their centres
nodes.statement: Let X be an analytic adic space. For x ∈ X let k(x) be the residue field of the local ring O_{X,x}, k(x)⁺ ⊆ k(x) the valuation ring of the valuation v_x, and κ(x) = (k(x)^∧, k(x)⁺^∧) the completed residue affinoid field with its canonical morphism ι_x: Spa κ(x) → X (AdicSpaces anchor, Layer 5; see requests). A valuation ring of X is a pair (x, A) with x ∈ X and A a valuation ring of the field k(x) such that A ⊆ k(x)⁺; X_v denotes the set of valuation rings of X (Huber 1996, 1.3.5). Since A ⊆ k(x)⁺ are valuation rings of the same field, A contains the maximal ideal of k(x)⁺, so A is open in k(x) and its closure Â in k(x)^∧ is a valuation ring making (k(x)^∧, Â) an affinoid field (Hübner, §2) with a canonical morphism j: Spa κ(x) → Spa(k(x)^∧, Â). For a morphism g: Spa κ(x) → Z to an adic space Z, a point z ∈ Z is a centre of (x, A) on Z with respect to g if there is a morphism c: Spa(k(x)^∧, Â) → Z with c ∘ j = g and c(s) = z, s the closed point of Spa(k(x)^∧, Â). A centre of (x, A) on X means a centre with respect to ι_x; for a morphism f: X → Y, a centre of (x, A) on Y means a centre with respect to f ∘ ι_x. Topology: X_v carries the topology generated by the sets D(U, h) = {(x, A) ∈ X_v : x ∈ U, h(x) ∈ A} for U ⊆ X open and h ∈ O_X(U), h(x) the image of h in k(x).
hypotheses: X analytic (every point analytic)
A ranges over valuation rings of k(x) contained in k(x)⁺ (not over all valuation rings of k(x))
The subbasic sets D(U, h) are read as {x ∈ U, h(x) ∈ A}; this reading of Huber's notation is fixed here (see gaps)
proofSteps: Definition of X_v and of centres as stated; the morphism j and the affinoid field (k(x)^∧, Â) exist because A ⊇ 𝔪_{k(x)⁺} is open and A ⊆ k(x)⁺ ⊆ k(x)°.

Huber 1.3.6 (recorded in the reviewed decomposition): on an affinoid Z = Spa(B, B⁺) with g induced by φ: B → k(x)^∧, (x, A) has a centre with respect to g if and only if φ(B⁺) ⊆ Â, and then the extension c is unique; the proof uses the existence and uniqueness of a valuation with given support and centre (Huber 1.1.10(iii)) and the universal property of Spa (Huber 1994, Proposition 2.1, anchor Layer 5).
acceptance: (x, k(x)⁺) has exactly one centre on X, namely x itself.
On D, at the Gauss point x_G, the valuation ring A_a (preimage of the valuation ring of k(T) at T = a, a ∈ k) has exactly one centre (the type-5 point in direction a), while A_∞ has none.

uniqueness of centres (1.3.6, 1.3.7) separates the generalisation sets of points over a point

nodes.title: Valuative criterion for separatedness (Huber 1.3.7)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of analytic adic spaces which is quasi-separated and locally of weakly finite type. Then f is separated if and only if for every (x, A) ∈ X_v (R0/adic-valuation-rings-and-centres) and every centre y of (x, A) on Y there is at most one centre z of (x, A) on X with f(z) = y.
hypotheses: X, Y analytic

f locally of weakly finite type

nodes.title: Valuative criterion for universal specialization (Huber 1.3.8)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of analytic adic spaces, locally of weakly finite type, and x₀ ∈ X. Then f is universally specializing at x₀ (R0/universally-specializing-morphism) if and only if, for every valuation ring A of k(x₀) with A ⊆ k(x₀)⁺, every centre of (x₀, A) on Y is the image of a centre of (x₀, A) on X.
hypotheses: X, Y analytic
f locally of weakly finite type
x₀ fixed; the criterion is pointwise
proofSteps: (⇒) Let y be a centre of (x₀, A) on Y, given by c: Spa(k(x₀)^∧, Â) → Y extending f ∘ ι_{x₀}. Base change f along the adic morphism c (Y is analytic, so c is adic; R0/fibre-products-existence (b)). The pair (ι_{x₀}, j) defines a point x₀' of X' = X ×_Y Spa(k(x₀)^∧, Â) over x₀ whose image is the generic point of Spa(k(x₀)^∧, Â); universal specialization lifts the specialization to the closed point s to a specialization x₁' of x₀' over s (R0/fibre-product-points), and the image of x₁' in X is a centre of (x₀, A) on X over y.

(⇐) Given an adic g: Y' → Y, x₀' over x₀ and a specialization y' of f'(x₀'), construct a valuation ring A' ⊆ k(x₀')⁺ inducing k(y')⁺ (existence of valuation rings with prescribed centre, Huber 1.3.6(ii) as recorded), apply the hypothesis to the image pair on X and lift the centre to X' via the universal property of the fibre product.
acceptance: For the closed disc D → Spa(K, K°) the criterion fails at the Gauss point with A = A_∞ (R0/adic-valuation-rings-and-centres, test ValuationRing_test_gaussPoint), so D → Spa(K, K°) is not universally specializing at x_G.

nodes.title: Valuative criterion for partial properness and properness of analytic adic spaces (Huber 1.3.9)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of analytic adic spaces which is quasi-separated and locally of +weakly finite type. Then f is partially proper (R0/partially-proper-morphism) if and only if for every (x, A) ∈ X_v and every centre y of (x, A) on Y there is exactly one centre z of (x, A) on X with f(z) = y. If moreover f is of +weakly finite type (in particular quasi-compact), the same condition is equivalent to f being proper (R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism). Huber's Lemma 1.3.10 rephrases the condition as the unique extension of morphisms along Spa(K, K⁺) → Spa(K, K'⁺) for affinoid fields sharing the field K; the X_v form stated here is the declaration.
hypotheses: X, Y analytic adic spaces (the source proves the criterion only in this case)
f quasi-separated and locally of +weakly finite type; for the proper version f of +weakly finite type
proofSteps: Uniqueness of centres ⇔ separated: R0/valuative-criterion-separated (f is quasi-separated and locally of weakly finite type).
Existence of centres at every point ⇔ universally specializing: R0/valuative-criterion-specializing applied at each x₀ ∈ X.
Partially proper = locally +weakly finite type + separated + universally specializing (R0/partially-proper-morphism); combine the two steps.
Proper version: proper ⇔ partially proper and quasi-compact (R0/proper-iff-partially-proper-quasi-compact).
acceptance: Every finite morphism to an analytic adic space satisfies existence and uniqueness of centres, because integral plus rings are contained in every valuation ring containing the base plus ring (R0/finite-morphisms); hence finite ⇒ proper, and quasi-compact partially proper = proper (Huber 1.3.4).

Concrete instance: the closed unit disc D → Spa(K, K°) fails existence at (x_G, A_∞); the projective line P¹ → Spa(K, K°) satisfies existence and uniqueness; the open unit disc satisfies both and is partially proper but not quasi-compact.
For analytic adic spaces the criterion can be phrased with S = Spa(K, K⁺) → T = Spa(K, K'⁺), (K, K⁺) and (K, K'⁺) affinoid fields sharing the field K (Huber 1.3.10).

sources.match: This is the criterion (b) of Corollary 1.3.9.

nodes.title: Proper equals partially proper and quasi-compact (Huber 1.3.4)
nodes.statement: A morphism f: X → Y of adic spaces is proper if and only if it is partially proper and quasi-compact.
hypotheses: f: X → Y any morphism of adic spaces (no analyticity hypothesis)
proofSteps: (⇒) Of +weakly finite type means quasi-compact and locally of +weakly finite type (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes); universally closed implies universally specializing because a closed continuous map is specializing (Mathlib IsClosedMap.specializingMap), applied to every adic base change.

(⇐) Let g: Y' → Y be adic and f': X' → Y' the base change; f' is quasi-compact (quasi-compactness of the base-changed leg, Corollary 1.2.3 in R0/fibre-products-existence) and specializing (universal specialization).

A quasi-compact specializing morphism is closed: closedness is local on Y', so take Y' affinoid (spectral, AdicSpaces anchor Layer 2); X' is covered by finitely many affinoids U_i, and each f'|U_i is a spectral map of spectral spaces because it comes from an adic ring homomorphism (R0/adic-ring-homomorphism, anchor Layer 2). For Z ⊆ X' closed, Z ∩ U_i is pro-constructible (TauCeti IsClosed.isProConstructible), its image is pro-constructible (spectral maps are continuous for the constructible topologies and pro-constructible subsets are spectral, Stacks 0A2S, TauCeti IsProConstructible.spectralSpace), and a finite union of pro-constructible sets is pro-constructible (TauCeti Set.Finite.isProConstructible_biUnion).
f'(Z) is stable under specialization (f' specializing, Z closed), so it is closed (Stacks 0903). Hence f is universally closed; with separatedness and +weakly finite type, f is proper.
acceptance: Open unit disc: partially proper, not quasi-compact, not proper. Closed unit disc: quasi-compact, not partially proper, not proper. P¹: proper.
Scheme analogue: Mathlib universallyClosed_eq_universallySpecializing (universally closed = universally specializing + quasi-compact).

nodes.title: The space of valuation rings of a qcqs analytic adic space is spectral (Huber 1.3.12)
nodes.statement: Let X be a quasi-compact quasi-separated analytic adic space. Then X_v, with the topology generated by the sets D(U, h) (R0/adic-valuation-rings-and-centres), is a spectral space, and the projection p: X_v → X, (x, A) ↦ x, is a spectral map.
hypotheses: X analytic, quasi-compact and quasi-separated
proofSteps: Reduce to X affinoid (finite affinoid cover, quasi-separatedness for the overlaps).

Consider X_v and X with their constructible topologies X_v^c, X^c; the map p: X_v^c → X^c has as fibre over x the set of valuation rings of k(x) inside k(x)⁺, i.e. the abstract Riemann surface of the residue field of k(x)⁺, which is quasi-compact.

Describe p(D) for a constructible D by finitely many polynomial inequalities (Huber's description (2) in the proof, recorded in the reviewed decomposition) to show p(D) is constructible; deduce quasi-compactness of X_v^c and that the D(U, h) generate a spectral topology (criterion for spectrality: quasi-compact, sober, quasi-compact opens closed under finite intersection and forming a basis; Mathlib SpectralSpace, anchor Layer 1.2).
acceptance: For X = Spa(K, K°) with K a rank-one field and residue field k, X_v is the Riemann–Zariski space of valuation rings of k (with the generic point the trivial valuation ring k), which is spectral.

nodes.title: Closures of quasi-compact sets under partially proper morphisms (Huber 1.3.13)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a partially proper morphism of analytic adic spaces with Y quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then the closure in X of every quasi-compact subset of X is quasi-compact.
hypotheses: X, Y analytic
f partially proper
Y quasi-compact and quasi-separated
proofSteps: Let T ⊆ X be quasi-compact; enlarge T to a quasi-compact open (finite union of affinoids) T₀. The set S of (x, A) ∈ (T₀)_v whose image pair has a centre on Y is pro-constructible in the spectral space (T₀)_v (R0/valuation-ring-space-spectral), hence quasi-compact.
By the valuative criterion (R0/separated-proper-partially-proper) every (x, A) ∈ S has a unique centre c(x, A) on X, and c: S → X is continuous.

The closure of T is contained in c(S ∩ p⁻¹(T)) ∪ T; every point of the closure of T is a specialization of a point of T (Stacks 0903 applied inside affinoids) and hence a centre; the image of the quasi-compact set S ∩ p⁻¹(closure) under the continuous c is quasi-compact.
acceptance: For the open unit disc B → Spa(K, K°) and T = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}, the closure of T in B is T together with its specializations and is quasi-compact.

nodes.title: The diagonal of a separated morphism is a closed embedding
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of adic spaces that is locally of weakly finite type (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes), with X covered by open affinoids Spa(B, B⁺) with B complete and stably sheafy (for instance X locally noetherian), so that X ×_Y X exists (R0/fibre-products-existence, case (b); f is adic). Then f is separated (R0/separated-morphism: the image of Δ_f is closed) if and only if the diagonal Δ_f: X → X ×_Y X is a closed embedding (R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings). The key step is general: a locally closed embedding h: T → Z of adic spaces whose image h(|T|) is closed in |Z| is a closed embedding.
hypotheses: f locally of weakly finite type
X covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings
proofSteps: (⇐) A closed embedding is a homeomorphism onto the closed set {z : 𝓘_z ≠ O_{Z,z}} (R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings), so the image of Δ_f is closed.
(⇒) By R0/diagonal-locally-closed, Δ_f factors as a closed embedding δ: X → W into the open subspace W ⊆ X ×_Y X (the union of the U ×_V U over affinoid charts) followed by the inclusion of W.

Locally closed with closed image ⇒ closed (the argument of Zavyalov, Lemma B.6.14): let 𝓘_W ⊆ O_W be the admissible ideal sheaf of δ and let 𝓘 be O on the open complement C of the closed set Δ_f(|X|). On W ∩ C the stalks of δ_*O_X vanish, so 𝓘_W = O there, and the two ideal sheaves glue to an ideal sheaf 𝓘 ⊆ O_{X ×_Y X} (gluing of sheaves along an open cover, anchor Layer 5).

𝓘 is admissible, since admissibility is affinoid-local: on affinoids of W it is the condition for 𝓘_W, and on affinoids Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ C the ideal is A itself with A/A = 0 sheafy. Hence V(𝓘) = δ(X) and Δ_f is X ×_Y X-isomorphic to the inclusion of V(𝓘), a closed embedding.
acceptance: For the closed unit disc X = Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) over Spa(K, K°), Δ_X is the closed embedding of X into the closed bidisc cut out by the ideal (T ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ T) of K⟨T₁, T₂⟩.
For the closed disc with doubled origin, Δ is a locally closed embedding whose image is not closed; it is not a closed embedding, and the space is not separated.

nodes.title: Closed embeddings are proper
nodes.statement: Let i: Z → X be a closed embedding of adic spaces (R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings), with X covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings. Then i is proper (R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism): it is quasi-compact and locally of +weakly finite type (R0/plus-weakly-finite-type), separated (R0/separated-morphism) and universally closed (R0/universally-closed-morphism); for every adic morphism g: X' → X from an adic space X' covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings, the base change Z ×_X X' → X' is the closed embedding V(𝓘·O_{X'}) → X'. No analyticity of X is assumed (Huber's route through finite morphisms, 1.4.5(ii),(iii), needs an analytic target in this blueprint, R0/finite-morphisms).
hypotheses: i a closed embedding
X covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings
proofSteps: Finiteness conditions: over an affinoid Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X where 𝓘 is admissible, i is Spa(A/J) → Spa(A) for the quotient pair A/J (Tau Ceti Huber.Pair.quotient): A → A/J is a surjective open continuous homomorphism, hence topologically of finite type with no variables, and the plus ring of A/J is the integral closure of the image of A⁺ (E = ∅ in R0/plus-weakly-finite-type). The preimage Spa(A/J) of the affinoid Spa(A) is quasi-compact, so i is quasi-compact and locally of +weakly finite type, hence of +weakly finite type.

Separated: i is a monomorphism (uniqueness in the universal property of V(𝓘), API AdicSpace.closedSubspace.lift of R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings), so (id_Z, id_Z) is a kernel pair of i (Mathlib CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.id_of_mono): Z ×_X Z = Z and Δ_i is an isomorphism, whose image is all of |Z ×_X Z|, a closed set.

Universally closed: for adic g: X' → X the base change is V(𝓘·O_{X'}) → X' (API AdicSpace.closedSubspace.pullback of R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings), again a closed embedding; its underlying map is a homeomorphism onto a closed subset, hence a closed map.
acceptance: The origin Spa(K, K°) → Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩), cut out by (T), is proper; so is the non-reduced point V(T²).

The open embedding of the open unit disc into the closed unit disc is not proper: it is not quasi-compact and its image is not closed. A locally closed embedding is proper exactly when it is a closed embedding (a proper one has closed image, R0/separated-diagonal-closed-embedding).

nodes.title: Universally closed, separated and proper morphisms are stable under adic base change
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of adic spaces locally of weakly finite type and g: Y' → Y an adic morphism (R0/adic-morphism), where all adic spaces involved are covered by open affinoids Spa(B, B⁺) with B complete and stably sheafy (for instance locally noetherian adic spaces, R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space with R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy), so that the fibre products below exist by R0/fibre-products-existence. Let f': X' = X ×_Y Y' → Y' be the base change (R0/fibre-products-existence, case (b)). If f is universally closed (resp. separated, resp. quasi-compact, resp. proper), then so is f' (R0/universally-closed-morphism, R0/separated-morphism, R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism).
hypotheses: f locally of weakly finite type, g adic
all spaces covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings
proofSteps: f' is locally of weakly finite type and the projection X' → X is adic (R0/base-change-stability (ii)).

Universally closed: for an adic h: Y'' → Y', the composite g ∘ h is adic (composites of adic morphisms are adic, R0/adic-morphism), and pasting the cartesian squares (Mathlib CategoryTheory.IsPullback.paste_horiz, CategoryTheory.IsPullback.of_right) identifies X' ×_{Y'} Y'' → Y'' with the base change X ×_Y Y'' → Y'' of f along g ∘ h, which is a closed map because f is universally closed.

Separated: by the same pasting, Δ_{f'} is the base change of Δ_f along the canonical morphism X' ×_{Y'} X' → X ×_Y X; Δ_f is a closed embedding (R0/separated-diagonal-closed-embedding) and closed embeddings are stable under base change (API AdicSpace.closedSubspace.pullback of R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings), so Δ_{f'} is a closed embedding and its image is closed.
Quasi-compact: R0/base-change-stability (vi). Locally of +weakly finite type: R0/base-change-stability (iii). Hence proper passes to f'.

Adicness of g is needed: the base change of the quasi-compact Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) → Spa(ℤ_p, ℤ_p) along the non-adic Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧) → Spa(ℤ_p) is the open unit disc over ℚ_p, which is not quasi-compact over Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧) (R0/base-change-stability).

nodes.title: Composites of universally closed, separated and proper morphisms

If f and g are universally closed (resp. separated, resp. quasi-compact, resp. proper), then so is g ∘ f.

all spaces covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings

Δ_g is a closed embedding (R0/separated-diagonal-closed-embedding), so j is a closed embedding (API AdicSpace.closedSubspace.pullback of R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings) and a closed map; hence Δ_{g∘f}(|X|) = j(Δ_f(|X|)) is closed.

nodes.statement: Let h: X → Y and g: Y → Z be morphisms of adic spaces with g ∘ h locally of weakly finite type and g separated (R0/separated-morphism; in particular g is locally of weakly finite type), where all adic spaces involved are covered by open affinoids Spa(B, B⁺) with B complete and stably sheafy (for instance locally noetherian adic spaces, R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space with R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy), so that the fibre products below exist by R0/fibre-products-existence. If g ∘ h is universally closed (resp. proper), then h is universally closed (resp. proper); in particular h(|X|) is closed in |Y|. This is the adic form of Stacks Tag 01W6 (Mathlib's AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper.of_comp for schemes).

proofSteps: h is locally of weakly finite type (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes: if g ∘ h is, so is h, Wedhorn 6.33(2)); if g ∘ h is locally of +weakly finite type so is h, because O_Z⁺(W) → O_X⁺(U) factors through O_Y⁺(V), so the integral closure of the image of O_Y⁺(V)[E ∪ O_X(U)°°] lies between that of O_Z⁺(W)[E ∪ O_X(U)°°] = O_X⁺(U) and O_X⁺(U) (R0/plus-weakly-finite-type).

The graph Γ_h = (id_X, h): X → X ×_Z Y is the base change of Δ_g: Y → Y ×_Z Y along h ×_Z id_Y: X ×_Z Y → Y ×_Z Y (pasting, Mathlib CategoryTheory.IsPullback.paste_horiz, CategoryTheory.IsPullback.of_right); Δ_g is a closed embedding (R0/separated-diagonal-closed-embedding), hence so is Γ_h (API AdicSpace.closedSubspace.pullback of R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings), and Γ_h is proper (R0/closed-embedding-proper).

The projection pr₂: X ×_Z Y → Y is the base change of g ∘ h along g, which is adic (locally of weakly finite type, R0/finite-type-morphism-classes); so pr₂ is universally closed (resp. proper) by R0/proper-base-change.
h = pr₂ ∘ Γ_h is universally closed (resp. proper) by R0/proper-comp.

nodes.title: Universal closedness descends along surjections
nodes.statement: Let S be an adic space, p: X → S and q: Y → S morphisms locally of weakly finite type and π: X → Y a surjective morphism with q ∘ π = p, where all adic spaces involved are covered by open affinoids Spa(B, B⁺) with B complete and stably sheafy (for instance locally noetherian adic spaces, R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space with R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy), so that the fibre products below exist by R0/fibre-products-existence. If p is universally closed (R0/universally-closed-morphism), then q is universally closed. If moreover q is separated, quasi-compact and locally of +weakly finite type, then q is proper (R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism). Surjectivity of π need not be assumed after base change: it is preserved by every adic base change (proof step 2).
hypotheses: π surjective on underlying points
p, q locally of weakly finite type
all spaces covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings
proofSteps: For an adic S' → S put X' = X ×_S S' and Y' = Y ×_S S' (R0/fibre-products-existence, case (b)). The projection Y' → Y is adic (R0/base-change-stability (v)) and π is locally of weakly finite type (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes, since q ∘ π is), so X ×_Y Y' exists, and pasting (Mathlib CategoryTheory.IsPullback.paste_horiz, CategoryTheory.IsPullback.of_right) identifies it with X', the base change π': X' → Y' of π corresponding to the projection.

π' is surjective: for y' ∈ |Y'| with image y ∈ |Y| choose x ∈ |X| with π(x) = y; the compatible pair (x, y') lifts to a point of X ×_Y Y' (R0/fibre-product-points: the comparison map to the set-theoretic fibre product is surjective).

For a closed T ⊆ |Y'|, q'(T) = q'(π'(π'⁻¹(T))) = p'(π'⁻¹(T)) by surjectivity (Mathlib Set.image_preimage_eq), which is closed because p' is closed; so q' is closed for every adic S' → S (the argument of Stacks Tag 03GN).
The proper case is the definition of properness.
