nodes.title: Finite morphism of complete Huber pairs
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) and (B, B⁺) be complete Huber pairs (Tau Ceti Huber.Pair on complete Hausdorff Huber rings A, B) and φ: (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) a morphism of Huber pairs (tauceti Huber.Pair.Hom: continuous, φ(A⁺) ⊆ B⁺). The morphism φ is finite if it is of topologically finite type as a morphism of affinoid rings (Huber 1994, §3: φ factors through a quotient mapping A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩_M → B, i.e. a surjective continuous open ring map with B⁺ the integral closure of the image of the plus ring) and the ring maps A → B and A⁺ → B⁺ are integral (Huber 1996, 1.4.2). Consequences (Huber 1.4.2; Zavyalov, Quotients, B.2.7-B.2.9 in the Tate case): B is a finite A-module, B carries the natural A-module topology, and B⁺ is the integral closure of φ(A⁺) in B. For complete Tate pairs, φ is finite if and only if A → B is module-finite (Mathlib RingHom.Finite) and A⁺ → B⁺ is integral.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺) complete (Hausdorff) Huber pairs
φ a morphism of Huber pairs
proofSteps: Definition as stated.
B⁺ = integral closure of φ(A⁺): ⊆ because B⁺ is integral over φ(A⁺); ⊇ because B⁺ is integrally closed in B and contains φ(A⁺) (tauceti Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements).

Tate case equivalence: finite ring map + integral plus ⇒ topologically finite type (Zavyalov B.2.8, using the universal property of A⟨X⟩, Huber 1994 Lemma 3.5(i)); topologically finite type + integral plus ⇒ finite ring map (Zavyalov B.2.9: rings of definition A₀ → B₀ finite by reduction mod a pseudo-uniformiser and completeness).
Natural topology: B is complete and first countable, hence (open mapping, Huber 1994 Lemma 2.4(i); tauceti Huber.IsTateRing.isModuleTopology) carries the natural A-module topology (Zavyalov B.3.4).

nodes.title: The Huber pair of a finite algebra over a noetherian affinoid ring
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Huber pair such that A is a complete noetherian Tate ring or has a noetherian ring of definition (for instance A strongly noetherian Tate, or an affinoid algebra over a complete nonarchimedean field). Let ψ: A → C be a finite A-algebra (C commutative and finitely generated as an A-module). Equip C with the natural A-module topology (the finest topology making C a topological A-module; Mathlib moduleTopology A C; Huber 1994, p. 524) and let C⁺ be the integral closure of ψ(A⁺) in C. Then: (i) C is a complete Hausdorff Huber ring, Tate if A is, every A-submodule of C is closed, and ψ is continuous; (ii) C⁺ is a ring of integral elements, so Huber.Pair.finiteAlgebra (C, C⁺) is a complete Huber pair; (iii) ψ is a finite morphism of Huber pairs (R0/finite-huber-pair-hom); (iv) universal property: for every complete Huber pair (D, D⁺) with a morphism χ: (A, A⁺) → (D, D⁺), morphisms of Huber pairs (C, C⁺) → (D, D⁺) under (A, A⁺) are exactly the A-algebra maps C → D; (v) if A is strongly noetherian Tate, so is C; (vi) Spa(C, C⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) is a finite morphism of adic spaces, and for A strongly noetherian Tate every finite morphism X → Spa(A, A⁺) is isomorphic over Spa(A, A⁺) to one of this form, with C = O_X(X). Convention: the noetherian hypothesis is part of the construction; for a non-noetherian complete Tate ring A a finite A-algebra C = A/J with J not closed has a non-Hausdorff natural topology, so no complete Huber pair structure exists on C itself.
hypotheses: A complete noetherian Tate ring, or A with a noetherian ring of definition
C finite A-algebra; natural A-module topology; C⁺ = integral closure of ψ(A⁺)
proofSteps: Topological ring: C with the module topology is a topological ring because C is module-finite (Mathlib IsModuleTopology.isTopologicalRing); ψ is continuous (IsModuleTopology.continuous_of_linearMap on A → C).

Completeness, Hausdorffness and closedness of submodules: Huber 1994 Lemma 2.3(ii) (noetherian ring of definition) and Lemma 2.4(ii) (complete noetherian Tate); in Tau Ceti tauceti TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.t2Space_moduleTopology, TauCeti.completeSpace_moduleTopology, TauCeti.Huber.isClosed_of_isNoetherian.

Huber ring: choose A-module generators 1 = c₀, c₁, …, c_m of C with structure constants c_i c_j = Σ a_{ijk} c_k; after multiplying the c_i (i ≥ 1) by a power of a pseudo-uniformiser (resp. of an element of the ideal of definition) all a_{ijk} lie in a ring of definition A₀, and C₀ = Σ A₀ c_i is an open bounded subring with the I·C₀-adic topology.

Ring of integral elements: after replacing each cᵢ (i ≥ 1) by ϖcᵢ the structure constants lie in ϖA₀ ⊆ A°° ⊆ A⁺, so R = ψ(A⁺)[c₁,…,c_m] is a subring of C that is finite over ψ(A⁺), hence integral over ψ(A⁺), and open (it contains ψ(ϖA₀)-multiples of the generators, hence ϖ²C₀). R ⊆ C° (bounded generators, adic ψ). Its integral closure equals the integral closure C⁺ of ψ(A⁺), which is therefore a ring of integral elements by tauceti TauCeti.Huber.Pair.isRingOfIntegralElements_integralClosure (integral closure of an open subring contained in the power-bounded subring).
Finite morphism: A → C module-finite and A⁺ → C⁺ integral; topologically finite type by the Tate-case lemma (Zavyalov B.2.8) or directly from the surjection A⟨X₁..X_m⟩ → C, X_i ↦ c_i.
Universal property: an A-algebra map C → D is continuous (source has the module topology) and maps C⁺ into D⁺ because D⁺ is integrally closed in D and contains χ(A⁺).
Strong noetherianity: C is topologically of finite type over A, so Huber 1994 Corollary 3.4(ii) applies.

nodes.title: Finiteness from monic relations with topologically nilpotent values (Huber 1.4.3)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) be a morphism of complete Tate Huber pairs which is of topologically finite type, presented by a quotient mapping A⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩ → B with images t₁,…,tₙ ∈ B⁺. Then the morphism is finite (R0/finite-huber-pair-hom) if and only if for each i there is a monic polynomial pᵢ ∈ A⁺[X] such that pᵢ(tᵢ) is topologically nilpotent in B.
hypotheses: A, B complete Tate; the presentation has tᵢ ∈ B⁺
proofSteps: (⇒) If the morphism is finite, each tᵢ ∈ B⁺ is integral over A⁺, so a monic pᵢ with pᵢ(tᵢ) = 0 exists.

(⇐) Take the ring of definition B₀ = image of A₀⟨T⟩ (open by openness of the quotient map). The relations pᵢ(tᵢ) ∈ B°° imply that B₀/ϖB₀ is integral and of finite type, hence finite, over A₀/ϖA₀ after enlarging A₀ to contain the coefficients (as in Zavyalov B.2.9).
Lift finiteness from B₀/ϖB₀ to B₀ by successive approximation and ϖ-adic completeness of B₀ ([M, 28.P Lemma] as cited by Huber; the complete Nakayama argument of Zavyalov B.2.9).

Pass to B = B₀[1/ϖ] (module-finite over A) and B⁺ (integral over A⁺ since B⁺ ⊆ B° and B° is integral over the image of A⁰... via B⁺ ⊆ integral closure of A⁺ in B once tᵢ are integral), giving finiteness.
acceptance: For A = K, B = K⟨T⟩/(T² − ϖ) with t = T: p(X) = X² gives p(t) = ϖ topologically nilpotent, so B is finite over K (indeed of dimension 2).

nodes.title: Finite morphisms are proper (Huber 1.4.5(ii))
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a finite morphism of adic spaces (R0/finite-morphism) with Y analytic. Then f is proper (R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism). (Huber states 1.4.5(ii) for arbitrary adic spaces, deducing the specializing property from Huber–Knebusch [HK, 2.1.2, 2.1.6]; that general case is recorded as a gap.)

proofSteps: Finite ⇒ quasi-compact, and quasi-separated (preimages of affinoids are affinoid, hence quasi-compact quasi-separated spectral spaces; AdicSpaces anchor Layer 2).

Finite ⇒ of +weakly finite type: affinoid-locally B is topologically of finite type over A and B⁺ is the integral closure of A⁺, which equals the integral closure of A⁺[B°°] because B°° ⊆ B⁺ (R0/finite-huber-pair-hom, R0/finite-type-morphism-classes).

Existence and uniqueness of centres: let (x, A) ∈ X_v and y a centre of (x, A) on Y; y and f(x) lie in a common affinoid V = Spa(A', A'⁺) (opens are stable under generalisation) with f⁻¹(V) = Spa(B, B⁺) finite over V. The image of A'⁺ in k(x) lies in A (API 1.3.6 of R0/adic-valuation-rings-and-centres); B⁺ is integral over A'⁺ and valuation rings are integrally closed, so the image of B⁺ lies in A, giving a centre on f⁻¹(V), unique by 1.3.6.

nodes.title: Topological nilpotence in a fibre spreads to a rational neighbourhood (Huber 1.4.8)
nodes.statement: Let f: X = Spa(B, B⁺) → Y = Spa(A, A⁺) be a morphism of finite type between analytic affinoid adic spaces with A Tate, y ∈ Y, and κ(y) = (k(y)^∧, k(y)⁺^∧). Let b ∈ B be an element whose image in the completed fibre algebra B ⊗̂_A k(y)^∧ (the ring of global sections of X ×_Y Spa κ(y)) is topologically nilpotent. Then there is a rational subset U ⊆ Y containing y such that the image of b in O_X(f⁻¹(U)) = B ⊗̂_A O_Y(U) is topologically nilpotent.
hypotheses: X, Y analytic affinoid; A Tate
f of finite type
b topologically nilpotent in the fibre algebra
proofSteps: Write the image of b in B ⊗_A K (K = k(y)^∧) as s·(b₁ ⊗ e₁/d₁ + … + b_r ⊗ e_r/d_r) with s topologically nilpotent, bᵢ ∈ B⁺-multiples and eᵢ, dᵢ ∈ A with dᵢ(y) ≠ 0 (density of the image of A in K).
Let U₁ = ∩ᵢ R(1/dᵢ) ∩ ∩ⱼ R(pⱼ/1) be the rational subset (AdicSpaces anchor Layer 2) on which the eᵢ/dᵢ and the auxiliary elements pⱼ are power-bounded; U₁ contains y.
On U₁ the identity b = s·(bounded element) holds in B'' = B ⊗̂_A O_Y(U₁) (R0/completed-tensor-rational-localisation), so b is topologically nilpotent there.

nodes.title: Finiteness near a point with proper fibre (Huber 1.4.6-1.4.7)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of finite type between analytic affinoid adic spaces. For every y ∈ Y such that the fibre X ×_Y Spa κ(y) → Spa κ(y) is proper, there is an open neighbourhood U of y such that f⁻¹(U) → U is finite. In particular, if f is proper then f is finite (Huber 1.4.6).
hypotheses: X, Y analytic affinoid
f of finite type
the fibre over y is proper
proofSteps: Shrink Y to a rational neighbourhood of y with Tate coordinate ring (AdicSpaces anchor Layer 2: the analytic locus is covered by rational subsets with Tate rings). Let K = k(y)^∧ with plus ring K⁺ and pseudo-uniformiser ϖ, and C the fibre algebra B ⊗̂_A K (R0/affinoid-fibre-product, R0/completed-tensor-product) with ring of definition C₀.

The scheme morphism g: Spec(C₀/ϖC₀) → Spec(K⁺/ϖK⁺) is proper: properness of the adic fibre is transferred to g by the valuative criterion (Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper.eq_valuativeCriterion; the transfer is Huber's reference [Hu4, 3.12.5], recorded as a gap).
g is affine and proper, hence finite (Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.iff_isProper_and_isAffineHom; Huber cites EGA IV 18.12.8); by completeness C₀ is finite over K⁺ and K → C is finite.

Choose topological generators tᵢ ∈ B⁺ of B over A; their images in C satisfy monic equations over K⁺; approximate the coefficients by elements of A⁺-localisations near y so that the resulting monic pᵢ(tᵢ) are topologically nilpotent in the fibre; spread this to a rational neighbourhood U (R0/fibre-nilpotence-spreading) and conclude finiteness over U by R0/finiteness-criterion-monic-relations.
If f is proper, every fibre is proper (base change, R0/base-change-stability); cover Y by the neighbourhoods U and use locality of finiteness on the target (R0/finite-morphism).

nodes.title: Finiteness descends along finite faithfully flat affinoid covers (Huber 1.4.9)
nodes.statement: Let T = Spa(A, A⁺) be an analytic affinoid adic space with A Tate, h: T' → T a finite morphism such that O_{T'}(T') is faithfully flat over A, and f: S → T a morphism of adic spaces locally of finite type. If the base change S' = S ×_T T' → T' is finite, then f is finite.
hypotheses: T analytic affinoid with Tate ring
h finite with O(T') faithfully flat over O(T)
f locally of finite type (so S' exists, R0/fibre-products-existence (a))
proofSteps: S' → T' finite gives O_{S'}(S') = O_S(S) ⊗̂_A O(T') module-finite over O(T'); since O(T') is module-finite over A, the completed tensor product is the ordinary one (Zavyalov B.3.5-B.3.6 in the noetherian case; in general the natural-topology argument of B.3.4), and O_S(S) is module-finite over A by faithfully flat descent (Mathlib Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat; Huber cites EGA IV 2.7.1).

O_S(S) is complete (ring of sections), hence carries the natural A-module topology (Zavyalov B.3.4); with plus ring the integral closure of A⁺ it defines a finite adic space Z → T (R0/finite-huber-pair-hom, R0/finite-algebra-over-affinoid where A is noetherian).

The canonical S → Z becomes an isomorphism after base change to T'; since T' → T is surjective (faithful flatness) and finite, S → Z is a homeomorphism which is a topological embedding with bijective ring maps on affinoids, hence an isomorphism (Zavyalov B.4.10 for the strongly noetherian case).

nodes.title: Base change of a finite algebra over a complete Tate ring needs no completion
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) be a finite morphism of complete Tate Huber pairs (R0/finite-huber-pair-hom) and φ: A → C a continuous homomorphism to a complete Tate ring C. Give B ⊗_A C the tensor-product topology (the topology of R0/completed-tensor-product before completion). (i) This is the natural C-module topology of the finite C-module B ⊗_A C (Mathlib moduleTopology). (ii) If A and C are noetherian, or if B is a finite projective A-module, then B ⊗_A C is complete and Hausdorff, so the canonical map B ⊗_A C → B ⊗̂_A C to the completed tensor product (R0/completed-tensor-product) is an isomorphism of topological rings, and (C, C⁺) → (B ⊗_A C, integral closure of the image of C⁺ ⊗ B⁺) is a finite morphism of complete Huber pairs. (iii) Consequently, if A is strongly noetherian or B is a finite projective A-module, then for f₁, …, f_n, g ∈ A generating the unit ideal the map B ⊗_A A⟨f/g⟩ → B⟨φ(f)/φ(g)⟩ is an isomorphism of topological rings: the preimage of the rational subset V = R(f/g) under Spa(B, B⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) is the rational subset R(φ(f)/φ(g)), with ring B ⊗_A O(V). No claim is made that f⁻¹(Spa A) is affinoid for a finite morphism f of adic spaces over a non-noetherian sheafy Spa(A, A⁺) (Zavyalov, Remark B.2.19).
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) a finite morphism of complete Tate Huber pairs
C a complete Tate ring with a continuous A → C
in (ii)-(iii): A and C noetherian, or B finite projective over A
proofSteps: (i) Zavyalov, Lemma B.3.5: choose a ring of definition B₀ and a surjection Aⁿ → B mapping A₀ⁿ onto B₀ (the natural topology of B, R0/finite-huber-pair-hom); tensoring gives surjections Cⁿ → B ⊗_A C and C₀ⁿ → (B ⊗_A C)₀, so Cⁿ → B ⊗_A C is open and the tensor topology is the quotient topology, i.e. the natural C-module topology (Mathlib IsModuleTopology.isOpenQuotientMap_of_surjective).

(ii), noetherian case: B ⊗_A C is a finite module over the complete noetherian Tate ring C, complete for its natural topology (Tau Ceti TauCeti.completeSpace_moduleTopology) and Hausdorff (Tau Ceti TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.t2Space_moduleTopology); this is Huber 1994 Lemma 2.4(ii) as used in Zavyalov, Lemma B.3.6.

(ii), projective case: B ⊗_A C is a finite projective C-module (Mathlib Module.Projective.tensorProduct), hence a direct summand of Cⁿ via an idempotent e; with the natural topology it is the closed subgroup ker(1 − e) of the complete Hausdorff Cⁿ, so complete and Hausdorff (Kedlaya–Liu, Lemma 2.2.12(a)); completeness also follows from Tau Ceti TauCeti.completeSpace_moduleTopology.

The completed tensor product B ⊗̂_A C is the Hausdorff completion of B ⊗_A C with plus ring the integral closure of the image (R0/completed-tensor-product), so the completion map is an isomorphism; B ⊗_A C is module-finite over C (Mathlib Module.Finite.base_change) with integral plus ring, i.e. finite over (C, C⁺).

(iii) Take C = A⟨f/g⟩: rational localisation commutes with completed tensor products (R0/completed-tensor-rational-localisation), and by (ii) the completion is not needed; for A strongly noetherian, A⟨f/g⟩ is noetherian (Zavyalov, Corollary B.3.7).
acceptance: For A = ℚ_p⟨T⟩, B = A[S]/(S² − T) and V = {|T| ≤ |p|}, B ⊗_A A⟨T/p⟩ = ℚ_p⟨T/p⟩[S]/(S² − T) is already complete, and the preimage of V in Spa B is {|S²| ≤ |p|}.
The finiteness hypothesis cannot be dropped: for B = A⟨X⟩ (topologically of finite type, not finite) the tensor product A⟨X⟩ ⊗_A C is not complete in general and must be completed to C⟨X⟩.

nodes.title: Locally quasi-finite and quasi-finite morphisms of adic spaces
nodes.statement: A morphism f: X → Y of adic spaces is locally quasi-finite if it is locally of weakly finite type (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes) and for every y ∈ Y the fibre f⁻¹(y) is a discrete subspace of |X|; it is quasi-finite if moreover it is quasi-compact (Huber 1996, 1.5.1). Conventions: discreteness is of the fibre with the subspace topology of |X| (not of the fibre adic space X ×_Y Spa κ(y)); for f of weakly finite type between analytic adic spaces quasi-finite is equivalent to finiteness of all fibres (R0/quasi-finite-fibre-criteria).
hypotheses: f locally of weakly finite type
proofSteps: Definition as stated; QuasiFinite is the conjunction LocallyQuasiFinite ∧ QuasiCompact.
acceptance: Finite morphisms locally of weakly finite type are quasi-finite; open embeddings are locally quasi-finite; unramified morphisms are locally quasi-finite (R0/unramified-locally-quasi-finite).

nodes.title: Fibre criteria for quasi-finiteness (Huber 1.5.2)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of weakly finite type between analytic adic spaces. The following are equivalent: (a) f is quasi-finite; (b) f⁻¹(y) is finite for every y ∈ Y; (c) f⁻¹(y) is finite for every maximal point y ∈ Y; (d) k(x)^∧ is a finite extension of k(f(x))^∧ for every x ∈ X; (e) the same for every maximal point x ∈ X; (f) for every maximal point y of Y, X ×_Y Spa κ(y) → Spa κ(y) is finite. Conditions (a), (b), (d) are equivalent without the analyticity hypothesis.
hypotheses: f of weakly finite type (quasi-compact and locally of weakly finite type)
X, Y analytic for the equivalence with (c), (e), (f)
proofSteps: Reduce by base change to the fibre over Spa(K, K⁺), K = k(y)^∧ (fibre products and their points: R0/fibre-products-existence, R0/fibre-product-points; Huber (1.2.4)).

For a Tate ring A topologically of finite type over the affinoid field (K, K⁺) choose a finite injective K⟨T₁,…,T_d⟩ → A (Noether normalisation, R0/affinoid-noether-normalisation) and use integrality of A° over K°⟨T⟩ (R0/affinoid-power-bounded-integral); each condition reads as d = 0.
Maximal points: every point specialises from a unique maximal (rank-one) point, and fibres over non-maximal points embed into fibres over their maximal generalisations.
acceptance: For S ↦ T² on discs every fibre has at most two points and all residue field extensions have degree ≤ 2, so all six conditions hold.

nodes.title: Stalk criterion for local quasi-finiteness (Huber 1.5.4)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism locally of weakly finite type between analytic adic spaces. Then f is locally quasi-finite if and only if for every maximal point x ∈ X the local ring O_{X,x} is a finite O_{Y,f(x)}-module. If f is locally of finite type, this is further equivalent to: every maximal point x ∈ X has open neighbourhoods U ∋ x, V ⊇ f(U) with f|_U: U → V finite.
hypotheses: X, Y analytic
f locally of weakly finite type (resp. locally of finite type for the last equivalence)
proofSteps: For B topologically of finite type over A (affinoid pieces) and x maximal, use condition (f) of R0/quasi-finite-fibre-criteria and R0/finite-from-proper-fibre to get finiteness over a neighbourhood of f(x) of a neighbourhood of x (the fibre is finite, hence proper).
Identify O_{Y,y₀} ⊗ O_X(f⁻¹V) with the product of the stalks O_{X,x} over y₀ (finite morphisms: stalks of the pushforward), giving module-finiteness of the stalk.
For the +weakly finite type case pass through Z = Spa(B, B°) as in the source; the converse uses that a finite stalk has finitely many points over y₀.
acceptance: For S ↦ T² the stalk of the source at T = 0 is a free module of rank 2 over the stalk of the target at S = 0.

nodes.title: Quasi-finite and proper equals finite (Huber 1.5.5)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism locally of finite type between analytic adic spaces. Then f is finite (R0/finite-morphism) if and only if f is quasi-finite (R0/quasi-finite-morphism) and proper (R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism).
hypotheses: X, Y analytic adic spaces
f locally of finite type
properness in the sense of Huber 1.3.2 (+weakly finite type, separated, universally closed)
proofSteps: (finite ⇒ quasi-finite and proper) Proper: R0/finite-morphisms. Quasi-finite: finite morphisms are quasi-compact and, by (f) of R0/quasi-finite-fibre-criteria, have finite fibres (a finite algebra over an affinoid field has finitely many points).

(⇐) Fix y ∈ Y. Choose an affinoid V ∋ y and a finite faithfully flat affinoid cover h: W → V such that the residue fields of the points of Z = f⁻¹(V) ×_V W over a point w ∈ W over y are purely inseparable over k(w)^∧ (the source asserts that such W exists without reference; see gaps).

The generalisation sets Gᵢ of the finitely many points zᵢ of Z over w are pairwise disjoint and open-closed in g⁻¹(G): this uses uniqueness of centres (Huber 1.3.6, R0/adic-valuation-rings-and-centres) and separatedness (R0/valuative-criterion-separated).

Choose affinoid Kᵢ ⊆ Z around zᵢ and obtain finiteness of Kᵢ ∩ g⁻¹(Lᵢ) → Lᵢ from R0/finite-from-proper-fibre (the fibre is finite, hence proper) and (1.2.4) (R0/fibre-product-points); shrink to L with g⁻¹(L) ⊆ ∪Kᵢ; conclude finiteness over h⁻¹(U) for an affinoid U ∋ y.
Descend finiteness along h (R0/finiteness-faithfully-flat-descent); finiteness is local on the target (R0/finite-morphism).
acceptance: Concrete instance: Spa(K⟨T⟩) → Spa(K⟨S⟩), S ↦ T², is proper, quasi-finite and finite.

The rational embedding {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} ⊆ D is quasi-finite and not proper (not partially proper), hence not finite; the open unit disc B ⊆ D is locally quasi-finite and partially proper but not quasi-compact, hence not finite.

Public use: Zavyalov (Quotients, Proposition 5.3.1) replaces EGA IV 18.12.4 by this proposition to prove quotients by finite groups are finite; Mathlib's AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.iff_isProper_and_locallyQuasiFinite is the scheme analogue.

nodes.title: Partially proper locally quasi-finite morphisms are finite near closures of points (Huber 1.5.6)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism locally of finite type between analytic adic spaces, with X quasi-separated and Y quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then f is locally quasi-finite and partially proper if and only if every x ∈ X has open neighbourhoods U ⊇ closure{x} and V ⊇ closure{f(x)} with f(U) ⊆ V and f|_U: U → V finite.
hypotheses: X, Y analytic; X quasi-separated; Y quasi-compact quasi-separated
f locally of finite type
proofSteps: (⇒) By R0/partially-proper-closure-quasi-compact enclose closure{x₀} in a quasi-compact open W. Let S be the set of valuation rings of W with a centre on Y but none on f⁻¹(y₀) ∩ W; it is pro-constructible in W_v (R0/valuation-ring-space-spectral).

Using the valuative criterion (R0/separated-proper-partially-proper) find an open V ∋ y₀ with S(V) = ∅, so W ∩ f⁻¹(V) → V is proper; it is quasi-finite, hence finite by R0/quasi-finite-and-finiteness-criteria.

(⇐) Finite morphisms are locally quasi-finite and proper (R0/finite-morphisms); separatedness and universal specialization are local around closures of points and follow from the finite pieces via the valuative criterion.
acceptance: For the open embedding of the open unit disc B into the closed unit disc D (partially proper and locally quasi-finite) and x ∈ B with |T(x)| ≤ r < 1, the condition holds with U = V = {|T| ≤ r'} for any r < r' < 1 in |K^×|, which contains closure{x}.

This proposition is the input of Huber's Lemma 1.5.9 comparing rigid and adic partial properness for locally quasi-finite maps without discreteness of the valuation (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/proper-separated-comparisons).

nodes.title: Module of continuous differentials of a topologically finite type map
nodes.statement: Let φ: A → B be a continuous homomorphism of complete Huber rings (complete Hausdorff f-adic rings) which is topologically of finite type (tauceti TauCeti.Huber.IsTopologicallyFiniteType). Let m: B ⊗̂_A B → B be the continuous extension of b ⊗ b' ↦ bb' to the completed tensor product (R0/completed-tensor-product) and I = ker m. The module of continuous differentials is Ωᶜ_{B/A} := I/I², a B-module via (B ⊗̂_A B)/I ≅ B, with the natural B-module topology, and d = d_{B/A}: B → Ωᶜ_{B/A}, d(b) = class of 1 ⊗ b − b ⊗ 1 (Huber 1996, (1.6.2)). Properties: (a) for every finite N ⊆ B with A[N] dense in B, I is generated by the 1 ⊗ n − n ⊗ 1 (n ∈ N); hence Ωᶜ_{B/A} is a finitely generated B-module generated by d(N). (b) d is a continuous A-derivation and is universal: for every complete Hausdorff topological B-module M and every continuous A-derivation D: B → M there is a unique continuous B-linear u: Ωᶜ_{B/A} → M with u ∘ d = D. (c) If A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩_M → B is a quotient mapping with kernel 𝔞, then Ωᶜ_{B/A} ≅ (⊕ᵢ B dXᵢ)/(B-span of Σᵢ (∂P/∂Xᵢ) dXᵢ, P ∈ 𝔞), where ∂/∂Xᵢ are the termwise partial derivatives (which preserve A⟨X⟩_M); in particular Ωᶜ_{A⟨X⟩_M/A} is free with basis dX₁,…,dXₙ. (d) If B is a finite A-module, the canonical B-linear map Ω[B⁄A] → Ωᶜ_{B/A} from Mathlib's KaehlerDifferential (induced by d) is an isomorphism. Convention: when B is noetherian (B strongly noetherian Tate, or with a noetherian ring of definition) Ωᶜ_{B/A} is complete and Hausdorff; no Hausdorffness is asserted in general. The sheaf Ω_{X/Y} on an adic space is glued from these modules by the localisation compatibility (API) and belongs to the coherent-sheaf layer AdicSpacesPartII:R3 (see requests).
hypotheses: A → B continuous, topologically of finite type, between complete Huber rings
M ranges over complete Hausdorff topological B-modules in the universal property
proofSteps: B ⊗̂_A B and the continuous multiplication m exist by R0/completed-tensor-product and its universal property (R0/completed-tensor-product-universal-property).

(a) Density argument (Huber's proof of (1.6.2)(ii)): the ideal generated by 1 ⊗ n − n ⊗ 1 (n ∈ N) is dense in I and, being the kernel-type ideal of the algebraic case (Mathlib KaehlerDifferential.ideal, KaehlerDifferential.submodule_span_range_eq_ideal), is closed of finite type; hence equal to I.

(b) Derivation property as in the algebraic case (Mathlib KaehlerDifferential.D). Universality: for D continuous define B ⊗_A B → M, b ⊗ b' ↦ b·D(b'), extend by continuity to B ⊗̂_A B (M complete Hausdorff), restrict to I; it vanishes on I² and on 1 ⊗ a − a ⊗ 1 correctly, giving u; uniqueness since d(N) generates.

(c) For R = A⟨X⟩_M: polynomials are dense (AdicSpaces anchor Layer 0.4, Wedhorn 5.49), so a continuous derivation is determined by the values D(Xᵢ), and any values mᵢ ∈ M give the continuous derivation f ↦ Σ ∂f/∂Xᵢ·mᵢ (convergence from completeness of M); hence Ωᶜ_{R/A} is free on dXᵢ. For B = R/𝔞 a continuous derivation of B is one of R killing 𝔞, which gives the presentation (FK Corollary 5.1.11 in the formal case).

(d) For B module-finite over A, B ⊗_A B is a finite B-module with the natural topology (Zavyalov B.3.5) and complete when B is noetherian (Zavyalov B.3.6), so B ⊗̂_A B = B ⊗_A B and I/I² is the algebraic Ω[B⁄A] (Mathlib definition KaehlerDifferential = (ideal R S).Cotangent); the general finite case is Huber (1.6.2)(iii).
Hausdorffness in the noetherian case: every submodule of a finite module over a noetherian complete Huber ring is closed (Huber 1994 Lemmas 2.3-2.4; tauceti TauCeti.Huber.isClosed_of_isNoetherian).
acceptance: Ωᶜ_{K⟨T⟩/K} is free of rank 1 on dT, whereas Mathlib's Ω[K⟨T⟩⁄K] is not finitely generated.

nodes.title: First fundamental exact sequence of continuous differentials (Huber 1.6.3)
nodes.statement: Let A → B → C be continuous homomorphisms of complete Huber rings with B topologically of finite type over A and C topologically of finite type over B (so C is topologically of finite type over A, Huber 1994 Lemma 3.3(iv)). Then the sequence of C-modules C ⊗_B Ωᶜ_{B/A} → Ωᶜ_{C/A} → Ωᶜ_{C/B} → 0 is exact, the maps being induced by functoriality (R0/continuous-differentials).

nodes.title: Stalks of continuous differentials of locally quasi-finite morphisms (Huber 1.6.4(i))
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a locally quasi-finite morphism between analytic adic spaces (R0/quasi-finite-morphism) and x ∈ X a maximal point, y = f(x). Then O_{X,x} is a finite O_{Y,y}-algebra (R0/quasi-finite-stalk-criterion), and the stalk Ωᶜ_{X/Y,x} := colim Ωᶜ_{O_X(U)/O_Y(V)} (over affinoid neighbourhoods U ∋ x, V ⊇ f(U); well defined by the localisation compatibility of R0/continuous-differentials) is canonically isomorphic, compatibly with the derivations, to Mathlib's Ω[O_{X,x}⁄O_{Y,y}].
hypotheses: X, Y analytic
f locally quasi-finite
x maximal
proofSteps: Finiteness of the stalk and the identification O_{Y,y} ⊗_{O_Y(V)} O_X(f⁻¹V) ≅ ∏ O_{X,x'} over the points x' over y, as in the proof of Huber 1.5.4 (R0/quasi-finite-stalk-criterion), after shrinking to a neighbourhood where f is finite.

For finite A → B the continuous differentials are the algebraic ones (R0/continuous-differentials (d)); Kähler differentials commute with filtered colimits and localisation (Mathlib KaehlerDifferential.isLocalizedModule, tensorKaehlerEquiv), giving the stalk statement.

nodes.title: Flat morphism of adic spaces
nodes.statement: A morphism f: X → Y of adic spaces is flat if for every x ∈ X the local homomorphism of stalks O_{Y,f(x)} → O_{X,x} is flat (Mathlib Module.Flat) (Huber 1996, 1.7.5(b); Zavyalov, Quotients, Definition B.4.1). Stalks are colimits of rings, with no topology (AdicSpaces anchor, Layer 3.3). Conventions: flatness is stalkwise; for morphisms of strongly noetherian Tate affinoids it implies flatness of O_Y(Y) → O_X(X) (Zavyalov B.4.3), and for affinoids of topologically finite type over a nonarchimedean field the two are equivalent (Zavyalov B.4.3, B.4.6); in general the converse is not known (Zavyalov B.4.9) and is not asserted.
hypotheses: f: X → Y morphism of adic spaces
proofSteps: Definition as stated (stalk maps exist for morphisms of adic spaces: anchor Layer 3.3-3.4).
acceptance: Open embeddings are flat; the closed embedding of the origin into the closed disc is not.

nodes.title: Unramified morphism of adic spaces
nodes.statement: A morphism f: X → Y of adic spaces is unramified if it is locally of finite type (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes) and for every complete Huber pair A, every closed ideal I ⊆ A with I² = 0 and every morphism Spa A → Y, the restriction map Hom_Y(Spa A, X) → Hom_Y(Spa(A/I), X) is injective (Huber 1996, 1.6.5). Test objects: A ranges over complete Huber pairs (A, A⁺) (Tau Ceti Huber.Pair on complete Hausdorff rings), Spa A is the affinoid pre-adic space of the AdicSpaces anchor (Layer 3.4; A need not be sheafy), and morphisms Spa A → Y are morphisms of pre-adic spaces; I ⊆ A is a closed ideal with I² = 0 and A/I is the quotient Huber pair (tauceti Huber.Pair.quotient), whose plus ring is A⁺/I because I ⊆ A°° ⊆ A⁺. Huber allows non-complete affinoid rings and arbitrary square-zero I; since Spa A = Spa Â and the closure of a square-zero ideal is square-zero, restricting to complete A and closed I changes nothing. The morphism Spa(A/I) → Spa A is a homeomorphism.

nodes.title: Étale morphism of adic spaces
nodes.statement: A morphism f: X → Y of adic spaces is étale if it is locally of finite presentation (R0/locally-finite-presentation) and for every complete Huber pair A, every closed ideal I ⊆ A with I² = 0 and every morphism Spa A → Y, the restriction map Hom_Y(Spa A, X) → Hom_Y(Spa(A/I), X) is bijective (Huber 1996, 1.6.5). Equivalently, f is smooth (R0/smooth-morphism) and unramified (R0/unramified-morphism). Test objects: A ranges over complete Huber pairs (A, A⁺) (Tau Ceti Huber.Pair on complete Hausdorff rings), Spa A is the affinoid pre-adic space of the AdicSpaces anchor (Layer 3.4; A need not be sheafy), and morphisms Spa A → Y are morphisms of pre-adic spaces; I ⊆ A is a closed ideal with I² = 0 and A/I is the quotient Huber pair (tauceti Huber.Pair.quotient), whose plus ring is A⁺/I because I ⊆ A°° ⊆ A⁺. Huber allows non-complete affinoid rings and arbitrary square-zero I; since Spa A = Spa Â and the closure of a square-zero ideal is square-zero, restricting to complete A and closed I changes nothing. The morphism Spa(A/I) → Spa A is a homeomorphism. Conventions: this is Huber's infinitesimal definition; the Kedlaya–Liu and Scholze–Weinstein definition ('locally an open immersion followed by a finite étale map') agrees with it for analytic adic spaces by R0/etale-local-open-finite-etale-factorisation, and the algebraic notion Algebra.Etale of Mathlib applied to coordinate rings does not (a rational embedding is étale but its ring map is not of finite type).

Let n ∈ K^× (as an integer) and T^± denote the annulus Spa(K⟨T, T⁻¹⟩, K°⟨T, T⁻¹⟩). tests.name: Etale_test_rationalEmbedding
tests.statement: Notation: K complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial rank-one valuation, K° its valuation ring, ϖ a pseudo-uniformiser, D = Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩). nodes.title: Open embeddings are étale (Huber 1.6.7)
nodes.statement: Every open embedding j: U → X of adic spaces is étale (R0/differentials-unramified-smooth-etale).
hypotheses: j an open embedding (isomorphism onto an open adic subspace, AdicSpaces anchor Layer 5.1)
proofSteps: Locally of finite presentation: locally U is a rational subset of an affinoid Spa A with coordinate ring A⟨T/s⟩, which is topologically of finite type over A (Huber 1994 Corollary 3.4(i)); the finite presentation condition of R0/locally-finite-presentation only involves discrete bases, where rational localisations are localisations A[1/s], finitely presented.

Lifting: a Y-morphism Spa A → U is the same as a Y-morphism Spa A → X with image in U (universal property of open subspaces, anchor Layer 5.1). Given a Y-morphism ḡ: Spa(A/I) → U and the structure map Spa A → Y, which here is Y = X-with-j, the problem is: Hom_X(Spa A, U) → Hom_X(Spa(A/I), U), where Spa A → X is given. Both sets have at most one element (j is a monomorphism); the left one is nonempty iff the image of Spa A lies in U, and since Spa(A/I) → Spa A is a homeomorphism (I nilpotent, so every valuation kills I) this holds iff the image of Spa(A/I) lies in U. So the map is bijective.
acceptance: The rational embedding {|T| ≤ |p|} ⊆ Spa(Q_p⟨T⟩, Z_p⟨T⟩) is étale.

nodes.title: Relative polydiscs are smooth (Huber 1.6.7)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Huber pair and M₁,…,Mₙ finite subsets of A with each MᵢA open. Then the structure morphism Spa A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩_M → Spa A (Huber 1994, §3: plus ring the integral closure of the series with coefficients in M^ν·A⁺) is smooth (R0/smooth-morphism), of relative dimension n.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Huber pair
M_i finite with M_iA open
proofSteps: Locally of finite presentation: A → A⟨X⟩_M is of topologically finite type (definition); over a discrete A the ring A⟨X⟩_M is the polynomial ring A[X], of finite presentation (R0/locally-finite-presentation).

Lifting: morphisms Spa C → Spa A⟨X⟩_M over Spa A correspond to continuous A-homomorphisms A⟨X⟩_M → C, i.e. (universal property, Huber 1994 Lemma 3.5(i)) to tuples (c₁,…,cₙ) ∈ Cⁿ with m·cᵢ ∈ C⁺ for m ∈ Mᵢ (Hom into affinoid adic spaces: Huber 1994 Proposition 2.1, anchor Layer 5). Given (c̄ᵢ) for C/I, choose any lifts cᵢ ∈ C; then m·cᵢ ∈ C⁺ + I = C⁺ since I ⊆ C°° ⊆ C⁺. Hence the restriction map is surjective.

nodes.title: Cancellation for unramified, smooth and étale morphisms (Huber 1.6.7)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y and g: Y → Z be morphisms of adic spaces, locally of finite type. (i) If g ∘ f is unramified, then f is unramified. (ii) If g ∘ f is smooth (resp. étale) and g is unramified, then f is smooth (resp. étale).
hypotheses: f, g locally of finite type
proofSteps: Finiteness: if g ∘ f is locally of finite type (resp. finite presentation) then so is f (Huber 1994 Lemma 3.5(iv) for the affinoid ring maps; R0/locally-finite-presentation).
(i) Two Y-lifts Spa A → X of a Y-morphism Spa(A/I) → X are in particular Z-lifts, hence equal.

(ii) Given Spa A → Y and a Y-morphism Spa(A/I) → X, a Z-lift h: Spa A → X exists (g ∘ f smooth); the two Y-morphisms f ∘ h and the given Spa A → Y agree on Spa(A/I) and are Z-morphisms, so they are equal because g is unramified; hence h is a Y-lift. Uniqueness in the étale case follows from (i).
acceptance: If U → D is étale over D and D → Spa(K, K°) is smooth, the composite is smooth; conversely a morphism between étale D-spaces is étale.

nodes.title: Unramified, smooth and étale are local on the source (Huber 1.6.7)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of adic spaces and X = ⋃ᵢ Uᵢ an open cover. If each f|_{Uᵢ} is unramified (resp. étale, resp. smooth), then f is unramified (resp. étale, resp. smooth).
hypotheses: Open cover of the source
proofSteps: Finiteness conditions are local on the source by definition (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes, R0/locally-finite-presentation).

Unramified: two lifts g₁, g₂: Spa A → X agreeing on Spa(A/I) have the same underlying map (Spa(A/I) → Spa A is a homeomorphism); cover Spa A by rational subsets Wⱼ with images in some Uᵢ; the restrictions to Wⱼ = Spa(A_{Wⱼ}), a thickening of Spa(A_{Wⱼ}/I A_{Wⱼ}) with square-zero ideal, agree by unramifiedness of f|_{Uᵢ}; morphisms of pre-adic spaces agreeing on an open cover are equal.
Étale: local lifts on the Wⱼ exist and are unique, so they glue.

Smooth: local lifts exist; gluing them requires the scheme argument (the local lifts form a torsor under Hom(ḡ*Ω_{X/Y}, I), and one needs vanishing of the first Čech cohomology of the corresponding module on rational covers of the test object Spa A). For arbitrary complete Huber pairs A this vanishing is not available (Tate acyclicity for modules is proved only under noetherian hypotheses, Huber 1994 Theorem 2.5); this step is recorded as a gap.
acceptance: X = D covered by {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} and {|ϖ| ≤ |T|}: each piece is smooth over Spa(K, K°), and so is D.

nodes.title: Unramified morphisms are locally quasi-finite (Huber 1.7.4)
nodes.statement: Every unramified morphism of adic spaces is locally quasi-finite (R0/quasi-finite-morphism). In particular étale morphisms are locally quasi-finite.
hypotheses: f unramified
proofSteps: Locally on X, f factors as a closed embedding into an étale Y-space (R0/infinitesimal-criteria, condition (d)); closed embeddings have discrete (singleton) fibres, so it suffices to treat étale f with X, Y affinoid.

By R0/etale-local-structure, X ≅ Spa(B/I) with B = A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩_T and unit Jacobian; the fibre over y is Spa of (B/I) ⊗̂ κ(y), a complete affinoid κ(y)-algebra of topologically finite type presented by n equations in n variables with invertible Jacobian, hence finite over κ(y) (its module of differentials vanishes and it is noetherian of dimension 0), so the fibre is finite and discrete.
acceptance: The squaring map restricted to {|T| = 1} is étale with fibres of cardinality at most 2.

nodes.title: Characterisations of unramified morphisms (Huber 1.6.8)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of adic spaces locally of finite type. The following are equivalent: (a) f is unramified (R0/unramified-morphism); (b) Ω_{X/Y} = 0, i.e. Ωᶜ_{O_X(U)/O_Y(V)} = 0 for all affinoid opens U ⊆ X, V ⊆ Y with f(U) ⊆ V (equivalently, for the members of one such affinoid cover, by the localisation compatibility of R0/continuous-differentials); (c) the diagonal Δ_f: X → X ×_Y X is an open embedding; (d) every x ∈ X has an open neighbourhood U such that f|_U factors as a closed embedding U → Z followed by an étale morphism Z → Y.
hypotheses: f locally of finite type
proofSteps: (a) ⇒ (b): affinoid-locally, the two continuous A-homomorphisms B → (B ⊗̂_A B)/I², b ↦ b ⊗ 1 and b ↦ 1 ⊗ b, agree modulo the square-zero ideal I/I² (I = kernel of multiplication, R0/continuous-differentials); unramifiedness forces them to be equal, so d = 0 and Ωᶜ = I/I² = 0 (EGA IV 17.4.1 transported). The thickening Spa((B ⊗̂_A B)/I²) is a test object of Definition 1.6.5.

(b) ⇒ (a): two lifts Spa A → X of Spa(A/I) → X over Y differ by an A-derivation into I (since I² = 0), which factors through Ωᶜ = 0 by the universal property (b) of R0/continuous-differentials (I is complete Hausdorff as a closed ideal); hence they agree.

(b) ⇔ (c): the ideal I of the diagonal is finitely generated (R0/continuous-differentials (a)) and I = I² locally, so I is locally generated by an idempotent and the diagonal (a locally closed embedding, R0/diagonal-locally-closed) is locally open and closed; conversely an open diagonal has I = 0 near Δ(X).

(a) ⇒ (d): locally embed X as a closed subspace of a relative polydisc Z' = Spa A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩_M (definition of finite type); Ω_{X/Y} = 0 makes J/J² → Ω_{Z'/Y} ⊗ O_X surjective (R0/conormal-sequence); choose f₁,…,fₙ ∈ J whose differentials form a basis near x and let Z = V(f₁,…,fₙ), étale over Y near x by R0/jacobian-criterion-closed-subspace; X is closed in Z.

(d) ⇒ (a): closed embeddings and étale morphisms are unramified (R0/immersion-unramified, R0/differentials-unramified-smooth-etale) and composites of unramified morphisms are unramified (R0/etale-smooth-composition).
acceptance: The squaring map D → D (2 ∈ K^×) has Ωᶜ = K⟨T⟩/(2T)·dT, supported at the origin; it is unramified exactly on the complement of the origin.

Scheme analogue: Mathlib Algebra.FormallyUnramified (defined by Ω = 0) and Algebra.FormallyUnramified.iff_comp_injective; Mathlib instance Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isOpenImmersion_SpecMap_lmul (the diagonal of a formally unramified finite-type map is an open immersion).

nodes.title: Continuous differentials of a smooth morphism are locally free (Huber 1.6.9(i))
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a smooth morphism of adic spaces. Then Ω_{X/Y} is locally free of finite rank: every x ∈ X has affinoid neighbourhoods U ∋ x, V ⊇ f(U) such that Ωᶜ_{O_X(U)/O_Y(V)} is a finite free O_X(U)-module.
hypotheses: f smooth
proofSteps: Locally embed X as a closed subspace V(J) of a relative polydisc Z' = Spa C, C = A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩_M (f locally of finite presentation).

Smoothness of X gives a retraction of the square-zero thickening Spa(C/J²) ⊇ X over Y (lift id_X along X → Spa(C/J²), Definition 1.6.5), hence the conormal sequence J/J² → Ω_{C/A} ⊗ C/J → Ωᶜ_{X/Y} → 0 (R0/conormal-sequence) is split exact on the left (EGA IV 17.2.3 transported), so Ωᶜ_{X/Y} is a direct summand of the free module ⊕ C/J·dXᵢ (R0/continuous-differentials (c)), hence finite projective.

A finite projective module over O_X(U) is free on the members of a finite cover of Spec O_X(U) by basic opens D(gₖ) with (gₖ) = (1); the rational subsets {v : |ϖ|^N ≤ |gₖ|} (ϖ topologically nilpotent, N ≥ 1) cover the analytic space U (AdicSpaces anchor Layer 2) and Ωᶜ localises to them (localisation compatibility of R0/continuous-differentials).
acceptance: For D → Spa(K, K°) the module Ωᶜ is free of rank 1; for the node Spa(K⟨T₁,T₂⟩/(T₁T₂)) it is not locally free at the origin, so that space is not smooth.
Scheme analogue: Mathlib Algebra.FormallySmooth (Ω projective and H¹ of the cotangent complex zero).

nodes.title: Jacobian criterion for closed subspaces of smooth spaces (Huber 1.6.9(ii))
nodes.statement: Let g: Z → Y be a smooth morphism of adic spaces, X ⊆ Z a closed adic subspace with ideal sheaf J (R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings), and x ∈ X. Then X → Y is étale (resp. smooth) on an open neighbourhood of x if and only if there are sections g₁,…,g_r of J on a neighbourhood of x generating J there such that dg₁,…,dg_r form a basis (resp. part of a basis) of the free module Ω_{Z/Y} near x (R0/smooth-differentials-locally-free).
hypotheses: g smooth
X closed in Z, x ∈ X
proofSteps: (⇐) With generators whose differentials are (part of) a basis, the conormal map J/J² → Ω_{Z/Y} ⊗ O_X (R0/conormal-sequence) is split injective and its cokernel Ω_{X/Y} is free (resp. zero); lift morphisms from square-zero thickenings along the smooth Z (Definition 1.6.5) and correct the lift by a derivation to land in X, using the splitting (EGA IV 17.12.1 transported).

nodes.title: Differential criterion for étale and smooth morphisms between smooth spaces (Huber 1.6.9(iii))
nodes.statement: Let X and X' be smooth over Y and h: X → X' a Y-morphism, x ∈ X. Then h is étale on a neighbourhood of x if and only if the canonical map h*Ω_{X'/Y} → Ω_{X/Y} is bijective at x (on the stalk, equivalently after ⊗ k(x)); h is smooth on a neighbourhood of x if and only if this map is injective with a left inverse (split injective) near x.
hypotheses: X, X' smooth over Y
h a Y-morphism
proofSteps: Both sides are locally free (R0/smooth-differentials-locally-free); the map comes from the first fundamental sequence O_X ⊗ Ω_{X'/Y} → Ω_{X/Y} → Ω_{X/X'} → 0 (R0/first-fundamental-sequence).

(⇐) Bijectivity at x spreads to a neighbourhood (finite free modules, determinant a unit on a rational neighbourhood); then Ω_{X/X'} = 0, so h is unramified (R0/infinitesimal-criteria); h is locally of finite presentation (cancellation of finiteness, Huber 1994 Lemma 3.5(iv)); smoothness of h follows by lifting along X' and correcting with the split derivations (EGA IV 17.11.1-17.11.2 transported); étale = smooth + unramified.
(⇒) If h is étale then Ω_{X/X'} = 0 and the left exactness of the first fundamental sequence for smooth h (EGA IV 17.2.3 transported) gives bijectivity; the smooth case is analogous.

nodes.title: Finite étale adic spaces over a noetherian affinoid are finite étale algebras (Huber 1.6.6(ii))
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete strongly noetherian Tate Huber pair. The functor C ↦ Spa(Huber.Pair.finiteAlgebra C) (R0/finite-algebra-over-affinoid), from finite étale A-algebras (Mathlib Algebra.Etale A C with C a finite A-module) and A-algebra maps, to adic spaces X with a finite (R0/finite-morphism) and étale (R0/differentials-unramified-smooth-etale) morphism X → Spa(A, A⁺) and Spa(A, A⁺)-morphisms, is an equivalence of categories, with quasi-inverse X ↦ O_X(X). The plus ring of the adic space attached to C is the integral closure of A⁺ in C. (Huber states 1.6.6(ii) for noetherian complete f-adic A; the essential surjectivity beyond the strongly noetherian Tate case rests on [Hu4] and is recorded as a gap.)
hypotheses: A complete strongly noetherian Tate ring (the construction of R0/finite-algebra-over-affinoid and Zavyalov B.2.18 are available here)
proofSteps: Full faithfulness: Spa(A, A⁺)-morphisms Spa(C', C'⁺) → Spa(C, C⁺) are morphisms of Huber pairs (C, C⁺) → (C', C'⁺) over (A, A⁺) (Huber 1994 Proposition 2.1, anchor Layer 5; the spaces are adic since C, C' are strongly noetherian, Huber 1994 Theorem 2.2), which are the A-algebra maps C → C' (universal property of R0/finite-algebra-over-affinoid).

Algebraic étale ⇒ adic étale: Spa C → Spa A is finite, hence locally of finite type = locally of finite presentation over the analytic base; for the lifting, Y-morphisms Spa D → Spa C are A-algebra maps C → D (continuity and plus rings automatic), and Algebra.FormallyEtale A C gives bijectivity of Hom_A(C, D) → Hom_A(C, D/I) (Mathlib Algebra.FormallyEtale.iff_comp_bijective).

Finite and adic étale ⇒ algebraic étale: X = Spa(C, C⁺) with C finite over A (Zavyalov B.2.18); Ω_{X/Y} = 0 (R0/infinitesimal-criteria) and Ωᶜ = Ω[C⁄A] for finite C (R0/continuous-differentials (d)), so C is formally unramified; A → C is flat (R0/etale-flat-unramified and R0/etale-ring-flatness, or Zavyalov B.4.3); C is finitely presented (finite over noetherian); hence Algebra.Etale A C (Mathlib Algebra.Etale.of_formallyUnramified_of_flat).
acceptance: For A = K a complete nonarchimedean field: finite étale adic spaces over Spa(K, K°) are the finite disjoint unions of Spa(L, L°) for L/K finite separable (Mathlib Algebra.Etale.iff_exists_algEquiv_prod over a field).

Kedlaya–Liu, Lemma 8.2.17(a): for adic Banach rings, finite étale morphisms to Spa(A, A⁺) (in their ad hoc sense) ≃ FÉt(A); this node identifies Huber's finite étale morphisms with the same category in the strongly noetherian case.

nodes.title: Morphisms of Huber pairs of algebraically finite type
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair (not necessarily complete). For finite subsets M₁,…,Mₙ ⊆ A with each MᵢA open, let A[X₁,…,Xₙ]_M be the polynomial ring A[X] with the subspace topology of A⟨X⟩_M (Huber 1994, §3; for Tate A and Mᵢ = {1} the Gauss-norm topology) and plus ring the integral closure of A⁺[m·Xᵢ : m ∈ Mᵢ, 1 ≤ i ≤ n]. A morphism of Huber pairs φ: (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) is of algebraically finite type if it factors through a quotient mapping A[X₁,…,Xₙ]_M → B, i.e. a surjective, continuous, open ring homomorphism with B⁺ the integral closure of the image of the plus ring. This is the polynomial analogue of Huber's topologically finite type and the affinoid-ring notion behind Huber 1996, Corollary 1.7.3(iii) and Remark 1.2.6; the completion of such a φ is topologically of finite type, and Spa B = Spa B̂.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) Huber pair, completeness not required
Mᵢ finite with MᵢA open
proofSteps: Definition as stated; the topology of A[X]_M is the one induced from A⟨X⟩_M (Huber 1994, p. 533).

Completion: the completion of A[X]_M is A⟨X⟩_M (Huber 1994, §3; anchor Layer 0.4, Wedhorn 5.49 density of polynomials), and completion preserves quotient mappings, so φ̂ is topologically of finite type.
acceptance: For the p-adic Huber pair (W(κ)[1/p][T^{±1}], W(κ)[T^{±1}]) → (R₀, R₀⁺) of Scholze 2013 Lemma 6.12, (R₀, R₀⁺) is of algebraically finite type and its completion is the étale affinoid (R, R⁺).

nodes.title: Standard étale presentation of étale affinoid maps (Huber 1.7.1)
nodes.statement: Let A = (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair (not necessarily complete) and s: X → Y = Spa A a morphism of adic spaces with X affinoid. The following are equivalent: (i) s is étale (R0/differentials-unramified-smooth-etale); (ii) there are n ≥ 0, finite subsets T₁,…,Tₙ ⊆ A with each TᵢA open, and f₁,…,fₙ ∈ B := A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩_{T₁,…,Tₙ} such that, with I = (f₁,…,fₙ) ⊆ B, the image of det(∂fᵢ/∂Xⱼ) in B/I is a unit and X is Y-isomorphic to Spa(B/I); (iii) the same with f₁,…,fₙ ∈ A[X₁,…,Xₙ]. Here B/I is the quotient Huber pair (plus ring the integral closure of the image), and Spa(B/I) is Spa of its completion. The number of equations equals the number of variables.
hypotheses: X affinoid, Y = Spa A affinoid (A not necessarily complete)
proofSteps: (i) ⇒ (ii): the affinoid ring map of an affinoid morphism locally of finite type is of topologically finite type (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes), so X ≅ Spa(C/J) with C = A⟨X₁,…,X_m⟩_T; since X is étale, Ω_{X/Y} = 0 and J/J² ≅ Ω_{C/A} ⊗ C/J (R0/conormal-sequence, R0/infinitesimal-criteria, R0/jacobian-criterion-closed-subspace), a free module on the dXᵢ (R0/continuous-differentials (c)). Choose f₁,…,f_m ∈ J whose classes form a basis of J/J²; then J = (f₁,…,f_m) + J² gives j ∈ J with (1 + j)J ⊆ (f₁,…,f_m) (J finitely generated); invert 1 + j by a rational localisation (X ⊆ {1 + j invertible}; R0/open-embedding-etale) presented by an extra variable X_{m+1} with f_{m+1} = 1 − (1 + j)X_{m+1}; the Jacobian of (f₁,…,f_{m+1}) is a unit on X.

(ii) ⇒ (iii): Huber's preparatory points: (1) an inverse-function statement for convergent power series with unit linear part over an f-adic ring ([B, III.4.4 Proposition 5]); (2) perturbation of the values of a continuous A-algebra map A⟨X⟩_T → B; (3) small perturbations of topological generators define automorphisms (using a noetherian ring of definition or discreteness); (4) rational subsets of Spa A⟨X⟩_T are preserved by nearby morphisms (AdicSpaces anchor Layer 2, Wedhorn Proposition 7.34). Replace fᵢ by nearby polynomials fᵢ + sᵢ (polynomials are dense, anchor Layer 0.4) and show Spa(B/I') ≅ Spa(B/I) inside U = {v(sᵢ) ≤ v(Δ) ≠ 0}, Δ the Jacobian (R0/etale-presentation-perturbation). The exact statements of (1)-(3) are recorded as a gap.

(iii) ⇒ (i): Spa B → Y is smooth (R0/restricted-power-series-smooth); Spa(B/I) is a closed subspace cut out by f₁,…,fₙ whose differentials form a basis of Ωᶜ_{B/A} ⊗ B/I (unit Jacobian), hence étale over Y (R0/jacobian-criterion-closed-subspace); isomorphisms and open embeddings are étale (R0/open-embedding-etale).
acceptance: Tate case: over a Tate A all Tᵢ can be taken {1}, so X ≅ Spa(A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩/(f₁,…,fₙ)) with unit Jacobian (R0/etale-presentation-perturbation).
Instance: for n ∈ K^×, the Kummer cover of the annulus is Spa(K⟨S^{±1}⟩⟨T⟩/(Tⁿ − S)) with Jacobian nTⁿ⁻¹ a unit.

nodes.statement: Let A be a Huber pair, B = A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩_{T₁,…,Tₙ} and f₁,…,fₙ ∈ B such that det(∂fᵢ/∂Xⱼ) is a unit in B/(f₁,…,fₙ). nodes.title: Algebraic models of affinoid étale maps (Huber 1.7.3(iii))
nodes.statement: Let A = (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair (not necessarily complete) and Y → Spa A a morphism with Y affinoid. Then Y → Spa A is étale if and only if Y is Spa A-isomorphic to Spa B for a morphism of Huber pairs A → B of algebraically finite type (R0/algebraically-finite-type-ring-map) whose underlying ring map A → B is étale (Mathlib Algebra.Etale).
hypotheses: Y affinoid; A need not be complete (e.g. the p-adic pair (W(κ)[1/p][T^{±1}], W(κ)[T^{±1}]))
proofSteps: (⇒) By R0/etale-local-structure (iii), Y ≅ Spa(B'/I) with B' = A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩_T and f₁,…,fₙ ∈ A[X] with Jacobian Δ a unit on Y. Let B = A[X₁,…,Xₙ, X_{n+1}]/(f₁,…,fₙ, 1 − ΔX_{n+1}) with weights T and, for X_{n+1}, a finite set T_{n+1} with T_{n+1}·Δ⁻¹ power-bounded on Y. Then A → B has a submersive presentation of relative dimension 0 (Jacobian −Δ·det(∂f/∂X) invertible), so Algebra.Etale A B (Mathlib Algebra.Etale.iff_isStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension_zero), A → B is of algebraically finite type, and Spa B ≅ Y (completion, R0/algebraically-finite-type-ring-map).

(⇐) If A → B is algebraically étale, it has a global submersive presentation of relative dimension 0 (Mathlib Algebra.Etale.iff_isStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension_zero); after completion this is a presentation as in R0/etale-local-structure (ii) (weights chosen from the algebraically finite type structure), so Spa B → Spa A is étale.

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms are locally étale over relative polydiscs (Huber 1.6.10)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair and f: X → Spa A a morphism of adic spaces. Then f is smooth if and only if every x ∈ X has an open neighbourhood U for which there are n ≥ 0, finite subsets M₁,…,Mₙ ⊆ A with each MᵢA open, and an étale morphism g: U → Spa A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩_M with f|_U equal to the composite of g and the structure morphism (Huber's diagram (*)). If A is Tate and f is smooth, one can take M₁ = … = Mₙ = {1}, i.e. g: U → Spa A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩ étale.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) Huber pair; Tate for the simplified form
proofSteps: (⇒) Ω_{X/Spa A} is locally free (R0/smooth-differentials-locally-free); choose sᵢ ∈ O_X(U) with dsᵢ a basis near x, and finite Mᵢ with Mᵢ·sᵢ ⊆ O_X⁺(U) (if A is Tate, replace sᵢ by ϖ^k sᵢ, which keeps dsᵢ a basis, so Mᵢ = {1} suffices).

Define g by the universal property of A⟨X⟩_M (Huber 1994 Lemma 3.5(i)), Xᵢ ↦ sᵢ; g*Ω of the polydisc (free on dXᵢ, R0/continuous-differentials (c)) → Ω_{U/Spa A} is bijective near x, so g is étale near x (R0/differential-criterion-morphism; the polydisc is smooth, R0/restricted-power-series-smooth).

(⇐) The polydisc is smooth (R0/restricted-power-series-smooth), composites are smooth (R0/etale-smooth-composition) and smoothness is local on the source (R0/etale-smooth-locality; see the gap recorded there).

nodes.title: Étale morphisms of affinoids over a field embed locally into finite étale covers (de Jong–van der Put 3.1.4)
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field with a nontrivial rank-one valuation and f: Y → X an étale morphism (R0/differentials-unramified-smooth-etale) of affinoid adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°), X = Spa(A, A°) and Y = Spa(B, B°) with A, B K-affinoid algebras. (i) For every rank-one point a ∈ X there are a rational subset U ⊆ X containing the closure of {a}, a K-affinoid algebra C that is finite étale over O_X(U) (so that g: Z = Spa(C, C°) → U is finite and étale, R0/finite-etale-algebra-comparison) and an open embedding h: f⁻¹(U) → Z with f|_{f⁻¹(U)} = g ∘ h. (ii) Consequently X is covered by finitely many such rational subsets U_1, …, U_m, and each f⁻¹(U_j) is covered by finitely many subsets T' that are rational in Y and (via h_j) in Z_j; on each T' the morphism f is the composite of a rational embedding T' ⊆ Z_j, the finite étale Z_j → U_j and the rational embedding U_j ⊆ X.
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially rank-one valued
X, Y affinoid and locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°)
f étale
proofSteps: Dictionary: A, B are strongly noetherian, so f is étale if and only if A → B is flat and unramified with Ω_{B/A} = 0 (R0/etale-flat-unramified, R0/etale-ring-flatness), which is de Jong–van der Put's notion (their Observation 3.1.1). Their analytic points of Sp A are the rank-one points of X (continuous multiplicative seminorms), a wide neighbourhood of a is a rational U whose defining functions have |f_i|_a < 1, which contains the closure of {a}, and the Berkovich space M(X) of rank-one points is compact.

Reduction (proof of dJvdP 3.1.4): every point of X is a specialisation of a rank-one point (anchor Layer 2), and rational subsets containing the closure of a point contain its specialisations; by compactness of M(X) finitely many wide neighbourhoods cover X, so (ii) follows from (i).

Fibre: f is unramified, so its fibres are finite (R0/unramified-locally-quasi-finite); by dJvdP Lemma 3.1.6 a wide neighbourhood of a splits f⁻¹ according to the points b over a, and it suffices to treat one b, whose completed residue field F_b is finite separable over F_a (dJvdP Observation 3.1.3).

Finite étale cover: by dJvdP Lemma 2.1.1 and Remark 2.1.2 (henselian local rings at analytic points) there are a wide neighbourhood U of a and a finite étale V = Spa(C, C°) → U with one point v over a and F_v ≅ F_b (R0/finite-algebra-over-affinoid, R0/finite-etale-algebra-comparison).

Open embedding: the projection Y ×_X V → V is étale (Y ×_X V = Spa(B ⊗_A C), R0/finite-algebra-tensor-complete, R0/affinoid-fibre-product) with a point c over (b, v) such that F_c = F_v; by dJvdP Lemma 3.1.5 a wide neighbourhood of c maps isomorphically onto an open affinoid subdomain of V, and the other projection is finite étale onto f⁻¹(U). Shrinking U (Lemma 3.1.6) identifies f⁻¹(U) with an open subspace of V: this is h, with Z = V.

Rational refinements: every quasi-compact open subset of an affinoid adic space is a finite union of rational subsets, and a rational subset of a rational subset is rational (anchor Layer 2); a rational subset of Z contained in the affinoid h(f⁻¹(U)) is rational there, hence in Y.
acceptance: The Kummer map f: Y = {|T| = 1} → X = {|T| = 1}, T ↦ Tⁿ, on the unit circle over K of characteristic prime to n is finite étale; (i) holds with U = X, Z = Y, h = id.
The rational embedding Y = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} ⊆ X = Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) is étale and not finite; (i) holds with Z = U = X and h the inclusion, so the finite étale factor can be trivial.

nodes.title: Étale maps are locally open embeddings into finite étale covers (Huber 2.2.8)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of locally noetherian analytic adic spaces (R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space). Then f is étale (R0/differentials-unramified-smooth-etale) if and only if for every x ∈ X there are open subspaces U ∋ x of X and V ⊇ f(U) of Y, an adic space W, an open embedding U → W and a finite (R0/finite-morphism) étale morphism W → V such that f|_U: U → V is the composite. (This is the characterisation of étale maps used as a definition by Kedlaya–Liu, Definition 8.2.16, and for perfectoid spaces by Scholze–Weinstein, Definition 7.5.1; Scholze 2013 uses the refinement that, for f quasi-compact and y ∈ Y, W can be taken over a rational neighbourhood of the closure of y.)
hypotheses: X, Y locally noetherian analytic adic spaces (Huber's Lemma 2.2.8 is not public; its exact hypotheses are recorded as a gap)
proofSteps: (⇐) Open embeddings and finite étale maps are étale (R0/open-embedding-etale), composites of étale maps are étale (R0/etale-smooth-composition), and étaleness is local on the source (R0/etale-smooth-locality).

(⇒) for X and Y locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°), K a complete nonarchimedean field: cover Y by affinoid opens mapping into affinoid opens of X and apply AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-affinoid-finite-etale-embedding (de Jong–van der Put, Proposition 3.1.4) to each, which gives U, W = Z_j and V = U_j.

(⇒) for general locally noetherian analytic X and Y this direction is Huber 1996, Lemma 2.2.8, which is not public and not in the reviewed decomposition; its statement is known here through Scholze–Weinstein (Berkeley Lecture 7), Kedlaya–Liu (§8.2) and Scholze 2013 (§5). It is recorded as a gap, and no proof is claimed in this blueprint.

nodes.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field, V an affinoid adic space smooth over Spa(K, K°), and x ∈ V with closure M = closure{x} ⊆ V. Then there is a rational subset U ⊆ V containing M together with an étale morphism U → Tⁿ = Spa(K⟨T₁^{±1},…,Tₙ^{±1}⟩, K°⟨T₁^{±1},…,Tₙ^{±1}⟩) which factors as a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps.

V affinoid, smooth over Spa(K, K°)
proofSteps: M is the intersection of the rational subsets of V containing it (for a point of an affinoid adic space; Huber 1.5.10 in the analytic Tate case).

nodes.title: Étale equals flat and unramified for analytic adic spaces (Huber 1.7.5)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism locally of finite type between analytic adic spaces. The following are equivalent: (a) f is étale; (b) f is flat (R0/flat-morphism) and unramified (R0/unramified-morphism); (c) for every maximal point x ∈ X, O_{X,x} is flat over O_{Y,f(x)} and O_{X,x}/𝔪_{f(x)}O_{X,x} is a finite separable field extension of the residue field of O_{Y,f(x)}.
hypotheses: X, Y analytic
f locally of finite type
proofSteps: (a) ⇒ (c): f is locally quasi-finite (R0/unramified-locally-quasi-finite), so at a maximal x the stalk O_{X,x} is finite over O_{Y,f(x)} (R0/quasi-finite-stalk-criterion) and is a localisation of the finite algebra given near x by the standard presentation (R0/etale-local-structure), which is algebraically étale (submersive presentation of relative dimension 0); étale local algebras are flat with finite separable fibres.

(c) ⇒ (b): flatness at maximal points spreads to all points (every point specialises from a maximal point, and stalks at specialisations map to stalks at generalisations; Huber's argument via 1.5.2); the fibre condition and Nakayama give Ωᶜ_{X/Y,x} = 0 at maximal points (R0/quasi-finite-stalk-differentials), hence Ω_{X/Y} = 0 near every point, so f is unramified (R0/infinitesimal-criteria).

(b) ⇒ (a): locally f = g ∘ i with i a closed embedding into an étale Z → Y (R0/infinitesimal-criteria (d)); i is flat, by the graph argument using that the diagonal of the unramified Z → Y is an open embedding (Huber's proof, recorded in the reviewed decomposition); a flat closed embedding cut out by a finitely generated ideal is locally an open embedding (the ideal is stalkwise generated by an idempotent; Stacks 04PW for the scheme case), hence f is locally an open embedding followed by an étale map and so étale (R0/open-embedding-etale, R0/etale-smooth-composition).
acceptance: The closed embedding of the origin into D is unramified but not flat, hence not étale; the Frobenius S ↦ T^p in characteristic p is flat but not unramified, hence not étale.

nodes.title: Flatness of the ring map of an étale affinoid morphism (Huber 1.7.6)
nodes.statement: Let s: X → Y be an étale morphism between affinoid adic spaces, Y = Spa(A, A⁺) with A complete, and assume that A has a noetherian ring of definition or that A is a strongly noetherian Tate ring. Then O_Y(Y) → O_X(X) is flat.
hypotheses: Y affinoid with A having a noetherian ring of definition, or A strongly noetherian Tate (the only two cases proved in the source)
proofSteps: Case (i), noetherian ring of definition: by R0/etale-local-structure, O_X(X) is the completion of an algebraically étale A-algebra C_Δ; B is flat over A[X] ([Hu1, 1.7.i], completion of noetherian adic rings), and C_Δ is étale over A, hence flat.

Case (ii), strongly noetherian Tate: reduce to n = 1, show that pA⟨X⟩ is prime for the relevant p, and use that torsion-free modules over localisations of Dedekind rings are flat (as in Huber's proof).
acceptance: For A = K a field every module is flat; for the rational embedding {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} ⊆ D, K⟨T⟩ → K⟨T, T/ϖ⟩ is flat (also tauceti TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.flat_toCompletionLoc for rational localisations).

nodes.title: The affine chart of X ×_Y S: the increasing union of the affinoids Spa(A_k, A_k⁺) and its universal property on affinoid test objects
nodes.statement: Let λ: B → A be a ring homomorphism, where (A, A⁺) is a complete Huber pair such that A has a noetherian ring of definition or is a strongly noetherian Tate ring, and let C = B[T₁,…,Tₙ]/I be a finitely generated B-algebra. Choose a finite set E of topologically nilpotent elements of A with E·A open, and put E(k) = {e₁⋯e_k : eᵢ ∈ E} for k ≥ 1. Let A(k) = A⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩_{E(k),…,E(k)} be Huber's restricted power-series ring with weights E(k) (the separated completion of the weighted restricted series ring, with plus ring the integral closure of the series whose ν-th coefficient lies in E(k)^{|ν|}·A⁺), let λ_k: B[T] → A(k) extend λ by Tᵢ ↦ Tᵢ, let A_k = A(k)/λ_k(I)·A(k) with the quotient topology, A_k⁺ the integral closure in A_k of the image of A(k)⁺, and R_k = Spa(A_k, A_k⁺). Then: (i) A_k is complete, has a noetherian ring of definition or is strongly noetherian Tate, and R_k is an affinoid adic space satisfying Huber's condition; (ii) for k ≤ h the continuous A-algebra map A_h → A_k with Tᵢ ↦ Tᵢ induces an isomorphism of R_k onto the rational subset {x ∈ R_h : |e·Tᵢ|_x ≤ 1 for all e ∈ E(k), i = 1,…,n} of R_h; (iii) the adic space R = ⋃_k R_k (increasing union along (ii)), with p: R → Spa(A, A⁺) and the morphism of locally ringed spaces q: R_ → Spec C induced by the ring maps C → A_k, satisfies: for every complete affinoid adic space U = Spa(D, D⁺) over Spa(A, A⁺) (structure map given by μ: A → D), the map w ↦ q ∘ w_ is a bijection from Hom_{Spa(A,A⁺)}(U, R) to the set of B-algebra homomorphisms C → D (B acting on D through μ∘λ), equivalently to Hom_{LRS/Spec B}(U_, Spec C). For a Tate ring A with pseudo-uniformizer ϖ one may take E = {ϖ}, so A(k) = A⟨ϖ^k T₁,…,ϖ^k Tₙ⟩ (the relative closed polydisc of radius |ϖ|^{-k}).
hypotheses: A complete with a noetherian ring of definition, or A a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring (Huber 1994 3.8 hypotheses at an affinoid chart)
E finite, consisting of topologically nilpotent elements, with E·A open; the result does not depend on E (by the universal property)
test objects in (iii) are affinoid adic spaces Spa(D, D⁺) with D complete; the general test object is handled in AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification by gluing
proofSteps: (i): A(k) is of topologically finite type over A; quotients and weighted restricted-series rings over A again have a noetherian ring of definition or are strongly noetherian Tate (Huber 1994 Cor 3.4(ii),(iii); AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-noetherian-stability; anchor Layer 0.5 for stability of strong noetherianness); ideals of such rings are closed, so A_k is complete; sheafiness of (A_k, A_k⁺) is the anchor's Layer 4 (strongly noetherian Tate) or Huber 1994 Thm 2.2.

(ii): the map A_h → A_k and the rational localisation of (A_h, A_h⁺) at {|e·Tᵢ| ≤ 1} satisfy the same universal property: a continuous map from A_h to a complete Huber pair extends through A_k exactly when the images of e·Tᵢ (e ∈ E(k)) are power-bounded and lie in the plus ring (weighted universal property tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_completion_weightedRestrictedSubring; rational-localisation universal property tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset).

(iii) existence: given a B-algebra map φ: C → D, let dᵢ = φ(Tᵢ). Since E is finite and consists of topologically nilpotent elements, E(k) tends to 0, so for k large e·dᵢ ∈ D⁺ for all e ∈ E(k) (D⁺ is open). The weighted universal property (Huber 1994 Lemma 3.5(i); ring-level form tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_completion_weightedRestrictedSubring) gives a continuous A-algebra map A(k) → D with Tᵢ ↦ dᵢ carrying A(k)⁺ into D⁺; it kills λ_k(I) because φ is a B-algebra map, so it factors through the quotient mapping A(k) → A_k, and A_k⁺ maps into D⁺ because D⁺ is integrally closed. This gives U → R_k ⊆ R.

(iii) uniqueness: U is quasi-compact (anchor Layer 2: Spa is spectral), so any morphism U → R lands in some R_k; morphisms Spa(D,D⁺) → R_k over Spa(A,A⁺) are continuous A-algebra maps (A_k, A_k⁺) → (D, D⁺) (full faithfulness of Spa on complete sheafy pairs, anchor Layers 3–5), which are determined by the images of the Tᵢ (uniqueness in the weighted universal property); compatibility in k is (ii).

The identification with Hom_{LRS/Spec B}(U_, Spec C) is the Γ–Spec adjunction for locally ringed spaces (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.ΓSpec.locallyRingedSpaceAdjunction; Stacks 01I1) together with O_U(U) = D (anchor Layer 3.5).
acceptance: A = K complete rank-one field, E = {ϖ}, B = K, C = K[T]: A_k = K⟨ϖ^k T⟩, A_k⁺ = K°⟨ϖ^k T⟩, R_k is the closed disc of radius |ϖ|^{-k}, and R_k ⊆ R_{k+1} is the rational subset {|ϖ^k T| ≤ 1} (Hübner Example 4.3).
For D = K and φ(T) = ϖ^{-3}, the map Spa(K,K°) → R factors through R_3 but not through R_2.

nodes.title: Huber's fibre product X ×_Y S of a scheme locally of finite type with an adic space over a scheme
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type, S an adic space satisfying Huber's condition (every point has an open affinoid neighbourhood Spa(A, A⁺) with A having a noetherian ring of definition or A a strongly noetherian Tate ring; AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space), and g: S_ → Y a morphism of locally ringed spaces, where S_ = (|S|, O_S) is the underlying locally ringed space of S (forgetting the topology of O_S and the valuations). Then there are an adic space R = X ×_Y S, a morphism of adic spaces p: R → S and a morphism of locally ringed spaces q: R_ → X with g ∘ p_ = f ∘ q, such that for every adic space U, every morphism of adic spaces u: U → S and every morphism of locally ringed spaces v: U_ → X with g ∘ u_ = f ∘ v there is a unique morphism of adic spaces w: U → R with p ∘ w = u and q ∘ w_ = v. The morphism p is locally of finite type (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-type-morphism-classes) and R satisfies Huber's condition. Over an affine open Spec B ⊆ Y, an affine open Spec C ⊆ f⁻¹(Spec B) with C = B[T₁,…,Tₙ]/I and an open affinoid Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ g⁻¹(Spec B), the open subspace p⁻¹(Spa(A,A⁺)) ∩ q⁻¹(Spec C) of R is the increasing union ⋃_k Spa(A_k, A_k⁺) of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affine-chart-analytification. A Y-morphism h: X₁ → X₂ of Y-schemes locally of finite type induces h_S: X₁ ×_Y S → X₂ ×_Y S; this is functorial, and the triple (R, p, q) is unique up to unique isomorphism, so the construction is independent of the charts, presentations and sets E chosen.
hypotheses: f: X → Y a morphism of schemes, locally of finite type
S satisfies Huber's condition (Huber 1994 3.8); Wedhorn 8.61 and Hübner 10.2 give the same construction for stable (stably sheafy) adic spaces S
g: S_ → Y is a morphism of locally ringed spaces; no topology on O_Y enters
proofSteps: Localisation on the source of test morphisms: morphisms of adic spaces glue along open covers (anchor Layer 5), so the universal property may be checked on affinoid test objects U = Spa(D, D⁺) with D complete.

Affine–affinoid case: AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affine-chart-analytification gives (R, p, q) with the universal property for affinoid U; for general U cover U by affinoids and glue the unique morphisms (uniqueness forces agreement on overlaps).

Localisation on X, Y and S: if (R, p, q) has the universal property for X → Y and S, then for Zariski opens X' ⊆ X, Y' ⊆ Y with f(X') ⊆ Y' and an open S' ⊆ S ∩ g⁻¹(Y'), the open subspace p⁻¹(S') ∩ q⁻¹(X') has it for X' → Y' and S', because a morphism into R factors through an open subspace iff its underlying map does, and open immersions of schemes are monomorphisms of locally ringed spaces (Stacks 01JN, 01I4).

Gluing: cover Y by affine opens Spec B, f⁻¹(Spec B) by affine opens Spec C, and g⁻¹(Spec B) by open affinoids of the kind in Huber's condition; glue the affine–affinoid pieces along the open subspaces of the previous step, the gluing isomorphisms and the cocycle condition being forced by uniqueness in the universal property; the glued adic space exists by the anchor's gluing (Layer 5.3).

p is locally of finite type because on each chart A → A_k factors through a quotient mapping from A⟨T⟩_{E(k)} (Huber 1994 Lemma 3.5(ii)); R satisfies Huber's condition by step (i) of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affine-chart-analytification.
Functoriality h_S and independence of choices follow formally from the universal property (Yoneda).
acceptance: Y = Spec K, X = A¹_K = Spec K[T], S = Spa(K, K°): R is the adic affine line ⋃_k Spa(K⟨ϖ^k T⟩, K°⟨ϖ^k T⟩) (Hübner Example 10.4; AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-affine-space).
X = Y and f = id: R = S with p = id and q = g.
Every pair (x, s) with f(x) = g(s) is the image of a point of R (Huber 1994 Lemma 3.9(ii); AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-points).

nodes.title: For a Tate ring of topologically finite type over K, the power-bounded subring is the only ring of integral elements making it of topologically finite type over (K, K°)
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete rank-one nonarchimedean field and A a Tate ring topologically of finite type over K (a K-affinoid algebra: a quotient of some K⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩ by a continuous open surjection). Among the rings of integral elements A⁺ of A containing the image of K°, exactly one makes the morphism of affinoid rings (K, K°) → (A, A⁺) topologically of finite type, namely A⁺ = A°. Equivalently, for every continuous open surjection g: K⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩ → A, the power-bounded subring A° is the integral closure of g(K°⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩) in A.
hypotheses: K complete for a nontrivial rank-one nonarchimedean absolute value
A a K-affinoid algebra, i.e. Tate and topologically of finite type over K (Wedhorn Definition 5.57)
proofSteps: If (K,K°) → (A,A⁺) is of topologically finite type, it factors through a quotient mapping g: (K,K°)⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩ → (A, A⁺) (Huber 1994 Lemma 3.5(iii), Tate case), so A⁺ is the integral closure of g(K°⟨T⟩) in A.
K⟨T⟩° = K°⟨T⟩ (power-bounded = Gauss norm at most 1).
Since g is surjective, A° is the integral closure of g(K°⟨T⟩) in A (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-power-bounded-integral, which is BGR 6.3.4/1 and 6.4.3 as cited by Huber); hence A⁺ = A°.
Conversely g itself exhibits (K,K°) → (A, A°) as topologically of finite type, since A° is the integral closure of g(K°⟨T⟩).
acceptance: A = K⟨T⟩/(T²) = K ⊕ K·T: A° = K° ⊕ K·T, which strictly contains the image K° ⊕ K°·T of K°⟨T⟩; the nilpotent elements b·T with |b| > 1 are integral over that image. So 'plus ring = image of K°⟨T⟩' is wrong and the integral closure is needed.
For A = K⟨T⟩ one gets A° = K°⟨T⟩, the plus ring of the anchor's closed polydisc (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.closedPolydisc).

nodes.title: The adic analytification X ↦ X^ad = X ×_{Spec K} Spa(K, K°) of schemes locally of finite type over K
nodes.statement: Fix a field K complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one, its valuation ring K° = {|x| ≤ 1}, a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ (0 < |ϖ| < 1), and Spa K := Spa(K, K°), a one-point adic space. The identity of K defines a morphism of locally ringed spaces c_K: (Spa K)_ → Spec K. For a scheme X locally of finite type over K, its analytification is X^ad := X ×_{Spec K} Spa K (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification), an adic space locally of finite type over Spa K, with the morphism of locally ringed spaces q_X: X^ad_ → X lying over c_K; a K-morphism h: X₁ → X₂ gives h^ad := h_{Spa K}. This defines a functor (·)^ad: Sch^{lft}_K → Adic^{lft}_K from K-schemes locally of finite type to adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa K, and q is a natural transformation (·)^ad_ → (·) of functors to locally ringed spaces over Spec K. For X = Spec K[T₁,…,Tₙ]/I, X^ad = ⋃_{k≥0} Spa(A_k, A_k°) with A_k = K⟨ϖ^k T₁,…,ϖ^k Tₙ⟩/I·K⟨ϖ^k T⟩ (functions on the closed polydisc of radius |ϖ|^{-k} modulo I), glued along the rational embeddings Spa(A_k, A_k°) = {|ϖ^k Tᵢ| ≤ 1 for all i} ⊆ Spa(A_h, A_h°) for k ≤ h; the plus ring of each chart is its power-bounded subring (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/tft-plus-ring-power-bounded). The result does not depend on ϖ or on the presentation, up to unique isomorphism over Spa K compatible with q.
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially valued, rank one; the construction itself only uses that K is a complete Tate field that is strongly noetherian, which the anchor's Layer 0.5 proves for complete rank-one fields (BGR 5.2.6)
X locally of finite type over K, with no separatedness or quasi-compactness assumption
proofSteps: Spa K satisfies Huber's condition: K is strongly noetherian (anchor Layer 0.5; tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsStronglyNoetherian) and sheafy (anchor Layer 4).
Apply AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification with Y = Spec K, S = Spa K and g = c_K; functoriality and naturality of q are schemePullback.map.

Explicit charts: AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affine-chart-analytification with A = K, B = K, E = {ϖ}, so A(k) = K⟨ϖ^k T⟩; the chart plus ring (integral closure of the image of K°⟨ϖ^k T⟩) equals A_k° by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/tft-plus-ring-power-bounded because (K, K°) → (A_k, A_k⁺) is of topologically finite type.
Independence of ϖ and of the presentation: both constructions satisfy the universal property of X ×_{Spec K} Spa K, hence are uniquely isomorphic.
acceptance: (A¹_K)^ad is the adic affine line ⋃_k Spa(K⟨ϖ^k T⟩, K°⟨ϖ^k T⟩) (Hübner Example 10.4), not the closed unit disc; see AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-affine-space.
(Spec L)^ad = Spa(L, L°) (one point) for every finite extension L/K.
