nodes.title: Universal property of X^ad: morphisms from adic spaces over Spa K into X^ad are morphisms of locally ringed spaces into X
nodes.statement: Let X be a scheme locally of finite type over K and Y an adic space over Spa K with structure morphism π: Y → Spa K. Composition with q_X gives a bijection, natural in Y and in X, Hom_{Spa K}(Y, X^ad) → Hom_{LRS/Spec K}(Y_, X), w ↦ q_X ∘ w_, onto the set of morphisms of locally ringed spaces v: Y_ → X whose composite with X → Spec K is c_K ∘ π_. In particular, for an affinoid Y = Spa(D, D⁺) over Spa K with D complete and an affine X = Spec C, Hom_{Spa K}(Y, X^ad) ≅ Hom_{K-alg}(C, D) = X(D); for X = A^n_K this is D^n; and for a finite field extension L/K, Hom_{Spa K}(Spa(L, L°), X^ad) = X(L).
hypotheses: X locally of finite type over K (K complete, rank one)
Y an arbitrary adic space over Spa K; no finiteness hypothesis on Y
proofSteps: Specialise the universal property of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification to Y = Spec K, S = Spa K, g = c_K: the datum u: Y → Spa K is forced to be π, so the lift w ↦ q_X ∘ w_ is bijective.
Naturality in Y is composition; naturality in X is schemePullback.map (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-functor).

Affinoid Y, affine X: morphisms of locally ringed spaces Y_ → Spec C are ring maps C → O_Y(Y) (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.ΓSpec.locallyRingedSpaceAdjunction; Stacks 01I1), and O_Y(Y) = D for a complete sheafy pair (anchor Layer 3.5).
For L/K finite, Spa(L, L°) is an adic space over Spa K with O(Spa(L,L°)) = L, so the previous step gives X(L).
acceptance: (A¹_K)^ad represents Y ↦ O_Y(Y) on adic spaces over Spa K, while the closed unit disc represents Y ↦ O⁺_Y(Y) (Scholze–Weinstein, Berkeley Lecture 4, 'the adic affine line').
Over a strongly noetherian Tate affinoid base S = Spa(A, A⁺) the same bijection is Zavyalov's Definition 6.1 of relative analytification.
X^ad(Spa(L, L°)) = X(L) for finite L/K (Conrad, genpaper §1.2 (i), rigid form).

nodes.title: The adic affine space A^{n,ad}: an increasing union of closed polydiscs, not quasi-compact, with entire functions as global sections
nodes.statement: Let n ≥ 1 and ϖ a pseudo-uniformizer of K. nodes.title: Analytification of open and closed immersions: open subspaces and closed adic subspaces cut out by the analytified ideal
nodes.statement: Let X be a K-scheme locally of finite type. (i) If j: U → X is an open immersion, j^ad is an open embedding with image q_X⁻¹(j(U)). (ii) If i: Z → X is a closed immersion with quasi-coherent ideal sheaf I ⊆ O_X, then i^ad is a closed embedding in the sense of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings: it identifies Z^ad with the closed adic subspace of X^ad defined by the ideal sheaf I·O_{X^ad} generated by q_X⁻¹I, and its image is q_X⁻¹(i(Z)). On an affine chart X = Spec K[T]/J, Z = Spec K[T]/(J + J'), the piece of Z^ad over Spa(A_k, A_k°) is Spa(A_k/J'A_k, (A_k/J'A_k)°), the quotient pair of the anchor's Layer 2.4. (iii) Consequently immersions analytify to locally closed embeddings, and (i)–(ii) hold verbatim for X ×_Y S → X' ×_Y S in the relative setting of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification.
hypotheses: X locally of finite type over K; I quasi-coherent (automatically of finite type since X is locally noetherian)
proofSteps: (i): the open subspace q_X⁻¹(j(U)) satisfies the universal property of U^ad (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-universal-property): a morphism into X^ad factors through it iff its composite with q_X factors through U (schemePullback.isoOpenSubscheme).

(ii) affine charts: X = Spec C, C = K[T]/J, Z = Spec C/J'. On the chart Spa(A_k, A_k°) the ideal J'A_k is closed (A_k is noetherian and complete, anchor Layer 0.5–0.6), the quotient pair (A_k/J'A_k, (A_k/J'A_k)°) (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotient; plus ring by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/tft-plus-ring-power-bounded) is a complete sheafy pair, and it satisfies the universal property of the chart of Z^ad: a continuous map A_k → D kills J'A_k iff the corresponding B-algebra map C → D factors through C/J' (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affine-chart-analytification).
(ii) image: a point x of Spa(A_k, A_k°) lies in the image iff J'A_k ⊆ supp(x) (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.range_spaComap_quotientHom), iff J' ⊆ ker(C → k(x)), iff q_X(x) ∈ Z.

(ii) gluing: the chart descriptions are compatible with restriction to rational subsets, so they glue to the closed adic subspace defined by I·O_{X^ad} (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings; anchor Layer 5 closed immersions via closed ideals).
(iii): an immersion is a closed immersion followed by an open immersion; combine (i) and (ii). The relative case uses the same charts over Spa(A, A⁺).

nodes.title: Points of X ×_Y S and of X^ad: surjectivity onto compatible pairs; classical points correspond to closed points; q_X is not injective
nodes.statement: (i) In the situation of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification, for every x ∈ X and s ∈ S with f(x) = g(s) there is r ∈ X ×_Y S with q(r) = x and p(r) = s. In particular q_X: X^ad → X is surjective onto the set of all points of X, closed and non-closed. (ii) Call x ∈ X^ad classical if its residue field k(x) = O_{X^ad,x}/m_x is finite over K. Then q_X restricts to a bijection from the classical points of X^ad onto the closed points of X; for a closed point x₀, q_X⁻¹(x₀) consists of exactly one point, it is classical, and q_X induces k(x₀) ≅ k(x). (iii) If dim X ≥ 1, q_X is not injective: the fibre over the generic point of a positive-dimensional irreducible component is infinite; for X = A¹_K the fibre over the generic point contains every non-classical point, among them the Gauss point of each disc |T| ≤ |ϖ|^{-k} and the rank-2 points.
hypotheses: (i) needs only Huber's hypotheses of 3.8; (ii)–(iii) are for K complete of rank one and X locally of finite type over K
proofSteps: (i): reduce to Y = Spec B, X = Spec C, S = Spa(A, A⁺); choose a prime q of C ⊗_B A over the given prime of C and the support of s, a valuation r of C ⊗_B A extending s with value group having the same divisible hull, and k with r(c ⊗ i) ≤ 1 for c in a finite generating set of C and i ∈ I^k (I an ideal of definition); then r is a point of the open affinoid Spa(D, D⁺) ⊆ R built from D₀ = A₀[c ⊗ i] (Huber 1994 Lemma 3.9(ii); Wedhorn Proposition 8.63).
Surjectivity of q_X: apply (i) with S = Spa K, whose only point maps to the only point of Spec K.

(ii) closed points: for x₀ closed with residue field L (finite over K by the Nullstellensatz; mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.isClosed_singleton_iff_locallyOfFiniteType, mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType.jacobsonSpace), the closed immersion Spec L → X analytifies to a closed embedding with image q_X⁻¹(x₀) (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-immersions), and (Spec L)^ad = Spa(L, L°) is one point with residue field L (a continuous valuation of L bounded by 1 on L° is the unique extension of |·|).

(ii) classical points: if k(x) is finite over K then k(q_X(x)) ⊆ k(x) (the stalk map is local) is finite over K, so q_X(x) is closed; hence q_X maps classical points to closed points, and by the previous step bijectively.

(iii): the Gauss point of K⟨ϖ^k T⟩ has support 0, so its image in Spec K[T] is the generic point; the rank-2 points of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-affine-space likewise have support 0. For general X, Noether normalisation gives an affine open U of the component with a finite surjection U → A^d, d ≥ 1; the fibre of q_{A^d} over the generic point is infinite (Gauss points of the polydiscs of radius |ϖ|^{-k}), and by (i) applied to U ×_{A^d} (A^d)^ad = U^ad each of these points lifts to a point of U^ad over the generic point of U.

nodes.title: Analytification commutes with fibre products and preserves finite products
nodes.statement: For morphisms X → Z ← Y of K-schemes locally of finite type, the natural morphism (X ×_Z Y)^ad → X^ad ×_{Z^ad} Y^ad (induced by the two projections) is an isomorphism of adic spaces over Spa K; the right side is the fibre product of adic spaces, which exists by AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence because X^ad → Z^ad is locally of finite type. Since (Spec K)^ad = Spa K is terminal among adic spaces over Spa K, (·)^ad preserves finite products: (X ×_K Y)^ad ≅ X^ad ×_{Spa K} Y^ad and (Spec K)^ad ≅ Spa K. Relatively, for S satisfying Huber's condition over Y and Y-schemes X₁ → X₂ ← X₃ locally of finite type, (X₁ ×_{X₂} X₃) ×_Y S ≅ (X₁ ×_Y S) ×_{(X₂ ×_Y S)} (X₃ ×_Y S).

the fibre product on the right is taken in the category of all adic spaces; it exists because one leg is locally of finite type

By the universal property again this is Hom(T, X^ad) ×_{Hom(T, Z^ad)} Hom(T, Y^ad) = Hom(T, X^ad ×_{Z^ad} Y^ad), using existence of the adic fibre product (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence); conclude by Yoneda.

nodes.title: Analytification of finite and finite locally free morphisms
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a finite morphism of schemes and S → Y as in AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification. For every open affinoid V = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ S mapping into an affine open Spec B ⊆ Y with f⁻¹(Spec B) = Spec C (C finite over B), the preimage of V in X ×_Y S is the affinoid Spa(C ⊗_B A, (C ⊗_B A)⁺), where C ⊗_B A carries its natural topology as a finite A-module and (C ⊗_B A)⁺ is the integral closure of the image of A⁺; hence p: X ×_Y S → S is finite in the sense of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-morphism. If moreover f is finite locally free of constant rank d (f_*O_X locally free of rank d), then for every such V the ring O(p⁻¹V) = C ⊗_B A is a finite projective A-module of constant rank d. In particular, for K-schemes locally of finite type: f finite ⇒ f^ad finite; f finite locally free of rank d ⇒ f^ad finite and O((f^ad)⁻¹V) finite projective of rank d over O(V) for every open affinoid V ⊆ Y^ad.
hypotheses: f finite (resp. finite locally free of rank d); S satisfies Huber's condition
proofSteps: Reduce to Y = Spec B, X = Spec C, S = Spa(A, A⁺); write C = B[T₁,…,Tₙ]/I with each Tᵢ satisfying a monic equation over B.

Put D = C ⊗_B A with its finite A-module topology and D⁺ the integral closure of the image of A⁺; (D, D⁺) is a complete Huber pair of the same noetherian type, finite over (A, A⁺) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-algebra-over-affinoid).

If tᵢ^m + a₁tᵢ^{m-1} + … + a_m = 0 in D with a_j ∈ A, then for e ∈ E(k) the element e·tᵢ satisfies (e tᵢ)^m + (e a₁)(e tᵢ)^{m-1} + … + e^m a_m = 0; since E(k) → 0 and A⁺ is open, e^j a_j ∈ A⁺ for k large, so e·tᵢ is integral over A⁺ and lies in D⁺.

Hence, for k large, the universal property of the chart R_k (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affine-chart-analytification) gives a map A_k → D inverse to the evident continuous map D → A_k (continuity of A-linear maps from a finite module), so R_k = Spa(D, D⁺) for all large k and the increasing union stabilises: X ×_Y S = Spa(D, D⁺) over V.
Finiteness in the sense of R0 (Huber 1996 (1.4.2), (1.4.4)): D is finite over A with the module topology and D⁺ is the integral closure of A⁺.
If C is a finite projective B-module of rank d then C ⊗_B A is a finite projective A-module of rank d (base change).

nodes.title: Affinoid subdomains of the maximal spectrum of a K-affinoid algebra
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one, A a K-affinoid algebra and X = Max A. A subset U ⊆ X is an affinoid subdomain if there is a homomorphism of K-affinoid algebras i : A → A_U such that Max(i) : Max A_U → X (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-residue-fields-finite) has image in U and is universal for this property: for every homomorphism φ : A → B into a K-affinoid algebra with Max(φ)(Max B) ⊆ U there is a unique K-algebra homomorphism φ_U : A_U → B with φ_U ∘ i = φ. The A-algebra A_U (the coordinate ring of U) is unique up to unique A-isomorphism; Max(i) is a bijection onto U inducing isomorphisms of residue fields; for affinoid subdomains V ⊆ U there is a unique A-algebra map ρ^U_V : A_U → A_V, with ρ^V_W ∘ ρ^U_V = ρ^U_W. Rational subdomains X(f₁,…,f_n/f₀) = {x : |f_j(x)| ≤ |f₀(x)| for all j}, for f₀,…,f_n ∈ A without common zero, are affinoid subdomains with coordinate ring A⟨f/f₀⟩ = A⟨T₁,…,T_n⟩/(f₀T_j − f_j) (Weierstrass domains f₀ = 1, Laurent domains as intersections). Lean name: RigidSpace.IsAffinoidSubdomain A U, with coordinate ring RigidSpace.IsAffinoidSubdomain.coordRing.
hypotheses: K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one

A is a K-affinoid algebra: a commutative K-algebra with a complete Hausdorff first-countable ring topology for which K → A is strictly topologically of finite type (Tau Ceti IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType (algebraMap K A): a continuous open surjection of K-algebras K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ = restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n K → A; Wedhorn Definition 5.57)
proofSteps: Definition by the universal property; uniqueness of A_U by the Yoneda lemma.

Max(i) is injective with image U and residue fields are preserved: test the universal property on the finite K-affinoid algebras A/m_x (x ∈ U) and their finite extensions (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-residue-fields-finite).

Rational subdomains: for φ : A → B, the elements φ(f_j)/φ(f₀) exist and are power-bounded iff |φ(f_j)(y)| ≤ |φ(f₀)(y)| for all y ∈ Max B (φ(f₀) is a unit because it has no zero on Max B, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-jacobson; power-boundedness by AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-power-bounded-iff-sup), and the universal property of relative Tate algebras (anchor Layer 0.4, requested) gives the factorisation (Conrad, Several approaches, Lemma 2.1.8).

Intersections and preimages: A_{U∩U'} = A_U ⊗̂_A A_{U'} and the coordinate ring of Max(φ)⁻¹(U) is A_U ⊗̂_A B, by the universal property of the completed tensor product (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product) and the universal property of A_U.
acceptance: U = X with A_U = A, and U = ∅ with A_U = 0, are affinoid subdomains.

nodes.title: Coordinate rings of affinoid subdomains are flat
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one, A a K-affinoid algebra and U ⊆ Max A an affinoid subdomain (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-subdomain). Then A → A_U is flat. If U₁,…,U_n are affinoid subdomains covering Max A, then A → ∏_i A_{U_i} is faithfully flat. Lean name: RigidSpace.IsAffinoidSubdomain.flat and RigidSpace.faithfullyFlat_pi_coordRing.
hypotheses: K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one

A is a K-affinoid algebra: a commutative K-algebra with a complete Hausdorff first-countable ring topology for which K → A is strictly topologically of finite type (Tau Ceti IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType (algebraMap K A): a continuous open surjection of K-algebras K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ = restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n K → A; Wedhorn Definition 5.57)
U an affinoid subdomain; for the second statement a finite covering by affinoid subdomains
proofSteps: For y ∈ Max A_U over x ∈ U, A/m_xᵏ → A_U/m_xᵏA_U is an isomorphism for all k (API quotient_pow_equiv of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-subdomain, BGR 7.2.2/1), so the local homomorphism A_{m_x} → (A_U)_{m_y} of noetherian local rings induces an isomorphism of completions (Mathlib AdicCompletion).

A local homomorphism of noetherian local rings inducing an isomorphism of completions is flat (completion is faithfully flat), and flatness of A → A_U may be checked at the maximal ideals of A_U (BGR 7.3.2/6; Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.5.17). Proof source BGR, not public; recorded as a gap on this node.

Faithful flatness of the covering: the product is flat, and every maximal ideal of A lies under a maximal ideal of some A_{U_i} (the U_i cover Max A and Max A_{U_i} → U_i is bijective), so ∏ A_{U_i} ⊗_A A/m ≠ 0 for all m (Mathlib Module.FaithfullyFlat criterion; Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 2.5.18).
acceptance: For the covering of Max K⟨T⟩ by {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} and {|T| ≥ |ϖ|}, K⟨T⟩ → K⟨S⟩ × K⟨T, U⟩/(TU − ϖ) (T ↦ (ϖS, T)) is faithfully flat.
The single affinoid subdomain {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} gives a flat but not faithfully flat map K⟨T⟩ → K⟨S⟩ (the point T = 1 is missed).

sources.excerpt: it can be shown (by a method entirely different from the case of schemes) that AU is A-flat for any affinoid subdomain U ⊆ M (A).
sources.match: The flatness statement.

nodes.title: The Gerritzen–Grauert theorem
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one, A a K-affinoid algebra and U ⊆ Max A an affinoid subdomain. Then there are finitely many rational subdomains V₁,…,V_n covering Max A — induced by a rational covering of Spa(A, A°) — such that U ∩ V_i is a rational subdomain of Max A_{V_i} for every i. In particular U is a finite union of rational subdomains of Max A, and affinoid subdomains are open in the canonical topology. Lean name: RigidSpace.IsAffinoidSubdomain.exists_rationalCover.
hypotheses: K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one

A is a K-affinoid algebra: a commutative K-algebra with a complete Hausdorff first-countable ring topology for which K → A is strictly topologically of finite type (Tau Ceti IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType (algebraMap K A): a continuous open surjection of K-algebras K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ = restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n K → A; Wedhorn Definition 5.57)
U an affinoid subdomain (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-subdomain)
proofSteps: BGR 7.3.5/1: there are finitely many rational subdomains W_j covering Max A with U ∩ W_j rational in W_j. Proof source: BGR 7.3.5, or Temkin's proof (J. reine angew. Math. 2005, Theorem 3.1); neither is among the sources read; recorded as a gap on this node.

Refinement to a covering induced by a rational covering of Spa(A, A°): every finite covering of Max A by rational subdomains is refined by a standard rational covering (Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.5.10), obtained from Tau Ceti exists_span_eq_top_forall_rationalSubset_subset_of_isTateRing on Spa(A, A°); U ∩ V_i remains rational in V_i by transitivity of rational subdomains (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-subdomain, API trans and inter).
Finite union: U = ⋃_i (U ∩ V_i) and a rational subdomain of a rational subdomain is rational in Max A.
acceptance: Every Weierstrass, Laurent or rational domain satisfies the theorem trivially (n = 1).

The converse fails: not every finite union of rational subdomains is an affinoid subdomain (Kedlaya–Liu, Theorem 2.5.11, final sentence); the theorem asserts only that affinoid subdomains are finite unions of rational ones.

sources.match: The Gerritzen–Grauert theorem in its finite-union form.

nodes.title: Tate's acyclicity theorem for finite coverings by affinoid subdomains
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one, A a K-affinoid algebra, M an A-module and U₁,…,U_n affinoid subdomains covering Max A (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-subdomain). Then the augmented Čech complex 0 → M → ∏_i M ⊗_A A_{U_i} → ∏_{i<j} M ⊗_A A_{U_i ∩ U_j} → ⋯ is exact. In particular U ↦ A_U is a sheaf for finite coverings of affinoid subdomains by affinoid subdomains, with vanishing higher Čech cohomology, and it extends uniquely to a sheaf O_A for the Tate topology on Max A. Lean name: RigidSpace.cech_exact_of_affinoidCover.
hypotheses: K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one

A is a K-affinoid algebra: a commutative K-algebra with a complete Hausdorff first-countable ring topology for which K → A is strictly topologically of finite type (Tau Ceti IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType (algebraMap K A): a continuous open surjection of K-algebras K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ = restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n K → A; Wedhorn Definition 5.57)
M an arbitrary A-module
{U_i} a finite covering of Max A by affinoid subdomains
proofSteps: Reduction to M = A: A → A_{U_I} is flat for every finite intersection U_I (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-subdomain-flat), so the Čech complex of M is M ⊗_A (Čech complex of A) and flat base change preserves exactness.

Rational refinement: by the Gerritzen–Grauert theorem (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/gerritzen-grauert) there is a covering of Max A induced by a rational covering {V_j} of Spa(A, A°) such that each U_i ∩ V_j is rational in V_j; on each V_j and each finite intersection the induced coverings are refined by standard rational coverings (Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.5.10; Tau Ceti exists_span_eq_top_forall_rationalSubset_subset_of_isTateRing).

Standard rational coverings of the strongly noetherian Tate rings A_V (V rational) are Čech acyclic in all degrees (anchor Layer 4.1, requested; the coordinate rings of rational subdomains are the anchor's completed rational localisations, API rational_compat of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-subdomain).

Passage along refinements: if a covering 𝔙 refines 𝔘 and the restrictions of 𝔙 to all finite intersections of members of 𝔘, and of 𝔘 to all members of 𝔙, are acyclic, then 𝔘 is acyclic (the Čech double-complex comparison of BGR 8.1.4 and 8.2.1–8.2.2). Proof source BGR, not public; recorded as a gap on this node.
The extension to the Tate topology follows by the definition of admissible coverings (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space uses this node).
acceptance: For the Laurent covering {|f| ≤ 1}, {|f| ≥ 1} of Max A: 0 → A → A⟨f⟩ × A⟨f⁻¹⟩ → A⟨f, f⁻¹⟩ → 0 is exact.
For the covering of Max K⟨T⟩ by {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} and {|T| ≥ |ϖ|} (Conrad, Several approaches, Exercise 2.3.4), a pair of compatible functions glues to a unique element of K⟨T⟩.

nodes.title: Local rings of affinoid spaces at points are noetherian with the algebraic completion
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one, A a K-affinoid algebra, x ∈ Max A with maximal ideal m, and O_x = colim_{U ∋ x} A_U the colimit over the affinoid subdomains of Max A containing x (the stalk of Sp A at x). Then O_x is a noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m·O_x, the map A_m → O_x is faithfully flat, and A/mᵏ → O_x/mᵏO_x is an isomorphism for every k ≥ 1; hence the completions agree, Â_m ≅ Ô_x. Lean name: RigidSpace.stalk_completion_equiv.
hypotheses: K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one

A is a K-affinoid algebra: a commutative K-algebra with a complete Hausdorff first-countable ring topology for which K → A is strictly topologically of finite type (Tau Ceti IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType (algebraMap K A): a continuous open surjection of K-algebras K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ = restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n K → A; Wedhorn Definition 5.57)
x ∈ Max A
proofSteps: A/mᵏ ≅ A_U/mᵏA_U for every affinoid subdomain U ∋ x (API quotient_pow_equiv of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-subdomain, BGR 7.2.2/1); pass to the colimit.

O_x is local with maximal ideal m·O_x: if f(x) ≠ 0 then f is a unit on the Laurent domain {|f| ≥ |f(x)|}, an affinoid subdomain containing x (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-subdomain, API rational; AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-jacobson for units).

O_x is noetherian (BGR 7.3.2/3): the transition maps are flat (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-subdomain-flat) and m·O_x is finitely generated with m-adically separated O_x. Proof source BGR, not public; recorded as a gap on this node.
Faithful flatness: A_m → O_x is a local homomorphism of noetherian local rings inducing an isomorphism of completions (Mathlib AdicCompletion), hence faithfully flat.
acceptance: At the origin of Max K⟨T⟩, O_0 is the ring of power series converging on some disc around 0, strictly between K[T]_{(T)} and K⟦T⟧, with completion K⟦T⟧ (Conrad, Several approaches, Exercise 2.3.6).
For A = K⟨T⟩/(T²) at the origin, O_0 = A (every affinoid subdomain containing the only point is all of Max A).

nodes.title: Rigid-analytic spaces over K in the sense of Tate (BGR 9.3.1)
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete rank-one nonarchimedean field. For a K-affinoid algebra A (a quotient of some Tate algebra K⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩, with its Banach topology), the affinoid space Sp(A) is the set Max A of maximal ideals with the Tate (strong) G-topology: a subset U ⊆ Max A is admissible open if it has a covering {U_i} by affinoid subdomains such that for every affinoid subdomain V ⊆ Max A contained in U the covering {V ∩ U_i} of V admits a finite refinement by affinoid subdomains, and a covering of an admissible open by admissible opens is admissible if it has the same finiteness property on every affinoid subdomain V ⊆ U (BGR 9.1.4); together with Tate's structure sheaf O_A, U ↦ A_U on affinoid subdomains. A rigid-analytic space over K is a pair (X, O_X) of a G-topologized set X and a sheaf of K-algebras O_X with local stalks, admitting an admissible covering by open subspaces isomorphic to affinoid spaces Sp(A_i). Morphisms are morphisms of locally G-ringed K-spaces. Rig_K denotes this category. A morphism f is separated if its diagonal is a closed immersion, quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact, and proper (Kiehl) if it is separated, quasi-compact and relatively compact over an admissible affinoid covering of the target (Conrad AWS Definition 3.2.3).
hypotheses: K complete for a nontrivial rank-one nonarchimedean absolute value

K-affinoid algebras are strongly noetherian Tate rings (anchor Layer 0.5), so Tate's acyclicity for finite rational coverings is the anchor's Layer 4; the extension to finite coverings by affinoid subdomains uses the Gerritzen–Grauert theorem, whose proof (BGR 7.3.5) is not in a public source read here
proofSteps: Affinoid subdomains, rational subdomains and the weak/strong G-topologies on Max A (BGR 7.2, 9.1); by the Gerritzen–Grauert theorem every affinoid subdomain is a finite union of rational subdomains, so the Tate topology is generated by finite rational coverings.

Tate's acyclicity: U ↦ A_U is a sheaf for finite rational coverings (anchor Layer 4, strongly noetherian Tate rings; tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.faithfullyFlat_pi_toCompletionLoc for injectivity) and hence for the Tate topology.
Locally G-ringed spaces, open subspaces and gluing along admissible opens (Conrad AWS §2.3–2.4; BGR 9.1–9.3); Sp is a fully faithful contravariant functor from K-affinoid algebras.
acceptance: Sp(K) is a point with structure sheaf K; O(Sp A) = A.
In the closed unit disc, {|T| < 1} and {|T| = 1} are admissible opens that cover the disc set-theoretically but do not form an admissible covering (Conrad AWS Example 2.2.8).

nodes.title: Every maximal ideal of a K-affinoid domain has height equal to its dimension
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete rank-one nonarchimedean field and A a K-affinoid algebra (a quotient of a Tate algebra T_n(K) = K⟨X_1, …, X_n⟩; AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space) which is an integral domain of Krull dimension d. Then every maximal ideal m of A has height d (Ideal.height m = d); equivalently dim A_m = d for every point of Sp(A). In particular every maximal ideal of T_d(K) has height d, and if T_e(K) → A is a finite injective K-algebra homomorphism then e = d. (Conrad, Irreducible components of rigid spaces, Lemma 2.1.5, first assertion.)
hypotheses: K complete for a nontrivial rank-one nonarchimedean absolute value
A a K-affinoid algebra that is an integral domain
proofSteps: A is noetherian: K-affinoid algebras are complete strongly noetherian Tate rings (anchor Layer 0.5; tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isNoetherianRing_of_isStronglyNoetherian), so heights are finite (mathlib Ideal.height).

Tate algebras at rational points: for a maximal ideal m of T_d(K) with residue field K (the point a ∈ (K°)^d), T_d(K)/m^k ≅ K[X]/(X − a)^k for every k, so the m-adic completion of T_d(K) is K⟦X_1 − a_1, …, X_d − a_d⟧, of dimension d; a noetherian local ring and its completion have the same dimension, so ht m = d.

Tate algebras at all maximal ideals: the residue field T_d(K)/m is finite over K (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-residue-fields-finite); for a finite extension K′/K containing it, T_d(K′) = T_d(K) ⊗_K K′ is finite free over T_d(K), there is a K′-rational maximal ideal m′ lying over m (mathlib Ideal.exists_ideal_over_prime_of_isIntegral), and since the extension is flat it has going down (mathlib Algebra.HasGoingDown.of_flat), so ht m′ = ht m + ht(m′/mT_d(K′)) (mathlib Ideal.height_eq_height_add_of_liesOver_of_hasGoingDown); the fibre T_d(K′)/mT_d(K′) is finite over the field T_d(K)/m, so its primes are minimal and the second summand is 0 (mathlib Ideal.height_eq_zero_iff); hence ht m = d.

General A: Noether normalisation (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-noether-normalisation) gives a finite injective K-algebra homomorphism T_e(K) → A. T_e(K) is factorial, hence integrally closed (mathlib IsIntegrallyClosed), so the integral extension of domains T_e(K) ⊆ A has going down (mathlib Algebra.HasGoingDown; the instance for integral extensions of integrally closed domains, Stacks 00H8). For a maximal ideal m of A, n = m ∩ T_e(K) is maximal (mathlib Ideal.isMaximal_comap_of_isIntegral_of_isMaximal) and ht m = ht n + ht(m/nA) = e + 0, because A/nA is finite over the field T_e(K)/n. So all maximal ideals of A have height e, and d = dim A, the supremum of these heights, equals e (Conrad, Lemma 2.1.5).

nodes.title: Identity principle on connected normal rigid spaces
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete rank-one nonarchimedean field and X a rigid-analytic space over K (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space) that is connected (every admissible covering {V, W} of X by disjoint admissible opens has V = ∅ or W = ∅; equivalently O_X(X) has no idempotents other than 0 and 1) and normal (every local ring O_{X,x} is a normal domain; for an affinoid open Sp(A) ⊆ X this holds at its points iff A is a normal ring). An analytic subset of X is the zero locus Z = {x ∈ X : 𝓘_x ≠ O_{X,x}} of a coherent ideal sheaf 𝓘 ⊆ O_X (on an affinoid open Sp(A), Z ∩ Sp(A) = {m ∈ Max A : I ⊆ m} for the ideal I = 𝓘(Sp A)). Let U ⊆ X be a nonempty admissible open. Then: (i) the only analytic subset of X containing U is X; (ii) if X = Z₁ ∪ Z₂ for analytic subsets Z₁, Z₂, then Z₁ = X or Z₂ = X; (iii) if f ∈ O_X(X) has f|_U = 0, then f = 0, and more generally a section s of a locally free O_X-module ℰ of finite rank with s|_U = 0 is 0. Parts (i)–(ii) are Conrad, Irreducible components of rigid spaces, Lemma 2.1.4; (iii) is the argument in the proof of his Theorem 2.1.2.
hypotheses: K complete for a nontrivial rank-one nonarchimedean absolute value
X connected and normal
U ⊆ X a nonempty admissible open
proofSteps: Constant dimension: for x in an affinoid open Sp(A) ⊆ X with maximal ideal m, the local map A_m → O_{X,x} induces an isomorphism of completions (Conrad, §1.2; AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-local-ring-completion), so dim O_{X,x} = ht m and O_{X,x} is normal iff A_m is. A connected normal affinoid Sp(A) has A a normal noetherian ring without nontrivial idempotents, hence a domain, so all its points have dim O_{X,x} = dim A (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-domain-equidimensional). Covering X by connected affinoids and using that X is connected (chains of overlapping connected affinoids), all O_{X,x} have one dimension n (Conrad, proof of Lemma 2.1.4).

(i) Give Z its reduced structure (the radical of 𝓘). Shrink U to a nonempty connected affinoid subdomain V₀ ⊆ U (an affinoid Sp(C) is the disjoint union of the finitely many connected affinoids Sp(Ce_i), e_i the primitive idempotents of the noetherian ring C) and replace Z by its connected component containing V₀. Put Z_n = {z ∈ Z : dim O_{Z,z} = n} and Z_< = {z ∈ Z : dim O_{Z,z} < n}.

Normality: if Z_n meets a connected affinoid subdomain V = Sp(C) of X, then V ⊆ Z_n. Indeed C is a normal domain of dimension n, Z ∩ V = V(I) with I radical, and if I ≠ 0 then for every maximal m ⊇ I the ideal I·C_m has height ≥ 1 (0 is the only minimal prime of the domain C_m; mathlib Ideal.height_eq_zero_iff), so dim (C/I)_m ≤ dim C_m − 1 < n and no point of V lies in Z_n; hence I = 0. Therefore Z_n and Z_< are unions of intersections of Z with members of an admissible covering of X by connected affinoids, {Z_n, Z_<} is an admissible covering of Z by disjoint admissible opens, and since Z is connected and V₀ ⊆ Z_n, Z = Z_n (Conrad, proof of Lemma 2.1.4).
Z therefore contains every connected affinoid subdomain of X that it meets, so {Z, X − Z} is an admissible covering of X by disjoint admissible opens; X is connected and Z ⊇ V₀ is nonempty, so Z = X.
(ii) If Z₁ ≠ X, then X − Z₁ is a nonempty admissible open contained in Z₂, so Z₂ = X by (i).

(iii) The zero locus of f is the analytic subset of the coherent ideal f·O_X and contains U, so it is X by (i): f vanishes in the residue field of every point. On each affinoid open Sp(A) ⊆ X, A is reduced (normal, mathlib IsReduced) and Jacobson (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-jacobson, mathlib IsJacobsonRing), so f|_{Sp A} lies in the intersection of all maximal ideals, which is the nilradical 0; hence f = 0 (Conrad, proof of Theorem 2.1.2). For ℰ, choose an admissible affinoid covering on which ℰ is free; the zero locus of s is an analytic subset (locally the common zero locus of the coordinates of s) containing U, hence X, and each coordinate vanishes at every point of a reduced affinoid, hence is 0.
acceptance: In the closed unit disc Sp K⟨T⟩ (connected and normal) an f ∈ K⟨T⟩ vanishing on the open disc {|T| < 1} (an admissible open) is 0, and the only analytic subset containing {|T − 1| ≤ |ϖ|} is the disc.

Normality is needed: X = Sp K⟨S, T⟩/(ST) (two discs meeting in one point) is connected and not normal; its Laurent domain {|T| ≥ |ϖ|} is a nonempty admissible open on which T is a unit and hence S = 0, so the analytic subset {S = 0} ≠ X contains it and the nonzero function S restricts to 0 on it.
Connectedness is needed: on X = Sp(K⟨T⟩ × K⟨T⟩) the idempotent (1, 0) vanishes on the second disc and is nonzero.

nodes.title: Huber's functor r_K from rigid-analytic spaces to adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°)
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete rank-one nonarchimedean field. There is a functor r_K: Rig_K → Adic^{lft}_K together with, for each rigid space X, a morphism of ringed sites ρ_X: (|r_K(X)|, O_{r_K(X)}) → (X, O_X) over Sp K = Spa K (Huber 1994 Proposition 4.3) such that r_K(X) is locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°), ρ_X is locally coherent, and (r_K(X), ρ_X) is final: for every adic space Z locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°) and every locally coherent morphism of ringed sites λ: (|Z|, O_Z) → (X, O_X) over Sp K there is a unique morphism f: Z → r_K(X) over Spa K with ρ_X ∘ f = λ. Moreover (Huber 1996 (1.1.11)): (a) r_K(Sp A) = Spa(A, A°) and r_K of a morphism of affinoids is induced by the K-algebra map; (b) r_K carries open immersions to open embeddings and r_K(U ∩ V) = r_K(U) ∩ r_K(V); (c) a family of admissible opens is an admissible covering iff the r_K(U_i) cover r_K(X); (d) the points of X correspond bijectively to the classical points of r_K(X) (points x with k(x) finite over K), with r_K(U) ∩ X = U for admissible U; (e) r_K commutes with fibre products.
hypotheses: K complete of rank one (Huber 1994 §4 hypothesis)
rigid-analytic varieties in the sense of BGR 9.3.1 (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space)
proofSteps: Affinoid case: r_K(Sp A) := Spa(A, A°), an adic space because A is strongly noetherian Tate (anchor Layer 4), locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°) by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/tft-plus-ring-power-bounded.

Rational subsets of Spa(A, A°) correspond bijectively to rational subdomains of Max A via U ↦ U ∩ Max A, because constructible subsets of Spa(A, A°) are determined by their classical points (Huber 1993 Theorem 4.1, Corollaries 4.2–4.3); this gives a coherent morphism of sites m: |Spa(A, A°)| → |Sp A| and an isomorphism of structure sheaves θ (same rings A_U on both sides), i.e. ρ_{Sp A} = (m, θ).

Universal property on affinoids (proof of Huber 1994 4.3): a locally coherent λ lifts uniquely to a morphism of ringed spaces g; g respects the valuations because its restriction to classical points does (the valuation of K extends uniquely to finite extensions) and those determine the rational inequalities (Huber 1993 Corollary 4.3).
Globalisation: glue along admissible opens, which r_K sends to open subspaces (b); the universal property makes the gluing canonical.

(c)–(e): (c) from the correspondence of rational subsets and quasi-compactness of rational subsets; (d) from Wedhorn Example 7.58 / Huber 1993 §4 on affinoids; (e) from the universal property and the affinoid fibre product Spa(B ⊗̂_A C, (B ⊗̂_A C)°) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-fibre-product).
Details beyond the affinoid step are stated but not written out in Huber 1994 ('(i)-(iv) follow from the proof of (4.3)'); the missing write-up is recorded as a gap.
acceptance: r_K(Sp A) = Spa(A, A°); admissibility of a covering is detected by set-theoretic covering of r_K(X).

nodes.title: At a classical point, the local ring of X^ad has the same completion as the local ring of X
nodes.statement: Let X be a K-scheme locally of finite type, x ∈ X^ad a classical point and x₀ = q_X(x) the corresponding closed point (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-points). Then O_{X^ad,x} is a noetherian local ring, q^♯_x: O_{X,x₀} → O_{X^ad,x} is a local homomorphism inducing an isomorphism of residue fields and an isomorphism of completions Ô_{X,x₀} ≅ Ô_{X^ad,x}; in particular the Zariski cotangent spaces m_{x₀}/m_{x₀}² ≅ m_x/m_x² agree and dim O_{X,x₀} = dim O_{X^ad,x}.
hypotheses: K complete of rank one; x classical (k(x) finite over K)
proofSteps: Reduce to X affine, then to a chart Spa(A_k, A_k°) containing x, where x corresponds to a maximal ideal m of the affinoid algebra A_k (Wedhorn Example 7.58).

The stalk of Spa(A_k, A_k°) at a classical point equals the local ring of the rigid space Sp(A_k) at m (Conrad, adic notes Example 3.15 and the paragraph after it): classical points are dense in constructible sets (Huber 1993 Corollary 4.2), rational subsets of Spa correspond bijectively to rational subdomains of Max A_k (Huber 1993 §4, after Corollary 4.3), so the two colimits of rings A_U agree.

The rigid local ring O_{Sp A_k, m} is noetherian with completion equal to the m-adic completion of A_k (Conrad AWS §2.3, after Exercise 2.3.6), and the local map O_{X,x₀} → (A_k)_m induces an isomorphism on completions because every maximal ideal of K⟨ϖ^k T⟩ is generated by polynomials (Conrad, irreducible components Lemma A.1.2(2), citing BGR 7.1.1/3).

Residue fields: both are the finite extension k(x₀) = A_k/m; the cotangent space and dimension statements follow from the completion isomorphism (IsLocalRing.CotangentSpace is unchanged by completion).
acceptance: At the origin of A^{1,ad}_K, O_{X^ad,0} is the ring of power series converging on some disc around 0, strictly between K[T]_{(T)} and K[[T]], and both complete to K[[T]].
For the node y² = x²(x + 1) (char K ≠ 2) the completed local ring of X^ad at the origin is K[[x, y]]/(y² − x²(x+1)), which is not a domain although O_{X,0} is.

nodes.title: The analytification morphism q_X: X^ad → X is flat
nodes.statement: Let X be a K-scheme locally of finite type. For every point x ∈ X^ad (classical or not) the local homomorphism q^♯_x: O_{X,q_X(x)} → O_{X^ad,x} is flat. Relatively (Zavyalov Lemma 6.7): for a strongly noetherian Tate affinoid S = Spa(A, A⁺) and a scheme X locally of finite type over Spec A, the morphism X ×_{Spec A} S → X is flat.
hypotheses: K complete of rank one (absolute case); S a strongly noetherian Tate affinoid (relative case)
proofSteps: Reduce to X = Spec C affine and a chart Spa(A_k, A_k°) containing x, with C → A_k the chart map.

C → A_k is flat: A_k is noetherian, so it suffices that C_{n} → (A_k)_m is flat for every maximal ideal m of A_k over n ⊆ C; this local map of noetherian local rings induces an isomorphism on completions (the argument of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-completed-local-rings, Conrad Lemma A.1.2(2)), hence is flat.

O_{X^ad,x} is the filtered colimit of the rings A_U over rational neighbourhoods U of x in the chart, each A_k → A_U flat (Wedhorn Proposition 8.30; anchor Layer 4.1; tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.flat_toCompletionLoc), so O_{X^ad,x} is flat over A_k, hence over C and over its localisation O_{X,q_X(x)}.

Relative case: Zavyalov's proof reduces, by the closed-immersion compatibility of stalks, to X = A^d_A, then by scaling to the relative unit polydisc, and factors Spa(A⟨T⟩) → Spec A⟨T⟩ → Spec A[T] into two flat maps.
acceptance: The Gauss point x of the unit disc: O_{X^ad,x} is a field extension of K(T) = O_{A¹,η}, flat as every module over a field.
Consequently F ↦ q_X^*F is exact on O_X-modules (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-of-modules).

nodes.title: Analytification of O_X-modules F ↦ F^ad = q_X^*F, its exactness, and analytified ideal sheaves
nodes.statement: For a K-scheme X locally of finite type and an O_X-module F, put F^ad := q_X^*F = O_{X^ad} ⊗_{q_X⁻¹O_X} q_X⁻¹F, the pullback of sheaves of modules along the morphism of ringed spaces q_X: X^ad_ → X (mathlib:SheafOfModules.pullback for the continuous functor of opens V ↦ q_X⁻¹(V) and the ring map q_X^♯; O_{X^ad} regarded as a sheaf of rings). Then F ↦ F^ad is an exact functor O_X-Mod → O_{X^ad}-Mod, it commutes with tensor products and with pullback along analytified morphisms ((h^*G)^ad ≅ (h^ad)^*G^ad), (O_X)^ad = O_{X^ad}, and for a quasi-coherent ideal I ⊆ O_X the map I^ad → O_{X^ad} is injective with image the ideal sheaf I·O_{X^ad} of the closed adic subspace V(I)^ad (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-immersions). The same holds relatively for X ×_Y S → X with S a strongly noetherian Tate affinoid.

coherence of F^ad for coherent F uses the coherent-sheaf notion of AdicSpacesPartII:R3/coherent-sheaf and is proved there
proofSteps: Define F^ad as the pullback of sheaves of modules along q_X (mathlib:SheafOfModules.pullback; the structure sheaf of X^ad is the anchor's sheaf of complete rings with its topology forgotten).
Exactness: pullback is right exact, and left exact because the stalk maps O_{X,q(x)} → O_{X^ad,x} are flat (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-map-flat); exactness of sheaves is checked on stalks.
Tensor compatibility and (O_X)^ad = O_{X^ad}: general properties of pullback of modules along a morphism of ringed spaces (mathlib:SheafOfModules.pullback and its monoidal structure).
Pullback along analytified morphisms: q_{X₂} ∘ h^ad_ = h ∘ q_{X₁} and pullback is pseudo-functorial (mathlib:SheafOfModules.pullbackComp).

Ideal sheaves: tensoring 0 → I → O_X with the flat O_{X^ad,x} over O_{X,q(x)} keeps the map injective, and its image is I·O_{X^ad}, the ideal of V(I)^ad by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-immersions (ii).

nodes.title: Continuous differentials of an analytification: Ω_{X^ad/Y^ad} is the analytification of Ω_{X/Y}
nodes.statement: Let h: X → Y be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type over a scheme B₀ and S → B₀ as in AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification (in particular B₀ = Spec K, S = Spa K). Write h_S: X_S → Y_S for the analytified morphism and q_X: X_S → X. There is a unique isomorphism of O_{X_S}-modules Ω_{X_S/Y_S} ≅ O_{X_S} ⊗_{q_X⁻¹O_X} q_X⁻¹Ω_{X/Y} (the analytification of Ω_{X/Y}, AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-of-modules) compatible with the universal derivations, where Ω_{X_S/Y_S} is the sheaf of continuous differentials of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/continuous-differentials. On charts X = Spec C, Y = Spec B', C = B'[T₁,…,Tₙ]/I, over an affinoid chart Spa(A', A'⁺) of Y_S with chart Spa(A_k, A_k⁺) of X_S, it is the isomorphism of finite A_k-modules A_k ⊗_C Ω_{C/B'} → Ω_{A_k/A'}, 1 ⊗ dTᵢ ↦ dTᵢ, where Ω_{C/B'} is the Kähler module (mathlib:KaehlerDifferential).
hypotheses: h locally of finite type; continuous differentials exist for morphisms locally of weakly finite type between adic spaces (Huber 1996 (1.6.2)); on the charts the maps A' → A_k are of topologically finite type
proofSteps: Chart presentation of continuous differentials: for A_k = A'⟨T⟩_{E(k)}/I·A'⟨T⟩_{E(k)}, Ω_{A_k/A'} is the quotient of the free module ⊕ A_k dTᵢ by the submodule generated by the differentials of the elements of I (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/continuous-differentials, Huber 1996 (1.6.2)(i) together with the conormal sequence of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/first-fundamental-sequence).

Algebraic presentation: Ω_{B'[T]/B'} is free on the dTᵢ (mathlib:KaehlerDifferential.mvPolynomialBasis) and Ω_{C/B'} is its quotient by the differentials of I (conormal sequence, mathlib:KaehlerDifferential.exact_kerCotangentToTensor_mapBaseChange).
Both presentations have the same generators and relations, so dTᵢ ↦ dTᵢ defines an isomorphism A_k ⊗_C Ω_{C/B'} ≅ Ω_{A_k/A'}; the formula d(φ(c)) = image of dc identifies the two derivations.

Compatibility with the chart embeddings R_k ⊆ R_h and with rational localisation (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/continuous-differentials, compatibility with localisations, Huber 1996 Proposition 1.6.3) and with the base change along Spa(A', A'⁺) → S lets the chart isomorphisms glue to a sheaf isomorphism; uniqueness holds because the dTᵢ generate.
No source states this comparison; the argument above is the proof, and the missing source is recorded as a gap.

nodes.title: Analytification preserves étale, smooth and unramified morphisms
nodes.statement: Let h: X₁ → X₂ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type over Y and S → Y as in AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification. If h is étale (resp. smooth, resp. unramified) then h_S: X₁ ×_Y S → X₂ ×_Y S is étale (resp. smooth, resp. unramified) in the sense of Huber 1996 Definition 1.6.5 (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/differentials-unramified-smooth-etale, R0/smooth-morphism, R0/unramified-morphism). In particular, for K-schemes locally of finite type, h étale / smooth / unramified ⇒ h^ad étale / smooth / unramified, and a smooth X of pure dimension d gives X^ad smooth over Spa K with Ω_{X^ad/Spa K} locally free of rank d.
hypotheses: h a morphism of Y-schemes locally of finite type; S satisfies Huber's condition
proofSteps: Smooth case, local structure: h is smooth iff locally on X₁ and X₂ the ring map is standard smooth, i.e. O(V) = B'[T₁,…,Tₙ]/(f₁,…,f_c) with det(∂fᵢ/∂Tⱼ)_{i,j ≤ c} a unit (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth.exists_isStandardSmooth, mathlib:Algebra.IsStandardSmooth, mathlib:Algebra.SubmersivePresentation).

On the chart A_k = A'⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩_{E(k)}/(f₁,…,f_c) of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affine-chart-analytification over an affinoid Spa(A', A'⁺) of X₂ ×_Y S, the same Jacobian minor is a unit. Writing A'⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩_{E(k)} = A''⟨T₁,…,T_c⟩_{E(k)} with A'' = A'⟨T_{c+1},…,Tₙ⟩_{E(k)} (iteration of restricted series, anchor Layer 0.5), Huber 1996 Proposition 1.7.1 ((ii) ⇒ (i), AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-local-structure) shows that the chart is étale over the relative polydisc Spa A'', which is smooth over Spa A' (Huber 1996 Proposition 1.6.7, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/infinitesimal-criteria); composites of étale and smooth morphisms are smooth (1.6.8).
Étale case: étale = smooth of relative dimension 0, i.e. c = n in the previous step, so the chart is étale by 1.7.1 directly (this is Huber 1996 Corollary 1.7.3(i)); étaleness is local on the source.

Unramified case: Ω_{X₁/X₂} = 0, so Ω_{X₁,S/X₂,S} = 0 by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-kahler-differentials, and a morphism locally of finite type with vanishing continuous differentials is unramified (Huber 1996 Proposition 1.6.9, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/infinitesimal-criteria).
Local freeness of Ω for smooth X of pure dimension d: AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-kahler-differentials and local freeness of Ω_{X/K}.
acceptance: For n invertible in K, the Kummer map G_m → G_m, x ↦ xⁿ, is finite étale; its analytification A^{1,ad} \ {0} → A^{1,ad} \ {0} is finite étale.
The standard étale algebra K[X]_{P'}/(P) (P monic separable) analytifies on each chart to Spa of K⟨ϖ^k X⟩⟨1/P'⟩/(P), étale by the Jacobian criterion.
The ramified map T ↦ T² (char K ≠ 2) is étale away from 0, and its analytification is étale exactly away from the point 0.

nodes.title: Rigid analytification X ↦ X^an of schemes locally of finite type over K
nodes.statement: For a K-scheme X locally of finite type there is a rigid-analytic space X^an with a morphism of locally G-ringed K-spaces i_X: X^an → X that is final among rigid spaces over K with such a morphism: for every rigid space Y over K, composition with i_X is a bijection Hom_{Rig_K}(Y, X^an) → Hom_K(Y, X). X ↦ X^an is a functor; A^{n,an} is the union of the closed polydiscs of radius |c|^{-j} (0 < |c| < 1); for affine X = V(I) ⊆ A^n, X^an is the closed analytic subspace of A^{n,an} cut out by I; and i_X is a bijection onto the closed points of X.
hypotheses: K complete of rank one; X locally of finite type over K
proofSteps: A morphism Y → Spec C from a rigid space is a K-algebra map C → O_Y(Y) (Conrad irred. Lemma A.1.1, the rigid form of Stacks 01I1).

A^{n,an}: glue the balls D_j ≅ B^n along D_j = {|ξ_{i,j+1}| ≤ |c|} ⊆ D_{j+1}; by the maximum modulus principle a map from an affinoid Sp(A) to A^{n,an} is an n-tuple of elements of A (Conrad AWS Example 2.4.3).
Affine X = Spec K[T]/I: the closed analytic subspace V(I) ⊆ A^{n,an} represents Hom_K(·, X).
General X: glue the affine pieces along Zariski opens, which are admissible and satisfy the universal property of U^an (method of SGA 1 XII 1.1, Conrad irred. Appendix A.1).
Closed points: Spec(k')^an = Sp(k') for finite k'/K, and closed points of X are the images of K-morphisms Spec k' → X (Conrad irred. Lemma A.1.2(1)).
acceptance: (A¹_K)^an is not quasi-compact; (Spec L)^an = Sp(L) for L/K finite.
The analytification of the affine line with doubled origin is not quasi-separated (Conrad irred. Appendix A.1).

nodes.title: r_K is fully faithful, generates the lft adic spaces, restricts to an equivalence on quasi-separated objects, and detects affinoids
nodes.statement: Let K be complete of rank one. (i) r_K: Rig_K → Adic_K is fully faithful (Huber 1994 4.5(ii)). (ii) The smallest saturated full subcategory of adic spaces over Spa(K, K°) containing the image of r_K (closed under open subspaces, open covers and isomorphism) consists of the adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°) (4.5(iii)). (iii) r_K restricts to an equivalence between quasi-separated rigid-analytic spaces over K and quasi-separated adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°) (4.5(iv); Huber 1996 (1.1.11), also over a rigid base X and r_K(X)). (iv) For a rigid space X, r_K(X) is affinoid iff X is affinoid (4.5(v)).
hypotheses: K complete of rank one; in (iii) both sides quasi-separated
proofSteps: (i), (iii): from the universal property of r_K (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor) and the bijection between quasi-compact admissible opens of a quasi-separated X and quasi-compact opens of r_K(X); Huber states that (i)–(iv) follow from the proof of 4.3 without writing the argument, and cites [Huber 1993, 4.6] for (i); the write-up is recorded as a gap.

(ii): every adic space locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°) is covered by affinoid opens Spa(B, B⁺) with (K, K°) → (B, B⁺) of topologically finite type (Huber 1994 3.6), and then B⁺ = B° (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/tft-plus-ring-power-bounded), so each such piece is r_K(Sp B).
(iv): if r_K(X) = Y is affinoid then (K, K°) → (O_Y(Y), O⁺_Y(Y)) is of topologically finite type (Huber 1994 3.6), so O⁺_Y(Y) = O_Y(Y)° and Y ≅ r_K(Sp O_Y(Y)); by (i) X ≅ Sp O_Y(Y).
acceptance: The adic affine line A^{1,ad}_K is quasi-separated and locally of finite type, so it is r_K of the rigid affine line.
The open unit disc {|T| < 1} ⊆ Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) is not affinoid, matching the rigid open disc not being affinoid.

nodes.title: Separated, partially proper and proper morphisms of rigid spaces versus their adic counterparts (Huber 1996 1.3.19)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of rigid-analytic spaces over K (K complete of rank one), with Kiehl's notions: separated (diagonal a closed immersion), partially proper (relative compactness of affinoid pieces, BGR/Kiehl) and proper (= quasi-compact and partially proper, AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space). (i) f is separated iff r_K(f) is separated (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/separated-morphism). (ii) If f is partially proper then r_K(f) is partially proper (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/partially-proper-morphism); the converse holds when K° is discretely valued. (iii) If f is proper then r_K(f) is proper (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism); the converse holds when K° is discretely valued. (iv) If f is locally quasi-finite, the converses in (ii)–(iii) hold for arbitrary K (Huber 1996 Lemma 1.5.9, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/quasi-finite-and-finiteness-criteria).
hypotheses: K complete of rank one; the converses of (ii)–(iii) need K° discrete in the source
the proofs of (i) and of the converses are in Huber's habilitation [Hu4, 3.11.21] and Lütkebohmert [L1], neither read
proofSteps: (ii), (iii) forward: relative compactness U ⋐_W V of affinoid pieces yields existence of centres for valuation rings, i.e. the valuative criterion of Huber 1996 Corollary 1.3.9 for r_K(f) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/separated-proper-partially-proper); the source calls this easy and points to the proof of 1.5.9. Properness then follows from Lemma 1.3.4 (proper = partially proper + quasi-compact), quasi-compactness being preserved by r_K on quasi-separated spaces.
(i) and the converses of (ii)–(iii): delegated by the source to [Hu4, 3.11.21(ii)] and to [L1] with 1.3.18(iii) (formal models over a discrete valuation ring); recorded as a gap.
(iv): Huber 1996 Lemma 1.5.9 (read with proof by the reviewed decomposition).

nodes.title: Closures of constructible sets are compatible with analytification; closedness is detected on X^ad
nodes.statement: Let X be a K-scheme locally of finite type and T ⊆ X a locally constructible subset. Then q_X⁻¹(closure(T)) = closure(q_X⁻¹(T)) in X^ad. Consequently T is closed (resp. open, resp. dense) in X iff q_X⁻¹(T) is closed (resp. open, resp. dense) in X^ad.
hypotheses: K complete of rank one; X locally of finite type over K; T locally constructible (for instance the image of an immersion)
proofSteps: q_X is continuous, so q_X⁻¹(closure T) is closed and contains closure(q_X⁻¹ T).

Reduction to classical points: let r ∈ q_X⁻¹(closure T) and N a rational neighbourhood of r in a chart. N ∩ q_X⁻¹(closure T) is a nonempty constructible subset of the chart, so it contains a classical point r' (classical points are dense for the constructible topology, Huber 1993 Corollary 4.2); N is also a neighbourhood of r', and w = q_X(r') is a closed point of closure(T) (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-points).

Classical case: write T as a finite union of locally closed sets E; w ∈ closure(E) for some E, and w is a specialisation of a point of E (Stacks 0060, 02JQ). Let Z = closure(E) with reduced structure, J the ideal of Z \ E. If N ∩ q_X⁻¹(E) were empty, J would vanish at every point of the neighbourhood N ∩ Z^ad of r' (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-immersions), hence be nilpotent on an affinoid neighbourhood of r' (a function vanishing at all classical points of a K-affinoid lies in every maximal ideal, and the nilradical of a K-affinoid algebra is the intersection of its maximal ideals — the Jacobson property, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-jacobson; residue fields at maximal ideals are finite by AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-residue-fields-finite), hence in Ô_{Z^ad,r'} ≅ Ô_{Z,w} (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-completed-local-rings), hence J_w is nilpotent (faithful flatness of completion) and Z \ E contains all generalisations of w, contradicting w being a specialisation of a point of E.

Closedness: if q_X⁻¹(T) is closed then q_X⁻¹(closure T) = q_X⁻¹(T), and surjectivity of q_X (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-points (i)) gives closure(T) = T. Openness and density follow by complements.
acceptance: The image of the diagonal of the affine line with doubled origin is not closed, and neither is its preimage in the analytification of the self-product; this is how non-separatedness is seen on X^ad.

nodes.title: X is connected iff X^ad is connected
nodes.statement: Let X be a K-scheme locally of finite type (K complete of rank one). Then X is connected iff X^ad is connected; more precisely, T ↦ q_X⁻¹(T) is a bijection from the open and closed subsets of X to those of X^ad.
hypotheses: K complete of rank one; X locally of finite type
proofSteps: Injectivity and preservation of clopenness: q_X is continuous and surjective (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-points).

Surjectivity: X is connected iff X^an is connected (Conrad, irreducible components Theorem A.1.3(1), via global irreducible components and chains of components, Theorem 2.3.1 there); X^an is connected in the rigid sense iff r_K(X^an) is connected, because the ringed topoi agree (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-topos-equivalence) and a decomposition into two disjoint admissible opens is a decomposition of the terminal sheaf; r_K(X^an) ≅ X^ad (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytification-comparison). Apply this to each connected component of X (open, as X is locally noetherian).
acceptance: A¹_K is connected, so A^{1,ad}_K is connected although its underlying space is not locally connected in the naive sense of the classical points.
Spec(K × K) analytifies to two points.

nodes.title: The analytified projective space P^{n,ad} → Spa K is proper; relatively (P^n_Y)^ad → Y^ad is proper
nodes.statement: For every n ≥ 0 the morphism (P^n_K)^ad → Spa(K, K°) is proper in Huber's sense (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism), and (P^n_K)^ad is covered by the n+1 closed unit polydiscs D_i = {|T_j| ≤ |T_i| for all j}, i = 0,…,n. For a K-scheme Y locally of finite type, (P^n_Y)^ad ≅ (P^n_K)^ad ×_{Spa K} Y^ad → Y^ad is proper. Relatively, for a scheme Y and an analytic adic space S satisfying Huber's condition with a morphism S_ → Y, P^n_Y ×_Y S → S is proper; over an affinoid Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ S it is covered by the n+1 relative closed unit polydiscs Spa(A⟨T_j/T_i⟩, (A⁺⟨T_j/T_i⟩)^~).
hypotheses: K complete of rank one
proofSteps: Cover: the i-th standard affine chart is A^n with coordinates T_j/T_i, and D_i is its closed unit polydisc, an affinoid (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-affine-space); every point x lies in some D_i: the finitely many values |T_j/T_i|_x in the totally ordered value group have a maximum (choose i with |T_j(x)| ≤ |T_i(x)|). Hence (P^n)^ad is quasi-compact.

Separated: P^n_K is separated (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.isSeparated), so its diagonal is a closed immersion, whose analytification is the diagonal of (P^n)^ad (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-fibre-products) and a closed embedding (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-immersions); hence the diagonal of (P^n)^ad has closed image.

Universally closed (valuative criterion, Huber 1996 Corollary 1.3.9, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/separated-proper-partially-proper): a valuation ring (x, A) with x ∈ (P^n)^ad has its centre in the polydisc D_i chosen as above, because the coordinates T_j/T_i take values in the valuation ring; centres are unique by separatedness.

Alternatively: P^{n,an} is Kiehl-proper (Conrad AWS Example 3.2.5) and properness passes to r_K (forward direction of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/proper-separated-comparisons (iii)), with r_K(P^{n,an}) ≅ (P^n)^ad (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytification-comparison).

Relative: (P^n_Y)^ad ≅ (P^n_K)^ad ×_{Spa K} Y^ad (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-fibre-products) and properness is stable under adic base change (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/proper-base-change). Over an analytic S the same three steps apply verbatim with the relative polydiscs Spa(A⟨T_j/T_i⟩) over affinoids Spa(A, A⁺) of S (quasi-compact over S), the relative diagonal, and Huber's valuative criterion for morphisms of analytic adic spaces.
acceptance: P^{1,ad}_K is the union of two closed unit discs glued along the annulus {|T| = 1}; it is proper and O(P^{1,ad}_K) = K (Hübner §4).
The open subspace A^{1,ad} ⊆ P^{1,ad} is not closed: its complement is the classical point ∞.

nodes.title: Separatedness and properness comparison: f is separated (proper) iff f^ad is
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of K-schemes locally of finite type (K complete of rank one). (i) f is separated iff f^ad is separated (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/separated-morphism). (ii) If f is proper then f^ad is proper (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism). (iii) If f is of finite type (quasi-compact) and f^ad is proper, then f is proper. In particular a K-scheme X of finite type is separated (resp. proper) iff X^ad is separated (resp. proper) over Spa(K, K°); for instance P^{n,ad} is proper and A^{1,ad} is separated but not proper. (ii′) Relatively: for a proper morphism f: X → Y of schemes and an analytic adic space S satisfying Huber's condition with S_ → Y, the projection X ×_Y S → S is proper; the forward direction of (i) also holds relatively.
hypotheses: K complete of rank one; in (iii) f quasi-compact (A^{1,ad} → Spa K is not quasi-compact, and neither is A¹ → Spec K proper)
proofSteps: (i) ⇒: Δ_f is a closed immersion, (Δ_f)^ad = Δ_{f^ad} (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-fibre-products) is a closed embedding (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-immersions), so its image is closed; f^ad is locally of finite type, hence locally of weakly finite type (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-type-morphism-classes): f^ad is separated in the sense of Huber 1996 1.3.1.

(i) ⇐: Δ_f is an immersion (Stacks 01KJ), quasi-compact because X ×_Y X is locally noetherian (Stacks 01OX); the image of Δ_{f^ad} = (Δ_f)^ad is q⁻¹(Δ_f(X)) (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-immersions (iii)). If it is closed, Δ_f(X) is closed by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-constructible-closure, so Δ_f is a closed immersion.

(ii): properness of f^ad is local on Y^ad, so let Y be affine, hence noetherian. By Chow's lemma (Stacks 0200) there are a proper surjective π: X' → X and an immersion X' → P^n_Y, which is a closed immersion because f∘π is proper and P^n_Y is separated. Thus (f∘π)^ad is a closed embedding (proper: AdicSpacesPartII:R0/closed-embedding-proper) followed by (P^n_Y)^ad → Y^ad (proper: AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-projective-space-proper), hence proper (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/proper-comp). π^ad is surjective after any base change (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-surjective; AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-points), so for closed Z ⊆ X^ad_T the image f^ad_T(Z) = (f∘π)^ad_T((π^ad_T)⁻¹ Z) is closed (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/universally-closed-of-surjective): f^ad is universally closed; it is separated by (i) and locally of +weakly finite type, hence proper.

(ii′): properness is local on S, so let S = Spa(A, A⁺) be affinoid, mapping into Spec B ⊆ Y; A is noetherian, and X ×_Y S = (X ×_Y Spec A) ×_{Spec A} S (schemePullback.trans), so replace Y by the noetherian scheme Spec A and run the argument of (ii) (with AdicSpacesPartII:R0/proper-base-change for the base change to S) with the relative projective space of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-projective-space-proper; this is the adic form of Zavyalov Remark 6.3 and of the remark after Huber 1996 Lemma 3.7.3 used by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H5.

(iii): f is separated by (i). With Y affine noetherian, Chow's lemma gives π: X' → X proper surjective and an open immersion j of X' onto a dense open of a closed subscheme P̄ ⊆ P^n_Y. (f∘π)^ad = f^ad ∘ π^ad is proper by (ii) and the hypothesis; since P̄^ad → Y^ad is separated, j^ad is proper (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/proper-of-comp-separated), so its image q⁻¹(j(X')) is open and closed in P̄^ad. By AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-constructible-closure j(X') is closed in P̄, hence equal to P̄ by density; so f∘π: X' ≅ P̄ → Y is proper, and f is proper because π is surjective and f is separated of finite type (Stacks 03GN).
acceptance: P^{n,ad}_K → Spa K is proper; the affine line A^{1,ad}_K is separated but not proper (not quasi-compact).

nodes.title: For f of finite type: f is finite (resp. a closed immersion) iff f^ad is
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of finite type between K-schemes locally of finite type (K complete of rank one). Then f is finite iff f^ad is finite (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-morphism), and f is a closed immersion iff f^ad is a closed embedding (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings).
hypotheses: f of finite type (quasi-compact); K complete of rank one
proofSteps: ⇒ in both cases: AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-finite and AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-immersions.

Finite ⇐: finite morphisms of adic spaces are proper (Huber 1996 Lemma 1.4.5(ii), AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-morphisms), so f is proper by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-separated-proper (iii). For a closed point y the fibre X_y analytifies to the fibre of f^ad over the classical point above y (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-fibre-products), which is finite over Spa(k(y), k(y)°), hence a finite set; so X_y has finitely many closed points, hence is finite (a scheme of finite type over a field with finitely many closed points is zero-dimensional). The locus of y with dim X_y ≥ 1 is constructible (Chevalley) and contains no closed point, so it is empty: f is quasi-finite. Proper and quasi-finite over a locally noetherian base is finite (Stacks 02OG).

Closed immersion ⇐: f is finite by the previous step. The cokernel Q of O_Y → f_*O_X is coherent, and Q^ad is the cokernel of O_{Y^ad} → f^ad_* O_{X^ad} (chart formula C ⊗_B A of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-finite and exactness of analytification, AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-of-modules), which vanishes because f^ad is a closed embedding. By Nakayama at closed points and the completed-local-ring comparison (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-completed-local-rings), Q = 0; a finite morphism with O_Y → f_*O_X surjective is a closed immersion.
acceptance: The normalisation of the cuspidal cubic A¹ → V(y² − x³), t ↦ (t², t³), is finite and bijective but not a closed immersion; its analytification is finite, bijective on points and not a closed embedding (the stalk map at the cusp is not surjective).
G_m → A¹ is not finite, and neither is its analytification (preimage of the unit disc is not affinoid).

nodes.title: f is étale (resp. smooth) iff f^ad is
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of K-schemes locally of finite type (K complete of rank one). Then f is étale (resp. smooth, resp. unramified) iff f^ad is étale (resp. smooth, resp. unramified) in the sense of Huber 1996 Definition 1.6.5.
hypotheses: K complete of rank one
proofSteps: ⇒: AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-etale-smooth.

Reduction to closed points: the étale, smooth and unramified loci of f are open (Zariski) and X is Jacobson (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType.jacobsonSpace), so it suffices to check closed points x, with y = f(x) and the classical points x', y' above them (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-points).

Unramified: Ω_{X^ad/Y^ad} = (Ω_{X/Y})^ad (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-kahler-differentials) vanishes near x' iff Ω_{X/Y,x} ⊗ Ô_{X,x} = 0 (completed local rings agree, AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-completed-local-rings), iff Ω_{X/Y,x} = 0 (faithful flatness of completion, Nakayama).

Flatness: O_{Y^ad,y'} → O_{X^ad,x'} flat (étale or smooth adic morphisms are flat at maximal points, Huber 1996 Proposition 1.7.5, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-flat-unramified) implies Ô_{Y,y} → Ô_{X,x} flat, hence O_{Y,y} → O_{X,x} flat (flatness is detected on completions of local noetherian rings).

Smooth: flat at x and Ω_{X/Y,x} generated by dim_x X_y elements (rank of Ω_{X^ad/Y^ad} = relative dimension, Huber 1996 Proposition 1.6.9, and dimension of fibres equal by completed local rings) gives smoothness at x (Stacks 01V9); étale = smooth + unramified.
acceptance: The Frobenius-type map A¹ → A¹, T ↦ T^p over K of characteristic p is flat, not étale; its analytification is not étale (Ω = K dT ≠ 0 relatively).
T ↦ T² (char K ≠ 2) is not étale at 0 and its analytification is not étale at the classical point 0.

nodes.title: Analytic groups: analytification of group schemes, finite locally free group schemes, abelian varieties and isogenies
nodes.statement: Let Sch^{lft}_K be the category of K-schemes locally of finite type (a full subcategory of Over(Spec K) closed under finite products, with its cartesian monoidal structure) and Adic^{lft}_K the category of adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa K = Spa(K, K°), which has finite products X ×_{Spa K} Y (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence) and terminal object Spa K. Because (·)^ad preserves finite products (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-fibre-products), it is a monoidal functor and carries group objects to group objects: a group scheme (G, m, e, i) locally of finite type over K gives the analytic group G^ad with multiplication m^ad, unit e^ad: Spa K → G^ad and inverse i^ad, and a homomorphism φ gives the homomorphism φ^ad; commutative group schemes give commutative group objects. Relatively, for a group scheme G → Y locally of finite type and S → Y as in AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification, G ×_Y S is a group object over S. Properties: (a) for an affinoid Spa(D, D⁺) over Spa K, the group of its points in G^ad is G(D); (b) if G is finite locally free of rank d over Y then G^ad → Y^ad is finite, with O over each affinoid finite projective of rank d; (c) if A is an abelian variety over K then A^ad is a commutative analytic group that is proper, smooth of dimension dim A and connected over Spa K; (d) if φ: A → B is an isogeny (a finite surjective homomorphism) then φ^ad is a finite surjective homomorphism whose kernel A^ad ×_{B^ad, e^ad} Spa K is (ker φ)^ad, a finite analytic group.
hypotheses: K complete of rank one; group schemes locally of finite type over K (resp. over Y)
the target category is adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa K, where finite products exist
proofSteps: Adic^{lft}_K has finite products (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence) and a terminal object, hence a cartesian monoidal structure (mathlib:CategoryTheory.CartesianMonoidalCategory).

The analytification functor preserves the terminal object and binary products (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-fibre-products), so it carries a monoidal structure (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.Monoidal.ofChosenFiniteProducts) and maps group objects to group objects (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.mapGrp, mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrpObj).
(a): AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-universal-property; the group law on points is induced by m.
(b): AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-finite.

(c): commutativity is preserved by mapGrp (Mathlib's rigidity gives commutativity of A: tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.isCommMonObj); properness by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-separated-proper; smoothness and dimension by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-etale-smooth with tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.smooth; connectedness by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-connected (A is geometrically integral).

(d): finiteness and surjectivity by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-finite and AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-surjective (tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.isIsogeny_iff: an isogeny is finite and surjective); the kernel is the fibre product A ×_{B, e} Spec K, preserved by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-fibre-products.
acceptance: G_a^ad = A^{1,ad}_K with addition, and G_m^ad = A^{1,ad}_K \ {0} with multiplication.

nodes.title: A finite locally free surjection of adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa K is an effective epimorphism
nodes.statement: Let p: X → Y be a morphism of adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa K that is finite, surjective and locally free (for every open affinoid V ⊆ Y, p⁻¹(V) is affinoid and O(p⁻¹V) is a finite projective O(V)-module). Then for every adic space Z locally of finite type over Spa K, composition with p is a bijection from Hom_{Spa K}(Y, Z) onto the set of morphisms h: X → Z with h ∘ pr₁ = h ∘ pr₂ on X ×_Y X; i.e. Y is the coequalizer of X ×_Y X ⇉ X in Adic^{lft}_K.
hypotheses: K complete of rank one; X, Y, Z locally of finite type over Spa K
the statement is not claimed for test objects Z outside Adic^{lft}_K; this is recorded as a gap
proofSteps: Injectivity: p is surjective and, O(V) → O(p⁻¹V) being injective, determined maps agree (morphisms into Z are determined by the underlying map and the pullback of functions).

Topology: p is finite, hence proper and universally closed (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-morphisms), and surjective, so it is a quotient map; h is constant on fibres of p because points of X ×_Y X surject onto pairs of points with equal image (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-points), so h induces a continuous map h̄: |Y| → |Z|.

Faithful flatness on affinoids: for V = Spa(A, A°) ⊆ Y with p⁻¹V = Spa(B, B°), A → B is finite and flat; every maximal ideal of A is a classical point with a preimage (surjectivity), so A → B is faithfully flat; B ⊗̂_A B = B ⊗_A B as B is finite over A (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-algebra-over-affinoid).

Descent of functions: for an open affinoid W = Spa(C, C°) ⊆ Z and a rational V' ⊆ V with h̄(V') ⊆ W, h gives C → B' = O(p⁻¹V') whose two images in B' ⊗_{A'} B' agree; by exactness of the Amitsur complex (Stacks 023M) it factors through A' = O(V'); the map C → A' is continuous (K-algebra maps between affinoid algebras are continuous, Wedhorn Proposition 5.60) and sends C° into A°, since an element of A' power-bounded in B' has |a(x)| ≤ 1 at all points of Spa A' (surjectivity of Spa B' → Spa A'; anchor Layer 2.3 description of the plus ring).
Gluing: these affinoid morphisms V' → W agree on overlaps by injectivity, glue to Y → Z (anchor Layer 5), and compose with p to h.
acceptance: For the Kummer covering G_m^ad → G_m^ad, x ↦ xⁿ (n invertible), functions on G_m^ad invariant under μ_n-translation descend.
The finite surjection Spa(K[T]/(T²)) → Spa K is locally free, and Spa K is its coequalizer.

nodes.title: Analytification of quotient maps by finite locally free subgroups: (A/G)^ad ≅ A^ad/G^ad
nodes.statement: Let π: A → B be a homomorphism of group schemes locally of finite type over K that is finite locally free and surjective, with kernel G = A ×_{B, e} Spec K (a finite locally free subgroup scheme) — for instance the quotient A → A/G of an abelian variety by a finite locally free subgroup scheme (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3) or the isogeny E → E/C of an elliptic curve by a finite locally free subgroup (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves#2b-isogenies-and-quotients). Then π^ad: A^ad → B^ad is a finite locally free surjective homomorphism of analytic groups with kernel G^ad; the morphism A^ad ×_{Spa K} G^ad → A^ad ×_{B^ad} A^ad, (a, g) ↦ (a, a·g), is an isomorphism; and B^ad is the quotient of A^ad by the right action of G^ad in Adic^{lft}_K: for every adic space Z locally of finite type over Spa K, composition with π^ad identifies Hom(B^ad, Z) with the morphisms h: A^ad → Z satisfying h(a·g) = h(a). In this sense (A/G)^ad ≅ A^ad/G^ad.
hypotheses: π finite locally free and surjective with kernel G; the algebraic quotient is an input (constructed by AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3 for abelian schemes and by tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves 2B for elliptic curves)

the quotient property is proved against test objects locally of finite type over Spa K; the existence of quotients of analytic groups by finite flat analytic subgroups not arising from algebra is not claimed
proofSteps: π^ad is finite locally free (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-finite) and surjective (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-surjective), a homomorphism with kernel (ker π)^ad = G^ad (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-group-objects (d)).

A ×_{Spa K}... algebraic torsor isomorphism: A × G → A ×_B A, (a, g) ↦ (a, ag), is an isomorphism of schemes because on T-points (a, a') with π(a) = π(a') is equivalent to a⁻¹a' ∈ G(T); analytify with AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-fibre-products.
Hence h ∘ pr₁ = h ∘ pr₂ on A^ad ×_{B^ad} A^ad iff h(a·g) = h(a); apply AdicSpacesPartII:R1/finite-locally-free-quotient to π^ad.
acceptance: For an elliptic curve E over K and n invertible, [n]: E → E has kernel E[n]; [n]^ad: E^ad → E^ad identifies E^ad with E^ad/E[n]^ad.

For E with a K-rational subgroup C of order p (possibly non-étale in characteristic p), (E/C)^ad is the quotient of E^ad by C^ad; in characteristic p with C = ker(Frobenius) the quotient map is the analytified relative Frobenius, finite flat of degree p and purely inseparable.

nodes.title: Invariant differentials of an analytified group: ω_{G^ad/Y^ad} ≅ (ω_{G/Y})^ad
nodes.statement: Let Y be a K-scheme locally of finite type, (G, m, e, i) a group scheme over Y locally of finite type with structure map f, and put ω_{G/Y} := e^*Ω¹_{G/Y} (an O_Y-module) and ω_{G^ad/Y^ad} := (e^ad)^*Ω¹_{G^ad/Y^ad}. There is a natural isomorphism of O_{Y^ad}-modules ω_{G^ad/Y^ad} ≅ (ω_{G/Y})^ad, compatible with pullback along homomorphisms (φ^* on ω) and with base change in Y. Moreover Ω¹_{G^ad/Y^ad} ≅ (f^ad)^*ω_{G^ad/Y^ad} (differentials of an analytic group are generated by invariant ones), and for G smooth of relative dimension g, ω_{G^ad/Y^ad} is locally free of rank g. For Y = Spec K, ω_{G^ad} = ω_G as K-vector spaces, and both equal the Zariski cotangent space m_e/m_e² of G at e; for G = Spec H affine this is the Hopf-algebra cotangent space I/I² of the augmentation ideal, and for an abelian variety it is the K-dual of its tangent space at 0.
hypotheses: K complete of rank one; G → Y a group scheme locally of finite type (smooth for the local-freeness statement)
proofSteps: Ω¹_{G^ad/Y^ad} ≅ (Ω¹_{G/Y})^ad (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-kahler-differentials).
(e^ad)^*(Ω¹_{G/Y})^ad ≅ (e^*Ω¹_{G/Y})^ad, using q_G ∘ e^ad_ = e ∘ q_Y and pseudo-functoriality of pullback (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-of-modules, pullbackIso).

Algebraic invariance Ω¹_{G/Y} ≅ f^*e^*Ω¹_{G/Y} (Stacks 047I) analytifies to Ω¹_{G^ad/Y^ad} ≅ (f^ad)^*ω_{G^ad/Y^ad}; local freeness of rank g for smooth G from Stacks 02G1 and exactness of analytification.

Y = Spec K: e is a K-rational point, (·)^ad over Spa K is ⊗_K K, and e^*Ω¹_{G/K} ≅ m_e/m_e² (the conormal sequence of a section, Stacks 0474), which is the Zariski cotangent space tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.ZariskiCotangentSpace; the adic side agrees by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-completed-local-rings. For affine G = Spec H it is I/I² (tauceti:TauCeti.Bialgebra.CotangentSpace).
Compatibility with homomorphisms and base change: naturality of the isomorphisms in AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-kahler-differentials and of pullback.
acceptance: G_m: ω_{G_m^ad} is spanned by dT/T, the analytification of the invariant differential of G_m.

For an elliptic curve E: y² + a₁xy + a₃y = x³ + … over K, ω_{E^ad} is spanned by the analytification of dx/(2y + a₁x + a₃) (tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.invariantDifferential), and [n]^* acts on ω_{E^ad} as multiplication by n.

For the universal elliptic curve over a modular curve, ω_{E^ad/X^ad} is the analytification of the Hodge line bundle ω_{E/X}, the sheaf whose (p−1)-st power carries the Hasse invariant used by AdicSpacesPartII:R2/hasse-domain.
