nodes.title: Rigid and adic étale, unramified and smooth morphisms agree under Huber's functor
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete rank-one nonarchimedean field and f: Y → X a morphism of rigid analytic spaces over K (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space), with r_K(f): r_K(Y) → r_K(X) the morphism of adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa K given by Huber's functor (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor). Call f étale (resp. unramified) in the rigid sense if for every point y of Y the local homomorphism O_{X,f(y)} → O_{Y,y} is flat and unramified (resp. unramified); for affinoids Y = Sp B → X = Sp A this means that A → B is flat and the universal finite differential module Ω^f_{B/A} vanishes (resp. that Ω^f_{B/A} = 0). Call f smooth in the rigid sense if Y is covered by admissible opens V each admitting an étale morphism in the rigid sense to a relative closed polydisc over X, V → 𝔹^n_X. Then: (a) r_K(f) is étale in Huber's sense (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/differentials-unramified-smooth-etale) iff f is étale in the rigid sense; (b) r_K(f) is unramified (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/unramified-morphism) iff f is unramified in the rigid sense; (c) r_K(f) is smooth (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-morphism) iff f is smooth in the rigid sense. In particular, for K-affinoid algebras A → B the morphism Spa(B, B°) → Spa(A, A°) is étale iff B ≅ A⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩/(G₁,…,Gₙ) with det(∂Gᵢ/∂Tⱼ) invertible in B (a special étale presentation). This is Huber 1996, Definition 1.7.10 and Proposition 1.7.11, as cited by Diao–Lan–Liu–Zhu (Remark 3.2.15).
hypotheses: K complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value of rank one.
f: Y → X a morphism of rigid analytic spaces over K; r_K is Huber's functor to adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa K.
Rigid étale and unramified are defined through the local rings of the rigid spaces (de Jong–van der Put §3.1); rigid smooth is 'locally étale over a relative closed polydisc'.
proofSteps: Locality: all six notions are local on Y and on X, and r_K carries admissible affinoid coverings to open affinoid coverings (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor), so one may assume X = Sp A, Y = Sp B affinoid with r_K(Y) = Spa(B, B°) and r_K(X) = Spa(A, A°).

(a), adic side: r_K(f) is étale iff Spa(B, B°) admits a standard étale presentation over Spa(A, A°) with invertible Jacobian (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-local-structure, (i) ⇔ (ii)); for K-affinoid algebras the weights may be taken trivial because A is Tate.

(a), rigid side: A → B is flat with Ω^f_{B/A} = 0 iff B has a special étale presentation (de Jong–van der Put, Observations 3.1.1 and 3.1.2, the latter reproducing Huber's proof of 1.7.1); the two presentations are the same algebraic datum, so (a) holds.

(b): unramifiedness of r_K(f) is the vanishing of the continuous differentials Ωᶜ_{B/A} (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/infinitesimal-criteria); by the presentation formula of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/continuous-differentials, Ωᶜ_{B/A} is the quotient of the free B-module on dT₁,…,dTₙ by the dG_j, which is de Jong–van der Put's Ω^f_{B/A}; its vanishing is checked at the completed local rings, which are the same for the rigid and the adic space at classical points (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-local-ring-completion), and a finite module over the Jacobson ring B vanishes iff it vanishes at every maximal ideal (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-jacobson).

(c): r_K(f) is smooth iff it is locally étale over a relative polydisc (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-local-structure, Tate case with trivial weights); r_K carries relative closed polydiscs over X to relative closed polydiscs over r_K(X), so (c) follows from (a) applied to V → 𝔹^n_X.
Huber's own proofs of 1.7.10–1.7.11 are not public; the route above uses only the listed nodes and the public de Jong–van der Put argument.
acceptance: The Kummer map T ↦ Tⁿ on the rigid annulus |T| = 1 over Q_p with p ∤ n is étale on both sides; T ↦ T^p on the closed unit disc over Q_p is neither (Jacobian pT^{p−1} vanishes at 0).
The inclusion of the affinoid subdomain {|T| ≤ |p|} into the closed unit disc is étale on both sides although K⟨T⟩ → K⟨T, T/p⟩ is not finite: étale here is not 'finite étale'.

nodes.title: Adic rings of finite ideal type and their ideals of definition
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative topological ring. An ideal J of A is an ideal of definition when J is open and every neighbourhood of 0 contains J^n for some n ≥ 1 (EGA 0, 7.1.2). The ring A is an adic ring of finite ideal type, written IsAdicRing A, when there is a finitely generated ideal I of A such that the topology of A is the I-adic topology (Mathlib IsAdic I: the powers I^n are open and form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0) and A is I-adically separated and complete (Mathlib IsAdicComplete I A). An adic noetherian ring is an adic ring of finite ideal type whose underlying ring is noetherian; then every ideal of definition is finitely generated. Conventions: completeness always includes separatedness; the topology is part of the data, so k⟦t⟧ with the discrete topology and k⟦t⟧ with the t-adic topology are different adic rings; morphisms of adic rings are continuous ring homomorphisms. For I as above, an ideal J is an ideal of definition if and only if IsAdic J holds, if and only if J is open and J^n ⊆ I for some n (EGA 0, 7.1.4(i)); so every statement below may use any ideal of definition.
hypotheses: A is a commutative ring with a topology making it a topological ring
the witnessing ideal I is finitely generated (automatic when A is noetherian)
IsAdicComplete I A: separated and complete for the I-adic filtration
proofSteps: This is a definition. Independence of the chosen ideal of definition: if IsAdic I and J is open with J^n ⊆ I, then I^m ⊆ J for some m (openness of J and IsAdic I, Mathlib isAdic_iff), so the I-adic and J-adic filtrations are cofinal and IsAdic J, IsAdicComplete J A follow (Mathlib IsAdic.isAdicComplete_iff, which reduces completeness to CompleteSpace and T2Space of the common topology).
Every ideal of definition lies in the Jacobson radical (Mathlib IsAdicComplete.le_jacobson_bot; EGA 0, 7.1.10), hence x ∈ A is a unit iff its image in A/I is a unit.

For noetherian A the set of topologically nilpotent elements is the radical of I, which is itself an ideal of definition, the largest one (EGA 0, 7.1.6–7.1.7): the radical is finitely generated, hence a power of it lies in I.
acceptance: ℤ_p with the p-adic topology, k⟦t₁,…,t_n⟧ with the (t₁,…,t_n)-adic topology and every complete noetherian local ring with the maximal-ideal-adic topology are adic noetherian rings; every ring with the discrete topology is adic with I = 0.
ℚ_p is not an adic ring: its only open ideal is ℚ_p itself, whose powers do not tend to 0.

O_K⟨X⟩ for a complete rank-one valuation ring O_K with pseudo-uniformiser ϖ, with the ϖ-adic topology, is an adic ring of finite ideal type which is not noetherian when the value group is not discrete (the finite-ideal-type setting is the one type-(S) formal schemes need).

uses.how: Spf A is defined for such A; its points are the open primes and its structure sheaf is the limit over the ideals of definition.
condition (S) asks the rings of affine formal opens to be adic with a finitely generated ideal of definition, noetherian in case (a) and not noetherian in case (b); R2 takes Spf of these rings.

the base of Grothendieck existence and algebraization is an adic noetherian ring A with ideal of definition I.

nodes.title: Noetherianity of adically complete rings and of adic completions
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and I a finitely generated ideal. (i) If R is I-adically complete (IsAdicComplete I R) and R ⧸ I is noetherian, then R is noetherian. (ii) If R is noetherian, then R̂ := AdicCompletion I R is noetherian; it is I·R̂-adically separated and complete, I^n·R̂ is the kernel of R̂ → R ⧸ I^n, and R̂ ⧸ I^n·R̂ ≅ R ⧸ I^n for all n. Consequently AdicCompletion I R with its I·R̂-adic topology is an adic noetherian ring (EGA 0, 7.2.6, 7.2.12, 7.3.1).
hypotheses: I finitely generated
(i): R is I-adically complete and R ⧸ I is noetherian
(ii): R noetherian
proofSteps: (i) Choose generators a₁,…,a_r of I. The associated graded ring gr_I R = ⊕ I^n/I^{n+1} is a quotient of (R/I)[T₁,…,T_r], hence noetherian (Mathlib MvPolynomial.isNoetherianRing).

(i) For an ideal J of R, the associated graded ideal of J in gr_I R is finitely generated; lift homogeneous generators to elements of J and show by successive approximation, using IsPrecomplete I R, that they generate J (every x ∈ J is a convergent series in them); IsHausdorff I R gives uniqueness. This is the argument of EGA 0, 7.2.6 and of the lemma isNoetherianRing_of_isAdicComplete_of_fg of mathlib4#38331, whose name and shape the node follows.

(ii) R̂ is I·R̂-adically complete because I is finitely generated (Mathlib AdicCompletion.isAdicComplete); the kernel of the evaluation R̂ → R ⧸ I^n is I^n·R̂ (Mathlib AdicCompletion.pow_smul_top_eq_ker_eval) and evaluation is surjective (Mathlib AdicCompletion.surjective_evalₐ), so R̂ ⧸ I·R̂ ≅ R ⧸ I is noetherian; apply (i).
acceptance: ℤ_p = AdicCompletion (p) ℤ and k⟦t⟧ = AdicCompletion (t) k[t] are noetherian (base cases).
For R = k[t₁, t₂, …] (infinitely many variables, not noetherian) and I = (t₁), (i) does not apply; the hypothesis that R ⧸ I is noetherian cannot be dropped.

nodes.title: The completed localisation A_{f} of an adic ring
nodes.statement: Let A be an adic ring of finite ideal type with ideal of definition I and let f ∈ A. The completed localisation is A_{f} := AdicCompletion (I·A_f) A_f, where A_f = Localization.Away f, with the I·A_{f}-adic topology; equivalently A_{f} = lim_n (A ⧸ I^{n+1})_f (EGA 0, 7.6.1–7.6.2, 7.6.15). It does not depend on the choice of I. The canonical map A → A_{f} is continuous and sends f to a unit; it has the universal property: every continuous ring homomorphism u : A → B into a complete separated linearly topologised ring B with u(f) a unit factors uniquely through a continuous homomorphism A_{f} → B (EGA 0, 7.6.6). A_{f} is an adic ring of finite ideal type with ideal of definition I·A_{f}, and A_{f} ⧸ I^{n+1}A_{f} ≅ (A ⧸ I^{n+1})_f; if A is noetherian then A_{f} is noetherian and flat over A (EGA 0, 7.6.11, 7.6.13). For g a multiple of f in A (g ∈ √(fA) mod I suffices) there is a unique continuous A-algebra map A_{f} → A_{g}.
hypotheses: A adic of finite ideal type (IsAdicRing A), with ideal of definition I
f ∈ A arbitrary; A_{f} = 0 exactly when f is nilpotent modulo I
proofSteps: Define A_{f} as the I·A_f-adic completion of A_f; I·A_f is finitely generated, so A_{f} is complete (Mathlib AdicCompletion.isAdicComplete) and A_{f}/I^{n+1}A_{f} ≅ A_f/I^{n+1}A_f = (A/I^{n+1})_f (Mathlib AdicCompletion.pow_smul_top_eq_ker_eval, AdicCompletion.surjective_evalₐ, exactness of localisation).
Independence of I: two ideals of definition give cofinal systems of powers (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring).

Universal property: given u with u(f) a unit, u factors through A_f; the preimage of each open ideal of B contains some I^n A_f by continuity, so the maps A_f → B/𝔟 factor through (A/I^n)_f and assemble by completeness of B (Mathlib IsAdicComplete.liftRingHom when B is adic; the limit over open ideals in general).

Noetherianity for noetherian A: A_f is noetherian, apply AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-completion-noetherian (ii). Flatness: A_f is flat over A and the adic completion of a noetherian ring is flat (Mathlib AdicCompletion.flat_of_isNoetherian); compose.
acceptance: For A = ℤ_p (I = (p)) and f = p, A_{f} = 0 since p is nilpotent in A/I; for f = 1, A_{f} = A.
For A = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ with I = (p, T) and f = 1 + T (a unit), A_{f} = A; for A = k⟦T⟧[X] completed along (T) (that is k[X]⟦T⟧) and f = X, A_{f} = k[X, X⁻¹]⟦T⟧.

a continuous φ : A → B induces continuous maps A_{f} → B_{φ(f)} compatible with restriction; this builds the morphism Spf B → Spf A.
for A = O_K⟨X⟩ the rings A_{f} are the rings of the affine formal opens D(f) of the formal model.

nodes.title: Restricted power series over an adic noetherian ring
nodes.statement: Let A be an adic ring of finite ideal type with ideal of definition I, and let A{T₁,…,T_r} be the ring of restricted power series (Tau Ceti restrictedMvPowerSeriesSubring r A: power series whose coefficients tend to 0 along the cofinite filter), with the topology in which the ideals I^n·A{T} form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0. Then: (i) A{T} is an adic ring of finite ideal type with ideal of definition I·A{T}, and A{T} ⧸ I^{n+1}A{T} ≅ (A ⧸ I^{n+1})[T₁,…,T_r]; (ii) if A is noetherian, A{T} is noetherian; (iii) universal property: for every complete separated linearly topologised A-algebra B (continuous structure map u) and elements b₁,…,b_r ∈ B there is a unique continuous A-algebra homomorphism A{T} → B with T_i ↦ b_i (EGA 0, 7.5.1–7.5.4).
hypotheses: A adic of finite ideal type with ideal of definition I
(ii) needs A noetherian

(iii) B complete, separated and linearly topologised; no condition on the b_i (in contrast with Huber-ring restricted series, where the b_i must be power-bounded, every element of a linearly topologised ring is power-bounded)
proofSteps: (i) A{T} = lim_n (A/I^{n+1})[T]: the reduction of coefficients modulo I^{n+1} kills all but finitely many terms of a restricted series (definition of Tau Ceti IsRestricted), giving a surjection with kernel I^{n+1}A{T} (EGA 0, 7.5.1 and the proof of 7.5.4 (ii)); completeness and separatedness pass to the limit.
(ii) A{T} is I·A{T}-adically complete with A{T}/I·A{T} = (A/I)[T] noetherian (Mathlib MvPolynomial.isNoetherianRing); apply AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-completion-noetherian (i).

(iii) Define the map on a restricted series Σ c_α T^α as Σ u(c_α) b^α, which converges because u(c_α) → 0 and B is complete and linearly topologised; uniqueness because polynomials are dense (EGA 0, 7.5.3).
acceptance: For A = ℤ_p, A{T} = ℤ_p⟨T⟩ is the ring of power series Σ a_n T^n with a_n → 0 p-adically; ℤ_p⟨T⟩/p^{n+1} = (ℤ/p^{n+1})[T].
For A discrete (I = 0), A{T} = A[T].

nodes.title: Adic algebras topologically of finite type over an adic noetherian ring
nodes.statement: Let A be an adic noetherian ring with ideal of definition I and φ : A → B a continuous homomorphism to a complete separated linearly topologised ring B. The following are equivalent (EGA 0, 7.5.5): (a) B is noetherian and I·B-adic (IsAdic (I.map φ) and IsAdicComplete), and B ⧸ I·B is a finitely generated A ⧸ I-algebra; (b) B ≅ lim_n B_n topologically as A-algebras, with B_n := B ⧸ I^{n+1}B, and B₁ = B ⧸ I²B is a finitely generated A ⧸ I²-algebra; (c) B is topologically A-isomorphic to a quotient A{T₁,…,T_r} ⧸ 𝔞 by an ideal 𝔞 (necessarily closed).
hypotheses: A adic noetherian with ideal of definition I
φ : A → B continuous, B complete separated linearly topologised
proofSteps: (c) ⇒ (a): A{T} is adic noetherian with ideal of definition I·A{T} (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/restricted-power-series-adic); quotients by ideals of a noetherian adic ring are adic noetherian with the image ideal (API IsAdicRing.quotient of AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring), and B/IB is a quotient of (A/I)[T].

(a) ⇒ (b): B ≅ lim B/I^{n+1}B since B is IB-adically complete (Mathlib IsAdicComplete); B/I²B is generated over A/I² by lifts of generators of B/IB together with generators of IB/I²B, a finite B/IB-module since B is noetherian.

(b) ⇒ (c): choose c_1,…,c_r ∈ B generating B₁ over A/I² (lifts of algebra generators of B/IB and of I-linear combinations generating IB/I²B); the continuous map u : A{T} → B with T_i ↦ c_i (universal property, AdicSpacesPartII:F0/restricted-power-series-adic (iii)) induces surjections on associated graded rings for the I-adic filtrations; since A{T} is complete, u is surjective and strict (EGA 0, 7.5.5, via the graded criterion of Bourbaki AC III §2 no 8).
acceptance: B = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ is not topologically of finite type over A = ℤ_p (p-adic topology): B is not pB-adic, since its topology is the (p,T)-adic one; condition (a) fails although B is noetherian.
B = ℤ_p⟨T⟩ ⧸ (T² − p) ≅ ℤ_p[√p] is topologically of finite type over ℤ_p.

nodes.title: Completed tensor product of adic rings of finite ideal type
nodes.statement: Let φ : A → B and ψ : A → C be continuous homomorphisms of adic rings of finite ideal type, with ideals of definition I_B ⊆ B and I_C ⊆ C. Let J ⊆ B ⊗_A C be the ideal generated by I_B ⊗ 1 and 1 ⊗ I_C (finitely generated). The completed tensor product is B ⊗̂_A C := AdicCompletion J (B ⊗_A C) with its J-adic topology. It is an adic ring of finite ideal type (ideal of definition J·(B ⊗̂_A C)), independent of the choice of I_B, I_C, and B ⊗̂_A C ⧸ J^{n+1} ≅ (B ⧸ I_B^{n+1}) ⊗_{A} (C ⧸ I_C^{n+1}) modulo J^{n+1}. Universal property (EGA 0, 7.7.6, used in EGA I, 10.7.2): the canonical continuous maps B → B ⊗̂_A C ← C induce a bijection between continuous A-algebra maps B ⊗̂_A C → D and pairs of continuous A-algebra maps (B → D, C → D), for every adic ring D of finite ideal type (more generally every complete separated linearly topologised A-algebra D). Warning: B ⊗̂_A C need not be noetherian when B and C are (EGA I, 10.7.4); it is noetherian when B is topologically of finite type over A and C is noetherian (EGA I, 10.13.5).
hypotheses: A, B, C adic rings of finite ideal type; φ, ψ continuous (not necessarily adic)
noetherianity of the result only under the finite-type hypothesis of AdicSpacesPartII:F0/topologically-finite-type-criterion
proofSteps: J is finitely generated, so B ⊗̂_A C is J-adically complete (Mathlib AdicCompletion.isAdicComplete) with quotients (B ⊗_A C)/J^n (Mathlib AdicCompletion.pow_smul_top_eq_ker_eval).
Independence: replacing I_B, I_C by other ideals of definition changes J to an ideal with cofinal powers (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring).

Universal property: continuous maps β : B → D, γ : C → D give β ⊗ γ : B ⊗_A C → D sending J into a topologically nilpotent ideal, hence continuous for the J-adic topology; extend to the completion by completeness of D (Mathlib IsAdicComplete.liftRingHom for adic D). Uniqueness: the image of B ⊗_A C is dense.
Noetherian case: if B ≅ A{T}/𝔞 (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/topologically-finite-type-criterion) then B ⊗̂_A C ≅ C{T}/𝔞C{T}, which is noetherian by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/restricted-power-series-adic (ii).
acceptance: ℤ_p⟦S⟧ ⊗̂_{ℤ_p} ℤ_p⟦T⟧ ≅ ℤ_p⟦S, T⟧ (ideals of definition (p,S), (p,T)); here neither structure map is adic.
A{S} ⊗̂_A A{T} ≅ A{S, T}.

nodes.title: Inverse limits of Mittag-Leffler systems of abelian groups
nodes.statement: Let 0 → (A_n) → (B_n) → (C_n) → 0 be a short exact sequence of inverse systems of abelian groups indexed by ℕ. (i) If (B_n) satisfies the Mittag-Leffler condition, so does (C_n); if (A_n) and (C_n) do, so does (B_n) (EGA 0_III, 13.2.1). (ii) If (A_n) satisfies the Mittag-Leffler condition, then 0 → lim A_n → lim B_n → lim C_n → 0 is exact (EGA 0_III, 13.2.2). (iii) An inverse system with surjective transition maps satisfies the Mittag-Leffler condition; a system of artinian modules does (EGA 0_III, 13.1.2). The Mittag-Leffler condition is Mathlib's CategoryTheory.Functor.IsMittagLeffler for the functor ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Type.
hypotheses: systems indexed by ℕ (a countable cofinal subset suffices)
Mittag-Leffler condition on the kernel system for (ii)
proofSteps: (i) Diagram chase with eventual images (EGA 0_III, 13.2.1).

(ii) Left exactness of lim is formal; for surjectivity, the fibres over a compatible (c_n) form an inverse system of nonempty torsors under (A_n); by Mittag-Leffler, the eventual images are nonempty with surjective transitions, and a countable inverse system of nonempty sets with surjective transitions has nonempty limit (Mathlib CategoryTheory.Functor.IsMittagLeffler with its eventual-range API).
(iii) Surjective transitions: the images are constant; artinian: descending chains of images stabilise.
acceptance: For A_n = p^n ℤ ⊂ ℤ = B_n (inclusions as transitions) the system (A_n) is not Mittag-Leffler and lim(ℤ/p^n) = ℤ_p is not the image of lim ℤ = ℤ: exactness on the right fails without the hypothesis.

nodes.title: The formal spectrum Spf A of an adic ring
nodes.statement: Let A be an adic ring of finite ideal type (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring) with ideal of definition I. The formal spectrum Spf A is the locally ringed space defined as follows. Its underlying space is the closed subspace of Spec A consisting of the open prime ideals, which is V(I) = PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus I and is homeomorphic to Spec(A ⧸ I^{n+1}) for every n via the quotient maps (EGA I, 10.1.1–10.1.2). For each n let O_n be the structure sheaf of Spec(A ⧸ I^{n+1}) transported to V(I); the structure sheaf is O_{Spf A} := lim_n O_n, the limit in sheaves of commutative rings along the reduction maps. Then: Γ(Spf A, O) ≅ A (EGA I, 10.1.3); for f ∈ A and D(f) := D(f) ∩ V(I), Γ(D(f), O) ≅ A_{f} (the completed localisation, AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-localization) and (D(f), O|_{D(f)}) ≅ Spf A_{f} (EGA I, 10.1.4); the stalk at an open prime p is colim_{f ∉ p} A_{f}, a local ring with residue field Frac(A ⧸ p), noetherian when A is noetherian (EGA I, 10.1.6). A continuous homomorphism φ : B → A induces a morphism of locally ringed spaces Spf φ : Spf A → Spf B, q ↦ φ⁻¹(q) (EGA I, 10.2.1). Convention: Spf A is a locally ringed space (Mathlib LocallyRingedSpace); the topology of the rings of sections is not part of the data (see AdicSpacesPartII:F0/locally-noetherian-formal-scheme), and for quasi-compact open U the ring Γ(U, O) carries the limit topology of the discrete rings Γ(U, O_n), recorded as an API item.
hypotheses: A adic of finite ideal type; noetherianity only for the noetherian statements (noetherian stalks)
φ continuous for functoriality
proofSteps: Underlying space: an open prime contains some power of I, hence I (primality), so the open primes are V(I); V(I) = V(I^{n+1}) and Spec(A/I^{n+1}) → Spec A is a closed embedding with image V(I^{n+1}) (Mathlib PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus, PrimeSpectrum.isClosed_zeroLocus, PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus_radical).

Structure sheaf: the reduction maps A/I^{n+2} → A/I^{n+1} induce morphisms O_{n+1} → O_n of sheaves of rings on V(I); take the limit in TopCat.Sheaf CommRingCat (limits of sheaves are computed sectionwise; Mathlib TopCat.Sheaf).

Sections over D(f): Γ(D(f), O) = lim_n Γ(D(f), O_n) = lim_n (A/I^{n+1})_f, which is A_{f} by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-localization (quotient equivalence); for f = 1 this is lim A/I^{n+1} = A because A is I-adically complete (Mathlib IsAdicComplete).
Restriction to D(f): the systems (Spec(A/I^{n+1}) restricted to D(f)) and (Spec(A_{f}/I^{n+1}A_{f})) agree, since A_{f}/I^{n+1} ≅ (A/I^{n+1})_f; hence (D(f), O|) ≅ Spf A_{f}.

Stalks: the D(f) form a basis, so the stalk at p is colim_{f∉p} A_{f}; it is local with residue field Frac(A/p), and noetherian for noetherian A (EGA 0, 7.6.17–7.6.18, recorded in AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-localization).

Functoriality: φ(I_B)^N ⊆ I_A for some N by continuity, so φ induces compatible maps B/I_B^{N(n+1)} → A/I_A^{n+1}; the induced maps on basic opens B_{g} → A_{φ(g)} (universal property of completed localisation) give the sheaf map, and stalk maps are local because φ⁻¹ of an open prime is open (EGA I, 10.2.1).
acceptance: Spf ℤ_p (p-adic) is a single point with Γ = ℤ_p and stalk ℤ_p; Spec ℤ_p has two points, so Spf ℤ_p ≠ Spec ℤ_p.
Spf k[x]⟦t⟧ (t-adic) has underlying space Spec k[x], and Γ(D(x), O) = k[x, x⁻¹]⟦t⟧.
For A discrete, Spf A = Spec A as locally ringed spaces.

nodes.title: Spf A depends only on the topology of A
nodes.statement: Let A be an adic ring of finite ideal type and I, J two ideals of definition of A. The locally ringed spaces Spf_I A and Spf_J A constructed from the systems (Spec A ⧸ I^{n+1})_n and (Spec A ⧸ J^{n+1})_n are canonically isomorphic: the isomorphism is the identity on the common underlying space V(I) = V(J) ⊆ Spec A, is compatible with the identifications of global sections with A, and commutes with the canonical morphisms Spec(A ⧸ I^{n+1}) → Spf A and Spec(A ⧸ J^{m+1}) → Spf A. Both agree with EGA's limit over the filtered set of all ideals of definition (EGA I, 10.1.1–10.1.2). Consequently Spf A is a functor of the topological ring A alone.
hypotheses: I, J ideals of definition of the same adic ring A (same topology)
proofSteps: By AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring (API isAdic_iff_of_isAdic), there are m, n with I^m ⊆ J and J^n ⊆ I; hence √I = √J and V(I) = V(J) (Mathlib PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus_radical).

The systems (A/I^{k})_k and (A/J^{k})_k are mutually cofinal among the quotients by ideals of definition (ideals of definition form a filtered fundamental system, EGA 0, 7.1.2); the limits of the corresponding structure sheaves over mutually cofinal subdiagrams are canonically isomorphic (a final subdiagram does not change the limit).
Compatibility with global sections: both identifications with A are the canonical maps A → lim A/I^k and A → lim A/J^k (Mathlib IsAdicComplete), which correspond under the cofinality isomorphism.
acceptance: For A = k[x]⟦t⟧, I = (t) and J = (t², x t) are ideals of definition; both constructions give underlying space Spec k[x] and the same sheaf.
For A = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ with I = (p, T) and J = (p², T), Spf is a single point in both constructions.

nodes.title: Morphisms into Spf A and automatic continuity
nodes.statement: Let X be a formal scheme (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/locally-noetherian-formal-scheme) and A an adic ring of finite ideal type with ideal of definition I. Taking global sections gives a bijection between morphisms of locally ringed spaces X → Spf A and ring homomorphisms φ : A → Γ(X, O_X) that are continuous on affine formal opens, i.e. such that for every affine formal open U ≅ Spf B of X the composite A → Γ(U, O_X) ≅ B is continuous; equivalently φ(a) vanishes in the residue field κ(x) for all a ∈ I and x ∈ X (EGA I, 10.2.2, 10.4.6). In particular, for adic rings A, B of finite ideal type, Hom_LRS(Spf B, Spf A) ≃ {continuous ring homomorphisms A → B}, so Spf is a fully faithful contravariant functor from adic rings of finite ideal type (with continuous homomorphisms) to locally ringed spaces, and every morphism of locally ringed spaces between formal schemes is continuous on rings of sections (it is a morphism of topologically ringed spaces in the sense of EGA I, 10.4.5).
hypotheses: X a formal scheme; A adic of finite ideal type (the ideal of definition I is finitely generated, which is used for automatic continuity)
proofSteps: Affine case, necessity: let (ψ, θ) : Spf B → Spf A be a morphism of locally ringed spaces and φ = Γ(θ) : A → B (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-spectrum, global sections). For q ∈ Spf B, locality of θ_q and the description of residue fields give ψ(q) = φ⁻¹(q); since ψ(q) is an open prime it contains I, so φ(I) ⊆ q for every open prime q of B, i.e. φ(I) ⊆ √(I_B).
Automatic continuity: I is finitely generated, so φ(I)^N ⊆ I_B for some N (each generator has a power in I_B), and φ is continuous (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring, API continuous_iff_map_le_radical).

θ is determined by φ: on basic opens, θ(D(f)) : A_{f} → B_{φ(f)} is a continuous map extending A → B, hence equal to the map given by the universal property of completed localisation (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-localization); basic opens form a basis, so θ = Spf.map φ (EGA I, 10.2.2).
Sufficiency: a continuous φ gives Spf.map φ (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-spectrum, functoriality), whose global-sections map is φ.

General X: cover X by affine formal opens U_i ≅ Spf B_i and their intersections by affine formal opens (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/locally-noetherian-formal-scheme, basis of affine formal opens); a morphism X → Spf A is the same as compatible morphisms U_i → Spf A (sheaf property of morphisms of locally ringed spaces), and a ring map A → Γ(X, O_X) is the same as compatible maps A → Γ(U_i, O) (sheaf property of O_X); apply the affine case (EGA I, 10.4.6, proof as in EGA I, 2.2.4).
acceptance: Hom(Spf ℤ_p⟦T⟧, Spf ℤ_p⟦S⟧) ≃ the maximal ideal (p, T) of ℤ_p⟦T⟧, via S ↦ image of S (continuity forces the image of S to be topologically nilpotent).
Hom(Spec F_p, Spf ℤ_p) is a single point (p ↦ 0), whereas Hom(Spec ℚ_p, Spf ℤ_p) is empty: the ring map ℤ_p → ℚ_p is not continuous for the discrete topology on ℚ_p since p is not nilpotent.

nodes.title: Formal schemes and locally noetherian formal schemes
nodes.statement: A formal scheme (of finite ideal type) is a locally ringed space X such that every point has an open neighbourhood U with (U, O_X|_U) isomorphic, as a locally ringed space, to Spf A for some adic ring A of finite ideal type (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-spectrum); such U are the affine formal opens. X is locally noetherian if every point has an affine formal open neighbourhood Spf A with A noetherian, and noetherian if moreover its underlying space is quasi-compact (EGA I, 10.4.2). Morphisms of formal schemes are morphisms of locally ringed spaces; by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/spf-morphism-correspondence they are automatically continuous on rings of sections, so this category agrees with EGA's category of formal preschemes of this type (EGA I, 10.4.5). Pinned conventions: (1) 'scheme' means Mathlib's Scheme (EGA's préschéma; no separatedness); (2) the topology on Γ(U, O_X) for an affine formal open U is recovered, not stored: it is the J-adic topology for any finitely generated ideal J ⊆ Γ(U, O_X) whose radical is the ideal of sections vanishing at every point of U; (3) every scheme is a formal scheme (take A discrete) and Scheme → FormalScheme is fully faithful (EGA I, 10.4.8).
hypotheses: affine pieces Spf A with A adic of finite ideal type; for 'locally noetherian' the A are noetherian
proofSteps: Definition. Open subspaces of formal schemes are formal schemes because basic opens D(f) of Spf A are affine formal (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-spectrum, restrictBasicOpenIso), so affine formal opens form a basis (EGA I, 10.4.3); for locally noetherian X the noetherian affine formal opens form a basis because A_{f} is noetherian for noetherian A (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-localization).

The intrinsic topology: for U ≅ Spf A the set of sections vanishing at every point is √I; a finitely generated J with √J = √I has J^n ⊆ I and I^m ⊆ J, so the J-adic and I-adic topologies agree (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring).

Schemes: Spec R with R discrete is Spf R (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-spectrum, compatibility with Spec), so the Mathlib functor Scheme.forgetToLocallyRingedSpace lands in formal schemes, fully faithfully (Mathlib Scheme.fullyFaithfulForgetToLocallyRingedSpace).
acceptance: Spf ℤ_p, Spf k⟦t⟧ and every locally noetherian scheme are locally noetherian formal schemes.
Spf O_C (O_C the ring of integers of ℂ_p with the p-adic topology) is a formal scheme that is not locally noetherian, although its underlying space is a point.
The completion of P¹_{ℤ_p} along its special fibre is a noetherian formal scheme that is not affine (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-scheme-gluing).

nodes.title: Gluing formal schemes along open subschemes
nodes.statement: A glue datum of formal schemes is a glue datum of locally ringed spaces (Mathlib LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData: pieces U_i, open immersions V_ij → U_i, isomorphisms t_ij : V_ij ≅ V_ji with the cocycle condition) in which every U_i is a formal scheme. The glued locally ringed space X is a formal scheme; each ι_i : U_i → X is an open immersion with image covering X; X is locally noetherian if every U_i is, and noetherian if moreover the index set is finite and every U_i is noetherian. Universal property: morphisms X → Y of formal schemes correspond to families of morphisms f_i : U_i → Y agreeing on the V_ij (EGA 0, 4.1.7; EGA I, 10.4.2 is local, and EGA I, 10.7.3 constructs products by gluing affine pieces as in the scheme case). Gluing commutes with FormalScheme.ofScheme (Mathlib Scheme.GlueData).
hypotheses: pieces are formal schemes (finite ideal type); cocycle condition of Mathlib GlueData
proofSteps: Form the glued locally ringed space with Mathlib LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData; each ι_i is an open immersion (Mathlib LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData.ι_isOpenImmersion).

Formal-scheme condition is local: every point lies in some ι_i(U_i), which is isomorphic to U_i and hence has affine formal neighbourhoods (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/locally-noetherian-formal-scheme); likewise for local noetherianity; quasi-compactness from finitely many quasi-compact pieces.
Universal property from the colimit property of the glued space in locally ringed spaces; morphisms of formal schemes are morphisms of locally ringed spaces.

nodes.title: Ideals of definition of a formal scheme and the thickenings X_n
nodes.statement: Let X be a formal scheme. An ideal-sheaf datum on X is, as in Mathlib Scheme.IdealSheafData, an ideal 𝒥(U) ⊆ Γ(U, O_X) for each affine formal open U, with 𝒥(D(f)) = 𝒥(U)·A_{f} for basic opens (it is the sheaf 𝒥(U)^Δ on U). It is an ideal of definition when 𝒥(U) is an ideal of definition of the adic ring Γ(U, O_X) for every affine formal open U; it suffices to check this on an affine formal open cover (EGA I, 10.3.3, 10.3.5, 10.5.1). For an ideal of definition 𝒥: (X, O_X/𝒥) is a scheme X_𝒥 (affine if X is, locally noetherian if X is), with a canonical morphism X_𝒥 → X which is a homeomorphism on spaces (EGA I, 10.5.2); O_X = lim_n O_X/𝒥^{n+1} (EGA I, 10.5.3). Notation: X_n := (X, O_X/𝒥^{n+1}), n ≥ 0. If X is locally noetherian: the powers 𝒥^{n+1} are ideals of definition and form a fundamental system; there is a largest ideal of definition 𝒯, the unique one with X_𝒯 reduced, 𝒯(U) = √(𝒥(U)) = sections vanishing at every point, and X_red := X_𝒯 (EGA I, 10.5.1, 10.5.4).
hypotheses: X a formal scheme; the largest ideal of definition and the power statements need X locally noetherian
proofSteps: On Spf A, ideals of definition of X correspond bijectively to ideals of definition J of A via J ↦ J^Δ (EGA I, 10.3.5): Γ(Spf A, 𝒥) is an open ideal and the quasi-coherence of 𝒥/J'^Δ on Spec(A/J') for a smaller ideal of definition J' identifies 𝒥 (proof of EGA I, 10.3.5, using AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-spectrum).
(X, O/𝒥) is a scheme: on Spf A it is Spec(A/J) via Spf.fromSpecQuotient (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-spectrum).
Powers: for noetherian A, (J^n)^Δ = (J^Δ)^n because (J^n)_{f} = (J_{f})^n (EGA 0, 7.6.12, recorded in AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-localization).

Largest ideal of definition: for noetherian A, √J is the largest ideal of definition of A (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring, radical_isAdic); these glue because √ commutes with completed localisation and A/√J is reduced, and uniqueness follows since X_𝒯 = X_red (EGA I, 10.5.4).
acceptance: For X = Spf ℤ_p⟦T⟧, the ideals of definition correspond to ideals J with (p,T)^m ⊆ J ⊆ (p,T); 𝒯 = (p,T)^Δ and X_red = Spec F_p.
For X = Spf O_C (not noetherian), the ideal of sections vanishing at the point is 𝔪_C, which is not finitely generated and not an ideal of definition: no largest ideal of definition exists.

nodes.title: The formal scheme attached to an adic system of thickenings
nodes.statement: An adic thickening system is a sequence of schemes X_0 → X_1 → X_2 → ⋯ with closed immersions u_n : X_n → X_{n+1} that are homeomorphisms on underlying spaces, such that, writing O_n for the structure sheaves on the common space T and 𝒥_n = ker(O_n → O_0): (a) 𝒥_n is locally nilpotent; (b) ker(O_n → O_m) = 𝒥_n^{m+1} for m ≤ n; (c) 𝒥_1 = 𝒥_1/𝒥_1² is an O_0-module of finite type. Then the locally ringed space X := (T, lim_n O_n) is a formal scheme; the maps lim O_k → O_n are surjective; 𝒥 := ker(lim O_k → O_0) is an ideal of definition with ker(lim O_k → O_n) = 𝒥^{n+1} and 𝒥/𝒥² ≅ 𝒥_1; the canonical morphisms ι_n : X_n → X form a cocone; X is locally noetherian (resp. noetherian) when X_0 is (EGA I, 10.6.3–10.6.4). On affine opens: if X_0 = Spec A_0 then every X_n = Spec A_n and X = Spf(lim A_n), with lim A_n adic of ideal of definition ker(lim A_n → A_0) (EGA 0, 7.2.7). EGA 10.6.3 without (b)–(c) produces formal preschemes that need not be of finite ideal type; those are outside this carrier.
hypotheses: closed immersions X_n → X_{n+1} that are homeomorphisms, with locally nilpotent kernels
adic conditions (b) and (c) (EGA I, 10.6.4)
proofSteps: Affine case: if X_0 = Spec A_0 is affine then each X_n is affine (a scheme with an affine closed subscheme defined by a nilpotent ideal is affine, EGA I, 5.1.9); write A_n = Γ(X_n); the system (A_n) satisfies EGA 0, 7.2.7 (surjective transitions, kernels I_n^{m+1}, I_1 finite over A_0), so A = lim A_n is adic with ideal of definition I = ker(A → A_0), A/I^{n+1} = A_n; hence (T, lim O_n) = Spf A (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-spectrum). Noetherianity of A when A_0 is noetherian: A is I-adically complete with A/I = A_0 noetherian (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-completion-noetherian (i)).
General case: every point has an open U affine in X_0, hence in every X_n; apply the affine case on U, so (T, lim O_n) is a formal scheme (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/locally-noetherian-formal-scheme).
The kernels form the ideal of definition 𝒥 with its powers (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/ideal-of-definition), computed affine-locally.
acceptance: X_n = Spec(ℤ/p^{n+1}) gives Spf ℤ_p; X_n = Spec(k[x][t]/(t^{n+1})) gives Spf k[x]⟦t⟧.
The system A_n = k[x_1, x_2, …]/((x_1,…,x_n)^n + (x_{n+1}, x_{n+2}, …)) satisfies (a) but not (b); its limit is an admissible, non-adic ring and is not covered.

nodes.title: A locally noetherian formal scheme is the colimit of its thickenings
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian formal scheme and 𝒥 an ideal of definition; let X_n = (X, O_X/𝒥^{n+1}) with the canonical closed immersions X_m → X_n and morphisms ι_n : X_n → X (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/ideal-of-definition). Then (X_n) is an adic thickening system with X_0 locally noetherian, and (X, (ι_n)) is a colimit of the diagram (X_n) in the category of formal schemes (EGA I, 10.6.2): for every formal scheme Y and compatible morphisms g_n : X_n → Y there is a unique g : X → Y with g ∘ ι_n = g_n. Consequently the canonical morphism ofThickenings(X_n) → X is an isomorphism, and ofThickenings is an equivalence from adic thickening systems with locally noetherian X_0 to pairs (X, 𝒥) of a locally noetherian formal scheme with an ideal of definition (EGA I, 10.6.4 and the remark after it).
hypotheses: X locally noetherian; 𝒥 an ideal of definition (exists: take the largest one 𝒯)
proofSteps: The system (X_n) satisfies the adic conditions: ker(O/𝒥^{n+1} → O/𝒥^{m+1}) = 𝒥^{m+1}/𝒥^{n+1} and 𝒥/𝒥² is of finite type because 𝒥 is coherent on locally noetherian X (affine-locally J/J² is a finite A/J-module, A noetherian) (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/ideal-of-definition).

Universal property: compatible g_n have one underlying continuous map (the X_n share their space) and a projective system of sheaf maps O_Y → g_*(O_X/𝒥^{n+1}); pass to the limit using O_X = lim O_X/𝒥^{n+1} (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/ideal-of-definition, structureSheafIsoLimit). The limit map has local stalk maps: this is local, and on affine pieces X = Spf A, Y = Spf B it is Spf of the continuous map B → lim A/J^{n+1} = A given by the compatible maps, by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/spf-morphism-correspondence and Mathlib IsAdicComplete.liftRingHom.
Equivalence: AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings constructs the inverse; the comparison ofThickenings(X_n) → X is the identity on spaces and the identity O_X = lim O_X/𝒥^{n+1} on sheaves.
acceptance: X = Spf ℤ_p with 𝒥 = (p): X = colim Spec(ℤ/p^{n+1}) in formal schemes; a compatible system of morphisms Spec(ℤ/p^{n+1}) → Y is a morphism Spf ℤ_p → Y.

The canonical morphism Spf ℤ_p → FormalScheme.ofScheme(Spec ℤ_p) induced by the compatible maps Spec(ℤ/p^{n+1}) → Spec ℤ_p is not an isomorphism of formal schemes (one point against two): the colimit is taken in formal schemes, not in schemes.

nodes.statement: Let X, Y be locally noetherian formal schemes with ideals of definition 𝒥 ⊆ O_X and 𝒦 ⊆ O_Y, and X_n = (X, O_X/𝒥^{n+1}), Y_n = (Y, O_Y/𝒦^{n+1}). (i) For every morphism f : X → Y, f*(𝒦)·O_X ⊆ 𝒯_X, the largest ideal of definition of X (EGA I, 10.6.10(i)). (ii) If f*(𝒦)·O_X ⊆ 𝒥 then f*(𝒦^{n+1})·O_X ⊆ 𝒥^{n+1} and f induces morphisms of schemes f_n : X_n → Y_n with commuting squares (EGA I, 10.6.7); the map f ↦ (f_n) is a bijection from {f : f*(𝒦)O_X ⊆ 𝒥} onto compatible sequences (f_n) (EGA I, 10.6.9). In particular, with 𝒥 = 𝒯_X, Hom(X, Y) ≃ lim_n Hom(X_n, Y_n) (EGA I, 10.6.10(ii)). (iii) Over a locally noetherian base S with ideal of definition ℒ, f*(ℒ)O_X ⊆ 𝒥, g*(ℒ)O_Y = 𝒦 and S_n = (S, O_S/ℒ^{n+1}): Hom_S(X, Y) ≃ lim_n Hom_{S_n}(X_n, Y_n) (EGA I, 10.6.11).
hypotheses: X, Y (and S) locally noetherian formal schemes with chosen ideals of definition
proofSteps: (i) Local on X and Y; for Spf A → Spf B given by continuous φ : B → A (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/spf-morphism-correspondence), elements of an ideal of definition of B are topologically nilpotent, so their images are topologically nilpotent in A, hence lie in √I_A = 𝒯(Spf A) (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring, isTopologicallyNilpotent_iff and radical_isAdic).

(ii) Given f with the ideal condition, the reduction f_n is the unique morphism X_n → Y_n compatible with the canonical morphisms (EGA I, 10.5.6, affine case: φ(K^{n+1}) ⊆ J^{n+1} induces B/K^{n+1} → A/J^{n+1}). Conversely a compatible (f_n) induces f = colim f_n by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-scheme-as-colimit; the ideal condition holds because, affine-locally, the limit map φ = lim φ_n satisfies φ(K) ⊆ J from the commutativity at n = 0 (EGA I, 10.6.9).
(iii) An S-morphism satisfies the ideal condition for 𝒥, 𝒦 as above; apply (ii) and note that compatibility with the structure maps is checked levelwise.
acceptance: Hom(Spf ℤ_p⟦T⟧, Spf ℤ_p⟦S⟧) ≃ lim_n Hom(Spec ℤ_p⟦T⟧/(p,T)^{n+1}, Spec ℤ_p⟦S⟧/(p,S)^{n+1}) ≃ (p, T)ℤ_p⟦T⟧ (the image of S).
For 𝒥 strictly smaller than 𝒯_X, not every morphism satisfies f*(𝒦)O_X ⊆ 𝒥: the identity of Spf k⟦t⟧ with 𝒥 = (t²) and 𝒦 = (t) does not.

nodes.title: A formal scheme of finite ideal type is the colimit of its thickenings along an ideal of definition of finite type
nodes.statement: Let X be a formal scheme of finite ideal type (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/locally-noetherian-formal-scheme: locally Spf A for adic rings A with a finitely generated ideal of definition; no noetherian hypothesis) and 𝒥 ⊆ O_X an ideal of definition of finite type, i.e. an ideal of definition (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/ideal-of-definition) such that on every affine formal open U ≅ Spf A one has 𝒥|_U = J^Δ for a finitely generated ideal of definition J ⊆ A. Put X_n = (X, O_X/𝒥^{n+1}) (n ≥ 0), with the canonical closed immersions X_m → X_n (m ≤ n) and ι_n : X_n → X. Then: (i) J^Δ = J·O_U and (𝒥|_U)^{n+1} = (J^{n+1})^Δ, so the powers 𝒥^{n+1} are ideals of definition of finite type forming a fundamental system of ideals of definition, and X_n|_U = Spec(A/J^{n+1}); (ii) (X_n)_n is an adic thickening system in the sense of AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings, with 𝒥_n = 𝒥/𝒥^{n+1}; (iii) (X, (ι_n)) is a colimit of the diagram (X_n) in the category of formal schemes: for every formal scheme Y and every family of morphisms g_n : X_n → Y with g_n ∘ (X_m → X_n) = g_m for m ≤ n, there is a unique morphism g : X → Y with g ∘ ι_n = g_n for all n. For locally noetherian X every ideal of definition is of finite type and this is AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-scheme-as-colimit.
hypotheses: X a formal scheme of finite ideal type; no noetherian hypothesis
𝒥 an ideal of definition of X of finite type
proofSteps: (i) The statement is local on X. On U ≅ Spf A, 𝒥|_U = J^Δ for a finitely generated ideal of definition J ⊆ A (Fujiwara–Kato I, Proposition 1.1.22). For f ∈ A the completed localisation A_{f} is the J-adic completion of A_f (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-localization) and, J being finitely generated, the closure of J·A_f in A_{f} is J·A_{f}; hence J^Δ = J·O_U and (J^Δ)^n = (J^n)^Δ (Fujiwara–Kato I, Proposition 1.1.20 and Corollary 1.1.21, which replace the noetherian EGA I, (10.3.6)). The J^{n+1} are ideals of definition of A forming a fundamental system (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring), so the 𝒥^{n+1} form a fundamental system of ideals of definition of X (Fujiwara–Kato I, Corollary 1.1.24), and X_n|_U = Spec(A/J^{n+1}) (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/ideal-of-definition, the scheme X_𝒥).

(ii) ker(O_{X_n} → O_{X_m}) = 𝒥^{m+1}/𝒥^{n+1} = 𝒥_n^{m+1} for 𝒥_n := 𝒥/𝒥^{n+1}; 𝒥_n is nilpotent (𝒥_n^{n+1} = 0), the transition maps are surjective, and 𝒥_1 = 𝒥/𝒥² is an O_{X_0}-module of finite type because 𝒥 is of finite type: these are conditions (a)–(c) of AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings.

(iii) EGA I, (10.6.2), whose statement and proof use only a fundamental system of ideals of definition of an arbitrary formal prescheme (EGA I, (10.6.1)); here the system (𝒥^{n+1}) of (i). Compatible g_n have a common underlying continuous map ψ : X → Y, and the maps ψ⁻¹O_Y → O_X/𝒥^{n+1} form a projective system whose limit ψ⁻¹O_Y → lim_n O_X/𝒥^{n+1} = O_X (EGA I, (10.5.3)) is the unique map of ringed spaces with g ∘ ι_n = g_n. It is a morphism of formal schemes (local on stalks) because on affine formal opens Spf A ⊆ X, Spf B ⊆ Y it is Spf of the continuous homomorphism lim_n (B → A/J^{n+1}) : B → A = lim_n A/J^{n+1} (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/spf-morphism-correspondence, AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring). Fujiwara–Kato I, Proposition 1.4.1 restates (10.6.2) for arbitrary formal schemes.
acceptance: For K a complete rank-one nonarchimedean field with non-discrete value group (so O_K⟨T⟩ is not noetherian) and X = Spf O_K⟨T⟩ with 𝒥 = ϖ·O_X: X_n = Spec (O_K/ϖ^{n+1})[T], and morphisms X → Y into any formal scheme Y are the compatible families Spec (O_K/ϖ^{n+1})[T] → Y.
For 𝒥 = ϖ²·O_X on the same X the thickenings are X'_n = Spec (O_K/ϖ^{2n+2})[T], a cofinal subsystem of the previous one, with the same colimit X.

nodes.title: Morphisms of formal schemes of finite ideal type as compatible systems of morphisms of thickenings
nodes.statement: Let X, Y be formal schemes of finite ideal type (no noetherian hypothesis) with ideals of definition of finite type 𝒥 ⊆ O_X and 𝒦 ⊆ O_Y, and X_n = (X, O_X/𝒥^{n+1}), Y_n = (Y, O_Y/𝒦^{n+1}) with ι^X_n, ι^Y_n as in AdicSpacesPartII:F0/thickening-colimit-finite-ideal-type. (i) If f : X → Y satisfies f*(𝒦)·O_X ⊆ 𝒥, then f*(𝒦^{n+1})·O_X ⊆ 𝒥^{n+1} for all n, and there are unique morphisms of schemes f_n : X_n → Y_n with ι^Y_n ∘ f_n = f ∘ ι^X_n; they satisfy f_n ∘ (X_m → X_n) = (Y_m → Y_n) ∘ f_m for m ≤ n (EGA I, (10.5.6), (10.6.7)). (ii) The map f ↦ (f_n)_n is a bijection from the set of morphisms f : X → Y with f*(𝒦)·O_X ⊆ 𝒥 onto the set of sequences of morphisms of schemes f_n : X_n → Y_n with f_n ∘ (X_m → X_n) = (Y_m → Y_n) ∘ f_m for all m ≤ n. (iii) Relative form: let S be a formal scheme of finite ideal type with an ideal of definition ℒ of finite type, S_n = (S, O_S/ℒ^{n+1}), and p : X → S, q : Y → S morphisms with p*(ℒ)·O_X ⊆ 𝒥 and q*(ℒ)·O_Y = 𝒦 (Y adic over S, with its ideal of definition ℒO_Y). Then every S-morphism u : X → Y satisfies u*(𝒦)·O_X ⊆ 𝒥, and u ↦ (u_n) is a bijection Hom_S(X, Y) ≃ lim_n Hom_{S_n}(X_n, Y_n), the limit along the maps Hom_{S_n}(X_n, Y_n) → Hom_{S_m}(X_m, Y_m), u_n ↦ u_n ×_{S_n} S_m (EGA I, (10.6.11)). In particular, for X and Y adic over S and 𝒥 = ℒO_X, 𝒦 = ℒO_Y, Hom_S(X, Y) ≃ lim_n Hom_{S_n}(X_n, Y_n) (Fujiwara–Kato I, Exercise I.1.7). For locally noetherian X, Y, S these are parts (ii)–(iii) of AdicSpacesPartII:F0/morphisms-as-compatible-systems; a formal scheme of finite ideal type need not have a largest ideal of definition, so the ideal condition in (ii) is part of the statement.
hypotheses: X, Y (and S) formal schemes of finite ideal type; no noetherian hypothesis
𝒥, 𝒦 (and ℒ) ideals of definition of finite type
(iii): p*(ℒ)·O_X ⊆ 𝒥 and q*(ℒ)·O_Y = 𝒦
proofSteps: (i) EGA I, (10.5.6) and (10.6.7) are stated and proved for arbitrary formal preschemes with ideals of definition: f*(𝒦)O_X ⊆ 𝒥 gives f*(𝒦^{n+1})O_X ⊆ 𝒥^{n+1}, and passing to quotients gives the unique morphism of locally ringed spaces f_n with ι^Y_n ∘ f_n = f ∘ ι^X_n; X_n, Y_n are schemes (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/thickening-colimit-finite-ideal-type (i)). Affine-locally f = Spf φ for a continuous φ : B → A (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/spf-morphism-correspondence), 𝒥 = J^Δ, 𝒦 = K^Δ with J, K finitely generated ideals of definition, the ideal condition is φ(K) ⊆ J, and f_n = Spec(B/K^{n+1} → A/J^{n+1}).

(ii) Given a compatible sequence (f_n), the morphisms ι^Y_n ∘ f_n : X_n → Y form a compatible family, so there is a unique f : X → Y with f ∘ ι^X_n = ι^Y_n ∘ f_n for all n (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/thickening-colimit-finite-ideal-type (iii); EGA I, (10.6.8)). The same universal property shows that f is determined by (f_n), so f ↦ (f_n) is injective.

(ii) The limit f satisfies the ideal condition (EGA I, proof of (10.6.9), with its noetherian input (10.3.6) replaced by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/thickening-colimit-finite-ideal-type (i)): locally X = Spf A, Y = Spf B, X_n = Spec A/J^{n+1}, Y_n = Spec B/K^{n+1}, f_n = Spec φ_n and f = Spf φ with φ = lim_n φ_n; commutativity of the square for m = 0 gives φ_n(K/K^{n+1}) ⊆ J/J^{n+1} for all n, so φ(K) ⊆ lim_n J/J^{n+1} = J because the open ideal J is closed (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring); hence f*(𝒦)O_X ⊆ 𝒥 (EGA I, (10.5.6)(ii)).

(iii) For an S-morphism u (q ∘ u = p): u*(𝒦)O_X = u*(q*(ℒ)O_Y)O_X = p*(ℒ)O_X ⊆ 𝒥, so (ii) applies; a compatible sequence (u_n) consists of S_n-morphisms iff its limit is an S-morphism, by uniqueness in AdicSpacesPartII:F0/thickening-colimit-finite-ideal-type (iii) applied to X → S. Since 𝒦 = ℒO_Y, Y_m = Y_n ×_{S_n} S_m, so an S_n-morphism u_n determines the S_m-morphism u_m and the sequences are the elements of the limit (EGA I, remark after (10.6.11)).
acceptance: For K a complete rank-one nonarchimedean field (possibly non-discretely valued, so the rings below are not noetherian), S = Spf O_K, ℒ = ϖO_K, X = Spf O_K⟨T⟩, Y = Spf O_K⟨U⟩: Hom_{O_K}(X, Y) ≃ lim_n Hom_{O_K/ϖ^{n+1}}(Spec (O_K/ϖ^{n+1})[T], Spec (O_K/ϖ^{n+1})[U]) ≃ lim_n (O_K/ϖ^{n+1})[T] = O_K⟨T⟩, the image of U.

The ideal condition in (ii) is needed: on X = Spf O_K⟨T⟩ with 𝒥 = ϖ²O_X and 𝒦 = ϖO_X the identity does not satisfy id*(𝒦)O_X ⊆ 𝒥, and there is no morphism X_0 = Spec O_K⟨T⟩/(ϖ²) → Y_0 = Spec O_K⟨T⟩/(ϖ) compatible with ι (it would send ϖ to 0 in O_K⟨T⟩/(ϖ²)).

nodes.title: Fibre products of formal schemes
nodes.statement: Let f : X → S and g : Y → S be morphisms of formal schemes (finite ideal type). The fibre product X ×_S Y exists in formal schemes; for affine formal schemes, Spf B ×_{Spf A} Spf C ≅ Spf(B ⊗̂_A C) with the projections induced by the canonical maps into the completed tensor product (EGA I, 10.7.2–10.7.3); every open cover of X, Y, S by affine formal opens gives an affine formal cover of X ×_S Y. If S, X, Y have ideals of definition ℒ, 𝒥, 𝒦 with f*(ℒ)O_X ⊆ 𝒥 and g*(ℒ)O_Y ⊆ 𝒦, then X ×_S Y is the colimit in formal schemes of the schemes X_n ×_{S_n} Y_n, and the ideal generated by 𝒥 and 𝒦 is an ideal of definition of X ×_S Y whose powers are cofinal with the kernels of the X_n ×_{S_n} Y_n (EGA I, 10.7.4). If S, X, Y are locally noetherian and f is of finite type, then X ×_S Y is locally noetherian and X ×_S Y → Y is of finite type (EGA I, 10.13.5 (ii)); in general X ×_S Y need not be locally noetherian (EGA I, 10.7.4).
hypotheses: formal schemes of finite ideal type; local noetherianity of the product only when f is of finite type
proofSteps: Affine case: by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/spf-morphism-correspondence, morphisms Spf D → Spf(B ⊗̂_A C) are continuous maps B ⊗̂_A C → D, which by the universal property of AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-tensor-product-adic are pairs of continuous A-maps B → D, C → D; extend from affine D to arbitrary formal schemes D with AdicSpacesPartII:F0/spf-morphism-correspondence (general X).
General case: glue the affine products over affine formal covers as in the scheme case (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-scheme-gluing; EGA I, 10.7.3 via 3.2.6).

System description: affine-locally B ⊗̂_A C = lim_n (B/J^{n+1} ⊗_{A/L^{n+1}} C/K^{n+1}), since the ideals J^{n+1}⊗1 + 1⊗K^{n+1} and (J⊗1 + 1⊗K)^{n+1} of B ⊗_A C have cofinal powers (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-tensor-product-adic); a compatible family X_n ×_{S_n} Y_n → T glues to X ×_S Y → T as in AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings.

Noetherian case: if B is topologically of finite type over A, B ⊗̂_A C is noetherian and topologically of finite type over C (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-tensor-product-adic, isNoetherianRing; AdicSpacesPartII:F0/topologically-finite-type-criterion); finite type of X ×_S Y → Y is checked on X_0 ×_{S_0} Y_0 → Y_0 (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-morphism-finite-type).

nodes.title: Adic morphisms of locally noetherian formal schemes
nodes.statement: A morphism f : X → Y of locally noetherian formal schemes is adic if there is an ideal of definition 𝒦 of Y such that f*(𝒦)·O_X is an ideal of definition of X; then f*(𝒦′)·O_X is an ideal of definition of X for every ideal of definition 𝒦′ of Y (EGA I, 10.12.1). An adic formal scheme over S is a locally noetherian formal S-scheme with adic structure morphism; every S-morphism between adic S-formal schemes is adic. For affine X = Spf A, Y = Spf B, f = Spf φ is adic iff I_B·A is an ideal of definition of A (IsAdic (I_B.map φ)). Notation: for fixed 𝒦 and 𝒥 := f*(𝒦)O_X, f_n : X_n → Y_n denotes the reduction modulo 𝒥^{n+1}, 𝒦^{n+1} (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/morphisms-as-compatible-systems); f is adic iff every square X_m → X_n over Y_m → Y_n is cartesian, i.e. X_m = X_n ×_{Y_n} Y_m (EGA I, 10.12.3).
hypotheses: X, Y locally noetherian formal schemes
proofSteps: Independence of 𝒦: locally, K′^n ⊆ K and K^m ⊆ K′, so KA and K′A have cofinal powers and one is an ideal of definition iff the other is (EGA I, 10.12.1; AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring).
S-morphisms between adic S-formal schemes: if f = g ∘ u then u*(g*(ℒ)O_Y)O_X = f*(ℒ)O_X is an ideal of definition (EGA I, 10.12.1).
Cartesian squares: affine-locally, KA ideal of definition gives A/K^{m+1}A = (A/K^{n+1}A) ⊗_{B/K^{n+1}} B/K^{m+1}.
acceptance: Spf ℤ_p⟨T⟩ → Spf ℤ_p is adic; Spf ℤ_p⟦T⟧ → Spf ℤ_p is not adic (pℤ_p⟦T⟧ is not an ideal of definition of the (p,T)-adic ring).
For a morphism f : X → Y of locally noetherian schemes and Y′ ⊆ Y closed, f̂ : X̂_{/f⁻¹Y′} → Ŷ_{/Y′} is adic.

uses.how: a morphism of finite type is adic with f_0 of finite type.
formal schemes proper over Spf A are adic over Spf A; their systems X_n = X ×_{Spf A} Spec A/I^{n+1} are the data algebraised.
Huber’s criterion: t(f) is adic iff f is adic; t(f) locally of finite type iff f locally of finite type.
morphisms of type-(S) formal schemes are called adic in the same sense; R2 extends the definition beyond the noetherian case.

nodes.title: Adic formal S-schemes are adic inductive systems of S_n-schemes
nodes.statement: Let S be a locally noetherian formal scheme with ideal of definition ℒ and S_n = (S, O_S/ℒ^{n+1}). An (S_n)-adic inductive system is a sequence of locally noetherian S_n-schemes X_n with morphisms X_m → X_n over S_m → S_n identifying X_m with X_n ×_{S_n} S_m for m ≤ n; morphisms are compatible sequences of S_n-morphisms. The functor X ↦ (X ×_S S_n)_n = (X, O_X/(ℒO_X)^{n+1})_n is an equivalence from adic formal S-schemes (locally noetherian, adic structure morphism) to (S_n)-adic inductive systems with X_0 locally noetherian; its quasi-inverse sends (X_n) to its colimit (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings), whose structure morphism to S is adic (EGA I, 10.12.3, 10.12.3.1). In particular Hom_S(X, Y) ≃ lim_n Hom_{S_n}(X_n, Y_n) (EGA I, 10.12.3.2).
hypotheses: S locally noetherian formal scheme with ideal of definition ℒ; X_0 locally noetherian
proofSteps: From X to systems: 𝒥 := ℒO_X is an ideal of definition; X_n → S_n is induced and the squares are cartesian (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-morphism-of-formal-schemes, isAdic_iff_isPullback).

From systems to X: the kernels of O_{X_n} → O_{X_m} are 𝒥_n^{m+1} where 𝒥_n = ℒO_{X_n}, pulled back from S (base change of the closed immersions S_m → S_n); 𝒥_1 is of finite type over O_{X_0} because ℒ/ℒ² is; hence (X_n) is an adic thickening system (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings), its colimit X is locally noetherian, and the limit of the structure maps f_n is a morphism f : X → S (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/morphisms-as-compatible-systems).

f is adic: affine-locally S = Spf A, X_n = Spec B_n, B = lim B_n; the image of the ideal I of A is dense in ker(B → B_0) and every ideal of the noetherian adic ring B is closed, so IB is the ideal of definition ker(B → B_0) (EGA I, proof of 10.12.3.1; AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring, API quotient: ideals are closed).
Morphisms: AdicSpacesPartII:F0/morphisms-as-compatible-systems (iii).
acceptance: For S = Spf ℤ_p, the system X_n = P¹_{ℤ/p^{n+1}} is adic; its colimit is the p-adic completion of P¹_{ℤ_p}.
The system X_n = Spec(ℤ/p^{n+1})[T]/(T^{n+1}) over S_n = Spec ℤ/p^{n+1} is not adic (X_0 = Spec F_p[T]/(T) but X_1 ×_{S_1} S_0 = Spec F_p[T]/(T²) ≠ X_0).

nodes.title: Formal schemes of finite ideal type adic over S are adic inductive systems of S_n-schemes
nodes.statement: Let S be a formal scheme of finite ideal type with an ideal of definition ℒ of finite type and S_n = (S, O_S/ℒ^{n+1}). A formal scheme X of finite ideal type with a morphism f : X → S is adic over S if ℒ·O_X is an ideal of definition of X (it is then of finite type; Fujiwara–Kato I, Definition 1.3.1; for locally noetherian X, S this is AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-morphism-of-formal-schemes). An (S_n)-adic inductive system is a sequence of S_n-schemes X_n (no finiteness hypothesis) with S_n-morphisms X_m → X_n (m ≤ n) over S_m → S_n identifying X_m with X_n ×_{S_n} S_m; its morphisms are sequences of S_n-morphisms compatible with the transition maps. Then X ↦ (X_n)_n := ((X, O_X/(ℒO_X)^{n+1}))_n = (X ×_S S_n)_n is an equivalence from the category of formal schemes of finite ideal type adic over S (with S-morphisms) to the category of (S_n)-adic inductive systems. A quasi-inverse sends (X_n) to the formal scheme X attached to the adic thickening system (X_n) (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings) with the limit f : X → S of the structure maps; f is adic over S, with ℒ·O_X = ker(O_X → O_{X_0}) and (ℒO_X)^{n+1} = ker(O_X → O_{X_n}) (Fujiwara–Kato I, Exercise I.1.8). X is locally noetherian iff X_0 is (EGA I, (10.6.4)), and for locally noetherian S this is AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-systems-equivalence. In particular Hom_S(X, Y) ≃ lim_n Hom_{S_n}(X_n, Y_n) for X, Y adic over S.
hypotheses: S a formal scheme of finite ideal type with an ideal of definition ℒ of finite type; no noetherian hypothesis
proofSteps: Forward functor: 𝒥 := ℒO_X is an ideal of definition of finite type and X_n = (X, O_X/𝒥^{n+1}); since pulling back ideals is compatible with quotients, the ideal of X_n defining X_m is 𝒥^{m+1}/𝒥^{n+1} = ℒ^{m+1}O_{X_n}, so X_m = X_n ×_{S_n} S_m (EGA I, proof of (10.12.3), which is valid for arbitrary formal schemes); an S-morphism u gives the compatible S_n-morphisms u_n (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/morphisms-as-compatible-systems-finite-ideal-type (i)).

Quasi-inverse: for an adic system, the ideal of X_n defining X_m is ℒ^{m+1}O_{X_n} (base change of S_m ⊆ S_n), nilpotent because ℒ^{n+1}O_{S_n} = 0, the transition maps are surjective, and 𝒥_1 = ℒO_{X_1} is an O_{X_0}-module of finite type because ℒ is of finite type; so (X_n) satisfies (a)–(c) of AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings, and X := colim X_n is a formal scheme of finite ideal type with ideal of definition 𝒥 = ker(O_X → O_{X_0}) of finite type and ker(O_X → O_{X_n}) = 𝒥^{n+1} (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings; EGA I, (10.6.4); Fujiwara–Kato I, Proposition 1.4.3). Hence X_n = (X, O_X/𝒥^{n+1}), and the compatible structure maps X_n → S_n → S define f : X → S (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/thickening-colimit-finite-ideal-type (iii)).

f is adic over S, i.e. ℒ·O_X = 𝒥; this is the step where EGA's proof of (10.12.3.1) uses that every ideal of a noetherian adic ring is closed. Affine-locally S = Spf A with a finitely generated ideal of definition L (ℒ = L^Δ), X_n = Spec B_n with B_m = B_n/L^{m+1}B_n, and B = lim_n B_n. By Fujiwara–Kato I, Proposition 0.7.2.12, B is complete for the filtration F(n) = ker(B → B_{n−1}) and F(1) = L·B: indeed B/F(1) = B_0 = B/LB + F(n) gives F(1) = LB + F(n) for all n, Proposition 0.7.2.11 gives F(n) = F(1)^n with F(1) finitely generated, and LB + F(1)² = F(1) with F(1) contained in the Jacobson radical of the F(1)-adically complete ring B (mathlib IsAdicComplete.le_jacobson_bot) gives F(1) = LB by Nakayama's lemma (mathlib Submodule.le_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson_bot). So ℒO_X = (LB)^Δ = 𝒥 on Spf B.

Full faithfulness is AdicSpacesPartII:F0/morphisms-as-compatible-systems-finite-ideal-type (iii) with 𝒥 = ℒO_X and 𝒦 = ℒO_Y. Essential surjectivity and the quasi-inverse: for X adic over S, colim_n (X, O_X/(ℒO_X)^{n+1}) ≅ X by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/thickening-colimit-finite-ideal-type (iii); for an adic system (X_n), the reductions of its colimit along ℒO_X = 𝒥 are the X_n by the previous two steps.
acceptance: For K a complete rank-one nonarchimedean field (possibly non-discretely valued), S = Spf O_K and ℒ = ϖO_K: the system X_n = Spec (O_K/ϖ^{n+1})[T_1, …, T_d] is (S_n)-adic with colimit Spf O_K⟨T_1, …, T_d⟩, which is adic over S with ideal of definition ϖ·O.

Étale O_K/ϖ-schemes lift uniquely to adic systems of étale S_n-schemes (topological invariance of the étale site), hence to formal schemes adic and étale over Spf O_K: Spec (O_K/ϖ)[T, (T² + 1)⁻¹] lifts to Spf O_K⟨T, (T² + 1)⁻¹⟩.
The system X_n = Spec (ℤ/p^{n+1})[T]/(T^{n+1}) over S_n = Spec ℤ/p^{n+1} is not adic: X_1 ×_{S_1} S_0 = Spec 𝔽_p[T]/(T²) ≠ X_0 = Spec 𝔽_p.

nodes.title: Morphisms of finite type of locally noetherian formal schemes
nodes.statement: Let Y be a locally noetherian formal scheme with ideal of definition 𝒦 and f : X → Y a morphism of formal schemes. f is of finite type if X is locally noetherian, f is adic, and the reduction f_0 : (X, O_X/𝒥) → (Y, O_Y/𝒦) with 𝒥 = f*(𝒦)O_X is a morphism of schemes of finite type (Mathlib LocallyOfFiniteType and QuasiCompact) (EGA I, 10.13.1 (a), 10.13.3). Equivalent conditions: (b) X is locally noetherian and the colimit of an adic system (X_n) over (Y_n) with X_0 → Y_0 of finite type; (c) every point of Y has a noetherian affine formal neighbourhood V = Spf B such that f⁻¹(V) is a finite union of noetherian affine formal opens Spf A_i with each A_i ≅ B{T_1,…,T_r}/𝔞 topologically (EGA I, 10.13.1). The condition does not depend on 𝒦, and then every f_n is of finite type. Affine criterion: Spf A → Spf B (noetherian) is of finite type iff A is topologically a quotient of some B{T} (EGA I, 10.13.4). The local variant f locally of finite type (Huber’s notion used in R2) drops quasi-compactness of f_0.
hypotheses: Y locally noetherian; 'finite type' of schemes includes quasi-compactness (EGA I, 6.3.1)
proofSteps: (a) ⇒ (b): AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-systems-equivalence.

(b) ⇒ (c): locally Y = Spf B; X_0 is a finite union of affines U_i finite type over B/K; U_i is affine in every X_n, and the formal open on U_i is Spf(lim A_{i,n}) with A_{i,n} = A_{i,m}/K^{n+1}A_{i,m}; AdicSpacesPartII:F0/topologically-finite-type-criterion ((a) ⇒ (c)) gives the presentation.
(c) ⇒ (a): AdicSpacesPartII:F0/topologically-finite-type-criterion ((c) ⇒ (a)): A/KA is of finite type over B/K and KA is an ideal of definition.
Independence of 𝒦: (c) does not mention 𝒦.
acceptance: Spf B{T₁,…,T_r} → Spf B is of finite type; Spf ℤ_p⟦T⟧ → Spf ℤ_p is not (not adic).
For a morphism of finite type of locally noetherian schemes f : X → Y and Y′ closed, f̂ is of finite type (EGA I, 10.13.6).

nodes.title: Proper morphisms of locally noetherian formal schemes
nodes.statement: A morphism f : X → Y of locally noetherian formal schemes is proper if f is of finite type (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-morphism-finite-type) and, for an ideal of definition 𝒦 of Y and 𝒥 = f*(𝒦)O_X, the reduction f_0 : (X, O_X/𝒥) → (Y, O_Y/𝒦) is a proper morphism of schemes (Mathlib IsProper) (EGA III, 3.4.1). This does not depend on 𝒦, and then every f_n : X_n → Y_n is proper. A closed subset Z of X is proper over Y if, viewed in X_0, it is proper over Y_0 (the reduced closed subscheme on Z is proper over Y_0). For a proper morphism g : X → Y of locally noetherian schemes, a closed subset Y′ ⊆ Y and X′ = g⁻¹(Y′), the completion ĝ : X̂_{/X′} → Ŷ_{/Y′} is proper (EGA III, 3.4.1).
hypotheses: X, Y locally noetherian formal schemes
proofSteps: f_n proper for all n: f is adic, so X_0 = X_n ×_{Y_n} Y_0 (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-morphism-of-formal-schemes), Y_0 ⊆ Y_n is a thickening and all f_n are of finite type (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-morphism-finite-type); AdicSpacesPartII:F0/thickening-invariance gives f_n proper iff f_0 proper.

Independence of 𝒦: for another ideal of definition 𝒦′ ⊆ 𝒦 the reductions modulo 𝒦 and 𝒦′ are members of such adic systems (𝒦 contains a power of 𝒦′ and conversely), so the same invariance applies (EGA III, 3.4.1).

Completion: ĝ is adic of finite type (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-morphism-finite-type) and its reduction is the base change of g to V(𝓘) ⊆ Y, which is proper (Mathlib IsProper.isStableUnderBaseChange).
acceptance: The p-adic completion of P¹_{ℤ_p} (or of any proper ℤ_p-scheme) is proper over Spf ℤ_p; Spf ℤ_p⟨T⟩ is not proper over Spf ℤ_p since A¹_{F_p} is not proper over F_p.

A formal scheme X proper over Spf A need not be the completion of a scheme proper over Spec A (EGA III, 5.4.3); the ample-line-bundle hypothesis of AdicSpacesPartII:F0/grothendieck-algebraization is what makes it algebraic.

nodes.statement: Let Y ⊆ Y′ be a closed immersion of schemes that is a homeomorphism (a thickening, e.g. defined by a locally nilpotent ideal), f′ : X′ → Y′ a morphism and X = Y ×_{Y′} X′ with f : X → Y the base change, and assume f and f′ are locally of finite type. Then f′ is proper (resp. finite, a closed immersion) if and only if f is (Stacks Tag 0BPG).
hypotheses: (Y ⊆ Y′) a thickening; X = Y ×_{Y′} X′; f and f′ locally of finite type
proofSteps: If f′ has the property, so does its base change f (Mathlib IsProper.isStableUnderBaseChange; finite morphisms and closed immersions are stable under base change).

Conversely: underlying spaces and continuous maps of f and f′ coincide and remain so after any base change (a base change of a thickening is a thickening), so universal closedness transfers; the diagonal of f′ is a thickening of the diagonal of f, and a closed-embedding thickening with surjective stalk maps after reduction is a closed immersion, so separatedness transfers; hence properness (Mathlib IsProper = separated + universally closed + locally of finite type).

Closed immersions: topologically a closed embedding, and surjectivity of O_{Y′} → f′_*O_{X′} follows from surjectivity modulo the nilpotent ideal by Nakayama on stalks; finiteness: f′ is affine (affineness of a thickening, EGA I, 5.1.9) and integral since f is (Stacks Tag 0BPG).
acceptance: For Y′ = Spec ℤ/p², Y = Spec F_p and X′ = P¹_{ℤ/p²}: X′ → Y′ is proper because P¹_{F_p} → Spec F_p is.

Without the condition X = Y ×_{Y′} X′ the statement fails: for Y′ = Spec ℤ/p², Y = Spec F_p, X′ = A¹_{Y′} and X ⊂ X′ the closed point V(p, t), X → Y is an isomorphism (proper) while X′ → Y′ is not proper.

nodes.title: Closed formal subschemes and closed immersions
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian formal scheme and 𝒜 ⊆ O_X a coherent ideal (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-formal-module). Its support Y = Supp(O_X/𝒜) is closed and (Y, (O_X/𝒜)|_Y) is a locally noetherian formal scheme, noetherian if X is (EGA I, 10.14.1): the closed formal subscheme X.subscheme 𝒜, with canonical morphism j : X.subscheme 𝒜 → X. The assignment 𝒜 ↦ X.subscheme 𝒜 is a bijection from coherent ideals onto closed formal subschemes. A closed immersion is a morphism isomorphic over X to some j (EGA I, 10.14.2). On X = Spf A (A adic noetherian) every coherent ideal is 𝔞^Δ for an ideal 𝔞 of A and Spf A.subscheme 𝔞^Δ ≅ Spf(A/𝔞), with j = Spf of the quotient map. Closed immersions are adic and of finite type (EGA I, 10.14.3); for a locally noetherian scheme X with closed subset X′ and a closed subscheme Z of X, the completion Ẑ_{/Z∩X′} is the closed formal subscheme of X̂ defined by the completed ideal (EGA I, 10.14.7, used in EGA III, 5.1.8).
hypotheses: X locally noetherian formal scheme; 𝒜 coherent ideal of O_X
proofSteps: For an ideal of definition 𝒥, the O_X/(𝒜 + 𝒥^{n+1}) are coherent O_{X_n}-modules with support Y (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system); the schemes Y_n := V(𝒜 + 𝒥^{n+1}) ⊆ X_n form an adic thickening system with Y_0 locally noetherian, and O_X/𝒜 = lim O_X/(𝒜 + 𝒥^{n+1}); hence (Y, O_X/𝒜) is the formal scheme ofThickenings(Y_n) (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings; EGA I, 10.14.1).
Affine case: 𝒜 = 𝔞^Δ by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence, and exactness of (-)^Δ gives O/𝒜 = (A/𝔞)^Δ, so the subscheme is Spf(A/𝔞) (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring, API quotient).
Adic and finite type: affine-locally Spf(A/𝔞) → Spf A has I(A/𝔞) an ideal of definition and A/𝔞 a quotient of A{∅} (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-morphism-finite-type).
Completion of closed subschemes: exactness of completion of coherent sheaves (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact) applied to 0 → 𝓐 → O_X → O_Z → 0.
acceptance: Spf ℤ_p⟦T⟧.subscheme (T − p)^Δ ≅ Spf ℤ_p (a section of Spf ℤ_p⟦T⟧ → Spf ℤ_p).
An ideal of definition 𝒥 is coherent and X.subscheme 𝒥 = X_0 is a scheme.

nodes.title: An adic morphism is a closed immersion iff its reduction is
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be an adic morphism of locally noetherian formal schemes, 𝒦 an ideal of definition of Y and 𝒥 = f*(𝒦)O_X. Then f is a closed immersion if and only if f_0 : (X, O_X/𝒥) → (Y, O_Y/𝒦) is a closed immersion of schemes (EGA III, 4.8.10).
hypotheses: f adic; X, Y locally noetherian
proofSteps: Necessity: base change of the closed immersion f along Y_0 → Y (X_0 = X ×_Y Y_0 by adicness, AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-morphism-of-formal-schemes).

Sufficiency, local on Y: let Y = Spf B with ideal of definition K. X_0 is affine (closed in the affine Y_0), hence every X_n is affine (EGA I, 5.1.9, as in AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings), X_n = Spec A_n, and X = Spf A with A = lim A_n, A_n = A/K^{n+1}A by adicness.

A is a finite B-module generated by 1: the system (A_n) satisfies the hypotheses of AdicSpacesPartII:F0/finite-module-inverse-limit over B with A_0 = A/KA cyclic over B/K (f_0 closed immersion), so A is finite over B; by Nakayama (Mathlib Submodule.eq_bot_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson_bot, with K ⊆ Jacobson radical of B by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring) the cyclic generator 1 of A/KA generates A, i.e. B → A is surjective.
Hence A = B/𝔞 and f is the closed immersion Spf(B/𝔞) → Spf B (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-formal-subscheme, subscheme_Spf).
acceptance: Spf ℤ_p⟦T⟧ → Spf ℤ_p⟦S, T⟧ (S ↦ 0) is adic with reduction Spec F_p → Spec F_p an isomorphism; it is a closed immersion.
Without adicness the criterion fails: Spf ℤ_p⟦T⟧ → Spf ℤ_p has reduction (modulo (p,T) and (p)) an isomorphism Spec F_p → Spec F_p but is not a closed immersion.

nodes.title: Finite modules over an adic noetherian ring as compatible systems
nodes.statement: Let A be an adic noetherian ring with ideal of definition I and A_n = A/I^{n+1}. (i) Every finite A-module M is I-adically separated and complete, and every A-linear map between finite A-modules is continuous for the I-adic topologies (EGA 0, 7.3.6, 7.2.10). (ii) If (M_n) is an inverse system with M_n a finite A_n-module, surjective transitions M_{n+1} → M_n with kernel I^{n+1}M_{n+1} (equivalently M_{n+1} ⊗ A_n ≅ M_n), then M := lim M_n is a finite A-module and M/I^{n+1}M ≅ M_n (EGA 0, 7.2.9). (iii) Morphisms of such systems correspond bijectively to A-linear maps of the limits (EGA 0, 7.2.10). Hence M ↦ (M/I^{n+1}M)_n is an equivalence from finite A-modules to such compatible systems.
hypotheses: A adic noetherian; systems indexed by ℕ with the stated kernel condition
proofSteps: (i) M ≅ AdicCompletion I M because M ⊗ Â → M̂ is bijective for finite M over noetherian A (Mathlib AdicCompletion.ofTensorProductEquivOfFiniteNoetherian) and A = Â; separatedness by Krull (Mathlib Ideal.iInf_pow_smul_eq_bot_of_le_jacobson with I ⊆ Jacobson radical, AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring). Continuity: h(I^n M) ⊆ I^n N.

(ii) Choose x_1,…,x_s ∈ M lifting generators of M_0; the induced maps A_n^s → M_n are surjective by Nakayama (nilpotent I), their kernels K_n form a system with surjective transitions (from the kernel condition), which is Mittag-Leffler, so A^s → M is surjective (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/mittag-leffler-exactness); the kernel of M → M_n is I^{n+1}M by the same exact-sequence argument (EGA 0, 7.2.9; Stacks Tag 087W).
(iii) A compatible family (h_n) has limit h; conversely h(I^{n+1}M) ⊆ I^{n+1}N gives h_n.
acceptance: For A = ℤ_p and M_n = ℤ/p^{n+1} ⊕ ℤ/p, lim M_n = ℤ_p ⊕ ℤ/p.
For A = ℤ_p and M_n = ℤ/p^{n+1}·e_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ ℤ/p^{n+1}·e_n (rank growing with n) the kernel condition fails and lim M_n is not finite.

nodes.title: The formal completion of a locally noetherian scheme along a closed subset
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian scheme and X′ ⊆ X a closed subset. Let 𝓘 ⊆ O_X be a quasi-coherent ideal of finite type with V(𝓘) = X′ (for example the ideal of the reduced induced closed subscheme). The formal completion X̂ = X̂_{/X′} is the locally noetherian formal scheme ofThickenings(V(𝓘^{n+1}))_n (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings): its underlying space is X′ and O_X̂ = lim_n (O_X/𝓘^{n+1})|_{X′}. It does not depend on 𝓘: all such ideals form a filtered set Φ, and on noetherian opens the powers of any one member are cofinal in Φ (EGA I, 10.8.2); 𝓘O_X̂ is an ideal of definition. For X = Spec A (A noetherian) and X′ = V(I): X̂ ≅ Spf Â where Â = AdicCompletion I A with the I-adic topology (EGA I, 10.8.5). Further: X̂_red is the reduced closed subscheme with space X′; X̂ is noetherian iff X′ is quasi-compact (EGA I, 10.8.6); there is a canonical morphism of locally ringed spaces i_X : X̂ → X (the inclusion of X′ with O_X → i_*O_X̂ the limit of the quotient maps) (EGA I, 10.8.7), which is flat (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact); for U ⊆ X open, Û_{/U∩X′} is the open formal subscheme of X̂ on U ∩ X′; for X′ = X, X̂ = X.
hypotheses: X locally noetherian scheme (Mathlib IsLocallyNoetherian)
X′ closed subset; 𝓘 quasi-coherent of finite type with V(𝓘) = X′
proofSteps: The schemes X_n := V(𝓘^{n+1}) (Mathlib Scheme.IdealSheafData.subscheme) all have underlying space X′; the closed immersions X_n → X_{n+1} have kernel 𝓘^{n+1}/𝓘^{n+2}, and 𝓘/𝓘² is of finite type over O_{X_0}; so (X_n) is an adic thickening system with X_0 locally noetherian and ofThickenings gives a locally noetherian formal scheme (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings).
Affine case: Γ(X_n) = A/I^{n+1}, so X̂ = Spf(lim A/I^{n+1}) = Spf Â, and Â is noetherian and I·Â-adic (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-completion-noetherian (ii), AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-spectrum).

Independence of 𝓘: for 𝓘, 𝓘′ ∈ Φ, on a noetherian affine open 𝓘^n ⊆ 𝓘′ and 𝓘′^m ⊆ 𝓘 (EGA I, 10.8.2; nilradical of O_X/𝓘 nilpotent on noetherian opens), so the two systems are cofinal and the limit sheaves agree (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/spf-ideal-independence affine-locally).
The canonical morphism i_X: the maps O_X → O_X/𝓘^{n+1} are compatible and give O_X → i_*lim O_X/𝓘^{n+1}; stalk maps are local because each O_{X,x} → O_{X_n,x} is surjective (EGA I, 10.8.7).
acceptance: The completion of Spec ℤ along V(p) is Spf ℤ_p; the completion of A²_k = Spec k[x,y] along the x-axis V(y) is Spf k[x]⟦y⟧.
The completion of P¹_{ℤ_p} along its special fibre V(p) is the non-affine noetherian formal scheme obtained by gluing (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-scheme-gluing).
For X′ = X the completion is X itself (𝓘 = 0), and for X′ = ∅ it is empty.

nodes.title: Extension of a morphism to formal completions
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of locally noetherian schemes and X′ ⊆ X, Y′ ⊆ Y closed with f(X′) ⊆ Y′. There is a unique morphism of formal schemes f̂ : X̂_{/X′} → Ŷ_{/Y′} with i_Y ∘ f̂ = f ∘ i_X; it is the colimit of the morphisms V(𝓘^{n+1}) → V(𝓚^{n+1}) induced by f for ideals with f*(𝓚)O_X ⊆ 𝓘, and does not depend on the ideals (EGA I, 10.9.1–10.9.2). On underlying spaces f̂ is the restriction of f to X′. Functoriality: (g ∘ f)^ = ĝ ∘ f̂ and id^ = id (EGA I, 10.9.3). Affine case: for f = Spec φ, φ : B → A, f̂ = Spf φ̂ with φ̂ : B̂ → Â the continuous extension (EGA I, 10.9.1). Base change: if X′ = f⁻¹(Y′) then X̂ ≅ X ×_Y Ŷ as formal schemes, where X is viewed as a formal scheme (EGA I, 10.9.9), and f̂ is adic; completion commutes with fibre products (EGA I, 10.9.7).
hypotheses: X, Y locally noetherian; f(X′) ⊆ Y′
base change statement needs X′ = f⁻¹(Y′); product statement needs X ×_S Y locally noetherian
proofSteps: Choose 𝓚 of finite type with V(𝓚) = Y′ and 𝓘 with V(𝓘) = X′ and f*(𝓚)O_X ⊆ 𝓘 (take 𝓘 the ideal of the reduced induced structure; EGA I, 10.9.1); then f*(𝓚^{n+1})O_X ⊆ 𝓘^{n+1} and f induces compatible f_n; define f̂ = colim f_n (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/morphisms-as-compatible-systems (ii)).

Uniqueness and independence: two choices of ideals give cofinal systems; the compatibility with i_X, i_Y determines f̂ on the sheaf level since O_X̂ is the limit (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-completion).

nodes.title: Morphisms with equal completions agree near the closed subset
nodes.statement: Let S be a scheme, X and Y locally noetherian S-schemes with Y of finite type over S, X′ ⊆ X and Y′ ⊆ Y closed, and f, g : X → Y two S-morphisms with f(X′) ⊆ Y′ and g(X′) ⊆ Y′. Then f̂ = ĝ as morphisms X̂_{/X′} → Ŷ_{/Y′} if and only if f and g coincide on an open neighbourhood of X′ (EGA I, 10.9.4).
hypotheses: Y of finite type over S (needed for necessity)
X, Y locally noetherian
proofSteps: Sufficiency: completion only depends on a neighbourhood of X′ (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-completion, restrict; AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-morphism).
Necessity: f̂ = ĝ gives f(x) = g(x) on X′; the question is local, so take X, Y, S affine with rings A, B, R, B of finite type over R generated by b_1,…,b_r, and f, g given by ρ, σ : B → A.

The continuous extensions of ρ, σ to the completions agree, so for each b_i the section ρ(b_i) − σ(b_i) of O_X maps to 0 in Γ(X̂, O_X̂); by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-detects-near-closed (kernel of Γ(X, F) → Γ(X̂, F̂)) it vanishes on a neighbourhood of X′; finitely many generators give one neighbourhood on which ρ = σ, hence a basic open D(h) ⊇ X′ ∩ Spec A on which f = g (EGA I, 10.9.4).
acceptance: Two sections of A¹_{ℤ_p} → Spec ℤ_p given by x ↦ a, x ↦ b with a ≡ b mod p^n for all n are equal (ℤ_p separated): with X = Spec ℤ_p, X′ = V(p) the completion determines them.
