nodes.title: Admissible formal blow-ups and strict transforms
nodes.statement: Let X be an admissible formal O_K-scheme and 𝒜 ⊆ O_X a coherent open ideal (coherent, and ϖ^N O_X ⊆ 𝒜 for some N). The admissible blow-up of 𝒜 is X' := lim_m Proj(⊕_{n≥0} 𝒜ⁿ ⊗_{O_X} O_X/ϖ^{m+1}) with its projection φ: X' → X. (a) Over a formal affine open Spf A with 𝒜 ↔ a = (f_0, …, f_r) ∋ ϖ^N, φ⁻¹(Spf A) is the ϖ-adic completion of the scheme-theoretic blow-up of a on Spec A, covered by the charts Spf A'_i with A'_i = A⟨ζ_j : j ≠ i⟩/(f_iζ_j − f_j)_{j≠i} modulo its ϖ-torsion (which equals its f_i-torsion), Spf A'_i being the locus where f_i generates 𝒜O_{X'}. (b) X' is admissible and 𝒜O_{X'} is invertible. (c) Universal property: every morphism ψ: Z → X of formal O_K-schemes (Z not necessarily admissible) with 𝒜O_Z invertible factors uniquely through φ. Further: φ is an isomorphism over X ∖ V(𝒜); formation commutes with flat base change and, in the admissible category, with arbitrary base change (strict transform); φ is proper and surjective on special fibres; blowing up 𝒜 and then ℬO_{X'} is blowing up 𝒜ℬ; for X quasi-compact a composite of admissible blow-ups is an admissible blow-up (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I 2.5), blow-ups of finitely many opens extend to X and are dominated by one admissible blow-up of X (2.6), and any two admissible blow-ups of X are dominated by a third, so admissible blow-ups of X form a cofiltered system. The strict transform of a coherent O_X-module ℳ is ℳ' = φ*ℳ/𝒩, 𝒩 the submodule of sections supported in φ⁻¹(V(𝒜)); if ℳ' has no ϖ-torsion, 𝒩 is the ϖ-torsion of φ*ℳ.
hypotheses: X admissible over O_K; X quasi-compact for composition (2.5) and extension (2.6)
𝒜 coherent and open; a non-open centre changes the generic fibre
Composition 2.5 uses [RG, 5.1.4] and [EGA I_new 6.9.9]; extension 2.6 uses [EGA I_new 6.9.7]
proofSteps: Define X' as the formal scheme attached to the adic thickening system of projective schemes Proj(⊕ 𝒜ⁿ ⊗ O/ϖ^{m+1}) (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings, valid for finite ideal type); locally this is the ϖ-adic completion of the scheme blow-up (Rees algebra ⊕ aⁿ, mathlib reesAlgebra).

(a) Chart description: Bosch–Lütkebohmert I Lemma 2.2; in the non-noetherian case, completion of A[ζ]/(f_iζ_j − f_j) is computed by the exact sequence of completions, the ideal being closed by node flat-tft-is-tfp (Lemma 1.2(b)); the ϖ-torsion of the completed chart is finitely generated by node saturated-submodule-finitely-generated and coincides with the f_i-torsion.
(b) Charts are tft and ϖ-torsion-free, hence admissible by node flat-tft-is-tfp; 𝒜O_{X'} is locally principal and open, hence contains ϖ^N, and has no ϖ-torsion, so it is invertible.

(c) From the universal property of the scheme blow-up on each Spec A/ϖ^{m+1} and passage to the limit; morphisms into X' are compatible systems of morphisms into the levels (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/morphisms-as-compatible-systems-finite-ideal-type (ii), with the ideal of definition ϖ·O_{X'} of X' and, on Z, an ideal of definition of finite type containing ϖ·O_Z).

Isomorphism away from V(𝒜), properness (Proj), surjectivity on special fibres (a non-empty X has X'_0 non-empty: otherwise aⁿ = 0 mod ϖ for n ≫ 0 forces A = 0 since A has no ϖ-torsion), multiplicativity: Bosch–Lütkebohmert I Remark 2.4.
Composition (2.5), extension (2.6) and domination: blow up the product of the relevant ideals; the non-noetherian steps cite [RG 5.1.4] and [EGA I_new 6.9.7, 6.9.9] (recorded as unread imports).
Strict transform: 𝒩 = Ann(𝒜O_{X'}) on φ*ℳ is coherent by node tfp-algebra-coherent (annihilators, Lemma 1.4).
acceptance: The admissible blow-up of (T, ϖ) on Spf O_K⟨T⟩ has charts Spf O_K⟨U⟩ (T = ϖU) and Spf O_K⟨T, V⟩/(TV − ϖ); its special fibre is P¹_k ∪ A¹_k meeting in one point.
Blowing up an invertible open ideal (e.g. ϖ^n O_X) is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: The generic fibre of an admissible blow-up is an isomorphism
nodes.statement: Let φ: X' → X be the admissible blow-up of a coherent open ideal 𝒜 on an admissible formal O_K-scheme X. Then d(φ): d(X') → d(X) is an isomorphism of adic spaces (equivalently φ_rig is an isomorphism of rigid spaces). Over Spf A with 𝒜 = (f_0, …, f_r): the f_i generate the unit ideal of A_K, the chart Spf A'_i has generic fibre the rational subset R(f_0, …, f_r / f_i) of Spa(A_K, A_K°) (the locus where |f_i| is maximal), and these rational subsets cover Spa(A_K, A_K°).
hypotheses: 𝒜 coherent and open (ϖ^N ∈ 𝒜)
X admissible

nodes.title: Raynaud's theorem: quasi-compact admissible formal schemes localised at admissible blow-ups are quasi-compact quasi-separated rigid spaces
nodes.statement: Let K be complete with nontrivial rank-one valuation (not necessarily discrete). The functor X ↦ X_rig from quasi-compact admissible formal O_K-schemes to rigid K-spaces sends admissible blow-ups to isomorphisms and induces an equivalence between (1) the category of quasi-compact admissible formal O_K-schemes localised by admissible blow-ups and (2) the category of quasi-compact quasi-separated rigid K-spaces. Composing with node raynaud-generic-fibre and Huber's equivalence r between quasi-separated rigid K-spaces and quasi-separated adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(K, O_K) (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor), X ↦ d(X) induces an equivalence between (1) and the category of quasi-compact quasi-separated adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(K, O_K). Concretely: (a) admissible blow-ups become isomorphisms; (b) morphisms φ, ψ: Y → X with φ_rig = ψ_rig are equal; (c) for quasi-compact X, Y and any morphism g: Y_rig → X_rig there are an admissible blow-up Y' → Y and a morphism φ: Y' → X inducing g; (d) if g is an isomorphism, φ can be chosen to be an admissible blow-up of X as well; (e) every quasi-compact quasi-separated rigid K-space (resp. adic space as above) has a quasi-compact admissible formal model. Morphisms in the localised category are Hom(X, Y) = colim over admissible blow-ups X' → X of Hom(X', Y) (calculus of fractions, Bosch–Lütkebohmert I §5).
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivial rank one; O_K may be non-noetherian

Quasi-compactness of formal models and quasi-compactness plus quasi-separatedness of rigid spaces are necessary: X ↦ X_rig produces only quasi-separated spaces, and the open unit disc has no quasi-compact formal model
proofSteps: (a): node generic-fibre-inverts-admissible-blow-ups.
(b): φ and ψ agree on rig-points (node rig-point, 3.4) and hence on points (special fibres of rig-points, 3.5); on affines Spf B → Spf A they agree because A → A_K and B → B_K are injective.

(c): choose finite affinoid covers of X_rig and Y_rig with g mapping pieces into pieces; realise them on blow-ups by node quasi-compact-opens-from-blow-ups; in the affine case extend the K-algebra map A_K → B_K to admissible algebras after the blow-up Spf B[g(A)] → Spf B of node bounded-functions-blow-up (g(A) ⊆ B_K° since morphisms of affinoids preserve power-boundedness); glue using (b) and node admissible-blow-up (extension 2.6).

(d): if g is an isomorphism of affinoids, the admissible subalgebra C ⊆ A_K° generated by A and B is a common admissible blow-up of Spf A and Spf B (node bounded-functions-blow-up); globalise with quasi-compact-opens-from-blow-ups and 2.6.

(e): induction on the number of affinoids in a finite cover; affinoids have models (node affinoid-admissible-model); for X = U ∪ V with U ∩ V quasi-compact (quasi-separatedness), make U ∩ V a formal open in both models after blow-up (quasi-compact-opens-from-blow-ups), dominate the two induced models of U ∩ V by a third via (d), extend the blow-ups (2.6) and glue.

Localisation: admissible blow-ups of X satisfy Ore-type axioms (L1)–(L3) (domination by the blow-up of a product ideal, node admissible-blow-up), so the localised category is computed by the colimit formula; (a),(b),(c) give full faithfulness and (e) essential surjectivity.
Adic form: compose with R1's equivalence r for quasi-separated spaces and node raynaud-generic-fibre.

The rigid projective line has formal models P̂¹_{O_K} and all its admissible blow-ups; morphisms between rigid projective lines of degree d are realised on suitable blow-ups.

nodes.title: Generators modulo ϖ generate topologically (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Lemma 1.3(a))
nodes.statement: Conventions: K is complete for a nontrivial rank-one valuation, O_K its valuation ring, ϖ a pseudouniformiser; formal schemes are formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation (node admissible-formal-scheme), X_λ = X ⊗ O_K/ϖ^{λ+1}, X_0 has the underlying space of X, and for t ∈ T_0 the fibre X ⊗ k(t) is X_0 ×_{T_0} Spec k(t). Let f: X → Y be an affine morphism of formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation, ℳ a coherent O_X-module and E ⊆ Γ(X, ℳ) a family of sections, possibly infinite. If the images of E generate f_*(ℳ/ϖℳ) as an O_{Y_0}-module, then E generates f_*ℳ topologically over O_Y: over every formal affine open Spf A ⊆ Y, with f⁻¹(Spf A) = Spf B and ℳ corresponding to the finite B-module M, every m ∈ M is a ϖ-adically convergent sum Σ_{e∈E} a_e e with a_e ∈ A and a_e → 0 (for each λ only finitely many a_e lie outside ϖ^λ A); equivalently the A-linear map Â^{(E)} → M from the ϖ-adic completion of the free A-module on E is surjective.
hypotheses: f affine; X and Y locally of tf presentation over O_K
Generation is required modulo ϖ (the ideal of definition), not modulo m_K
E may be infinite; the conclusion is topological generation, not generation
proofSteps: Reduce to Y = Spf A and X = Spf B affine: the statement is local on Y and f is affine.

M is ϖ-adically complete and separated: it is a finite module over the tfp algebra B, and finitely generated modules over tfp algebras are complete and closed in finite free modules (node saturated-submodule-finitely-generated, Bosch–Lütkebohmert I Lemma 1.2(a),(b)); A is ϖ-adically complete (node topologically-finitely-presented-algebra).

Successive approximation, as in the proof of Bosch–Lütkebohmert I Lemma 1.5 (Nakayama for the nilpotent ideals ϖA/ϖ^{λ+1}A): write m = Σ_e a_e^{(0)} e + ϖm_1 with finitely many a_e^{(0)} ≠ 0, then m_1 = Σ_e a_e^{(1)} e + ϖm_2, and so on; a_e := Σ_k ϖ^k a_e^{(k)} converges in A, for each λ only finitely many a_e lie outside ϖ^λ A, and Σ_e a_e e converges to m in the complete separated module M.
Â^{(E)} is by definition the module of families (a_e) with a_e → 0, so the last formulation is a restatement.

Concretely, over an affine open Spf A ∋ t with Y_0 = V(f̄_{r+1}, …, f̄_n) ⊆ A^n_{A_0} and an (n − r)-minor Δ̄ of the Jacobian matrix (∂f̄_i/∂ξ_j) invertible on Y_0, one may take Y = V(f_{r+1}, …, f_n) ⊆ D^n_T = Spf A⟨ξ_1, …, ξ_n⟩ for arbitrary lifts f_i ∈ A⟨ξ⟩ of the f̄_i, restricted to the open where the lift Δ of Δ̄ is a unit.

The lift is not unique; only its existence after shrinking is claimed

nodes.title: Lifting factorisations through smooth and étale morphisms (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Lemma 1.4(b))
nodes.statement: Let f: (X, x) → (T, t) be a pointed morphism of formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation and suppose the reduction factors as f_0 = h_0 ∘ g_0 with g_0: (X_0, x) → (Y_0, y) and h_0: (Y_0, y) → (T_0, t) smooth. If h_0 is étale (not necessarily affine), the lift (Y, h) exists without shrinking and is unique up to unique isomorphism, and g is unique.

Shrinking is needed in the smooth case only

nodes.title: Connected elementary étale neighbourhoods at points with geometrically irreducible closure are geometrically irreducible (Raynaud–Gruson I, Lemme 1.1.2)
nodes.statement: Let k be a field, Z a k-scheme of finite type that is geometrically normal, z ∈ Z a point whose closure is geometrically irreducible, and (T, t) → (Z, z) a connected elementary étale neighbourhood (T → Z étale, t over z with k(t) = k(z), T connected). Then T is geometrically irreducible over k.
hypotheses: Z geometrically normal and of finite type over k
Elementary: k(t) = k(z)
T connected
proofSteps: For a finite extension k'/k: since the closure of z is geometrically irreducible, k(z) is a primary extension of k, so the fibre of T' = T ⊗_k k' over t, isomorphic to Spec(k' ⊗_k k(t)) = Spec(k' ⊗_k k(z)), consists of one point t'.
Z' = Z ⊗_k k' is normal (Z geometrically normal) and T' is étale over Z', hence normal (Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.Etale), so the connected components of T' are irreducible.

T' → T is finite and flat, so every connected component T'_1 of T' (open and closed) maps onto an open and closed subset of the connected T, i.e. onto T; hence T'_1 contains t'. So T' is connected, hence irreducible; as k' was arbitrary, T is geometrically irreducible.
acceptance: Z = A¹_k, z its generic point, T = A¹_k ∖ {0}: T is geometrically irreducible.
The residue condition is needed: for k = ℝ, Z = Spec ℝ and T = Spec ℂ (connected, étale, k(t) ≠ k(z)), T ⊗_ℝ ℂ = Spec(ℂ × ℂ) is not irreducible.

nodes.title: After an elementary étale base change, a smooth morphism has geometrically integral fibres near a geometrically integral fibre (Raynaud–Gruson I, Lemme 1.1.3)
nodes.statement: Let (S, s) be a pointed scheme and T → S a smooth morphism such that T ⊗ k(s) is geometrically integral of dimension n. There are an elementary étale neighbourhood (S', s') → (S, s) and an open subscheme U' ⊆ T' = T ×_S S' containing T ⊗ k(s') such that all fibres of U' → S' are geometrically integral of dimension n.
hypotheses: T → S smooth
Only the fibre over s is assumed geometrically integral
proofSteps: Let (S̄, s̄) be a strict henselisation of (S, s); T̄ = T ×_S S̄ → S̄ is smooth with non-empty closed fibre, so it has a section σ̄ (EGA IV 17.16.3).

Writing S̄ as a filtered limit of schemes finite étale over the henselisation, obtain an elementary étale neighbourhood (S', s') and a finite étale surjective S_1 → S' with a single point s_1 over s' such that T_1 = T ×_S S_1 has a section σ_1.

The union U_1 of the connected components of the fibres of T_1 → S_1 meeting σ_1(S_1) is open (EGA IV 15.6.5) and contains T_1 ⊗ k(s_1); the smooth U_1 → S_1 has a section and connected fibres, which are therefore geometrically integral (node rg-etale-neighbourhood-irreducible), of dimension n after shrinking S'.
p: T_1 → T' is finite, hence closed; U' := T' ∖ p(T_1 ∖ U_1) is open, contains T ⊗ k(s') and satisfies p⁻¹(U') ⊆ U_1, so the fibres of U' → S' are geometrically integral of dimension n.
acceptance: If all fibres of T → S are geometrically integral (for instance T = A^n_S), one can take S' = S and U' = T.
Shrinking is needed: over S = Spec k[u], T = A¹_S ⊔ A¹_{D(u)} is smooth with geometrically integral fibre over s = (u) but two-component fibres over u ≠ 0; U' = A¹_S works and U' ≠ T.

nodes.title: Étale-local structure of a morphism locally of finite type: finite over smooth with geometrically integral fibres (Raynaud–Gruson I, Théorème 1.1.1)
nodes.statement: Let f: (X, x) → (S, s) be a pointed morphism of schemes with X locally of finite type over S, and n = dim_x(X ⊗ k(s)). There is a commutative diagram of pointed schemes (Y, y) → (T, t) → (S', s') over (X, x) → (S, s) such that (a) Y, T and S' are affine and (Y, y) → (X, x), (S', s') → (S, s) are elementary étale neighbourhoods; (b) T → S' is smooth with geometrically integral fibres of dimension n; (c) Y → T is finite and y is the only point of Y above t.
hypotheses: X locally of finite type over S (no noetherian hypothesis)
Elementary étale: trivial residue field extension at the marked points
proofSteps: Localise: S = Spec A, X = Spec B, with every irreducible component of f⁻¹(s) through x. Choose a closed specialisation ξ of x in f⁻¹(s) and b_1, …, b_n ∈ B whose images form a system of parameters of B_ξ ⊗ k(s) (the first r of them one of B_x ⊗ k(s)); the morphism g: X → Z = A^n_S = Spec A[T_1, …, T_n] they define is quasi-finite at x (EGA IV 13.1.3) and the closure of z = g(x) in Z ⊗ k(s) is geometrically integral.

Zariski's Main Theorem, étale-locally: after an elementary étale neighbourhood (Z_1, z_1) → (Z, z) there is an open and closed Y_1 ⊆ X ×_Z Z_1, finite over Z_1, in which the point x_1 over (x, z_1) is the only point above z_1 (Raynaud–Gruson use EGA IV 18.5.11 over the henselisation and pass to the limit; Mathlib's AlgebraicGeometry.exists_etale_isCompl_of_quasiFiniteAt gives the decomposition for separated f over an étale, not necessarily elementary, neighbourhood).
Z_1 → S is smooth, and after shrinking Z_1 ⊗ k(s) is geometrically integral (node rg-etale-neighbourhood-irreducible, applied to A^n_{k(s)} and the point z).

Apply node rg-geometrically-integral-fibres-etale-locally to Z_1 → S at s: an elementary étale (S', s') and an open U' ⊆ Z_1 ×_S S' with geometrically integral fibres of dimension n; let T be an affine open neighbourhood in U' of the point over (z_1, s'), shrunk so that T → S' is surjective (smooth morphisms are open), and Y = Y_1 ×_{Z_1} T with y the point over (x_1, t).

X = A^n_S: T = X restricted to an affine open neighbourhood, Y = T.
X = Spec k[a, b]/(b² − a³) over S = Spec k at the cusp: n = 1, T = A¹_k with coordinate a, and Y → T finite of degree 2 with a single point over a = 0.

The dimension is that of the fibre of the reduction at x

nodes.title: A smooth algebra with geometrically integral fibres is a projective module (Raynaud–Gruson I, Proposition 3.3.1)
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring and B a smooth A-algebra (Mathlib Algebra.Smooth: finitely presented and formally smooth) all of whose fibres B ⊗_A k(p), p ∈ Spec A, are geometrically integral. Then B is a projective A-module (Mathlib Module.Projective).
hypotheses: A arbitrary (no noetherian hypothesis)
Every fibre geometrically integral (empty fibres excluded)
proofSteps: Reduce to A noetherian: descend to a finitely generated ℤ-subalgebra A_0 ⊆ A with a smooth A_0-algebra B_0 and B ≅ A ⊗_{A_0} B_0 (Mathlib Algebra.Smooth.exists_finiteType), keeping geometric integrality of the fibres (EGA IV 9.7.7); projectivity is stable under base change.

B is countably presented as an A-module, so projectivity may be checked after a faithfully flat extension A → A' (Raynaud–Gruson 3.1.4); after the base change A → B the algebra has an augmentation (codiagonal) with ideal I.
B smooth gives I/I² finite projective and gr_I(B) ≅ Sym(I/I²) (EGA 0_IV 19.5.4); localising (again 3.1.4) make I/I² free of rank n, so the I-adic completion B̂ is A[[t_1, …, t_n]].

By Raynaud–Gruson 3.1.5 it suffices that B → B̂ be A-universally injective; B̂ is B-flat, so by Raynaud–Gruson 3.2.6 this holds once the image of Spec B̂ contains Ass_{B/A}(B), which follows from the faithful flatness of B̂ over A and the integrality of the fibres of B.
acceptance: B = A[t_1, …, t_n]: free on the monomials.
B = A[t, t⁻¹]: free on the t^k, k ∈ ℤ.

The fibre hypothesis is needed: B = k[u, u⁻¹] over A = k[u] is smooth with empty fibre over u = 0, and is not a projective k[u]-module (a projective module over a principal ideal domain is free, and k[u, u⁻¹] is u-divisible).

nodes.title: Ideals of coefficients (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Definition 2.1, Remark 2.2)
nodes.statement: Let h: Z → T be a morphism of formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation and 𝒥 ⊆ O_Z a coherent ideal, with closed formal subscheme V(𝒥) (locally Spf(B/b), b finitely generated). A coherent ideal 𝒞 ⊆ O_T is an ideal of coefficients of 𝒥 if (i) the projection Z ×_T V(𝒞) → Z factors through V(𝒥), and (ii) for every morphism T' → T of formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation such that Z ×_T T' → Z factors through V(𝒥), the morphism T' → T factors through V(𝒞). Equivalently: 𝒥 ⊆ 𝒞O_Z, 𝒞 is the smallest coherent ideal of O_T with this property, and this remains true after every base change T' → T. An ideal of coefficients is unique when it exists; its formation commutes with base change (𝒞O_{T'} is the ideal of coefficients of 𝒥O_{Z×_T T'}) and with restriction to opens of T, so local ideals of coefficients glue. Set-theoretically, V(𝒞) ∩ T_0 is the set of t ∈ T_0 whose fibre Z ⊗ k(t) is contained in V(𝒥). nodes.title: Existence of ideals of coefficients for open ideals along smooth morphisms with geometrically irreducible fibres (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Proposition 2.3(b))
nodes.statement: Let h: Z → T be a quasi-compact morphism of formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation that is, locally on T, affine, smooth and surjective with geometrically irreducible fibres of constant dimension. (a) Every open coherent ideal 𝒥 ⊆ O_Z (ϖ^N O_Z ⊆ 𝒥) has an ideal of coefficients in O_T (node ideal-of-coefficients), and it is open. In the affine case Z = Spf B → T = Spf A with a topological basis (e_i) of B over A and 𝒥 ↔ b = (f_1, …, f_r), it is the ideal a = (a_{ij}) of coordinates f_j = Σ_i a_{ij} e_i, which is finitely generated. (b) If T = Spf R with R a complete valuation ring of height one (R = O_L, L/K finite), every finitely generated ideal b ⊆ B has an ideal of coefficients, generated by the coordinate of largest absolute value of each generator; in particular every content c(f) is principal. (Bosch–Lütkebohmert state (a) more generally for affine pure flat morphisms and for flat morphisms with geometrically irreducible fibres without embedded components; only the smooth case is used.)
hypotheses: h smooth, surjective, fibres geometrically irreducible of constant dimension
𝒥 open in (a); b arbitrary finitely generated in (b)
proofSteps: Locally on T_0, B has a topological basis over A (node smooth-geometrically-irreducible-topological-basis); by uniqueness and base-change compatibility (node ideal-of-coefficients) local ideals of coefficients glue, so assume Z = Spf B → T = Spf A with a topological basis (e_i).

(a) Since b is open, ϖ^λ ∈ b ⊆ B·(closure of the coordinate ideal), hence ϖ^λ ∈ a; modulo ϖ^λ each f_j has only finitely many non-zero coordinates, so a is generated by ϖ^λ and finitely many a_{ij}: a is finitely generated and open.

a is the ideal of coefficients: finitely generated ideals of B are closed (node flat-tft-is-tfp (b)), so b ⊆ Ba; if b ⊆ Bc then all a_{ij} ∈ c by uniqueness of coordinates (Bc = {Σ c_i e_i : c_i ∈ c} for c finitely generated); both properties persist after base change A → A' because (e_i ⊗ 1) is a topological basis of B ⊗̂_A A' and the coordinates of f_j ⊗ 1 are the images of the a_{ij}.
(b) Over R, the coordinates of f ∈ B tend to 0, so the ideal they generate is generated by one of maximal absolute value; the argument of the previous step applies to this finitely generated ideal.
acceptance: Z = Spf O_K⟨a, ζ⟩ → T = Spf O_K⟨a⟩ and 𝒥 = (aζ + ϖ, ϖ²): the coordinates are ϖ, a, ϖ², so 𝒞 = (a, ϖ).
Over R = O_K: c(ϖ + ϖ²ζ + ζ²) = O_K and c(ϖ³ζ + ϖ²) = (ϖ²).

nodes.statement: Let a smooth surjective morphism h: Z = Spf B → T = Spf A of formal schemes locally of tf presentation over a complete valuation ring R of height one (R = O_K, or R = O_L for a finite extension L/K, as needed after base change to rig-points) whose fibres Z ⊗ k(t), t ∈ T_0, are geometrically irreducible of one dimension m, and let f ∈ B be an element that does not vanish identically on any fibre of Z_0 → T_0. Then for every λ ∈ ℕ the image of f in B_λ = B/ϖ^{λ+1}B is a non-zero-divisor.

proofSteps: Z_λ = Spec B_λ → T_λ = Spec A_λ is smooth with geometrically integral fibres (the fibres of Z_λ are those of Z_0; smooth fibres are geometrically reduced); the claim is local on T_λ and may be checked after an étale surjective base change, after which Z_λ ∖ V(f) → T_λ has a section.

nodes.title: Fibres over the generic fibre of the base are integral (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Proposition 2.4(a), classical rigid case)
nodes.statement: Let h: Z = Spf B → T = Spf A be a smooth surjective morphism of admissible formal O_K-schemes whose fibres Z ⊗ k(t), t ∈ T_0, are geometrically irreducible of constant dimension m. For every prime p ⊆ A with ϖ ∉ p (a point of Spec A_K), pB is a prime ideal of B lying over p; it is the generic point of the fibre of Spec B → Spec A over p, and that fibre is irreducible and reduced. (Over primes containing ϖ the fibres are those of Z_0 → T_0, geometrically integral by hypothesis, so all fibres of Spec B → Spec A are irreducible and reduced.)
hypotheses: A, B admissible
h smooth, surjective, fibres geometrically irreducible of constant dimension
proofSteps: Reduction to 'A a domain ⇒ B a domain': A/p is topologically of finite type without ϖ-torsion, hence admissible (node flat-tft-is-tfp), so p is finitely generated and B/pB = B ⊗̂_A A/p is smooth surjective over A/p with the same fibres over V(ϖ); if B/pB is a domain then pB is prime, pB ∩ A = p, and B ⊗_A k(p), a localisation of B/pB, is integral with generic point pB.

Let A be a domain and f_1 f_2 = 0 with f_1, f_2 ≠ 0. The rigid ideals of coefficients a_i ⊆ A_K of (f_i)_K exist and are non-zero (node rig-ideal-of-coefficients-existence (i)); A_K is a Jacobson domain (node R0/affinoid-jacobson), so some maximal ideal m ⊆ A_K satisfies a_1 a_2 ⊄ m.

m corresponds to a rig-point u: Spf V' → T whose normalisation V is the valuation ring of the finite extension A_K/m of K (node rig-point); by base change (node ideal-of-coefficients) the contents of u*f_i in B_V = B ⊗̂_A V are a_iV ≠ 0.
Over the valuation ring V, node content-ideal-product gives c(u*f_1 · u*f_2) = c(u*f_1)c(u*f_2) ≠ 0 (V a domain), so u*(f_1 f_2) ≠ 0, contradicting f_1 f_2 = 0.
acceptance: A = O_K⟨a⟩, B = A⟨ζ⟩ and p = (a − ϖ): pB is prime with B/pB ≅ O_K⟨ζ⟩.
Smoothness is needed: for B = A⟨ζ⟩/(ζ² − a) (not smooth along a = 0 in T_0) and p = (a − ϖ²), B/pB = O_K⟨ζ⟩/((ζ − ϖ)(ζ + ϖ)) is not a domain.

nodes.title: Associated primes of B are generic points of fibres over the generic fibre (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Proposition 2.4(b))
nodes.statement: In the situation of node smooth-geometrically-irreducible-generic-fibres-integral (A admissible), every associated prime q of B — in the sense of Raynaud–Gruson I 3.2.1: qB_q is the radical of the annihilator in B_q of an element of B_q (Mathlib associatedPrimes applied to B_q) — is of the form pB with p an associated prime of A not containing ϖ; in particular q is the generic point of a fibre over a point outside the special fibre, and B has no ϖ-torsion.
hypotheses: A admissible (no ϖ-torsion)
proofSteps: B is flat over A (h smooth, node smooth-formal-scheme) and A has no ϖ-torsion, so ϖ is a non-zero-divisor on B; no associated prime contains ϖ, and Ass(B) = Ass(B_K) under Spec B_K ⊆ Spec B.

B_K and A_K are noetherian (anchor Layer 0) and B_K is flat over A_K, so the associated primes of B_K are those of the fibres B_K/pB_K ⊗ k(p) over the associated primes p of A_K (Bourbaki, Algèbre commutative IV §2 no 6 Théorème 2).
By node smooth-geometrically-irreducible-generic-fibres-integral the fibre over p is integral with generic point pB, which is therefore its only associated prime.
acceptance: A = O_K⟨a⟩ and B = A⟨ζ⟩: the only associated prime of B is (0) = (0)B.

nodes.title: T-dévissages of a coherent module in one dimension (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Definition 3.1)
nodes.statement: Conventions: K is complete for a nontrivial rank-one valuation, O_K its valuation ring, ϖ a pseudouniformiser; formal schemes are formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation (node admissible-formal-scheme), X_λ = X ⊗ O_K/ϖ^{λ+1}, X_0 has the underlying space of X, and for t ∈ T_0 the fibre X ⊗ k(t) is X_0 ×_{T_0} Spec k(t). Let f: X → T be a morphism of quasi-compact formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation, ℳ a coherent O_X-module (node admissible-formal-scheme, coherent modules), x ∈ X_0, t = f(x) and n ∈ ℕ. A T-dévissage of ℳ in dimension n at x is a tuple D = (g: (Y, y) → (Z, z), ℳ, α: ℒ → 𝒩, 𝒫) consisting of (a) a pointed closed immersion (Y, y) → (X, x) of finite presentation whose ideal annihilates ℳ, so that ℳ is the direct image of a coherent O_Y-module, again written ℳ; (b) a pointed factorisation (Y, y) →g (Z, z) →h (T, t) of Y → T with g finite, y the only point of Y_0 above z, and h affine and smooth with geometrically irreducible fibres of dimension n; (c) a homomorphism α: ℒ = O_Z^ℓ → 𝒩 := g_*ℳ of coherent O_Z-modules such that α ⊗ k(ζ) is bijective, ζ the generic point of the fibre Z ⊗ k(t); 𝒫 := coker α. Then dim_z(𝒫 ⊗ k(t)) ≤ n − 1, and 𝒫 is a module over a closed formal subscheme Y' ⊆ Z of finite presentation with dim(Y' ⊗ k(t)) ≤ n − 1. The fibre dimension of ℳ at x is at most n (Definition 3.1 does not require equality). Dévissages pull back along pointed base changes (T', t') → (T, t).
hypotheses: X, T quasi-compact and locally of tf presentation over O_K (Bosch–Lütkebohmert's standing assumption in §3)
h has geometrically irreducible fibres, so the fibre over t has a single generic point ζ
ℓ = 0 is allowed (then 𝒩 ⊗ k(ζ) = 0)
proofSteps: dim_z(𝒫 ⊗ k(t)) ≤ n − 1: α ⊗ k(ζ) is surjective, so 𝒫_ζ = 0 by Nakayama, and the support of 𝒫 ⊗ k(t) is a closed subset of the irreducible n-dimensional fibre not containing ζ.

The closed subscheme Y': the annihilator of 𝒫 contains a finitely generated ideal with the same image in the noetherian ring of the fibre (Raynaud–Gruson I 1.2.1.1; node tfp-algebra-coherent for coherence of annihilators).

Base change: closed immersions of finite presentation, finite morphisms, smoothness with geometrically irreducible fibres and bijectivity of α ⊗ k(ζ) at the generic point of the base-changed fibre are preserved (fibre products of formal schemes, node F0/formal-fibre-product).
acceptance: X = Z = D^n_T = Spf A⟨ξ_1, …, ξ_n⟩ → T = Spf A, ℳ = O_X^ℓ, g = id and α = id: a T-dévissage in dimension n with 𝒫 = 0.

nodes.title: T-dévissages in several dimensions and complete dévissages (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Definition 3.2)
nodes.statement: In the setting of node formal-devissage-step, a T-dévissage of ℳ at x in dimensions N = n¹ > n² > … > n^r = n ≥ 0 (between N and n) is a sequence (D¹, …, D^r) of T-dévissages D^i = (g^i: (Y^i, y^i) → (Z^i, z^i), ℳ^i, α^i: ℒ^i → 𝒩^i = g^i_*ℳ^i, 𝒫^i) such that D¹ is a T-dévissage of ℳ at x in dimension n¹ and, for i = 2, …, r, D^i is a T-dévissage of the coherent O_{Z^{i−1}}-module 𝒫^{i−1} at z^{i−1} in dimension n^i; thus ℳ¹ = ℳ|_{Y¹} and ℳ^i = 𝒫^{i−1}|_{Y^i}. Its length is r; it is complete if 𝒫^r = 0. Dévissages, complete or not, are stable under base change (T', t') → (T, t), and truncations (D¹, …, D^k) are dévissages in dimensions between N and n^k. The support of 𝒩^i has relative dimension ≤ n^i and that of 𝒫^i relative dimension < n^i, which is what makes dévissages the vehicle for induction on relative dimension.
hypotheses: Dimensions strictly decreasing
Completeness is the condition 𝒫^r = 0
proofSteps: Well-definedness and base change follow step by step from node formal-devissage-step.
Truncation is immediate from the recursive definition.
acceptance: For ℳ = O_X^ℓ on X = D^N_T, the one-step dévissage with α = id is complete of length 1.

nodes.title: Existence of complete dévissages after elementary étale localisation (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Proposition 3.3)
nodes.statement: Let f: (X, x) → (T, t) be a pointed morphism of formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation and ℳ a coherent O_X-module with ℳ_x ≠ 0; N = dim_x(ℳ ⊗ k(t)). There is a commutative square (X, x) ←u (X', x') →f' (T', t') →v (T, t) with u, v elementary étale affine neighbourhoods such that ℳ' = u*ℳ admits a complete T'-dévissage at x' in dimensions between N and some n ≥ 0 (node formal-devissage); for any prescribed m with 0 ≤ m ≤ N the dévissage can be chosen to have m among its dimensions. (Bosch–Lütkebohmert, following Raynaud–Gruson 1.2.3, moreover bound n ≥ N − r with r the codepth of ℳ_x ⊗ k(t); that bound, which needs depth theory, is not used by the flattening proof and is not part of this node.)
hypotheses: ℳ_x ≠ 0
Elementary étale localisation of both X and T is needed
proofSteps: Affine reduction; choose a closed formal subscheme Y ⊆ X of finite presentation with ℳ an O_Y-module and dim_x(Y ⊗ k(t)) = N (Raynaud–Gruson 1.2.1.1); elementary étale neighbourhoods of (Y, x) extend to elementary étale neighbourhoods of (X, x) (local structure of étale algebras, Mathlib Algebra.IsEtaleAt.exists_isStandardEtale, applied to the reductions and lifted by node formal-etale-site-invariance), so replace X by Y.

Node formal-zariski-local-structure: after elementary étale localisation, (X, x) →g (Z, z) →h (T, t) with h smooth with geometrically irreducible fibres of dimension N, g finite and x the only point above z; put 𝒩 = g_*ℳ.

The fibre Z ⊗ k(t) is integral, so (𝒩 ⊗ k(t))_ζ is a vector space over k(ζ) of some dimension ℓ; lifting a basis to sections of 𝒩 over the affine Z gives α: O_Z^ℓ → 𝒩 with α ⊗ k(ζ) bijective, and 𝒫 = coker α has fibre dimension ≤ N − 1 at z (node formal-devissage-step).

Recursion on dimension: if 𝒫_z = 0, shrink Z and T (smooth maps are open) so that 𝒫 = 0 and the dévissage is complete; otherwise apply the previous steps to 𝒫 on Z at z, after a further elementary étale localisation of T and base change of the first step (node formal-devissage-step, base change). The dimensions strictly decrease, so at most N + 1 steps occur.

Prescribed dimension m: when the current cokernel has fibre dimension d < m below the previous dimension, compose the finite map of the construction in dimension d with the zero section into Z ×_T D^{m−d}_T, whose fibres over T are geometrically irreducible of dimension m, and take ℓ = 0 (𝒩 ⊗ k(ζ) = 0 as the support has dimension d < m).
acceptance: X = Spf O_K⟨ζ, ξ⟩/(ζξ − ϖ) → T = Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩ at x = (ζ, ξ), ℳ = O_X: Z = D¹_T, g the closed immersion and α: O_Z → g_*O_X the quotient map give a complete dévissage of length one in dimension N = 1, without étale localisation.

nodes.title: Universal injectivity of α at z is bijectivity at the generic point of the fibre (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Lemma 3.6)
nodes.statement: Let h: (Z, z) → (T, t) be a pointed affine morphism of formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation that is smooth and surjective with all fibres geometrically irreducible of one dimension (as in a dévissage step), ζ the generic point of Z ⊗ k(t), and α: ℒ = O_Z^ℓ → 𝒩 a homomorphism to a coherent O_Z-module with α ⊗ k(ζ) bijective. The following are equivalent: (a) α_z: ℒ_z → 𝒩_z is O_{T,t}-universally injective; (b) α_z is injective; (c) α_ζ is bijective.
hypotheses: h smooth, surjective, all fibres geometrically irreducible of the same dimension (Bosch–Lütkebohmert assume this for the fibre over t; all fibres is the dévissage situation)
α ⊗ k(ζ) bijective
proofSteps: α_ζ is surjective by Nakayama. O_{Z,z} → O_{Z,ζ} is flat (node formal-stalk-generization-flat), so (a) ⇒ (b) ⇒ (c) (α_ζ = α_z ⊗ O_{Z,ζ}).

(c) ⇒ (a): in the square formed by α_z, α_ζ and the localisations it suffices that O_{Z,z} → O_{Z,ζ} be O_{T,t}-universally injective, i.e. (1) O_{Z,z} → O_{Z,ζ} is injective and (2) O_{Z,ζ}/O_{Z,z} is O_{T,t}-flat.

(2): for a finitely generated ideal a ⊆ O_{T,t}, O_{Z,ζ} is O_{T,t}-flat (h flat and the previous step), so it suffices that O_{Z,z}/aO_{Z,z} → O_{Z,ζ}/aO_{Z,ζ} is injective; a is induced by a coherent ideal near t, and replacing T by V(a) (a base change keeping the hypotheses) reduces (2) to (1).

(1): a germ in the kernel is represented by g ∈ B⟨b⁻¹⟩ (Spf B⟨b⁻¹⟩ ∋ z) with fg = 0 for some f ∈ B⟨b⁻¹⟩ not vanishing at ζ; after shrinking T around t, f vanishes on no fibre, so f is a non-zero-divisor on B⟨b⁻¹⟩ (nodes nonvanishing-on-fibres-nonzerodivisor-levels and nonvanishing-on-fibres-nonzerodivisor; Bosch–Lütkebohmert quote the proof of Raynaud–Gruson 2.2 for the level-wise statement) and g = 0.
acceptance: Z = D¹_T for T = Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩, 𝒩 = O_Z/(ζξ − ϖ), α the quotient map, z = (ζ, ξ): ζξ − ϖ ≠ 0 in O_{Z,ζ}, so α_ζ is not bijective, and α_z is not injective, as (b) ⇔ (c) predicts.
α = id on ℒ = 𝒩 = O_Z^ℓ: all three conditions hold.

nodes.title: Flatness in terms of a dévissage (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Proposition 3.5)
nodes.statement: Let f: (X, x) → (T, t) and ℳ be as in node formal-devissage-existence, with elementary étale affine neighbourhoods u: (X', x') → (X, x), v: (T', t') → (T, t) such that ℳ' = u*ℳ admits a T'-dévissage (D¹, …, D^r) at x' in dimensions between N = n¹ and n = n^r (node formal-devissage), D^i = (g^i: (Y^i, y^i) → (Z^i, z^i), ℳ^i, α^i: ℒ^i → 𝒩^i, 𝒫^i), ζ^i the generic point of Z^i ⊗ k(t'). The following are equivalent: (a) ℳ_x is O_{T,t}-flat; (b) 𝒩^i_{z^i} is O_{T',t'}-flat for all i; (c) α^i is bijective at ζ^i for all i and 𝒫^r_{z^r} is O_{T',t'}-flat; (d) α^i is injective at z^i for all i and 𝒫^r_{z^r} is O_{T',t'}-flat; (e) α^i is T'-universally injective over an open neighbourhood of t' for all i and 𝒫^r_{z^r} is O_{T',t'}-flat.
hypotheses: A dévissage, not necessarily complete; for a complete one the conditions on 𝒫^r are empty
proofSteps: Induction on r reduces to r = 1: 𝒫¹ coincides with ℳ² as an O_{T'}-module near z¹ (g² finite, y² the only point above z²), so the conditions for (D², …, D^r) apply to 𝒫¹.
(a) ⇔ (b): flatness is étale local on source and target (u, v étale), and 𝒩_z ≅ ℳ'_{x'} as O_{T',t'}-modules because g is finite and x' is the only point above z.

nodes.title: Flat locus and flatness in dimension ≥ n (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II §3, after Corollary 3.8)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → T be a morphism of formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation and ℳ a coherent O_X-module. The flat locus of ℳ over T is F(ℳ/T) = {x ∈ X_0 : ℳ_x is a flat O_{T,f(x)}-module} ⊆ X_0 (points of X_0 are the points of X). For n ∈ ℕ and x ∈ X_0 with t = f(x), ℳ is T-flat in dimension ≥ n at x if dim_x((X_0 ∖ F(ℳ/T)) ∩ (X ⊗ k(t))) < n — the dimension at x of the non-flat locus inside the fibre, −∞ when x is not in its closure; ℳ is T-flat in dimension ≥ n if this holds at every x ∈ X_0, and T-flat in dimension ≥ n over an open U_0 ⊆ T_0 if it holds at every x over U_0. A morphism f is flat in dimension ≥ n if O_X is. Flatness in dimension ≥ n implies flatness in dimension ≥ n + 1, and if dim(X/T) ≤ n then every ℳ is T-flat in dimension ≥ n + 1. (Raynaud–Gruson 5.2.1 give the scheme-theoretic notion through a retrocompact open of flatness with small complement.)

nodes.statement: Let f: (X, x) → (T, t) be a pointed morphism of formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation, ℳ a coherent O_X-module with N = dim_x(ℳ ⊗ k(t)), n an integer with 0 ≤ n < N, and u: (X', x') → (X, x), v: (T', t') → (T, t) elementary étale affine neighbourhoods such that ℳ' = u*ℳ admits a T'-dévissage (D¹, …, D^r) at x' in dimensions between N = n¹ and n = n^r (node formal-devissage). nodes.title: Rig-flatness, relative rig-dimension and rig-flatness in dimension ≥ n (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I §5; II Definition 3.9 and §4)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → T be a morphism of quasi-compact formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation with T admissible, and ℳ a coherent O_X-module. (i) Rig-flatness: for formal affine opens Spf C ⊆ X and Spf A ⊆ T with f(Spf C) ⊆ Spf A, ℳ ↔ the finite C-module M, and a rig-point x of Spf C (a maximal ideal of C_K = C ⊗_{O_K} K, node rig-point), ℳ is rig-flat over T at x if the localisation M_x is a flat A-module (equivalently (M_K)_x is flat over (A_K)_y, y the image maximal ideal); this is independent of the charts and invariant under admissible blow-ups of X and of T (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I Proposition 5.3). (ii) Relative rig-dimension (II Definition 3.9): for a rig-point x of X over the rig-point t of T, dim_x(X/T) is the Krull dimension of the local ring at x of the affinoid algebra C_K ⊗_{A_K} K(t), K(t) = A_K/t — the dimension at x of the rigid fibre X_rig ×_{T_rig} t; for a closed formal subscheme Y ⊆ X, dim(Y/T)_rig is the supremum of dim_y(Y/T) over the rig-points y of Y (−∞ if there are none). (iii) ℳ is rig-flat over T in dimension ≥ n if there is a closed formal subscheme Y ⊆ X of finite presentation with dim(Y/T)_rig ≤ n − 1 such that ℳ is rig-flat at every rig-point of X not factoring through Y; above a rig-point t of T if this holds for the rig-points of X and Y over t. Rig-flat in dimension ≥ 0 means rig-flat at every rig-point ('f_rig flat' for ℳ = O_X); if dim(X/T)_rig ≤ n − 1 then ℳ is rig-flat in dimension ≥ n.
hypotheses: T admissible; X locally of tf presentation, possibly with ϖ-torsion
Dimensions are those of rigid fibres over rig-points of T
Bosch–Lütkebohmert's Proposition 3.11 (the non-rig-flat locus is Zariski closed) is not needed: (iii) quantifies over closed subschemes Y
proofSteps: Independence of charts and invariance under admissible blow-ups: the charts of an admissible blow-up have generic fibres rational subdomains (node generic-fibre-inverts-admissible-blow-ups), and restriction maps to rational subdomains of affinoids are flat (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.flat_toCompletionLoc), as in Bosch–Lütkebohmert I Lemmas 5.4, 5.5.
Relative dimension is well defined because rig-points correspond to maximal ideals of C_K and K(t) is finite over K (node rig-point).
The comparison with flatness of d(f) at classical points uses that the rigid local ring O_{d(X),x} is faithfully flat over (C_K)_x with the same completion (node R1/rigid-local-ring-completion).

nodes.title: Rig-flatness in top dimension is freeness at the generic point of the fibre (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Proposition 3.12)
nodes.statement: Let T = Spf A be admissible and h: Z = Spf B → T affine, smooth and surjective with geometrically irreducible fibres of dimension m. Let X → T be locally of tf presentation with a closed immersion Y ⊆ X of finite presentation, and ℳ a coherent O_X-module that is an O_Y-module admitting a T-dévissage (g: Y → Z, ℳ, α: ℒ → 𝒩, 𝒫) in dimension m (node formal-devissage-step), with m = dim(Y/T) = dim(Z/T); M = Γ(Y, ℳ), N = Γ(Z, 𝒩). Let t be a rig-point of T, viewed as a prime t ⊆ A with ϖ ∉ t, and ζ = tB, the prime ideal that is the generic point of the fibre over t (node smooth-geometrically-irreducible-generic-fibres-integral). The following are equivalent: (a) ℳ is rig-flat over T in dimension ≥ m above t (node rig-flat-in-dimension); (b) 𝒩 is rig-flat over T in dimension ≥ m above t; (c) N_ζ is flat over A_t; (d) N_ζ is free over B_ζ.
hypotheses: t a rig-point (a maximal ideal of A_K)
Fibres of h geometrically irreducible (Bosch–Lütkebohmert: geometrically connected, equivalent for smooth fibres)
proofSteps: (a) ⇔ (b): M and N coincide as A-modules and g is finite (node rig-flat-in-dimension, finite push-forward).

(b) ⇒ (c): the rigid fibre of Z over t is irreducible of dimension m (node smooth-geometrically-irreducible-generic-fibres-integral) and the non-rig-flat locus above t has dimension ≤ m − 1, so some rig-point z above t has N_z flat over A_t (rig-flatness on the affine chart, Bosch–Lütkebohmert I 5.3(a)); N_ζ is a localisation of N_z (ζ ⊆ z), hence A_t-flat.

(c) ⇒ (d): (B/tB)_ζ is a field, so (N/tN)_ζ is free over it; A_t → B_ζ is flat and local, and A_t, B_ζ are localisations of the noetherian affinoid algebras A_K, B_K (anchor Layer 0); by the fibrewise flatness criterion (Bourbaki, Algèbre commutative III §5 no 4 Proposition 3) N_ζ is B_ζ-flat, hence free (Mathlib Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing, N_ζ finite).

(d) ⇒ (a): N is free on a neighbourhood of ζ in Spec B_K and A_t → B_ζ is flat, so the non-rig-flat locus of 𝒩 above t misses a dense open of the irreducible m-dimensional rigid fibre and has dimension ≤ m − 1; conclude with (a) ⇔ (b).

nodes.title: Fitting ideals of coherent modules on formal schemes (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Definition 3.13)
nodes.statement: Let X be a formal O_K-scheme locally of tf presentation and ℳ a coherent O_X-module. For r ∈ ℕ the r-th Fitting ideal F_r(ℳ) ⊆ O_X is the coherent ideal given on a formal affine open U = Spf A by the ring-level Fitting ideal F_r(M) ⊆ A of the finitely presented A-module M = Γ(U, ℳ): for a presentation A^m →φ A^n → M → 0, F_r(M) is generated by the (n − r) × (n − r) minors of φ (F_r(M) = A if n − r ≤ 0), independently of the presentation and compatibly with base change, F_r(M ⊗_A A') = F_r(M)A' (Raynaud–Gruson I 5.4.1; the ring-level Fitting ideal of finitely presented modules is owned by the Tau Ceti roadmap StableReduction, Layer 0). These glue to a coherent ideal F_r(ℳ), compatible with restriction and with pull-back along morphisms of formal schemes; F_0(ℳ) ⊆ F_1(ℳ) ⊆ …; F_r(ℳ)_x = O_{X,x} iff ℳ_x is generated by r elements; if ℳ is locally free of rank r then F_{r−1}(ℳ) = 0 and F_r(ℳ) = O_X.

nodes.title: A principal Fitting ideal makes M/Ann_M(F_r(M)) generated by r elements (Raynaud–Gruson I, Lemme 5.4.2)
nodes.statement: Let A be a ring, M a finitely presented A-module and r ∈ ℕ. If the r-th Fitting ideal F_r(M) is locally principal, then M/Ann_M(F_r(M)) is locally generated by r elements (Ann_M(I) = {m ∈ M : Im = 0}).
hypotheses: M finitely presented
F_r(M) locally generated by one element
proofSteps: The statement is local: assume A local, with a presentation A^m →u A^n → M → 0; F_r(M), generated by the (n − r)-minors of u and monogenic over the local ring A, is generated by one of them; after renumbering (and replacing M by a module of which it is a quotient) F_r(M) = (D) with D = det(u_{ij})_{1≤i,j≤n−r}.

With m_1, …, m_n the images of the basis, Σ_j u_{ij} m_j = 0 for 1 ≤ i ≤ n − r; Cramer's rule (Mathlib Matrix.mulVec_cramer) gives D m_i + Σ_{n−r<j≤n} D_{ji} m_j = 0, where D_{ji} ∈ F_r(M) replaces the i-th column by the j-th; write D_{ji} = b_{ji} D.
Then D·(m_i + Σ_j b_{ji} m_j) = 0 and F_r(M) = (D), so m_i + Σ_j b_{ji} m_j ∈ Ann_M(F_r(M)): M/Ann_M(F_r(M)) is generated by the images of m_{n−r+1}, …, m_n.
acceptance: A a domain, a ≠ 0, M = A/(a) ⊕ A, r = 1: F_1(M) = (a), Ann_M((a)) = A/(a) ⊕ 0, and M/Ann_M(F_1(M)) ≅ A is generated by one element.

nodes.title: An invertible Fitting ideal and generic freeness give local freeness modulo the annihilator (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Lemma 3.14 = Raynaud–Gruson I, Lemme 5.4.3)
nodes.statement: Let A be a ring, M a finitely presented A-module and r ∈ ℕ. Assume that M is free of rank r at every associated point of A (in the sense of Raynaud–Gruson I 3.2.1: primes p such that pA_p is the radical of the annihilator of an element of A_p, Mathlib associatedPrimes applied to A_p) and that F_r(M) is an invertible ideal (locally generated by one non-zero-divisor). Then M/Ann_M(F_r(M)) is locally free of rank r.
hypotheses: M finitely presented; A arbitrary (associated points in the weak sense of Raynaud–Gruson)
F_r(M) invertible
proofSteps: Put N = M/Ann_M(F_r(M)). At an associated point p, M_p is free of rank r, so F_r(M)_p = A_p and Ann_M(F_r(M))_p = 0: N_p = M_p is free of rank r.
Locally, F_r(M) is principal, so node rg-fitting-ideal-principal-generators gives an exact sequence 0 → 𝒦 → A^r → N → 0.

𝒦 ⊆ A^r, so the associated points of 𝒦 are associated points of A (Mathlib associatedPrimes.subset_of_injective, after localising); at those points A^r → N is a surjection between free modules of rank r, hence an isomorphism, so 𝒦 vanishes at all its associated points. A non-zero module has an associated point in this sense (a minimal prime over the annihilator of a non-zero element), so 𝒦 = 0 and N ≅ A^r locally.
acceptance: A = O_K⟨ζ⟩, M = A/(ζ) ⊕ A: F_1(M) = (ζ) is invertible, M is free of rank 1 at the only associated point (0), and M/Ann_M(ζ) ≅ A.
Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Example 4.3: for a principal ideal domain A and M = A/(a_1) × … × A/(a_t) × A^{n−t}, F_{n−t}(M) = (a_1 ⋯ a_t) and M/Ann_M(F_{n−t}(M)) ≅ A^{n−t}.
Invertibility is needed: A = k[x, y], M = (x, y) ⊆ A, r = 1: F_1(M) = (x, y) is not invertible, Ann_M(F_1(M)) = 0, and M is not locally free.

Then 𝒥 is a coherent open ideal, and the admissible blow-up φ: T' → T of 𝒥 is a disjoint union T' = T'_1 ⊔ … ⊔ T'_k of open formal subschemes, T'_i being the locus where 𝒥_iO_{T'} = 𝒥O_{T'}, with generic fibre the part {e_i = 1} of the generic fibre of T. On the blow-up (node admissible-blow-up) 𝒥O_{T'} is invertible and T' has no ϖ-torsion: locally 𝒥O_{T'} = (j) with j = Σ j_i, j_i ∈ 𝒥_iO_{T'}, j_i j_l = 0 for i ≠ l; the opens T'_i = {𝒥_iO = 𝒥O} cover T', and T'_i ∩ T'_l = ∅ for i ≠ l because there j_i and j_l both generate, forcing j² ∈ (j_i j_l) = 0 for the non-zero-divisor j — the argument of Raynaud–Gruson 5.1.5.

nodes.title: Flattening for modules on smooth formal schemes with geometrically irreducible fibres (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Special case 4.4)
nodes.statement: Let T = Spf A be an affine admissible formal O_K-scheme, h: Z = Spf B → T affine, smooth and surjective with geometrically irreducible fibres of dimension m, and ℳ a coherent O_Z-module (M = Γ(Z, ℳ)) that is rig-flat over T in dimension ≥ m (node rig-flat-in-dimension). There is an admissible blow-up T' → T such that the strict transform ℳ' of ℳ on Z' = Z ×_T T' (the pull-back modulo its sections supported over the centre, node admissible-blow-up) is T'-flat in dimension ≥ m (node flat-in-dimension). Moreover the blow-up can be chosen to be an isomorphism over a neighbourhood of every t ∈ T_0 such that ℳ is T-flat at the generic point of Z ⊗ k(t) (equivalently, T-flat in dimension ≥ m at all points above t); in particular its centre is disjoint from any open U_0 ⊆ T_0 over which ℳ is T-flat in dimension ≥ m.
hypotheses: T affine admissible; Z → T smooth, surjective, fibres geometrically irreducible of dimension m
ℳ rig-flat in dimension ≥ m (for instance rig-flat in dimension ≥ n with n ≤ m)
proofSteps: For p ∈ Spec A_K, ζ_p = pB is prime and is the generic point of the fibre over p (node smooth-geometrically-irreducible-generic-fibres-integral), (B/pB)_{ζ_p} is a field, and r(p) := dim (M/pM)_{ζ_p}. For rig-points p, M_{ζ_p} is free over B_{ζ_p} of rank r(p) (node rig-flatness-generic-point-criterion); for arbitrary p it is a localisation of this (A_K is Jacobson, node R0/affinoid-jacobson).

r is locally constant on Spec A_K: choose b ∉ ζ_p with M_b free of rank r(p) over B_b, and a finitely generated a ⊆ A with a_K the ideal of coefficients of (Bb)_K (node rig-ideal-of-coefficients-existence (i)); then p ∉ V(a) and r(p') = r(p) for p' ∈ Spec A_K ∖ V(a), since b ∉ ζ_{p'}. Spec A_K is noetherian (anchor Layer 0), so r is constant on the parts of a finite partition into open and closed sets.

By node partition-by-admissible-blow-up, after an admissible blow-up of T and passing to the parts (the remaining constructions are local on T and canonical — Fitting ideals and ideals of coefficients are unique and compatible with base change — so they glue), assume r(p) = r for all p.

F_r(M) ⊆ B is finitely generated (node formal-fitting-ideal) and F_r(M)B_{ζ_p} = B_{ζ_p} for all p ∈ Spec A_K (M_{ζ_p} free of rank r); every rigid fibre therefore meets the complement of V(F_r(M)), A_K is the ideal of coefficients of F_r(M)_K, and F_r(M) has an open ideal of coefficients a ⊆ A (node rig-ideal-of-coefficients-existence (ii)).

Centre: if ℳ is T-flat at the generic point ξ of Z ⊗ k(t), t ∈ T_0, then M_ξ is free of rank r: take 0 → K_ξ → B_ξ^r →α M_ξ → 0 with α ⊗ k(t) bijective at ξ ((B/tB)_ξ is a field); K_ξ is finitely generated (M_ξ is A-flat, hence O_K-torsion-free, and node saturated-submodule-finitely-generated applies), flatness gives K_ξ/tK_ξ = 0 and Nakayama K_ξ = 0. Hence F_r(M)_ξ = B_ξ, aA_t = A_t and t ∉ V(a) (node ideal-of-coefficients); likewise r is constant near t, so the blow-up of step 3 is an isomorphism near t (node partition-by-admissible-blow-up, last assertion).

Blow up a (node admissible-blow-up); Fitting ideals and ideals of coefficients commute with base change, so assume a invertible. At the generic point ξ of every fibre of Spec B → Spec A (also over T_0), F_r(M)B_ξ = aB_ξ: a⁻¹F_r(M) is an integral ideal whose ideal of coefficients is A (node content-ideal-smul, c(a𝒥) = a c(𝒥)), so it is not contained in ξ; as a is invertible and A → B is flat, F_r(M) is invertible at ξ.

M is free of rank r at all associated primes of B, which are the ζ_p (node smooth-geometrically-irreducible-associated-primes). By node fitting-ideal-invertible-locally-free (on a neighbourhood of ξ where F_r(M) is invertible), M/Ann_M(F_r(M)) is free at ξ, and Ann_M(F_r(M))_ξ = Ann_M(a)_ξ equals the a-power torsion at ξ; so the strict transform M/(a-power torsion) is free, hence T'-flat, at the generic point of every fibre over T'_0. The non-flat locus is closed (node formal-flat-locus-open) and the fibres are irreducible of dimension m, so ℳ' is T'-flat in dimension ≥ m.
acceptance: ℳ = O_Z/(ζξ − ϖ) on Z = D¹_T = Spf O_K⟨ζ, ξ⟩ over T = Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩ (m = 1, the module of the annulus model): r = 0, F_0(M) = (ζξ − ϖ) with open ideal of coefficients a = (ζ, ϖ); after blowing up (ζ, ϖ) the strict transform is O_K⟨u, ξ⟩/(uξ − 1) on the chart ζ = ϖu and O_{T''}⟨ξ⟩/(ξ − v) ≅ O_{T''} on the chart ϖ = ζv, T'' = Spf O_K⟨ζ, v⟩/(ζv − ϖ): flat.
ℳ = O_Z: r = 1, F_1(M) = B, a = A, and nothing is blown up.

nodes.title: Torsion in extensions of a module of small support by a free module (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Lemma 4.5)
nodes.statement: Let T = Spf A be affine admissible and h: Z = Spf B → T affine, smooth and surjective with geometrically irreducible fibres of dimension m. Let 0 → ℒ → 𝒩 → 𝒫 → 0 be an exact sequence of coherent O_Z-modules with ℒ free and dim(𝒫/T) < m (the fibres of Supp 𝒫 ∩ Z_0 over T_0 have dimension < m), and 𝒯(𝒩), 𝒯(𝒫) the ϖ-power torsion submodules. Then (a) ℒ ∩ 𝒯(𝒩) = 0, so 𝒯(𝒩) → 𝒯(𝒫) is injective; (b) 𝒯(𝒩) → 𝒯(𝒫) is bijective; (c) 0 → ℒ → 𝒩/𝒯(𝒩) → 𝒫/𝒯(𝒫) → 0 is exact.
hypotheses: ℒ free
dim(𝒫/T) < m
proofSteps: If m = 0 then 𝒫 = 0 and everything is clear; assume m ≥ 1.
(a): ℒ is free and B has no ϖ-torsion (node smooth-geometrically-irreducible-associated-primes).

(b): pass to Z̃ = Spec B → T̃ = Spec A and the finite B-modules L, N, P with torsion T(N), T(P); let W = Z̃ ∖ Supp T(P), i: W → Z̃, and R = Ker(N → P/T(P)), so 0 → L → R → T(P) → 0 and i*L ≅ i*R. Supp T(P) ⊆ V(ϖ) ∩ Supp P has fibre dimensions < m, so W contains Z̃ ∖ Z_0 and all generic points of fibres over T_0, and L → i_*i*L is bijective (node smooth-geometrically-irreducible-extension, L free).
Hence R → i_*i*R ≅ i_*i*L ≅ L splits L → R, and K = Ker(R → i_*i*R) maps isomorphically onto T(P); K is supported in V(ϖ), so K ⊆ T(N) and T(N) → T(P) is surjective.
Coherent O_Z-modules correspond to finitely presented B-modules compatibly with torsion submodules (node tfp-algebra-coherent); (c) follows from (a) and (b).
acceptance: Z = D¹_T, 𝒩 = O_Z ⊕ O_Z/(ϖ, ζ), ℒ = O_Z ⊕ 0, 𝒫 = O_Z/(ϖ, ζ) (supported on a section of fibre dimension 0 < 1): 𝒯(𝒩) = 0 ⊕ O_Z/(ϖ, ζ) → 𝒯(𝒫) is bijective.
The dimension hypothesis is needed: 𝒩 = O_Z, ℒ = ϖO_Z ≅ O_Z, 𝒫 = O_Z/ϖ (fibre dimension m): 𝒯(𝒩) = 0 but 𝒯(𝒫) = 𝒫 ≠ 0.

nodes.title: One step of the flattening induction: enlarging the locus of flatness in dimension ≥ m (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Lemma 4.7)
nodes.statement: Let T be a quasi-compact admissible formal O_K-scheme, f: X → T a morphism of quasi-compact formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation, and ℳ a coherent O_X-module that is rig-flat over T in dimension ≥ n and T-flat in dimension ≥ m + 1, m ≥ n. Let T(1) → T be an admissible blow-up, X(1) = X ×_T T(1), ℳ̄(1) the strict transform of the pull-back of ℳ, and U_0 ⊊ T_0 an open subset such that ℳ̄(1) is flat in dimension ≥ m over U_0(1) = U_0 ×_T T(1). There are an admissible blow-up T(2) → T(1) with centre disjoint from U_0(1) and an open W_0 ⊆ T_0 with U_0 ⊊ W_0 such that the strict transform ℳ̄(2) of ℳ on X(2) = X ×_T T(2) is flat in dimension ≥ m over W_0(2).
hypotheses: Strict transforms are taken with respect to the composite blow-ups T(i) → T
proofSteps: Let t be a generic point of T_0 ∖ U_0 (T_0 is a noetherian space, node admissible-formal-scheme) and x ∈ X_0 a generic point of an m-dimensional component of the non-flat locus of ℳ̄(1) above t; there are finitely many such x (X quasi-compact). It suffices to find T(2) → T(1), with centre outside U_0(1), making the strict transform flat at all points above x: repeating for the finitely many x (composites of admissible blow-ups, node admissible-blow-up) makes it flat in dimension ≥ m above t, and upper semicontinuity of fibre dimension then yields W_0 ∋ t.

It suffices to work locally around t: blow-ups of open neighbourhoods extend to T (node admissible-blow-up, extension; Bosch–Lütkebohmert cite [FI, 2.5], see sourceIssues AdicSpacesPartII/E-R2-BL2-1).

Reduction to a dévissage over T: node formal-devissage-existence gives elementary étale affine neighbourhoods (X', x') → (X, x), (T', t') → (T, t) and a dévissage of ℳ' at x' in dimensions n¹ > … > n^r = m. A blow-up of T(1)' = T(1) ×_T T' with centre outside U(1)'_0 near t' is induced by one of T(1): after shrinking, the closure of t' maps isomorphically onto an open of the closure of t, and étale maps inducing isomorphisms on reductions are isomorphisms on thickenings (node formal-etale-site-invariance), so the centre is a subscheme of T(1); rig-flatness pulls back and flatness of strict transforms descends along the étale T' → T (nodes rig-flat-in-dimension, flat-in-dimension).

By node devissage-injectivity-and-rig-flatness, after shrinking, α^i is T-universally injective for i ≤ r − 1, hence an isomorphism at ζ^i (surjective by Nakayama); base change to T(1) gives a T(1)-dévissage of ℳ(1) at every point above x with the α^i (i ≤ r − 1) still injective.

Let 𝒩̄^i, 𝒫̄^i, ℳ̄^i be the strict transforms along T(1) → T. By node devissage-torsion-lemma, (D̄¹, …, D̄^{r−1}) is a T(1)-dévissage in dimensions ≥ m + 1; 𝒩̄^r := g^r_*𝒫̄^{r−1} on Z^r is T(1)-flat in dimension ≥ m over U_0 (node devissage-flatness-criterion) and rig-flat in dimension ≥ n (node devissage-injectivity-and-rig-flatness), and Z^r → T is smooth with geometrically irreducible fibres of dimension m.

Node flattening-smooth-special-case gives an admissible blow-up T(2) → T(1) with centre in T(1)_0 ∖ U(1)_0 such that the strict transform of 𝒩̄^r (equal to the strict transform of 𝒩^r along T(2) → T; strict transforms compose, node admissible-blow-up) is T(2)-flat in dimension ≥ m.

Pull (D¹, …, D^{r−1}) back to T(2) (the α^i stay injective) and take strict transforms along T(2) → T to obtain a T(2)-dévissage of ℳ̄(2) (node devissage-torsion-lemma); the ϖ-torsion of 𝒩^r(2) is induced by that of 𝒩^{r−1}(2), hence by that of ℳ(2), so the strict transform of ℳ induces that of 𝒩^r, and node devissage-flatness-criterion shows ℳ̄(2) T(2)-flat in dimension ≥ m at x.

nodes.title: Flattening a coherent module by an admissible blow-up of the base (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Theorem 4.1)
nodes.statement: Let T be a quasi-compact admissible formal O_K-scheme (K complete of rank one, not necessarily discretely valued), f: X → T a morphism of quasi-compact formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation, ℳ a coherent O_X-module and n ∈ ℕ such that ℳ is rig-flat over T in dimension ≥ n (node rig-flat-in-dimension). Then there is an admissible blow-up T' → T such that the strict transform ℳ' of ℳ on X' = X ×_T T' (node admissible-blow-up) is T'-flat in dimension ≥ n (node flat-in-dimension).
hypotheses: T quasi-compact admissible; X quasi-compact (Bosch–Lütkebohmert's standing assumption in §3) and locally of tf presentation, possibly with ϖ-torsion
The blow-up is of the base T, and ℳ' is the strict transform, not the pull-back
Classical rigid case only: Bosch–Lütkebohmert's noetherian base case uses parallel arguments that are not decomposed here
proofSteps: X is quasi-compact, so N := dim(X/T) = sup_x dim_x(X ⊗ k(f(x))) is finite and ℳ is T-flat in dimension ≥ N + 1 (node flat-in-dimension).

nodes.title: Flattening by admissible blow-up (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Theorem 5.2)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of quasi-compact admissible formal O_K-schemes (K complete of rank one, not necessarily discretely valued; Bosch–Lütkebohmert work over an admissible quasi-compact base S, and an S-morphism is in particular a morphism over Spf O_K) and n ∈ ℕ. If f_rig is flat, i.e. O_X is rig-flat over Y at every rig-point (resp. f_rig is flat in dimension ≥ n, i.e. O_X is rig-flat over Y in dimension ≥ n; node rig-flat-in-dimension), there is an admissible blow-up Y' → Y such that the induced morphism f': X' → Y' is flat (resp. flat in dimension ≥ n; node flat-in-dimension), where X' is the strict transform of X: the closed formal subscheme of X ×_Y Y' defined by the ideal of sections supported over the centre, i.e. the strict transform of the module O_X (node admissible-blow-up). This is the case T = Y, ℳ = O_X of the module flattening theorem (node module-flattening-by-blow-up, Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Theorem 4.1).
hypotheses: X, Y quasi-compact admissible over Spf O_K; f_rig flat (resp. flat in dimension ≥ n) in the sense of rig-flatness at rig-points
The blow-up is of Y (the target), and X' is the strict transform, not the total transform
Classical rigid case: the base is Spf O_K; Bosch–Lütkebohmert's noetherian base case (II) is proved by parallel noetherian arguments that are not decomposed here
proofSteps: f_rig flat (resp. flat in dimension ≥ n) means that O_X is rig-flat over Y in dimension ≥ 0 (resp. ≥ n) (node rig-flat-in-dimension).
Node module-flattening-by-blow-up with T = Y and ℳ = O_X gives an admissible blow-up Y' → Y such that the strict transform of O_X on X ×_Y Y' is Y'-flat in dimension ≥ n (n = 0 in the flat case).

The strict transform of O_X is O_{X'} (node admissible-blow-up, strict transforms along base change), so f' is flat in dimension ≥ n; flatness in dimension ≥ 0 is flatness (node formal-flat-locus-open).
In the flat case X' is flat over the admissible Y', hence admissible.
acceptance: Y = Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩, X = Spf O_K⟨ζ, ξ⟩/(ζξ − ϖ): f_rig is the open immersion of the annulus {|ϖ| ≤ |ζ| ≤ 1} into the disc, hence flat, but f is not flat (ζ is a zero-divisor on the special fibre k[ζ, ξ]/(ζξ)); after blowing up (ζ, ϖ) on Y the strict transform of X maps isomorphically onto the chart {ζ generates} of Y', so f' is an open immersion, in particular flat.

nodes.title: Quasi-finite and bounded-fibre-dimension formal models (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Corollary 5.3)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a morphism of quasi-compact admissible formal O_K-schemes (K complete of rank one). (a) If all fibres of f_rig have dimension ≤ n (dim(X/Y)_rig ≤ n, node rig-flat-in-dimension), there is an admissible blow-up Y' → Y such that the induced f': X' → Y' (X' the strict transform) has relative dimension ≤ n: every fibre of f'_0: X'_0 → Y'_0 has dimension ≤ n. (b) If f_rig is quasi-finite, there is an admissible blow-up Y' → Y with f': X' → Y' quasi-finite (f'_0 locally quasi-finite, Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyQuasiFinite).
hypotheses: X, Y quasi-compact admissible over Spf O_K (classical rigid case)
Dimensions of rigid fibres are taken at rig-points (node rig-flat-in-dimension)
proofSteps: (a): dim(X/Y)_rig ≤ n makes O_X rig-flat over Y in dimension ≥ n + 1 (node rig-flat-in-dimension), so node flattening-by-blow-up gives Y' → Y with f' flat in dimension ≥ n + 1 (node flat-in-dimension).

For every formal point Spf V → Y' with V a complete valuation ring of height one (for instance the normalisation of a rig-point, node rig-point), the base change f'_V is flat in dimension ≥ n + 1 and its generic fibre has dimension ≤ n, so its special fibre has dimension ≤ n (Bosch–Lütkebohmert: 'as in [EGA IV_3, 14.3.10]', recorded gap).

Every closed point of Y'_0 is the special point of a rig-point (node rig-point, 3.5), so the fibres of f'_0 over closed points have dimension ≤ n; by upper semicontinuity of fibre dimension this holds over all points (recorded gap).

(b): (a) with n = 0; f'_0 is quasi-compact and of finite type with zero-dimensional fibres, which are therefore finite over their residue fields, so f'_0 is locally quasi-finite (Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.locallyQuasiFinite_iff_isFinite_fiber).

nodes.title: Formal completion of a scheme, the morphism σ: d(X̂) → X and the comparison φ: d(X̂) → X ×_Y d(Ŷ)
nodes.statement: (1.9.4) For a scheme X and its formal completion X̂ along a closed subscheme, assumed of type (S), there is a natural morphism of locally ringed spaces σ_X: d(X̂) → X, the unique one such that for every open U ⊆ X, with e = (X̂ → X) ∘ λ, one has e⁻¹(U) ⊆ σ⁻¹(U) and e* = σ* on O_X(U). (1.9.5) Let f: X → Y be locally of finite type between schemes, Y' ⊆ Y closed and defined by a quasi-coherent ideal of finite type, X' = X ×_Y Y', and X̂, Ŷ the completions along X' and Y'. If Ŷ is of type (S) then so is X̂, f̂ is adic, and the square formed by σ_X, σ_Y, d(f̂) and f induces a d(Ŷ)-morphism φ: d(X̂) → X ×_Y d(Ŷ) into the fibre product of a scheme locally of finite type with an adic space (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification). Proposition 1.9.6: (i) φ is a local isomorphism; (ii) if f is separated, φ is injective; (iii) if f is universally specializing (e.g. universally closed, e.g. proper), φ is surjective. Hence if f is separated and universally specializing, φ is an isomorphism. The source says 'One can easily prove' and gives no proof; the proofs below are supplied here.
hypotheses: X̂ (resp. Ŷ) of type (S); the ideal defining Y' of finite type; f locally of finite type
(ii) requires f separated; (iii) requires f universally specializing
σ and the fibre product X ×_Y d(Ŷ) come from Huber 1994 [Hu, 4.6.iv], [Hu4, 3.10.7] and [Hu, 3.8]; [Hu4] is not public
proofSteps: σ_X: glue the maps d(Spf Â) → Spec A over affine opens Spec A ⊆ X induced by A → Â → O⁺; uniqueness by the stated characterisation (Huber 1994 Remark 4.6(iv) in the noetherian case).
φ: universal property of X ×_Y d(Ŷ) (R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification).

(i) Local isomorphism: reduce to Y = Spec A, X = Spec B with B = A[T_1, …, T_n]/J and Ŷ = Spf Â of type (S)(b) with s ∈ Â; then X ×_Y d(Ŷ) is the increasing union over m of the affinoids Spa(Â(1/s)⟨s^m T⟩/J) (construction of [Hu, 3.8], R1), and d(X̂) = Spa(B̂(1/s), integral closure) is the member m = 0, i.e. the rational subset {|T_i| ≤ 1}; so φ is an open immersion on each affine chart of X̂.

(ii) Injectivity: if φ(x_1) = φ(x_2) = y, the centres of x_1, x_2 give two extensions Spec κ(y)⁺ → X of Spec κ(y) → X over Spec κ(y)⁺ → Y; separatedness gives uniqueness of such extensions (valuative criterion, mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated.valuativeCriterion), so x_1, x_2 lie in one affine chart, on which φ is injective by (i).

(iii) Surjectivity: for y ∈ X ×_Y d(Ŷ), its image in d(Ŷ) has a centre in Ŷ giving Spec κ(y)⁺ → Y; universal specialisation lifts the specialisation in X ×_Y Spec κ(y)⁺ from the generic point, giving an extension Spec κ(y)⁺ → X whose closed point lies over Y'; this defines a point of d(X̂) over y (universal property of d on the affine chart containing the centre).
Proper implies universally closed implies universally specializing (mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyClosed.eq_valuativeCriterion); the source statement is used with this implication.

nodes.title: The generic fibre of the completion of an O_K-scheme is the integral (good-reduction) locus of the analytified generic fibre
nodes.statement: Let K be complete of rank one, X a separated O_K-scheme locally of finite type, X_K its generic fibre and X_K^ad = X ×_{Spec O_K} Spa(K, O_K) its adic analytification (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-functor). Let X̂ be the ϖ-adic completion of X (a formal O_K-scheme locally tft, of type (S)). Then the comparison map φ_X: d(X̂) → X_K^ad of node formal-completion-and-algebraic-comparison (with Y = Spec O_K, Y' = V(ϖ)) is an open embedding, whose image is the integral locus X_K^{ad,int} := {x ∈ X_K^ad : the morphism Spec κ(x) → X extends to Spec κ(x)⁺ → X}, κ(x) the completed residue field and κ(x)⁺ its valuation ring. Under φ_X the specialisation λ(x) ∈ X_s of x ∈ d(X̂) is the image of the closed point of that extension. If X is proper over O_K, φ_X is an isomorphism d(X̂) ≅ X_K^ad. A classical point of X_K^ad (residue field K' finite over K) lies in the integral locus iff it extends to an O_{K'}-point of X.

nodes.title: If the completion's generic fibre is all of the analytified generic fibre, a flat quasi-projective model is proper
nodes.statement: Let X be a quasi-projective O_K-scheme, flat and of finite type over O_K (hence of finite presentation). If φ_X: d(X̂) → X_K^ad is surjective, then X is proper over O_K. Flatness cannot be dropped: X = Spec O_K ⊔ A¹_{O_K/ϖ} is separated and of finite presentation, φ_X is an isomorphism (both sides are Spa(K, O_K)), and X is not proper.
hypotheses: X quasi-projective over O_K (for general separated X of finite type the compactification step needs Nagata's theorem over O_K, which this roadmap does not own)
X flat over O_K
proofSteps: Finite presentation: flat and of finite type over the domain O_K implies finitely presented (Fujiwara–Kato 0.9.2.3, after Raynaud–Gruson I (3.4.7)).

Compactify: X ⊆ P^N_{O_K} locally closed; let X̄ be the schematic closure of X_K in P^N_{O_K}. X̄ is projective and flat, X is open in X̄ (locally closed ⇒ open in its closure; X = closure of X_K ∩ X by flatness), and X̄_K ⊇ X_K is dense.

X̄ proper, so φ_X̄ is an isomorphism (node good-reduction-locus); by naturality φ_X = φ_X̄ restricted to d(X̂) = λ_X̄⁻¹(X_s) (generic fibre of an open formal subscheme). Surjectivity of φ_X gives X_K^ad = λ_X̄⁻¹(X_s), hence W^ad = λ_X̄⁻¹(Z) for W = X̄_K ∖ X_K and Z = X̄_s ∖ X_s (closed).

Z = ∅: otherwise take a closed point z ∈ Z and a rig-point of the completion of X̄ over z (node rig-point, 3.5); its classical point lies in the open tube ]Z[ (node tube), a nonempty open subset of X̄_K^ad contained in W^ad. But X_K is dense in X̄_K, so X_K^ad = q⁻¹(X_K) is dense in X̄_K^ad (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-constructible-closure), and its complement W^ad has empty interior: contradiction. (Alternatively: at a classical point, a non-zero-divisor vanishing on W would be nilpotent in the completed local ring, which is that of X̄_K by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-completed-local-rings.)

X_K = X̄_K: a classical point w ∈ X̄_K with residue field K' extends to Spec O_{K'} → X̄ (valuative criterion for X̄ proper); its special point lies in X̄_s = X_s ⊆ X, and Spec O_{K'} is local, so the whole O_{K'}-point lies in the open X, i.e. w ∈ X_K. Classical points are dense in the Jacobson scheme X̄_K, so W = ∅.
Hence X = X̄ as an open subscheme with the same points, so X is proper.
acceptance: X = P¹_{O_K} minus a closed point x of the special fibre: φ_X has image P^{1,ad}_K ∖ ]x[ ≠ X_K^ad, and X is not proper — consistent with the lemma.

X = Bl_x(P¹_{O_K}) ∖ (strict transform of P¹_k) has proper generic and special fibres, is flat and separated, but is not proper; its φ_X has image the residue disc ]x[ ≠ P^{1,ad}_K, as the lemma predicts.

nodes.title: Conrad's Berthelot-type functor (·)^rig on FS_C for arbitrary complete k
nodes.statement: Fix an adic noetherian ring C with a continuous map C → R to the valuation ring R of a complete nonarchimedean field k (no discreteness assumption on k; examples: C = R if k is discretely valued; C = R_0 a complete discrete valuation ring with R_0 → R local; C = Z discrete). FS_C is the category of locally noetherian formal schemes X over Spf C whose underlying reduced scheme is locally of finite type over C_red; affine opens have algebras that are quotients of C[[q_1, …, q_n]]{{T_1, …, T_m}} with the (I, q)-adic topology. For X in FS_C and a rigid space Z over k, Hom^cont_C(Z, X) is the set of morphisms of locally ringed G-topologised spaces whose ring maps are C-algebra maps landing in locally power-bounded sections and carrying locally topologically nilpotent sections to locally topologically nilpotent sections. Theorem 3.1.5: Hom^cont_C(·, X) is represented by a quasi-separated rigid space X^rig; (·)^rig takes open/closed immersions to open/closed immersions and open covers to admissible covers, commutes with fibre products (a), with analytic extension of k (b) and with change of C (c), preserves separatedness (d), and sends topologically finite type maps to quasi-compact maps (e). Spf(C[[q]])^rig is the open unit disc Δ = {|t| < 1}. Through AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor this gives an adic space r(X^rig) over Spa(k, R).
hypotheses: C adic noetherian with continuous C → R; k arbitrary complete nonarchimedean

Objects of FS_C are locally noetherian: the functor does not apply to non-noetherian formal O_K-models when k is not discretely valued (those are handled by nodes generic-fibre-functor-d and raynaud-generic-fibre)

Theorem 3.1.6 (preservation of finiteness, smoothness, properness, flatness, fibre dimension) is recorded in the API; its proof uses Raynaud's theory, Temkin [Te, Cor. 4.4, 4.5] for properness and Conrad Theorem A.2.1
proofSteps: Δ → Spf(C[[q]]) pulling q back to the coordinate represents Spf(C[[q]])^rig, because Δ is admissibly covered by the discs Δ_r (r ∈ (0,1) ∩ √|k^×|) and topologically nilpotent elements of a k-affinoid have sup-norm < 1.
For X = Spf(C[[q]]{{T}}/J) take the zero locus of J in Δ^n × B^m (power-boundedness condition gives the B^m factor).
Localisation: (Spf A_{a})^rig is the locus where a is a unit with power-bounded inverse, via A_{a} ≅ A{{T}}/(1 − aT); so open immersions of formal affines give quasi-compact open immersions.
Glue over open covers, first for separated X then in general; deduce (a)–(e) from the construction.
acceptance: Spf(Z[[q]])^rig over any k (C = Z discrete) is the open unit disc over k.
When k is discretely valued and C = R the functor recovers de Jong's [deJ, 7.2.4, 7.2.6].

nodes.title: Conrad's scheme lemma: a flat, locally finitely presented, separated morphism with finite fibres of locally constant rank is finite
nodes.statement: Lemma A.1.4: a flat morphism of schemes f: X → Y that is locally of finite presentation is finite if and only if it is separated with finite fibres and its fibre rank y ↦ dim_{κ(y)} Γ(X_y, O) is locally constant on Y. No quasi-compactness and no noetherian hypothesis is needed.
hypotheses: f flat and locally of finite presentation
Uses [EGA IV_4 18.5.11(c)] (structure of separated locally quasi-finite maps over henselian local bases), unread
proofSteps: Only if: a finite flat locally finitely presented morphism is given by a locally free O_Y-algebra of finite rank.

If, local case: reduce to constant rank d; by fpqc base change assume Y = Spec of a henselian local ring; [EGA IV_4 18.5.11(c)] splits X = X' ⊔ X'' with X' → Y finite and X'' with empty closed fibre; X' is finite free of rank d' and d' = d from the closed fibre; so X' → X is an isomorphism on all fibres, hence an isomorphism.

If, general case: for y ∈ Y the base change to Spec O_{Y,y} is finite flat of rank d; choose a quasi-compact open U ⊆ X containing X ×_Y Spec O_{Y,y}; by finite presentation, U → Y is finite locally free of rank d over a neighbourhood of y, and U → X is an isomorphism on fibres there, hence an isomorphism.
acceptance: The open immersion G_m ⊔ {0} → A¹ over a field? No: over Y = Spec k[t], X = Spec k[t] ⊔ Spec k[t, t⁻¹] has fibre rank 2 over t ≠ 0 and 1 over t = 0 (not locally constant) and is not finite, as the lemma predicts.

nodes.title: Conrad's fibral finiteness criterion for flat rigid (adic) morphisms
nodes.statement: Theorem A.1.2: a flat map f: X → Y of rigid spaces over k (k complete nonarchimedean, not necessarily discretely valued) is finite if and only if it is quasi-compact and separated with finite fibres and locally constant fibre rank on Y. Through AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor the same holds for flat morphisms of quasi-separated adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(k, k°), with fibres and ranks taken at classical points.
hypotheses: f flat; quasi-compact; separated (quasi-separated is insufficient, cf. Remark A.1.3); finite fibres; fibre rank locally constant on Y
k arbitrary complete nonarchimedean; formal models over Spf R with R possibly non-noetherian
Quasi-compactness is necessary: {|t| = 1} ⊔ {|t| < 1} → {|t| ≤ 1} is a bijective local isomorphism, flat with fibres of rank 1, not finite
proofSteps: Only if: finite rigid maps are classified by coherent O_Y-algebras, locally free for flat f.
If: work locally on Y; assume X, Y quasi-compact separated and constant fibre rank d; choose a formal model f: X → Y (node raynaud-theorem (c),(e)).

f is separated (node formal-model-separatedness); after admissible blow-up of Y and strict transform f is quasi-finite (node quasi-finite-formal-model) and flat (node flattening-by-blow-up); base change and passage to closed formal subschemes keep quasi-finiteness and separatedness.

It suffices that each f_n = f mod ϖ^{n+1} is finite; each is quasi-finite, separated, flat and finitely presented, so by node fibral-finiteness-scheme-lemma it suffices that the special-fibre map f̄ has fibres of constant rank d.

The locus of fibres of a given rank is constructible ([EGA IV_3 9.8.8], unread), so it suffices to check closed points y_0; by node rig-point (Conrad A.1.5) pick Spf B → Y through y_0 with B finite flat local over R; T = X ×_Y Spf B is quasi-finite flat over Spf B with one-point special fibre, hence T = Spf C with C finite free of rank d' over B; C ⊗_R k is the affinoid algebra of f⁻¹(y_k), of rank d, so d' = d.
acceptance: A finite flat rigid map has locally constant fibre rank, and conversely under the stated hypotheses.
Over a discretely valued k the statement is Abbes–Mokrane Lemme A.1 with 'separated' in place of 'quasi-separated'.

nodes.title: Topological invariance of affinoidness and finiteness (Conrad A.1.1)
nodes.statement: A rigid space X over k is affinoid iff X_red is affinoid; hence a morphism f: Y → Z of rigid spaces is finite iff Y_red → Z_red is finite. Through AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor (affinoids correspond to affinoids, 1.1.11) the same holds for quasi-separated adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(k, k°). No Serre-type cohomological criterion is available: over every nonarchimedean k there is a quasi-compact separated surface with vanishing higher coherent cohomology that is not affinoid [Liu].
hypotheses: Rigid spaces over a complete nonarchimedean field k; no discreteness
Inputs [BGR 6.1.1/4, 7.3.5/3, 9.5.3/5] are unread (recorded gap)
proofSteps: i: Y_red → Y induces a bijection of admissible opens and admissible coverings (reduce to affinoid Y; Gerritzen–Grauert [BGR 7.3.5/3]: affinoid subdomains are finite unions of rational subdomains, whose defining inequalities lift through nil-thickenings).
Hence X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated when X_red is affinoid; induct on a nilpotent coherent ideal to the square-zero case X_0 = Sp A_0 ⊆ X.
A = O_X(X) is a k-Banach algebra of countable type (left exact Čech sequence over a finite affinoid cover); 0 → I → A → A_0 → 0 with I a finite A_0-module.

Lift topological generators of A_0 to power-bounded a_r ∈ A (power-boundedness is insensitive to nilpotents) and generators of I; [BGR 6.1.1/4] gives a surjection k⟨t, u⟩ → A, and ι: X → Sp A is a closed immersion by [BGR 9.5.3/5], hence an isomorphism.
Finiteness statement: f finite iff f is affinoid over affinoids with module-finite rings; both conditions are insensitive to nilpotents by the first part and Nakayama.
acceptance: A finite morphism can be recognised on reduced spaces; Conrad uses this with A.1.2 in the canonical subgroup construction.
