nodes.statement: Let R be sousperfectoid and S a finite étale R-algebra (mathlib:Algebra.Etale and mathlib:Module.Finite), with its natural topology as a finite R-module and S⁺ the integral closure of R⁺ in S (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra). Then S is a complete Tate ring and is sousperfectoid, with frame S -> R̃ ⊗_R S (= R̃ ⊗̂_R S) split by σ ⊗_R id_S.
hypotheses: S finite étale over R as rings (finite, flat, finitely presented, unramified); topology = natural finite-module topology.
proofSteps: S is finite projective over R (finite étale ⇒ finite, flat and finitely presented; mathlib:Module.Flat, mathlib:Module.Projective), so its natural topology is complete Hausdorff and R̃ ⊗_R S is already complete: R̃ ⊗̂_R S = R̃ ⊗_R S (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra; AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product).

R̃ ⊗_R S is finite étale over R̃ (base change of étale algebras), hence perfectoid: finite étale algebras over an arbitrary perfectoid Tate ring are perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P3, requested; Berkeley Theorem 7.4.5(1), Hansen-Kedlaya Proposition 2.15(a)).
Splitting: σ ⊗_R id_S is S-linear and continuous (any R-linear map between finite projective modules with natural topologies is continuous); AdicSpacesPartII:R5/split-injection-completed-base-change.

nodes.title: Descent of the sousperfectoid property along faithfully flat finite étale maps (HK 7.5(b))
nodes.statement: Let R -> S be a finite étale and faithfully flat homomorphism of complete Tate rings (S with its natural topology). If S is sousperfectoid then so is R: for a frame (S̃, ι_S, σ_S) of S and any R-linear retraction τ: S -> R of R -> S, (S̃, ι_S ∘ (R -> S), τ ∘ σ_S) is a perfectoid frame of R.
hypotheses: R -> S finite étale and faithfully flat.
proofSteps: Existence of τ: R -> S is universally injective (faithfully flat), so S/R is flat; S/R is finitely presented (S finite projective), hence projective, and 0 -> R -> S -> S/R -> 0 splits R-linearly (mathlib:Module.Projective, mathlib:Module.Flat).
τ is continuous (linear maps between finite projective modules with natural topologies are continuous); σ_S is S-linear hence R-linear; τ ∘ σ_S ∘ ι_S = τ = id on R.

nodes.title: Finite extensions of Q_p are sousperfectoid
nodes.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p and K^cycl the completion of K(μ_{p^∞}). Then K -> K^cycl admits a continuous K-linear retraction, so (K^cycl, inclusion, retraction) is a perfectoid frame and K is sousperfectoid. More generally K⟨T_1, ..., T_n⟩ and every rational localisation and finite étale algebra of it are sousperfectoid.
hypotheses: K finite over Q_p (discretely valued, so orthonormal bases exist).
proofSteps: K^cycl is a perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P1, requested: cyclotomic perfectoid fields).

Retraction: equip the K-Banach space K^cycl with the lattice O_{K^cycl}; it is ϖ_K-adically complete and ϖ_K-torsion-free, so lifting a basis of O_{K^cycl}/ϖ_K O_{K^cycl} over the residue field of K that contains the class of 1 (nonzero since 1 ∉ ϖ_K O_{K^cycl}) gives an orthonormal basis (e_i) with e_0 = 1: every x is uniquely Σ a_i e_i with a_i ∈ K, a_i -> 0. The coordinate x ↦ a_0 is a continuous K-linear retraction.
The remaining claims: AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-rings, AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-rational-localisation, AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-finite-etale.

nodes.title: Étale spaces over a sousperfectoid space are sousperfectoid adic spaces
nodes.statement: Let X be a sousperfectoid adic space and f: Y -> X étale in the local-description sense of AdicEtaleGeometry A1 (Kedlaya-Liu Definition 8.2.16: every y ∈ Y has an open neighbourhood on which f factors as an open immersion, a finite étale morphism and an open immersion, where finite étale means affinoid-locally on the target Spa(S, S⁺) -> Spa(R, R⁺) with R -> S finite étale and S⁺ the integral closure of R⁺). Then Y is an adic space (not merely a preadic space) and is sousperfectoid. In particular every object of the étale site X_ét is a sousperfectoid adic space, and for a finite étale R-algebra S over a sousperfectoid R and a composite of rational localisations and finite étale maps R -> S', the ring S' itself is sousperfectoid. For a general étale map, sousperfectoidness is a property of the space Y, not of a global ring: Y is covered by sousperfectoid affinoids, while the sousperfectoid property of rings is not known to be of local nature.
hypotheses: X sousperfectoid; f étale in A1's local-description sense (for locally noetherian targets this is Huber's étale, AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-on-analytic-carriers).
proofSteps: Local structure: near y, f is j_2 ∘ g ∘ j_1 with j_1: V -> W, j_2: V' -> X open immersions and g: W -> V' finite étale.

Cover V' by sousperfectoid rational affinoids Spa(R_k, R_k⁺) (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-adic-space, AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-rational-localisation); over each, g^{-1}Spa(R_k) = Spa(S_k, S_k⁺) with S_k finite étale over R_k, which is sousperfectoid (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-finite-etale) and hence sheafy (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-sheafy): so W is covered by sousperfectoid affinoid adic spaces.
V is open in W, hence covered by rational subsets of the Spa(S_k), which are sousperfectoid (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-rational-localisation).
A preadic space covered by affinoid adic spaces is an adic space (anchor Layer 5), and it is sousperfectoid by definition.

nodes.title: Sousperfectoid spaces are stably adic
nodes.statement: Let X be a sousperfectoid adic space. The affinoid objects Spa(S, S⁺) of X_ét with S sousperfectoid form a stable basis of X_ét in the sense of Kedlaya-Liu Definition 8.2.19 (a basis of X_ét by adic affinoid spaces, closed under finite étale maps and rational subdomain embeddings); hence X is stably adic. Consequently (Kedlaya-Liu Theorem 8.2.22(c),(d), AdicSpacesPartII:R3) for affinoid X = Spa(R, R⁺): for every finite projective R-module M, M̃ is an acyclic sheaf on this basis of X_ét, and finite projective R-modules are equivalent to finite locally free O_{X_ét}-modules.
hypotheses: X sousperfectoid; X_ét in A1's local-description sense.
proofSteps: Basis: every object of X_ét is covered by such affinoids (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-etale-stability).

Stability: finite étale maps and rational subdomain embeddings preserve sousperfectoid affinoids (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-finite-etale, AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-rational-localisation), and they are adic spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-sheafy).

nodes.statement: Let Z be a sousperfectoid adic space, W a locally noetherian analytic adic space (e.g. a rigid space), g: Z -> W a morphism and f: Y -> W étale (R0). Then the fibre product Z ×_W Y exists in the category of adic spaces, the projection Z ×_W Y -> Z is étale in A1's local-description sense, and Z ×_W Y is sousperfectoid. Affinoid formula: if Y' ⊆ Y'' are opens with Y'' = Spa(B, B⁺) -> W' = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ W finite étale (A -> B finite étale, B⁺ the integral closure of A⁺) and Z' = Spa(C, C⁺) ⊆ g^{-1}(W') affinoid, then Z' ×_{W'} Y'' = Spa(C ⊗_A B, integral closure of C⁺) and Z' ×_W Y' is its open subspace lying over Y'.
hypotheses: W locally noetherian so that étale maps to W have the local open-immersion/finite-étale description (Huber Lemma 2.2.8 via A1); Z sousperfectoid, possibly non-noetherian (so Huber's fibre-product theorems, which assume noetherian or sheafy charts, do not apply directly).
proofSteps: Local description of f: AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-local-open-finite-etale-factorisation (Huber Lemma 2.2.8 for the locally noetherian analytic W; Berkeley p. 55).

Finite étale piece: C -> C ⊗_A B is finite étale (base change, mathlib:Algebra.Etale); with the natural topology and integral closure it is a complete affinoid ring (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra), sousperfectoid (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-finite-etale) and sheafy (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-sheafy); it is the pushout of complete affinoid rings (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product-universal-property; the completion is not needed since C ⊗_A B is finite projective over C), so Spa of it is the fibre product (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-fibre-product).
Open immersion pieces: base change of an open immersion is the open preimage (anchor Layer 5).
Glue the local fibre products along the canonical isomorphisms given by their universal properties (anchor Layer 5 gluing).

nodes.title: Perfectoid space times a polydisc: sousperfectoid, not perfectoid
nodes.statement: Let L be a perfectoid field, X = Spa(S, S⁺) an affinoid perfectoid space over L and B^n_L = Spa(L⟨T_1, ..., T_n⟩, O_L⟨T⟩). Then the fibre product X ×_L B^n_L exists in adic spaces and equals Spa(S⟨T_1, ..., T_n⟩, S⁺⟨T_1, ..., T_n⟩), which is a sousperfectoid affinoid adic space; for n ≥ 1 and S ≠ 0, S⟨T_1, ..., T_n⟩ is not perfectoid.
hypotheses: L perfectoid; S ≠ 0 for the non-perfectoid clause; n ≥ 1.
proofSteps: S ⊗̂_L L⟨T⟩ = S⟨T⟩ with plus ring S⁺⟨T⟩ (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-restricted-power-series).

S⟨T⟩ is sousperfectoid (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-rings, S perfectoid hence sousperfectoid) and so sheafy (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-sheafy); Spa of the completed tensor product is then the fibre product (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-fibre-product).

Not perfectoid: S is uniform with S° bounded, and S⟨T⟩° = S°⟨T⟩ (for every point v of Spa(S, S°) the Gauss extension v_G(Σ a_α T^α) = max_α v(a_α) is a point of Spa(S⟨T⟩, S°⟨T⟩), and power-bounded elements are ≤ 1 at every point, so v(a_α) ≤ 1 for all v and α, and a_α ∈ S° by the plus-ring criterion tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one). Then S⟨T⟩°/ϖ^p = (S°/ϖ^p)[T] and, since p ∈ ϖ^p S°, the Frobenius image of (S°/ϖ)[T] consists of polynomials in T_1^p, ..., T_n^p; T_1 is not among them because S°/ϖ^p ≠ 0. So Frobenius S⟨T⟩°/ϖ -> S⟨T⟩°/ϖ^p is not surjective (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras).

nodes.title: The product X ×_L Y of a perfectoid space and a smooth rigid space (BHW Corollary 3.4)
nodes.statement: Let L be a perfectoid field, L' a perfectoid field extension of L (complete, with L -> L' continuous), X a perfectoid space over L and Y a rigid space over L' (an adic space locally of topologically finite type over Spa(L', O_L')) that is smooth over L' (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-morphism). Then the fibre product X ×_L Y := X ×_{Spa(L, O_L)} Y exists in the category of adic spaces and is a sousperfectoid adic space. Construction: X ×_L Y = X' ×_{L'} Y with X' = X ×_L Spa(L', O_L') perfectoid; for affinoid perfectoid X' = Spa(S, S⁺) and an open V ⊆ Y with an étale map h: V -> B^n_{L'} (Huber 1.6.10), X' ×_{L'} V = (X' ×_{L'} B^n_{L'}) ×_{B^n_{L'}} V with X' ×_{L'} B^n = Spa(S⟨T_1, ..., T_n⟩, S⁺⟨T⟩); these pieces glue. It is not asserted, and is false in general, that X ×_L Y is perfectoid.
hypotheses: L, L' perfectoid fields (BHW: L a perfectoid extension of Q_p^cyc); the printed hypothesis 'a perfectoid extension of L'/L' means 'a perfectoid extension L' of L' (sourceIssues).
Y smooth over L' (so locally étale over polydiscs); X arbitrary perfectoid over L.
proofSteps: X' = X ×_L Spa L' exists and is perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), and X ×_L Y ≅ X' ×_{L'} Y by transitivity of fibre products, Y being over L'.
Cover X' by affinoid perfectoids Spa(S, S⁺) and Y by opens V with étale h: V -> B^n_{L'} (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-local-structure; Huber 1.6.10 with M_i = {1} over the Tate base L').
Polydisc step: AdicSpacesPartII:R5/perfectoid-times-polydisc.
Étale step: AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-etale-base-change with Z = Spa(S⟨T⟩), W = B^n_{L'}.
Glue over the covers of X' and Y using uniqueness of fibre products (anchor Layer 5 gluing); the result is sousperfectoid because each piece is.
acceptance: Y = Spa L': X ×_L Spa L' is the perfectoid fibre product.
Y = B^1_{L'}: X ×_L Y = Spa(S⟨T⟩) locally, sousperfectoid and not perfectoid.

nodes.title: Products with a smooth space preserve tilde-limits (BHW Corollary 3.5)
nodes.statement: Let L be a perfectoid field, (X_n)_{n ≥ 1} an inverse system of adic spaces over L with adic transition maps and X_∞ a perfectoid space over L with compatible maps such that X_∞ ∼ lim_n X_n (Huber's tilde-limit, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limits-and-cohomological-continuity), and U a rigid space smooth over L such that each X_n ×_L U exists as an adic space (e.g. X_n rigid over L, or sousperfectoid). Then X_∞ ×_L U (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/perfectoid-times-smooth-fibre-product) satisfies X_∞ ×_L U ∼ lim_n X_n ×_L U.
hypotheses: The affinoid criterion for tilde-limits (density of colim A_n in A_∞ together with the plus-ring condition implies |Spa A_∞| ≅ lim |Spa A_n|) is supplied by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H0 (requested).
proofSteps: Reduce to affinoid X_n = Spa(A_n, A_n⁺), X_∞ = Spa(A_∞, A_∞⁺) with colim A_n -> A_∞ of dense image, and affinoid U' = Spa(B, B⁺) ⊆ U, using that the tilde-limit condition is local (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limits-and-cohomological-continuity).

Density (condition (b)): colim_n (A_n ⊗̂_L B) -> A_∞ ⊗̂_L B has dense image by approximating each coefficient in a presentation of an element of A_∞ ⊗̂_L B (pointwise approximation; AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product).

Homeomorphism (condition (a)): the affinoid criterion (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0, requested), applied to the product affinoids, whose plus rings are the completed integral closures of A_n⁺ ⊗ B⁺ (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-fibre-product).

nodes.title: Profinite flat modules over the ring of integers of a p-adic field
nodes.statement: Let E be a finite extension of Q_p, O = O_E with uniformizer ϖ. A topological O-module M is linear-topological if 0 has a basis of neighbourhoods consisting of O-submodules, and M is a profinite flat O-module if it is flat over O (equivalently ϖ-torsion-free), linear-topological and compact (CHJ Definition 6.1). Then the topology of M is profinite, every open submodule has finite index, and M is ϖ-adically complete and separated.
hypotheses: O a complete discrete valuation ring with finite residue field (E/Q_p finite).
proofSteps: Define the predicate; compactness plus linear topology gives open submodules of finite index (M/N discrete and compact, hence finite).
acceptance: ∏_{i∈I} O with the product topology is profinite flat for every set I.

nodes.title: Pseudobases of profinite flat modules (CHJ Proposition 6.2)
nodes.statement: A topological O-module M is profinite flat if and only if it is isomorphic, as a topological O-module, to ∏_{i∈I} O with the product topology for some set I. A family (e_i)_{i∈I} realising such an isomorphism is a pseudobasis; the submodules M_{J,n} = ∏_{i∈J} ϖ^n O e_i × ∏_{i∉J} O e_i (J finite, n ≥ 1) form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0.
hypotheses: O a complete DVR with finite residue field.
proofSteps: (<=) Products of compact spaces are compact (Tychonoff); flatness and linear topology are evident.

(=>) CHJ imports this from SGA 3 Exposé VII_B 0.3.8 (not read; gap). Proof route used here: D = Hom_cont(M, E/O) is a discrete ϖ-divisible torsion O-module (divisible because M is torsion-free, discrete because M is compact); divisible modules over the DVR O are injective, hence D ≅ (E/O)^{(I)}; Pontryagin-Matlis duality M ≅ Hom(D, E/O) ≅ ∏_I O identifies the topologies.

nodes.title: Small Z_p-algebras
nodes.statement: A small Z_p-algebra (CHJ §1.4) is a ring R that is reduced, p-torsion-free and finite as an algebra over Z_p[[X_1, ..., X_d]] for some d ≥ 0. It carries its canonical adic profinite topology (the a-adic topology for an ideal of definition a, e.g. the Jacobson radical, independent of choices), for which it is a profinite flat Z_p-module (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/profinite-flat-module) and a noetherian semilocal ring, complete for its p-adic topology.
hypotheses: d unspecified; all constructions are independent of the choice of d and of the ideal of definition.
proofSteps: R is finite over the complete noetherian local ring Z_p[[X]], hence noetherian, semilocal and complete for the topology of the maximal ideal of Z_p[[X]] extended to R; torsion-freeness and compactness give profinite flatness.

nodes.title: The mixed completed tensor product V ⊗̂ M (CHJ §6.1)
nodes.statement: Let E be a finite extension of Q_p with O = O_E, ϖ a uniformizer, and M a profinite flat O-module. For an O-module X define X ⊗̂ M := lim_i (X ⊗_O M/I_i), the limit over any cofinal system (I_i) of open O-submodules of M (CHJ Definition 6.3; independent of the system). For an E-vector space V with an O-lattice V° ⊆ V (V°[1/ϖ] = V) define V ⊗̂ M := (V° ⊗̂ M)[1/ϖ] (CHJ Definition 6.6); when V is an E-Banach space, V° is always taken open and bounded, and V ⊗̂ M is then canonically independent of V°. If V is a Banach E-algebra and M is a small O-algebra (e.g. a small Z_p-algebra when E = Q_p), choosing the I_i to be ideals makes V ⊗̂ M a ring; it is a Banach E-algebra with unit ball V° ⊗̂ M, and with a pseudobasis (e_i) of M it is the Banach space of bounded I-indexed families in V.
hypotheses: M profinite flat; V Banach over E with open bounded lattice V° (for non-Banach V the lattice is part of the data and affects the result).
proofSteps: Define the inverse limit and its localisation; independence of (I_i) by cofinality (abstract nonsense).
Ring structure from the ring structures on X ⊗_O M/I_i when the I_i are ideals.
Independence of V°: AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-completed-tensor-exactness (CHJ Corollary 6.5(2)) since two open bounded lattices differ by bounded ϖ-torsion.
Banach structure and bounded-family description: AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-completed-tensor-product-formula.

nodes.title: Rational and integral coefficient sheaves agree: O_X ⊗̂ M = (O_X⁺ ⊗̂ M)[1/ϖ] on reduced affinoids
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field containing E, X = Spa(A, A°) a reduced affinoid rigid space over K and M a profinite flat O_E-module. For every rational subset U ⊆ X, O_X⁺(U) = O_X(U)° is an open bounded lattice of the Banach space O_X(U), and the natural map (O_X⁺(U) ⊗̂ M)[1/ϖ] -> O_X(U) ⊗̂ M is an isomorphism, compatible with restriction; more generally any two open bounded lattices give canonically isomorphic V ⊗̂ M. The presheaf U ↦ O_X⁺(U) ⊗̂ M ≅ ∏_I O_X⁺(U) is a sheaf on the rational subsets of X. For non-reduced X the power-bounded lattice is unbounded and the formula fails.
hypotheses: X reduced (so O_X(U) is uniform and O_X(U)° is bounded, for all rational U); rigid means A⁺ = A°, so O_X⁺(U) = O_X(U)°.
proofSteps: O_X(U) is a reduced affinoid algebra, hence uniform (reduced affinoid algebras are uniform), so O_X(U)° is open and bounded; for rigid X, O_X⁺(U) = O_X(U)°.
Two open bounded lattices V_0°, V_1° satisfy ϖ^N V_1° ⊆ V_0° ⊆ ϖ^{-N} V_1°; AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-completed-tensor-exactness (2) gives the canonical isomorphism.
Sheaf property of O⁺ ⊗̂ M: O⁺ is a sheaf and O⁺(U) is ϖ-adically complete, so by AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-completed-tensor-product-formula O⁺ ⊗̂ M ≅ ∏_I O⁺, a product of sheaves.

nodes.title: The coefficient sheaf R = O_X ⊗̂ R on an affinoid rigid space (CHJ §6.3)
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field of characteristic 0, X = Spa(A, A°) an affinoid rigid space over K and R a small Z_p-algebra (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/small-coefficient-algebra). On the site of rational subsets of X with finite rational covers, define R(U) := O_X(U) ⊗̂ R (the mixed completed tensor over Z_p of AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-completed-tensor, computed with an open bounded lattice of the Banach Q_p-space O_X(U)), with restriction maps induced by those of O_X. Each R(U) is a Banach K-algebra; the restriction maps are continuous algebra maps; R is a sheaf of rings with vanishing higher Čech cohomology on finite rational covers (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/coefficient-sheaf-tate-acyclicity), extended to all quasi-compact opens by finite covers. When X is reduced the unit ball of R(U) can be taken to be O_X°(U) ⊗̂ R (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/rational-integral-compatibility).
hypotheses: K of characteristic 0 (so O_X(U) is a Q_p-Banach space); X affinoid for this node (qcqs X by gluing on finite covers).
No discreteness of K is needed for the construction and the sheaf property; it is needed for noetherianity, flatness, Loc and Kiehl.
proofSteps: Functoriality of ⊗̂ in the Banach variable (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-completed-tensor) gives a presheaf of Banach K-algebras on rational subsets.
The sheaf property and acyclicity: AdicSpacesPartII:R5/coefficient-sheaf-tate-acyclicity.
acceptance: For R = Z_p, R = O_X.
For R = Z_p[[T]] and X the closed unit disc over K, R(X) = O_K⟨Y⟩[[T]][1/p]: power series in T whose coefficients are uniformly bounded elements of K⟨Y⟩.

nodes.statement: Let K be discretely valued of characteristic 0, X affinoid rigid over K, R small. For rational V ⊆ U ⊆ X, the restriction R(U) -> R(V) is flat.

nodes.title: Tate acyclicity for the coefficient sheaf (CHJ Proposition 6.15)
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field of characteristic 0 (not necessarily discretely valued), X affinoid rigid over K and R small. For every rational U ⊆ X and every finite rational cover 𝔘 of U, the augmented Čech complex 0 -> R(U) -> ∏ R(U_i) -> ∏ R(U_i ∩ U_j) -> ... is exact. Consequently R is a sheaf on the rational site and H^i(U, R) = 0 for i ≥ 1. The same holds on the étale site of X (CHJ Remark 6.17).
hypotheses: X affinoid; the unit ball of each R(U) is computed from an open bounded lattice (for reduced X, O_X°(U); in general a lattice from a presentation, see sourceIssues).
proofSteps: Choose a pseudobasis (e_i)_{i∈I} of R and open bounded lattices O_X(U)_0 compatible with restrictions; the augmented Čech complex of R is (∏_I C^•_aug(𝔘, O_{X,0}))[1/p] (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-completed-tensor-product-formula).
Tate's acyclicity for O_X (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid) and the open mapping theorem (anchor Layer 0) show that the cohomology of C^•_aug(𝔘, O_{X,0}) is killed by a fixed power p^N.
Products are exact, so the cohomology of ∏_I C^•_aug is killed by p^N, and inverting p gives exactness.
Čech-to-derived (Cartan): the rational subsets are closed under intersection, so vanishing Čech cohomology on all finite rational covers gives H^i = 0.
Étale version: replace rational covers by the stable basis of the étale site and use Tate acyclicity for O_{X_ét} (Kedlaya-Liu 8.2.22 via AdicSpacesPartII:R3).
acceptance: For X the closed disc, R = Z_p[[T]] and the Laurent cover {|Y| ≤ |p|}, {|p| ≤ |Y|}: 0 -> O_K⟨Y⟩[[T]][1/p] -> O_K⟨Y/p⟩[[T]][1/p] × O_K⟨Y, p/Y⟩[[T]][1/p] -> O_K⟨Y/p, p/Y⟩[[T]][1/p] -> 0 is exact.
For R = Z_p this is Tate's theorem.

nodes.title: The localisation functor Loc for R-modules (CHJ Definition 6.14, Proposition 6.16)
nodes.statement: Let X be affinoid rigid over K (characteristic 0), R small, U ⊆ X rational and M a finitely generated R(U)-module. Loc(M) is the presheaf of R|_U-modules V ↦ R(V) ⊗_{R(U)} M on rational V ⊆ U. If K is discretely valued: Loc is a fully faithful exact functor from finitely generated R(U)-modules to R-modules on U, Loc(M) is a sheaf, and Ȟ^i(𝔘, Loc(M)) = 0 = H^i(U, Loc(M)) for i ≥ 1 and every finite rational cover 𝔘. nodes.title: Coherent R-modules (CHJ Definition 6.18)
nodes.statement: Let K be discretely valued of characteristic 0, X affinoid rigid over K, R small. For a rational U ⊆ X and a finite rational cover 𝔘 of U, a sheaf F of R|_U-modules is 𝔘-coherent if for every U_i ∈ 𝔘 there is a finitely generated R(U_i)-module M_i with F|_{U_i} ≅ Loc(M_i); F is coherent if it is 𝔘-coherent for some finite rational cover 𝔘. F is locally projective if the M_i can be chosen projective.
hypotheses: K discretely valued (so that Loc is exact and fully faithful).
proofSteps: Define by existence of a trivialising cover; coherent modules form an abelian subcategory closed under kernels and cokernels (exactness of Loc, AdicSpacesPartII:R5/coefficient-sheaf-loc).
acceptance: Loc(M) is coherent for every finitely generated M.

nodes.title: Kiehl's theorem for coherent R-modules (CHJ Theorem 6.20)
nodes.statement: Let K be discretely valued of characteristic 0, X affinoid rigid over K, R small, and F a coherent R-module on X (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/coefficient-sheaf-coherent-module). Then there is a finitely generated R(X)-module M with F ≅ Loc(M) (namely M = F(X)); if F is locally projective, M is projective.
hypotheses: K discretely valued; F coherent for some finite rational cover.
The proof follows Ardakov-Wadsley §§5.3-5.5 (not read here; gap).
proofSteps: Reduce to a Laurent cover {X(f), X(1/f)} by the standard refinement argument (anchor Layer 2, Lemma 7.54 and Laurent refinement).

nodes.title: Base change of coefficient sheaves to C (CHJ Lemma 6.21)
nodes.statement: Let K be discretely valued of characteristic 0, C the completion of an algebraic closure of K, X affinoid rigid over K with X_C = X ×_K Spa(C, O_C) and f: X_C -> X, R small with R_C := O_{X_C} ⊗̂ R, and M a finitely generated projective R(X)-module. Then M ⊗_{R(X)} R_C(X_C) ≅ M ⊗_K C, and f^{-1}(Loc(M)) ⊗_{f^{-1}R} R_C ≅ Loc(M ⊗_K C). Arbitrary non-flat base change of the coefficient algebra is not part of this statement: for a map R -> R' of small algebras, H^0(Y, F ⊗ R') need not equal H^0(Y, F) ⊗_R R' on non-affinoid Y.
hypotheses: M projective; K discretely valued (so that Loc and Kiehl apply on X).
proofSteps: First isomorphism: as in AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-tensor-finite-projective-base-change, for M free it is R(X) ⊗̂ ... = O_{X_C}(X_C) ⊗̂ R computed coordinatewise; for projective M take a direct summand.

Second: f is open (base change of the field), so f^{-1} is computed on images of rational subsets, and the first isomorphism applies on each rational subset (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/coefficient-sheaf-loc).
acceptance: For M = R(X): R_C(X_C) = O_{X_C}(X_C) ⊗̂ R.

Non-example: for R = Z_p[[T]], R' = R/(T) and a coherent F on a non-affinoid space with H^1(F) having T-torsion, H^0(F)/T -> H^0(F/T) is not surjective (the Tor term of PerfectoidSpaces:P9/derived-coefficient-change); only flat or affinoid base change is asserted.

nodes.title: Tate algebras of polydiscs of radius rho are affinoid, and shrinking the radius is injective with dense image
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K), and let Γ* = √|K^×| ⊂ ℝ_{>0} be the divisible hull of the value group. For n ∈ ℕ and a real ρ > 0 let T_n(ρ) = K⟨ρ^{-1}X_1, …, ρ^{-1}X_n⟩ be the subring of K[[X_1, …, X_n]] of series f = Σ_ν a_ν X^ν with |a_ν| ρ^{|ν|} → 0 as |ν| = ν_1+…+ν_n → ∞ (Mathlib's MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring at the constant tuple ρ), with the Gauss norm |f|_ρ = max_ν |a_ν| ρ^{|ν|}. Then: (a) |·|_ρ is a multiplicative K-algebra norm for which T_n(ρ) is complete; (b) if ρ ∈ Γ*, T_n(ρ) with the |·|_ρ-topology is a K-affinoid algebra, i.e. the structure map K → T_n(ρ) is strictly topologically of finite type (an open continuous surjection from some Tate algebra K⟨Y_1, …, Y_N⟩ onto T_n(ρ) compatible with the K-algebra structures), hence T_n(ρ) is noetherian; (c) for real ρ' ≥ ρ > 0 the inclusion T_n(ρ') ⊆ T_n(ρ) is a continuous injective K-algebra map with |f|_ρ ≤ |f|_{ρ'} and dense image (polynomials are dense in every T_n(ρ)).
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued (rank one)
n ∈ ℕ
ρ > 0 real; in (b) ρ ∈ Γ* = √|K^×|
in (c) ρ' ≥ ρ
proofSteps: (a) Ultrametric inequality for the coefficients gives |f+g|_ρ ≤ max(|f|_ρ,|g|_ρ) and |fg|_ρ ≤ |f|_ρ|g|_ρ (Mathlib MvPowerSeries.isRestricted.mul supplies closure under products); equality |fg|_ρ = |f|_ρ|g|_ρ is Gauss's lemma for the weight ρ^{|ν|}: compare the lexicographically first indices where |a_ν|ρ^{|ν|} and |b_μ|ρ^{|μ|} attain their maxima. Completeness: a |·|_ρ-Cauchy sequence converges coefficientwise and the limit is ρ-restricted by the uniform bound.

(b) Choose c ∈ K^× and s ≥ 1 with ρ^s = |c|^{-1} (possible because ρ ∈ Γ*). If ρ ≥ 1, the continuous map K⟨T_{il} : 1 ≤ i ≤ n, 0 ≤ l ≤ s⟩ → T_n(ρ), T_{il} ↦ c X_i^l, is well defined because |c X_i^l|_ρ = |c|ρ^l ≤ 1, and surjective: write ν_i = s q_i + l_i with 0 ≤ l_i < s, so X^ν = c^{-|q|-n} Π_i (cX_i^s)^{q_i}(cX_i^{l_i}) and the new coefficient a_ν c^{-|q|-n} has absolute value |a_ν| ρ^{s|q|+sn} ≤ ρ^{sn}·|a_ν|ρ^{|ν|} → 0 (the argument of BGR 6.1.5/4 quoted in the proof of Grosse-Klönne Lemma 1.8). If ρ < 1, use instead K⟨Y_i, Z_i⟩ → T_n(ρ), Y_i ↦ c X_i^s, Z_i ↦ X_i (|cX_i^s|_ρ = 1, |X_i|_ρ = ρ ≤ 1); surjectivity follows from |a_ν| ρ^{s|q|} ≤ ρ^{-sn}|a_ν|ρ^{|ν|}. The map is open by the open mapping theorem for K-Banach spaces (anchor Layer 0.6), so K → T_n(ρ) is strictly topologically of finite type (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType, presented through tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion identified with the plain restricted-series ring by tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletionEquiv).
Noetherianity in (b): a quotient of K⟨Y_1..Y_N⟩, which is noetherian because every complete rank-one nonarchimedean field is strongly noetherian (anchor Layer 0.5, BGR 5.2.6).
(c) |a_ν|ρ^{|ν|} ≤ |a_ν|ρ'^{|ν|} gives the inclusion and the norm inequality; truncations of f are polynomials converging to f in |·|_ρ.
acceptance: For K = ℚ_p and ρ = p^{1/2} ∈ Γ*: c = p and s = 2 give ρ^2 = |p|^{-1}, and T_1(p^{1/2}) is the quotient of ℚ_p⟨T_0, T_1, T_2⟩ under T_l ↦ p X^l; the element Σ_m p^m X^{2m} lies in T_1(ρ') for every ρ' < p^{1/2} but not in T_1(p^{1/2}).
T_n(1) is the Tate algebra K⟨X_1..X_n⟩; for ℚ_p and 1 ≤ ρ < p^{1/2} the series Σ_m p^m X^{2m} lies in T_1(ρ) but not in T_1(p^{1/2}), so the inclusion T_1(p^{1/2}) ⊆ T_1(ρ) is strict.

nodes.title: The Monsky–Washnitzer algebra W_n = K⟨X_1, …, X_n⟩† of overconvergent power series
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K). For n ∈ ℕ define W_n = K⟨X_1, …, X_n⟩† := ⋃_{ρ>1} T_n(ρ) ⊆ K[[X_1, …, X_n]], the set of power series Σ_ν a_ν X^ν for which there is a real ρ > 1 with |a_ν| ρ^{|ν|} → 0 (equivalently: there are ρ > 1 and C ≥ 0 with |a_ν| ≤ C ρ^{-|ν|} for all ν; equivalently the series converges on a closed polydisc of some radius ρ > 1). Because ρ ↦ T_n(ρ) is antitone, the union is directed and W_n is a K-subalgebra of K[[X]]; the union may be taken over ρ ∈ Γ* ∩ (1, ∞) (Γ* = √|K^×|) but NOT only over ρ ∈ |K^×|. W_n ⊆ T_n = T_n(1), and W_n carries the Gauss norm |f| = max_ν |a_ν| restricted from T_n. Convention: the variables are X_1, …, X_n, |ν| = ν_1+…+ν_n, and ‘overconvergent’ always means ‘restricted at some radius strictly bigger than 1’.
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued (rank one)
n ∈ ℕ
proofSteps: Define W_n as the supremum ⨆_{ρ>1} T_n(ρ) of the Mathlib subrings MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring (fun _ ↦ ρ); the family is directed (ρ ≤ ρ' ⇒ T_n(ρ') ≤ T_n(ρ), F1/radius-tate-algebra-affinoid (c)), so membership is ∃ρ>1, restricted at ρ (Mathlib Subring.mem_iSup_of_directed).
Equivalence with the bound |a_ν| ≤ Cρ^{-|ν|}: restricted at ρ implies bounded by C = sup_ν |a_ν|ρ^{|ν|}; bounded at ρ implies restricted at every ρ' ∈ (1, ρ).
Cofinality of Γ* ∩ (1,∞): Γ* is dense in ℝ_{>0} because |K^×| ≠ {1}; for a discretely valued K the radii in |K^×| ∩ (1,∞) are bounded below by |π|^{-1} > 1, which is why they do not suffice.
Algebra structure: constants and the X_i are restricted at every ρ (Mathlib isRestricted_C, isRestricted_monomial).
acceptance: The series Σ_{m≥0} p^m X^{p^m} over K = ℚ_p lies in T_1 but not in W_1.
Σ_{m≥0} p^m X^{2m} over ℚ_p lies in W_1 (restricted at every ρ < p^{1/2}) although it is not restricted at any ρ ∈ |ℚ_p^×| ∩ (1,∞).

nodes.title: Weierstrass division and preparation in W_n, and distinguishedness after an automorphism
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K) and n ≥ 1; write W_n = K⟨Y_1, …, Y_n⟩† and regard g ∈ W_n as g = Σ_{m≥0} g_m Y_n^m with g_m ∈ W_{n-1}. Call g Y_n-distinguished of degree s if g_s is a unit of W_{n-1} and |g| = |g_s| > |g_m| for all m > s (Gauss norms), and call ω ∈ W_{n-1}[Y_n] a Weierstrass polynomial if it is monic with |ω| = 1. Then: (i) (division) if g is Y_n-distinguished of degree s, every f ∈ W_n can be written uniquely as f = gq + r with q ∈ W_n and r ∈ W_{n-1}[Y_n] of degree < s; (ii) (preparation) such g is uniquely e·ω with e a unit of W_n and ω a Weierstrass polynomial of degree s; (iii) (distinguishedness) for every 0 ≠ f ∈ W_n there is a K-algebra automorphism σ of W_n of the form Y_i ↦ Y_i + Y_n^{c_i} (i < n), Y_n ↦ Y_n, with c_i ∈ ℕ, such that σ(f) is Y_n-distinguished.
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued
Gauss norms on W_n and W_{n-1} (restricted from T_n, T_{n-1})
proofSteps: (iii) For 0 ≠ f ∈ T_n the Tate-algebra statement (BGR 5.2.4: some σ_c with c_i ≫ 0 makes f distinguished; anchor Layer 0.5 Weierstrass theory) gives c; σ_c and its inverse Y_i ↦ Y_i − Y_n^{c_i} map T_n(ρ_0) into T_n(ρ) whenever ρ^{max c_i} ≤ ρ_0, hence preserve W_n; the Gauss norms at radius 1 are those of T_n, so σ_c(f) is distinguished in W_n.

(i) existence: g ∈ T_n(ρ_0) for some ρ_0 > 1. Choose M ∈ ℕ larger than the number N_0 of monomials degrees for which the bound |a_ν| ≤ Cρ_0^{-|ν|} exceeds |g_s|; for real ρ > 1 close enough to 1 (with ρ^{M+N_0} < ρ_0), g is distinguished of degree s for the Gauss norm of polyradius (ρ, …, ρ, ρ^M): the terms m < s are dominated because ρ^{M(s−m)} ≥ ρ^{N_0} ≥ |g_m|_ρ/|g_s|_ρ, the terms m > s because |g_m| ≤ θ|g_s| (θ < 1) at radius 1 and |g_m|_{ρ_0}ρ_0^m → 0.

Choose a finite extension K'/K with the polyradius in |K'^×|; then T_n(ρ,…,ρ,ρ^M) ⊗_K K' ≅ K'⟨Y_1..Y_n⟩ by rescaling the variables, where Weierstrass division by a distinguished element holds (anchor Layer 0.5, over the complete field K'). Divide f ⊗ 1 by g ⊗ 1 there, expand quotient and remainder in a K-basis e_1 = 1, e_2, …, e_d of K' (T_n(ρ)⊗_K K' = ⊕ T_n(ρ)e_j), and keep the e_1-components: this gives f = gq + r with q ∈ T_n(ρ,…,ρ^M) ⊆ W_n and r ∈ T_{n-1}(ρ)[Y_n] of degree < s.
(i) uniqueness: W_n ⊆ T_n, g is distinguished in T_n, and division in T_n is unique (anchor Layer 0.5).

(ii) from (i) as in BGR 5.2.2: divide Y_n^s by g, Y_n^s = gq + r, put ω = Y_n^s − r and e = q^{-1}; |ω| = 1 and q is a unit because it is a unit in T_n and units of T_n lying in W_n are units of W_n (Dagger.isUnit_washnitzerAlgebra_iff, F1/overconvergent-tate-algebra).

g = Y_1 + Y_2^2 ∈ K⟨Y_1, Y_2⟩† is Y_2-distinguished of degree 0 only after the substitution Y_1 ↦ Y_1 + Y_2^c, as (iii) predicts.

nodes.title: W_n is a noetherian factorial Jacobson ring and every ideal of W_n is strictly closed
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K) and n ∈ ℕ. Then (1) W_n is noetherian, a unique factorisation domain, and a Jacobson ring; (2) every ideal I ⊆ W_n is strictly closed for the Gauss norm: I is closed and for every f ∈ W_n the residue norm inf_{g∈I} |f − g| is attained. Consequently the residue seminorm on W_n/I is a norm.
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued
n ∈ ℕ
proofSteps: Noetherian (BGR 5.2.6/1 pattern): induction on n; for 0 ≠ f ∈ W_n use F1/overconvergent-weierstrass-division (iii) to make f Y_n-distinguished, then (i) shows W_n/(f) is a finite W_{n-1}-module; W_{n-1} noetherian by induction, so every ideal containing f is finitely generated. (Kedlaya attributes noetherianity to Fulton.)

Factorial (BGR 5.2.6/2 pattern): by Weierstrass preparation every nonzero f is, after an automorphism, a unit times a Weierstrass polynomial in W_{n-1}[Y_n]; factoriality of W_{n-1} (induction) and Gauss's lemma for W_{n-1}[Y_n] give unique factorisation.

Jacobson (BGR 5.2.6/3 pattern): Noether normalisation (F1/dagger-noether-normalisation, proved from the same Weierstrass input and not using this item) shows W_n/m is finite over K for every maximal ideal m; a noetherian K-algebra all of whose quotients by maximal ideals are finite over K and in which every prime is an intersection of maximal ideals — proved by induction on dimension via finite maps W_d → W_n/p — is Jacobson.

Strictly closed (BGR 5.2.7/8 pattern): for I = (f_1..f_r), after Weierstrass reductions every f ∈ W_n has a division remainder of minimal norm; alternatively, by F1/overconvergent-faithful-flatness I = IT_n ∩ W_n, and IT_n is strictly closed in T_n (BGR 5.2.7/8), while W_n ⊆ T_n is isometric and the division remainders of f ∈ W_n computed in T_n lie in W_n by the radius argument of F1/overconvergent-weierstrass-division.
acceptance: For n = 1, W_1 is a principal ideal domain (noetherian UFD of dimension 1 in which every nonzero element is a unit times a polynomial).
The ideal (X_1) ⊂ W_1 is closed and W_1/(X_1) = K with the residue norm |·| of K.

nodes.title: W_n → T_n is faithfully flat, bijective on maximal ideals with equal residue fields, and W_n is regular of dimension n
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K) and n ∈ ℕ. Then (a) the inclusion W_n ⊆ T_n is faithfully flat; (b) for every maximal ideal m of T_n, m ∩ W_n is a maximal ideal of W_n and W_n/(m ∩ W_n) → T_n/m is bijective; m ↦ m ∩ W_n is a bijection Max(T_n) → Max(W_n); (c) every maximal ideal of W_n is generated by polynomials p_1, …, p_n ∈ K[Y_1..Y_n] with p_i monic in Y_i; (d) W_n is a regular ring (Mathlib IsRegularRing), equidimensional of Krull dimension n, and the maps of completed local rings (W_n)^_{m∩W_n} → (T_n)^_m are isomorphisms.
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued
n ∈ ℕ
proofSteps: Points: as sets Max(T_n) = ⋂_{ρ>1} Max(T_n(ρ)) = lim_ρ Max(T_n(ρ)) (a maximal ideal of T_n is the ideal of a Galois orbit of points of the closed unit polydisc, which lies in every polydisc of radius ρ > 1), and Spec W_n = lim_ρ Spec T_n(ρ) as topological spaces because W_n = colim_ρ T_n(ρ) (EGA IV 8.2.9, a limit statement for affine schemes); maximal ideals of W_n therefore come from compatible systems of maximal ideals of the T_n(ρ), so Max(T_n) → Max(W_n) is surjective, and injective because residue fields are finite and the evaluation is determined by the point.

Residue fields: W_n/(m ∩ W_n) → T_n/m is injective and both are finite over K; surjectivity because the point x ∈ K^a of the closed unit polydisc has T_n/m = K(x) = W_n/(m ∩ W_n) (polynomials already surject onto K(x)).

(c) from the corresponding statement for T_n (BGR 7.1.1/3: maximal ideals of T_n are generated by polynomials monic in successive variables), since those polynomials lie in W_n and generate a maximal ideal of W_n by (b).

(d) completed local rings: the map (W_n)^ → (T_n)^ at corresponding maximal ideals is surjective because the associated graded rings agree (m^k/m^{k+1} is a finite K-space generated by polynomials in both), and injective for dimension reasons (both regular local of dimension n by (c)); flatness of W_n → T_n follows by checking at maximal ideals, faithful flatness from surjectivity on maximal ideals (Mathlib Module.FaithfullyFlat, maximal-ideal criterion). Regularity and dimension n follow from (c) and the isomorphic completions.
acceptance: For n = 1 and K algebraically closed, the maximal ideals of W_1 are the (Y − a) with |a| ≤ 1, exactly as for T_1; for |a| > 1, Y − a = −a(1 − Y/a) is a unit of W_1 because Σ_k (Y/a)^k converges on the disc of radius |a| > 1.
W_n is not complete, yet the completion of its local ring at the origin is K[[Y_1..Y_n]], as for T_n.

nodes.title: Dagger algebras over a complete nonarchimedean field
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K). A K-dagger algebra is a commutative K-algebra A for which there exist n ∈ ℕ and a surjective K-algebra homomorphism W_n → A (equivalently A ≅ W_n/I for an ideal I). A morphism of dagger algebras is a K-algebra homomorphism (no continuity is imposed; it is automatic, F1/dagger-norm-and-continuity). Sp(A) denotes the set of maximal ideals of A. Attached data, each independent of the presentation up to canonical isomorphism: the residue norm class of a presentation (F1/dagger-norm-and-continuity), the completion A → Â (written A' by Grosse-Klönne), Â = T_n/IT_n, a K-affinoid algebra (F1/dagger-completion-comparison), the supremum seminorm |a|_sup = max_{m ∈ Sp(A)} |a mod m|, and the integral subring A^int = {a ∈ A : |a|_sup ≤ 1} = A ∩ (Â)°, which is the ring of power-bounded elements of A.
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued (rank one)
proofSteps: Definition as a predicate on K-algebras: Dagger.IsDaggerAlgebra K A :⇔ ∃ n, ∃ φ : W_n →ₐ[K] A surjective (W_n = F1/overconvergent-tate-algebra).
Sp(A) is Mathlib's MaximalSpectrum A; residue fields A/m are finite over K by F1/dagger-noether-normalisation.
The supremum seminorm is finite because it is bounded by any residue norm (|a mod m| ≤ |a| for the residue norm, BGR 6.2.1 applied to Â via F1/dagger-completion-comparison).
A^int = A ∩ (Â)°: an element of an affinoid algebra is power-bounded iff |·|_sup ≤ 1 (BGR 6.2.3/1), and |a|_sup is computed on Sp(A) = Sp(Â) (F1/dagger-completion-comparison).
acceptance: W_n/(X_1X_2 − 1) = K⟨X, X^{-1}⟩† is a dagger algebra with completion K⟨X, X^{-1}⟩.
K[X] is not a dagger algebra (its supremum seminorm is unbounded).

nodes.title: Noether normalisation for dagger algebras and finiteness of residue fields
nodes.statement: Let A be a K-dagger algebra (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)). Then (a) there are d ∈ ℕ and an injective finite K-algebra homomorphism W_d → A; (b) if the nilradical of an ideal q ⊆ A is a maximal ideal, then A/q is finite-dimensional over K; in particular A/m is a finite field extension of K for every maximal ideal m; (c) if φ : W_n → B is a finite morphism of dagger algebras and the kernel of φ contains a Weierstrass polynomial ω ∈ W_{n-1}[Y_n], then W_{n-1} → B is finite.
hypotheses: A a K-dagger algebra
K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued
proofSteps: (c) By F1/overconvergent-weierstrass-division (i), W_n/(ω) is a free W_{n-1}-module with basis 1, Y_n, …, Y_n^{s−1}; B is finite over W_n/(ω), hence over W_{n-1}.

(a) Induction on n for A = W_n/I: if I = 0 take d = n. Otherwise pick 0 ≠ f ∈ I; by F1/overconvergent-weierstrass-division (iii) and (ii) after an automorphism f = eω with ω a Weierstrass polynomial, so W_{n-1} → A is finite by (c); apply induction to the image of W_{n-1} (a quotient of W_{n-1}) and compose finite maps (BGR 6.1.2/2 pattern).

(b) Apply (a) to A/q: its only prime is the maximal ideal, so A/q is zero-dimensional; a finite injective W_d → A/q forces d = 0 (W_d has dimension d by F1/overconvergent-faithful-flatness and finite injective maps preserve dimension), so A/q is finite over W_0 = K.

nodes.title: Residue norms on dagger algebras and automatic continuity of morphisms
nodes.statement: Let A = W_n/I be a K-dagger algebra with a presentation (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)). (1) The residue seminorm |a| = inf{|f| : f ∈ W_n, f ↦ a} (Gauss norm on W_n) is a K-algebra norm on A, and the induced map α : W_n/I → T_n/IT_n is the completion of (A, |·|): an isometric embedding with dense image. (2) Every K-algebra homomorphism φ : W_n/I → W_m/J between dagger algebras is continuous for the residue norms. Consequently the residue norms of any two presentations of A are equivalent, every dagger algebra carries a canonical equivalence class of norms (its ‘affinoid topology’), and every finite A-module M carries a canonical topology, the one induced from the finite Â-module M ⊗_A Â, for which all A-linear maps of finite modules are continuous.
hypotheses: A = W_n/I, B = W_m/J K-dagger algebras
φ a K-algebra homomorphism (no continuity assumed)
proofSteps: (1) I is closed (F1/overconvergent-tate-algebra-properties (2)), so the residue seminorm is a norm; W_n → T_n is an isometry with dense image (F1/overconvergent-tate-algebra), and IT_n ∩ W_n = I (faithful flatness, F1/overconvergent-faithful-flatness), so W_n/I → T_n/IT_n is isometric with dense image into a complete space.

nodes.title: A dagger algebra and its completion: faithful flatness, points, completed local rings, reducedness and regularity, supremum norm
nodes.statement: Let A be a K-dagger algebra with completion τ : A → Â (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)). Then: (1) τ is faithfully flat and m ↦ τ^{-1}(m) is a bijection Max(Â) → Max(A) with isomorphic residue fields; (2) for corresponding maximal ideals τ induces isomorphisms of completed local rings A^_{τ^{-1}m} ≅ Â^_m; (3) A is reduced (resp. normal, resp. regular) if and only if Â is; (4) if A is reduced, the supremum seminorm |·|_sup on A is a norm lying in the canonical norm class of F1/dagger-norm-and-continuity. Moreover the completion is functorial: every morphism φ : A → B of dagger algebras extends uniquely to a continuous K-algebra map φ̂ : Â → B̂, and φ ↦ φ̂ is a functor.
hypotheses: A a K-dagger algebra
K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued
proofSteps: Write A = W_n/I; then Â = T_n/IT_n by F1/dagger-norm-and-continuity (1). (1): base change of the faithfully flat W_n → T_n (F1/overconvergent-faithful-flatness) along W_n → A; maximal ideals of T_n containing IT_n correspond to maximal ideals of W_n containing I with equal residue fields (same node, (b)).

(3): reducedness, normality and regularity of the excellent noetherian rings A and Â can be checked on completed local rings at maximal ideals (EGA IV 7.8; A is excellent as a quotient of W_n, Â as an affinoid algebra), which agree by (2).

nodes.title: Dagger algebras are weakly complete; elements of A^int with reduction 1 are units
nodes.statement: Let A be a K-dagger algebra (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)). (a) A is weakly complete: for all power-bounded x_1, …, x_n ∈ A (equivalently x_i ∈ A^int) the K-algebra map K[X_1..X_n] → A, X_i ↦ x_i, extends uniquely to a continuous K-algebra homomorphism W_n → A; moreover for every ρ > 1 the composite T_n(ρ) → T_n → Â factors through some fringe algebra A_{ρ'} of any fringe presentation of A (F1/fringe-presentation). (b) If a ∈ A is topologically nilpotent (|a|_sup < 1) then 1 − a is a unit of A with inverse Σ_{k≥0} a^k; in particular every element of A^int whose image in A^int/{|·|_sup < 1} is 1 is a unit. (c) An element a ∈ A is a unit iff its image in Â is a unit.
hypotheses: A a K-dagger algebra
x_1..x_n ∈ A power-bounded
proofSteps: (a) Write A = W_k/I with I generated by elements of T_k(λ_0). Let ψ : T_n → T_k/IT_k = Â be the continuous map with X_i ↦ x_i (universal property of T_n for power-bounded images, anchor Layer 0.4). For λ > 1, run the argument of F1/fringe-morphism-factorisation (GK Lemma 1.8): choose c ∈ K^×, s with λ^s = |c|^{-1}, present T_n(λ) as a quotient of T_{(s+1)n} via T_{il} ↦ cX_i^l (F1/radius-tate-algebra-affinoid (b)); the images of the topologically nilpotent elements cX_i^l lift to power-bounded elements of some A_{λ''}, and the kernel relations die in some A_{λ'}; so ψ(T_n(λ)) ⊆ image of A_{λ'} ⊆ A. Taking the union over λ gives W_n → A. Uniqueness: two continuous extensions agree on polynomials, which are dense in W_n.

(b) |a|_sup < 1 implies a is topologically nilpotent in some fringe algebra (Kedlaya Corollary 2.3.5, a consequence of (a) applied to x = a^N λ with |λ| > 1); then Σ a^k converges in that affinoid fringe algebra, and its image in A inverts 1 − a.
(c) If τ(a) is a unit of Â, a lies in no maximal ideal of A because Max(A) = Max(Â) (F1/dagger-completion-comparison (1)); so a is a unit.

nodes.title: Fringe (radius-indexed) presentations of a dagger algebra
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K) and A a K-dagger algebra. A fringe presentation of A consists of n ∈ ℕ, a radius ρ_0 ∈ Γ* with ρ_0 > 1, elements f_1, …, f_r ∈ T_n(ρ_0), and a K-algebra isomorphism W_n/(f_1, …, f_r)W_n ≅ A. For ρ ∈ Γ* ∩ (1, ρ_0] put A_ρ := T_n(ρ)/(f)T_n(ρ), a K-affinoid algebra (F1/radius-tate-algebra-affinoid), with transition maps A_{ρ'} → A_ρ for ρ ≤ ρ' induced by T_n(ρ') ⊆ T_n(ρ), and put A_1 := T_n/(f)T_n. Then A = colim_{ρ → 1+} A_ρ as K-algebras, and A_1 = Â is the completion. The fringe algebra of the presentation at radius ρ is the image B_ρ ⊆ A of A_ρ (equivalently of T_n(ρ)); A_ρ → A need not be injective. Geometrically, X_ρ = Sp(A_ρ) is a decreasing family of affinoids with ⋂_ρ X_ρ = Sp(Â) and Sp(Â) ⊆ X_ρ the Weierstrass domain {|X_1|, …, |X_n| ≤ 1}; this situation is written Sp(Â) ⊂† X_ρ.
hypotheses: A a K-dagger algebra
ρ_0 ∈ Γ* with ρ_0 > 1 and f_i ∈ T_n(ρ_0)
proofSteps: Existence: A ≅ W_n/I with I finitely generated (W_n noetherian, F1/overconvergent-tate-algebra-properties); finitely many generators lie in a common T_n(ρ_0) (directedness, F1/overconvergent-tate-algebra), and ρ_0 may be shrunk into Γ*.
Colimit: W_n = colim_ρ T_n(ρ) (directed union) and colimits commute with the quotient by the ideal generated by the images of f, so colim_ρ T_n(ρ)/(f) = W_n/(f)W_n.
A_1 = Â: F1/dagger-norm-and-continuity (1).
Weierstrass domain: T_n(ρ)/(f) → T_n/(f) is the restriction to {x ∈ X_ρ : |X_i(x)| ≤ 1}, since T_n(ρ)⟨X/1⟩ = T_n (a Weierstrass localisation of T_n(ρ)).
acceptance: A = W_1 with the identity presentation: A_ρ = T_1(ρ), B_ρ = T_1(ρ), A_1 = T_1.

nodes.title: Morphisms of dagger algebras respect fringe systems (independence of fringe presentations)
nodes.statement: Let ψ : A → B be a morphism of K-dagger algebras (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)) and choose fringe presentations A = W_n/(f_1..f_r) with f_i ∈ T_n(λ_A) and B = W_m/(g_1..g_s) with g_j ∈ T_m(λ_B), λ_A, λ_B ∈ Γ*, λ_A, λ_B > 1. Then for every λ ∈ Γ* with λ_A ≥ λ > 1 there is λ' ∈ Γ* with λ_B ≥ λ' > 1 such that A_λ → A → B factors through B_{λ'} → B. Consequently: every fringe algebra of A maps into a fringe algebra of B; any finitely many fringe algebras of A (from any presentations) lie in a common fringe algebra; and two fringe presentations of the same A give mutually cofinal ind-systems of affinoid algebras.

fringe presentations of A and B
proofSteps: Choose c ∈ K^× and s ∈ ℕ with λ^s = |c^{-1}|, and the surjection p : T_{(s+1)n} → T_n(λ), T_{il} ↦ cX_i^l (F1/radius-tate-algebra-affinoid (b)).

The elements φ_λ(β_λ(p(T_{il}))) = cX_i^l ∈ A are topologically nilpotent (their supremum norm is at most |c| = λ^{-s} < 1 because |X_i|_sup ≤ 1), and so are their images in B; topologically nilpotent elements of B lift to power-bounded elements t_{il} of some B_{λ''} (Kedlaya Corollary 2.3.5, via weak completeness of W_1 → B).

The continuous map q : T_{(s+1)n} → B_{λ''}, T_{il} ↦ t_{il}, satisfies γ_{λ''} ∘ q = ψ ∘ φ_λ ∘ β_λ ∘ p, so the finitely generated ideal q(ker(β_λ ∘ p))B_{λ''} = (r_1..r_k) maps to 0 in B = colim B_μ; some λ' ∈ (1, λ''] kills all r_j in B_{λ'}, and q descends to A_λ → B_{λ'}.

nodes.title: The fringe (direct limit) topology on dagger algebras and their finite modules
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K) and A a K-dagger algebra. The fringe topology on A is the finest locally K-convex topology for which every map A_ρ → A of a fringe presentation is continuous, A_ρ carrying its Banach topology; equivalently the direct limit of the intrinsic Banach topologies of the fringe algebras of A. It does not depend on the fringe presentation, is Hausdorff, is finer than the norm (affinoid) topology of F1/dagger-norm-and-continuity, and every K-algebra homomorphism of dagger algebras is continuous for it. A finite A-module M carries the fringe topology obtained as the quotient topology from A^r ↠ M (equivalently by base extension from a module over a fringe algebra), independent of choices; A-linear maps of finite modules are continuous. If K is spherically complete (in particular discretely valued), A with its fringe topology is a complete reflexive Hausdorff locally convex K-space.
hypotheses: A a K-dagger algebra
for completeness and reflexivity: K spherically complete
proofSteps: Define the topology via Dagger.FringePresentation.stage and the colimit (F1/fringe-presentation); independence of the presentation from F1/fringe-morphism-factorisation (mutually cofinal systems induce the same final topology).
Hausdorff and finer than the affinoid topology: each A_ρ → Â is continuous, so the final topology is finer than the one induced from Â, which is Hausdorff.
Continuity of morphisms: F1/fringe-morphism-factorisation maps each A_λ into some B_{λ'} continuously (a map of affinoid algebras is continuous).
Modules: F1/fringe-module-descent (GK 2.15) descends M to a finite A_ρ-module M_ρ; the final topology from the Banach modules M_{ρ'} (ρ' ≤ ρ) agrees with the quotient topology of A^r → M.

Completeness and reflexivity for spherically complete K: A is a compact-type (regular) inductive limit of the Banach spaces A_ρ with compact transition maps (Morita, A p-adic theory of hyperfunctions I, 3.3, 3.5, quoted by Grosse-Klönne 4.2; not read — recorded as a gap).
acceptance: For A = W_1 over ℚ_p, the truncations g_N = Σ_{m≤N} p^m X^{p^m} are Cauchy for the Gauss norm but not for the fringe topology (no fringe algebra T_1(ρ), ρ > 1, contains them with bounded ρ-norm).
For A = K, the fringe topology is the valuation topology of K.

nodes.title: Finite algebras over a dagger algebra are dagger algebras
nodes.statement: Let A be a K-dagger algebra (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)) and A → B a finite K-algebra homomorphism (B finitely generated as an A-module). Then B is a K-dagger algebra. More precisely, if A = W_n/IW_n and B = (W_n/JW_n)[X]/(f) with I ⊆ J ⊆ T_n(λ_0) and f ∈ T_n(λ_0)[X] monic with X power-bounded modulo J + (f), then B ≅ W_{n+1}/(J + f)W_{n+1}, and the fringe stages are D_λ = T_n(λ)[X]/(J + f) ≅ T_{n+1}(λ)/(J + f).
hypotheses: A a K-dagger algebra
B a finite A-algebra
proofSteps: Reduce to B generated by one element over a quotient of A: B is a successive extension by finitely many integral generators, each satisfying a monic polynomial (finite ⇒ integral).

Write A = W_n/IW_n and B = (W_n/JW_n)[X]/(f) with I ⊆ J ⊆ T_n(λ_0) and f ∈ T_n(λ_0)[X] monic (fringe presentation, F1/fringe-presentation); after rescaling X by an element of K we may assume X is power-bounded in T_n(λ_0)[X]/(J + f).

For 1 ≤ λ ≤ λ_0 the map D_λ = T_n(λ)[X]/(J + f) → T_n(λ)⟨λ^{-1}X⟩/(J + f) = T_{n+1}(λ)/(J + f) is bijective: a finite T_n(λ)-algebra in which X is power-bounded is already complete and X-restricted (BGR 6.1.1-type finiteness), so every restricted series in X reduces, via division by the monic f, to a polynomial of degree < deg f.
Pass to the colimit over λ > 1: B = colim D_λ ≅ colim T_{n+1}(λ)/(J + f) = W_{n+1}/(J + f).

nodes.statement: Let φ : A → B be a morphism of K-dagger algebras with completion φ̂ : Â → B̂ (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)). Then: (a) φ is surjective (resp. bijective) iff φ̂ is; (b) the following are equivalent: (i) φ is finite, (ii) φ̂ is finite, (iii) the map of reductions φ̃ : Ã → B̃ (R̃ = R°/R°° for the sup norm) is finite; (c) if φ is finite, φ is injective iff φ̂ is; (d) if φ is finite, the norm class on B from F1/dagger-norm-and-continuity coincides with the class of B as a finite A-module, and Â ⊗_A B → B̂ is an isomorphism; (e) if φ is finite, φ and φ̂ are strict.

nodes.title: Approximation of solutions and of morphisms from the completion (Bosch's rigid Artin approximation)
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K). (1) (Bosch) Let I ⊆ W_n, A = W_n/I ⊆ Â = T_n/IT_n with a Banach norm |·|_Â, and let (f_i)_{i∈Λ} be elements of A⟨Y_1..Y_m⟩† = W_{n+m}/IW_{n+m}. If there are ȳ_1..ȳ_m ∈ Â with |ȳ_j|_sup ≤ 1 and f_i(ȳ) = 0 for all i, then for every δ > 0 there are y_1..y_m ∈ A with |y_j|_sup ≤ 1, f_i(y) = 0 for all i, and |y − ȳ|_Â < δ. (2) Let p_1 : A_1 → B_1 and p_2 : A_2 → B_2 be surjective morphisms of dagger algebras, and φ_A : Â_1 → Â_2, φ_B : B̂_1 → B̂_2 morphisms with φ_B ∘ p̂_1 = p̂_2 ∘ φ_A. Then there are morphisms γ_A : A_1 → A_2 and γ_B : B_1 → B_2 with γ_B ∘ p_1 = p_2 ∘ γ_A, and for given ε > 0 and a Banach norm on Â_2, γ_A can be chosen with |γ̂_A − φ_A| < ε; if φ_A is an isomorphism, γ_A can be chosen an isomorphism. In particular two dagger algebras with isomorphic completions are isomorphic (non-canonically).
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued; for (1) as stated by Bosch, char K = 0 or [K : K^p] < ∞ (Vezzani's form, Proposition 2.8)
proofSteps: (1) is Bosch, 'A rigid analytic version of M. Artin's theorem on analytic equations' (Math. Ann. 255 (1981)); the source is not public and was not read: recorded as a gap. Grosse-Klönne quotes it as Proposition 1.13 and Vezzani states the morphism form as Proposition 2.8 (citing Grosse-Klönne's thesis 7.5.10).

(2) Write A_1 = W_n/(f_1..f_r), B_1 = W_n/(f_1..f_r, g_1..g_l), ker p_2 = (d_1..d_p). The pair (φ_A, φ_B) is a solution in Â_2 of the system f_q(x) = 0 (q ≤ r), g_j(x) = Σ_k y_{jk} d_k (j ≤ l) with |x_i|_sup ≤ 1; approximate it by a solution in A_2 by (1); this defines (γ_A, γ_B).

If φ_A is an isomorphism and |γ̂_A − φ_A| < 1, then γ̂_A is an isomorphism (a perturbation of an isomorphism of affinoid algebras of operator distance < 1), and γ_A is bijective by F1/dagger-finite-morphism-comparison (a).
acceptance: For A_1 = A_2 = W_1 and φ_A the automorphism X ↦ X + a of T_1 with a ∈ T_1, |a| < 1 not overconvergent, γ_A may be taken X ↦ X + a' with a' ∈ W_1 close to a.
Two dagger algebras A, A' with Â ≅ Â' are isomorphic; e.g. the dagger structure on a smooth affinoid is unique up to isomorphism (used in F1/dagger-to-rigid-functor (6)).

nodes.title: Reduced dagger algebras are integrally closed in their completions; A is a domain iff Â is
nodes.statement: Let A be a K-dagger algebra with completion Â (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)). (1) If A is reduced, A is integrally closed in Â (every element of Â integral over A lies in A). (2) A is an integral domain if and only if Â is.
hypotheses: A a K-dagger algebra
in (1): A reduced
proofSteps: (1) An element ξ ∈ Â integral over A satisfies a monic equation P(ξ) = 0 with P ∈ A[Y]; reducedness makes the solutions of P in a neighbourhood of ξ isolated, and Bosch's approximation (F1/dagger-approximation (1)) yields y ∈ A with P(y) = 0 and |y − ξ| small, forcing y = ξ (Bosch, section 2).

(2) ⇐: A ⊆ Â (faithful flatness, F1/dagger-completion-comparison). ⇒: A is japanese (BGR 6.1.2/4 argument via Noether normalisation, F1/dagger-noether-normalisation), so the normalisation A → B is finite; B is a dagger algebra (F1/dagger-finite-extension) and Â → B̂ is injective (F1/dagger-finite-morphism-comparison (c)).

B̂ is normal (F1/dagger-completion-comparison (3)), so its local rings are domains; Sp(B) is connected for the Zariski topology, hence Sp(B̂) is connected (Fieseler, Zariski's main theorem in nonarchimedean function theory, 3.3.3 — not read, gap), so the normal ring B̂ with connected spectrum is a domain, and so is its subring Â.
acceptance: A = W_1: W_1 is integrally closed in T_1 (e.g. the square root of 1 + πX in T_1 lies in W_1).

nodes.title: The dagger (overconvergent completed) tensor product A_1 ⊗†_B A_2
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K) and let α_1 : B → A_1, α_2 : B → A_2 be morphisms of K-dagger algebras with surjections f_1 : W_{n_1} → A_1, f_2 : W_{n_2} → A_2. Define A_1 ⊗†_B A_2 as the image of W_{n_1+n_2} = K⟨X, Y⟩† under the continuous map T_{n_1+n_2} → Â_1 ⊗̂_{B̂} Â_2 into the completed tensor product of the K-affinoid algebras Â_1, Â_2 over B̂ that sends X_i ↦ f̂_1(X_i) ⊗ 1 and Y_j ↦ 1 ⊗ f̂_2(Y_j). It is a K-dagger algebra with maps ι_i : A_i → A_1 ⊗†_B A_2, independent of the surjections up to unique isomorphism, and it is the pushout of α_1, α_2 in the category of dagger algebras: for morphisms u_i : A_i → C with u_1α_1 = u_2α_2 there is a unique u : A_1 ⊗†_B A_2 → C with u ι_i = u_i. Its completion is Â_1 ⊗̂_{B̂} Â_2. Equivalently (Kedlaya) A_1 ⊗†_K A_2 is the direct limit of the completed tensor products B_1 ⊗̂_K B_2 of fringe algebras B_i of A_i. Notation: for λ ∈ Γ*, K⟨λ^{-1}Z⟩† := ⋃_{ρ>λ} K⟨ρ^{-1}Z⟩ and A⟨λ^{-1}Z⟩† := A ⊗†_K K⟨λ^{-1}Z⟩†, A⟨Z⟩† := A⟨1^{-1}Z⟩†.
hypotheses: α_i : B → A_i morphisms of K-dagger algebras
proofSteps: Completed tensor products of K-affinoid algebras: Â_1 ⊗̂_{B̂} Â_2 is the completed tensor product of the Huber pairs (Â_i, Â_i°) over (B̂, B̂°) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product in the case of K-affinoid Tate algebras), a K-affinoid algebra with its universal property in complete affinoid K-algebras.

The images of the power-bounded f̂_1(X_i) ⊗ 1, 1 ⊗ f̂_2(Y_j) define T_{n_1+n_2} → Â_1 ⊗̂ Â_2 (universal property of the Tate algebra, anchor Layer 0.4); the image of W_{n_1+n_2} is a quotient of W_{n_1+n_2}, hence a dagger algebra.

Universal property: given u_i : A_i → C, the completions û_i (F1/dagger-completion-comparison) induce Â_1 ⊗̂_{B̂} Â_2 → Ĉ; the images of X_i, Y_j are power-bounded in C, so weak completeness (F1/dagger-weak-completeness) gives W_{n_1+n_2} → C, which factors through A_1 ⊗†_B A_2 because its completion factors through Â_1 ⊗̂ Â_2 and C → Ĉ is injective; uniqueness since the X_i, Y_j generate a dense subalgebra.
Independence of the surjections: the universal property.

Kedlaya's description: fringe algebras of A_1 ⊗† A_2 are images of the B_1 ⊗̂ B_2 (F1/fringe-morphism-factorisation), and the direct limit of the B_1 ⊗̂ B_2 maps isomorphically onto the image described above.
Finite case: if A_2 is finite over B, then A_1 ⊗_B A_2 is finite over A_1, hence a dagger algebra (F1/dagger-finite-extension) with the same universal property, so A_1 ⊗†_B A_2 = A_1 ⊗_B A_2.

nodes.title: Rational localisation A⟨f/g⟩† of a dagger algebra and its universal property
nodes.statement: Let A be a K-dagger algebra (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)) and g, f_1, …, f_m ∈ A without common zero on Sp(A) (equivalently generating the unit ideal). Define A⟨f/g⟩† := A⟨X_1, …, X_m⟩†/(gX_i − f_i)_{i≤m} (A⟨X⟩† from F1/dagger-tensor-product). The map A → A⟨f/g⟩† is universal among morphisms of dagger algebras φ : A → C such that Sp(φ) lands in R(f/g) := {x ∈ Sp(A) : |f_i(x)| ≤ |g(x)| for all i}: φ(g) is then a unit and φ factors uniquely through A⟨f/g⟩†. Special cases: Weierstrass localisations A⟨f⟩† (g = 1) and Laurent localisations A⟨f^{-1}⟩† = A⟨X⟩†/(fX − 1). Sp(A⟨f/g⟩†) = R(f/g), the completion of A⟨f/g⟩† is the affinoid rational localisation Â⟨f/g⟩, and A⟨f/g⟩† depends only on the subset R(f/g), not on (f, g).
hypotheses: A a K-dagger algebra
g, f_1..f_m ∈ A generate the unit ideal
proofSteps: Construction: A⟨X⟩† is a dagger algebra (F1/dagger-tensor-product), so is its quotient (F1/dagger-algebra).

Universal property: if Sp(φ) ⊆ R(f/g), then φ(g) vanishes at no point of Sp(C) (the f_i, g have no common zero), so φ(g) is a unit (Max(C) = Sp(C), F1/dagger-weak-completeness (c)); the elements φ(f_i)/φ(g) have |·|_sup ≤ 1, hence are power-bounded, and weak completeness (F1/dagger-weak-completeness (a)) extends X_i ↦ φ(f_i)/φ(g) to A⟨X⟩† → C, killing gX_i − f_i. Uniqueness: X_i must go to φ(f_i)/φ(g).

Completion: A⟨X⟩†/(gX − f) has completion Â⟨X⟩/(gX − f) (F1/dagger-completion-comparison and F1/dagger-tensor-product), which is the rational localisation of the Huber pair (Â, Â°) at T = {f_i}, s = g (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.completionLocalization with its universal property tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset; the identification Â⟨X⟩/(gX − f) ≅ Â⟨f/g⟩ is anchor Layer 3).
Points: Max of the localisation = maximal ideals x of A with |f_i(x)| ≤ |g(x)|, by the universal property applied to C = residue fields.
Independence of (f, g): two presentations of the same subset satisfy each other's universal property (Vezzani Proposition 2.12).
acceptance: W_1⟨X^{-1}⟩† = K⟨X, Y⟩†/(XY − 1) = K⟨X, X^{-1}⟩†, the dagger annulus |X| = 1.

nodes.title: The integral Monsky–Washnitzer algebra O_K⟨X_1, …, X_n⟩† = W_n ∩ O_K[[X]]
nodes.statement: Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K) and O_K = {a : |a| ≤ 1}. Define O_K⟨X_1..X_n⟩† := W_n ∩ O_K[[X_1..X_n]], the overconvergent power series with coefficients in O_K; it is W_n^int (F1/dagger-algebra). If O_K is a discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π, a series f ∈ O_K[[X]] lies in O_K⟨X⟩† iff there is c > 0 with f = Σ_{j≥0} π^j P_j(X), P_j ∈ O_K[X], deg P_j ≤ c(j+1) (the Monsky–Washnitzer degree growth condition), and then O_K⟨X⟩† is noetherian, O_K⟨X⟩†/π^m = O_K[X]/π^m for all m, its π-adic completion is O_K⟨X⟩ = T_n ∩ O_K[[X]], and O_K⟨X⟩† ⊗_{O_K} K = W_n.
hypotheses: K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued; for the degree-growth description, noetherianity and the π-adic statements: O_K a discrete valuation ring
proofSteps: O_K⟨X⟩† = W_n^int: the supremum norm on W_n is the Gauss norm (F1/dagger-completion-comparison (4), W_n reduced), so |f|_sup ≤ 1 iff all coefficients lie in O_K.
Degree growth: |a_ν| ≤ Cρ^{-|ν|} with ρ = |π|^{-1/c'} is v_π(a_ν) ≥ |ν|/c' − const; grouping monomials by j = v_π(a_ν) gives deg P_j ≤ c(j+1), and conversely.

Noetherian: Kedlaya (proof of Lemma 2.4.1, via a Gröbner-basis argument) and van der Put (2.2), from Weierstrass division for integral overconvergent series (F1/overconvergent-weierstrass-division applied to π-adically distinguished elements).
O_K⟨X⟩†/π^m = O_K[X]/π^m: coefficients tend to 0, so all but finitely many lie in π^m O_K; the π-adic completion is therefore lim_m O_K[X]/π^m = O_K⟨X⟩ (van der Put).
⊗ K: every f ∈ W_n has bounded coefficients (|a_ν| ≤ C), so π^m f ∈ O_K⟨X⟩† for m ≫ 0.
acceptance: Σ_j π^j X^j ∈ O_K⟨X⟩†; Σ_j π^j X^{j^2} ∈ O_K⟨X⟩ but ∉ O_K⟨X⟩†.

nodes.title: The Monsky–Washnitzer weak completion S† of a finitely generated O_K-algebra
nodes.statement: Let O_K is a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π, residue field k = O_K/π and fraction field K (any characteristic; K carries the π-adic absolute value). Let S be a finitely generated O_K-algebra and Ŝ = lim_m S/π^mS its π-adic completion. Choose generators x_1, …, x_n of S. The weak completion S† ⊆ Ŝ is the set of z ∈ Ŝ that can be written z = Σ_{j≥0} π^j P_j(x_1, …, x_n) (convergent in Ŝ) with P_j ∈ O_K[X_1..X_n] of total degree ≤ c(j+1) for some real c; equivalently, S† is the image of O_K⟨X_1..X_n⟩† → Ŝ, X_i ↦ x_i. S† is an O_K-subalgebra of Ŝ containing the image of S, and it does not depend on the choice of generators. The dagger algebra attached to S is A† := S† ⊗_{O_K} K (F1/weak-completion-generic-fibre).
hypotheses: O_K a complete discrete valuation ring
S a finitely generated O_K-algebra
proofSteps: Evaluation O_K⟨X⟩† → Ŝ, X_i ↦ x_i, is defined because Ŝ is π-adically complete and each series Σ π^j P_j(x) converges π-adically (F1/integral-overconvergent-tate-algebra, degree-growth form); its image is the set described.
Subalgebra: sums and products of degree-growth series have degree growth (deg(P_j Q_l) ≤ c(j+1) + c'(l+1) ≤ 2·max(c, c')·(j + l + 1)).

Independence of generators: if y_1..y_m is another generating set, each y_i = Q_i(x) with deg Q_i ≤ d and each x_i = R_i(y); a representation Σ π^j P_j(y) of degree growth c becomes Σ π^j P_j(Q(x)) of degree growth cd.
Mathlib model: Ŝ = AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {π}) S, and S† is the O_K-subalgebra of Ŝ given as the range of the evaluation map O_K⟨X⟩† → Ŝ.
acceptance: S = O_K[X]: S† = O_K⟨X⟩†.
S = O_K[z, z^{-1}]: S† is the ring of Laurent series Σ_{m∈ℤ} a_m z^m with a_m ∈ O_K and v(a_m) ≥ ε|m| − C for some ε > 0.

nodes.title: Presentation, noetherianity and reduction of a weak completion
nodes.statement: Let O_K is a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π, residue field k = O_K/π and fraction field K (any characteristic; K carries the π-adic absolute value) and S = O_K[X_1..X_n]/I a finitely generated O_K-algebra. Then (a) S† ≅ O_K⟨X⟩†/I·O_K⟨X⟩† (compatibly with S → S†); (b) S† is noetherian; (c) S†/π^mS† ≅ S/π^mS for all m ≥ 1; (d) π lies in the Jacobson radical of S†, S† is π-adically separated and its π-adic completion is Ŝ; (e) S† → Ŝ is faithfully flat.
hypotheses: O_K a complete DVR
S = O_K[X]/I finitely generated
proofSteps: Write R = O_K⟨X⟩†. R is noetherian with π in its Jacobson radical (F1/integral-overconvergent-tate-algebra: 1 + πf is a unit); its π-adic completion R̂ = O_K⟨X⟩ is faithfully flat over R (completion of a noetherian ring along an ideal in the Jacobson radical).
Ŝ = O_K⟨X⟩/I·O_K⟨X⟩ (completion of the finite R-module R/IR, exactness of completion for noetherian rings), so the kernel of R → Ŝ is IR̂ ∩ R = IR by faithful flatness: this is (a).
(b): quotient of the noetherian R. (c): R/π^m = O_K[X]/π^m (F1/integral-overconvergent-tate-algebra), so S†/π^m = (R/IR)/π^m = O_K[X]/(I, π^m) = S/π^m S.

(d): π ∈ Jac(R) ⇒ π ∈ Jac(S†); Krull's intersection theorem for the noetherian S† gives ⋂ π^mS† = 0; the completion is lim S†/π^m = lim S/π^m = Ŝ by (c). (e): completion of a noetherian ring along an ideal in its Jacobson radical is faithfully flat.

nodes.title: Weak completeness and the universal property of the weak completion
nodes.statement: Let O_K is a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π, residue field k = O_K/π and fraction field K (any characteristic; K carries the π-adic absolute value). Call an O_K-algebra B weakly complete finitely generated if B ≅ O_K⟨Y_1..Y_m⟩†/J for some m and ideal J. Then: (a) for every finitely generated O_K-algebra S, S† is weakly complete finitely generated, and for all y_1, …, y_r ∈ S† the map O_K[Y_1..Y_r] → S†, Y_i ↦ y_i, extends uniquely to O_K⟨Y⟩† → S†; (b) for every weakly complete finitely generated B and every O_K-algebra homomorphism φ : S → B there is a unique O_K-algebra homomorphism φ† : S† → B with φ†|_S = φ; (c) consequently S ↦ S† is a functor from finitely generated O_K-algebras to weakly complete finitely generated O_K-algebras, left adjoint to the inclusion, and (S†)† = S†.
hypotheses: O_K a complete DVR
S finitely generated over O_K
B weakly complete finitely generated
proofSteps: (a) S† = O_K⟨X⟩†/I O_K⟨X⟩† (F1/weak-completion-presentation). Substitution: for g = Σ π^{j_0} Q_{j_0}(Y) with deg Q_{j_0} ≤ c(j_0 + 1) and y_i = Σ_j π^j P_{ij}(x) with deg P_{ij} ≤ c'(j + 1), a monomial of π-exponent J = j_0 + Σ j_i in g(y) has x-degree ≤ c'(J + |μ|) ≤ c'(J + c(j_0 + 1)) ≤ c''(J + 1); so g(y) ∈ S†.

(b) Existence: write B = O_K⟨Y⟩†/J; for z ∈ S† choose g ∈ O_K⟨X⟩† mapping to z and put φ†(z) := g(φ(x_1), …, φ(x_n)), defined by weak completeness of B (the argument of (a) in B). Well defined: if g maps to 0 in Ŝ, then g ∈ I O_K⟨X⟩† (presentation lemma), and elements of I map to 0 under φ.

(b) Uniqueness: two extensions agree modulo π^m for every m because S†/π^m = S/π^m (presentation lemma (c)); B is noetherian with π in its Jacobson radical (1 + πb is a unit by weak completeness), so ⋂_m π^m B = 0 (Krull) and the extensions agree.
(c) formal from (b); (S†)† = S† because S† is already weakly complete finitely generated.

For S = O_K[x, x^{-1}] and B = O_K⟨x, x^{-1}⟩†, the map x ↦ x^q(1 + πx) extends because 1 + πx is a unit of B.

nodes.title: The generic fibre S† ⊗ K of a weak completion is a dagger algebra with completion Ŝ ⊗ K
nodes.statement: Let O_K is a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π, residue field k = O_K/π and fraction field K (any characteristic; K carries the π-adic absolute value), S = O_K[X_1..X_n]/I and A† := S† ⊗_{O_K} K. Then (a) A† ≅ W_n/IW_n is a K-dagger algebra; (b) its completion is Ŝ ⊗_{O_K} K = T_n/IT_n; (c) the image of S† lies in (A†)^int; if S is flat over O_K then S† → A† is injective, and if moreover S/πS is reduced then S† = (A†)^int, i.e. S† is exactly the set of elements of A† of supremum norm ≤ 1; (d) for S smooth over O_K, A† is a dagger algebra of Monsky–Washnitzer type with reduction S/πS (F1/mw-type-dagger-algebra).
hypotheses: O_K a complete DVR
S finitely generated over O_K; in (c) S flat over O_K; in (c) second half S/πS reduced; in (d) S smooth over O_K
proofSteps: (a) Localisation at π is exact: A† = O_K⟨X⟩†[1/π]/I = W_n/IW_n (F1/weak-completion-presentation (a), F1/integral-overconvergent-tate-algebra ⊗ K).
(b) Completion of W_n/IW_n is T_n/IT_n (F1/dagger-norm-and-continuity (1)) and Ŝ[1/π] = O_K⟨X⟩/I [1/π] = T_n/IT_n.

(c) Integral series have Gauss norm ≤ 1, so their images have |·|_sup ≤ 1. If S is flat over O_K, so is S† (S → S† is the base change of the flat map O_K[X] → O_K⟨X⟩†, van der Put 2.2), hence S† is π-torsion free and S† → S†[1/π] is injective. If S/πS is reduced, Ŝ/πŜ = S/πS is reduced, so Ŝ = (Ŝ ⊗ K)° (an affinoid unit ball with reduced reduction consists exactly of the power-bounded elements, BGR 6.4.3); thus (A†)^int = A† ∩ Ŝ (F1/dagger-algebra: A^int = A ∩ Â°), and A† ∩ Ŝ = S† because s/π^m ∈ Ŝ with s ∈ S† forces s ∈ π^mŜ ∩ S† = π^mS† (faithful flatness, F1/weak-completion-presentation (e)).

nodes.title: Dagger algebras of Monsky–Washnitzer type
nodes.statement: Let O_K is a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π, residue field k = O_K/π and fraction field K (any characteristic; K carries the π-adic absolute value). A K-dagger algebra A is of Monsky–Washnitzer type (MW-type) if A is a regular ring and the ring A^int/πA^int is a smooth k-algebra (A^int = elements of supremum norm ≤ 1, F1/dagger-algebra). Its reduction (special fibre) is A^int/πA^int. The regularity clause is part of the definition: it does not follow from smoothness of A^int/πA^int.

nodes.title: Lifting morphisms of smooth reductions to weak completions (van der Put 2.4.4 (ii))
nodes.statement: Let O_K is a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π, residue field k = O_K/π and fraction field K (any characteristic; K carries the π-adic absolute value). Let A_0, C_0 be smooth finitely generated k-algebras and A, C lifts of them: weakly complete finitely generated O_K-algebras, flat over O_K, with A/πA ≅ A_0 and C/πC ≅ C_0. Then every k-algebra homomorphism f : A_0 → C_0 lifts to an O_K-algebra homomorphism F : A → C (F mod π = f). More generally, every O_K-algebra homomorphism F̂ : A → Ĉ into the π-adic completion can be approximated: for every m there is F : A → C with F ≡ F̂ mod π^m.
hypotheses: O_K a complete DVR
A, C lifts of smooth finitely generated k-algebras
proofSteps: Infinitesimal lifting: A/π^mA is smooth over O_K/π^m for every m (flat with smooth reduction), so f lifts step by step to compatible O_K/π^m-algebra maps A/π^m → C/π^m (formal smoothness, Mathlib Algebra.FormallySmooth); their limit is F̂ : A → Ĉ lifting f.

Approximation: write A = O_K⟨X⟩†/(g_1..g_r). F̂ gives a solution (F̂(X_i)) in Ĉ of the equations g_j = 0; by the Artin approximation property of O_K⟨t⟩† (van der Put 2.4.1–2.4.3, proved by adapting Artin's argument; Bosch [4] in the non-discrete case — not read, recorded as a gap) there is a solution in C congruent to it modulo π^m. This defines F.
F mod π = F̂ mod π = f for m ≥ 1.

nodes.title: Existence and uniqueness of dagger algebras of MW-type with a given smooth reduction
nodes.statement: Let O_K is a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π, residue field k = O_K/π and fraction field K (any characteristic; K carries the π-adic absolute value) and A_0 a smooth finitely generated k-algebra. Then (a) there is a smooth finitely generated O_K-algebra B with B/πB ≅ A_0 (Elkik); (b) B† is a lift of A_0 (weakly complete finitely generated, flat over O_K, B†/πB† ≅ A_0) and B† ⊗ K is a dagger algebra of MW-type with reduction A_0; (c) any two lifts of A_0 are isomorphic as O_K-algebras (non-canonically), so any two dagger algebras of MW-type with isomorphic reductions are isomorphic.
hypotheses: O_K a complete DVR
A_0 smooth and finitely generated over k
proofSteps: (a) Elkik, 'Solutions d'équations à coefficients dans un anneau hensélien' (Ann. Sci. ÉNS 1973), Théorème 6: smooth algebras over the henselian pair (O_K, π) lift. Not read; recorded as a gap.
(b) F1/weak-completion-presentation (c) gives B†/π = B/π = A_0; flatness from flatness of B; MW-type by F1/weak-completion-generic-fibre (d).

(c) Given lifts A, B, F1/mw-morphism-lifting lifts id_{A_0} to h : A → B; h mod π is bijective, so h is surjective by the Weierstrass theorems (Nakayama for the π-adically separated weakly complete B: B = h(A) + πB implies B = h(A)), and injective because A has no π-torsion and h mod π is injective (ker h ⊆ ⋂ π^m A = 0 by flatness of B and separatedness, F1/weak-completion-presentation (d)).
For MW-type algebras A, A' with isomorphic reductions: A^int and A'^int are lifts (F1/mw-type-dagger-algebra), hence isomorphic, and A = A^int ⊗ K.
