requests.need: (A) (a) Wedhorn Lemma 6.20 = Huber 1994 Lemma 1.1, which Layer 0.4 states as the equivalent form of its standing hypothesis: for a Huber ring A and a subset T with T·A open, T^m·U is a neighbourhood of 0 for every m and every neighbourhood U of 0, i.e. Tau Ceti's `IsWeightFamily` holds for finite weights with each T_i·A open (Tau Ceti proves only the converse direction, `IsWeightFamily.isOpen_weightMul_top`). (b) Completion of Huber pairs: for a Huber pair (A, A⁺) the closure of the image of A⁺ in Â is a ring of integral elements, morphisms of pairs extend uniquely to completions, and Spa(Â, Â⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) is a homeomorphism matching rational subsets (Wedhorn Lemma 7.47, Proposition 7.48). (c) Layer 0.2 facts: Wedhorn Lemma 6.6 (an ideal is open iff it contains a power of I·A), Corollary 6.4 (intersections of rings of definition, and of a ring of definition with an open subring, are rings of definition), A° open and integrally closed. (B) Completion of Huber pairs, applied to the spectral topology A_sp of a Tate ring (item (b) of R0a's Layer 0 request): for a Huber pair (A, A⁺) the closure of the image of A⁺ in the completion Â is a ring of integral elements, and Spa(Â, Â⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) is a homeomorphism under which rational subsets correspond (Wedhorn Lemma 7.47, Proposition 7.48). (C) Strong noetherianness of every complete rank-one nonarchimedean field and of K-affinoid algebras (Layer 0.5, BGR 5.2.6), closedness of ideals in complete noetherian Tate rings, and completeness of their quotients (Layer 0.5–0.6); Weierstrass division and preparation in K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ by X_n-distinguished elements, including the automorphisms X_i ↦ X_i + X_n^{c_i} making a nonzero element distinguished (Layer 0.5 item 3, BGR 5.2.1–5.2.4); the universal property of K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ and of relative Tate algebras A⟨T₁,…,T_n⟩ over K-affinoid A for continuous maps sending the variables to power-bounded elements of complete Hausdorff targets (Layer 0.4, Wedhorn 5.50); and the open mapping theorem for continuous surjections of K-Banach spaces (Layer 0.6). (D) Layer 0.5 items 3–5: K⟨X_1, …, X_n⟩ is noetherian for every complete rank-one nonarchimedean field K and such K is strongly noetherian (BGR 5.2.6; TauCeti.Huber.IsStronglyNoetherian K), with quotients and iterated restricted series; R2 uses this for K-affinoid algebras A ⊗_{O_K} K of tfp O_K-algebras. (E) Density of the image of A[X] in A⟨X⟩ for a complete Tate ring A (Layer 0.4), and: for complete Tate rings metrised by the norms of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-ring-norm, an A-linear map of Banach A-modules is continuous iff it is bounded. (The Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.4.4 norm itself is AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-ring-norm.) (F) For a complete rank-one nonarchimedean field K (and every finite extension K'): Weierstrass division and preparation in the Tate algebra K⟨X_1..X_n⟩ by X_n-distinguished elements, including the automorphisms X_i ↦ X_i + X_n^{c_i} making a nonzero element distinguished (BGR 5.2.1–5.2.4); noetherianity of K⟨X_1..X_n⟩, i.e. an instance TauCeti.Huber.IsStronglyNoetherian K (BGR 5.2.6); the universal property of K⟨X⟩ for continuous maps sending the X_i to power-bounded elements of complete Hausdorff targets (Wedhorn 5.50); and the open mapping theorem for continuous surjections of K-Banach spaces (Layer 0.6). These are Layer 0.4–0.6 targets not yet in the pinned tree.

(A) Layer 1.4–1.5: restriction v|H of a valuation to a convex subgroup H of its value group containing the characteristic subgroup cΓ_v is a valuation (Huber 1993 §2, Wedhorn §4), and the continuity criterion Cont A = {v ∈ Spv(A, IA) : v(a) < 1 for a ∈ I} (Wedhorn Theorem 7.10), used to show that the restricted valuation of Huber 1994 Lemma 3.9(i) is continuous. (B) Two further facts of the pro-constructible calculus of Layer 1.3: (a) the image of a pro-constructible subset under a spectral map of spectral spaces is pro-constructible (Stacks 0A2S); (b) a pro-constructible subset of a spectral space that is stable under specialization is closed (Stacks 0903).

(A) Layer 2.2–2.3: finite intersections of rational subsets are rational with the product presentation (Wedhorn Remark 7.30(5)); the analytic-point theory including Wedhorn Lemma 7.45 (a complete affinoid ring has an analytic point whose support contracts to a prime containing a given non-open prime of a ring of definition), used for Wedhorn Lemma 7.46(2) in R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus; Huber 1994 Remark 3.1 (a point of Spa A is analytic iff its support is not open). (d) Wedhorn Lemma 7.54 = Huber 1994 Lemma 2.6 for complete, not necessarily Tate, affinoid rings (Tau Ceti proves only the Tate case, `exists_span_eq_top_forall_rationalSubset_subset_of_isTateRing`): every open covering of Spa(A, A⁺) is refined by a standard rational covering R(f₀, …, fₙ / f_i) with the f_i generating the unit ideal; rational subsets are a basis of quasi-compact opens stable under finite intersections, and a rational subset of a rational subset is rational (Wedhorn Proposition 8.2(2)); for a discrete ring A every valuation v with v(A⁺) ≤ 1 is continuous, so the trivial valuations v_𝔭 lie in Spa(A, A⁺). (B) The map Spa(B, B⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) induced by an adic homomorphism of Huber pairs is a spectral map (the Layer 2.1 statement of the exact hypotheses under which the induced map is spectral, in the adic case); the analytic locus is covered by rational subsets with Tate coordinate rings; Wedhorn Proposition 7.34 (perturbation of rational subsets). (C) Rational subsets form a basis of quasi-compact opens of Spa(A, A⁺) stable under finite intersections, so every quasi-compact open is a finite union of rational subsets (Layer 2.2), and spectrality of Spa (Layer 2.1). (D) Rational subsets form a basis of the topology of Spa(A, A⁺); finite intersections of rational subsets are rational (with the product presentation); and units of a complete Tate ring are detected pointwise on Spa(A, A⁺) (used to rescale in the standard-Laurent refinement). (E) Wedhorn Proposition 7.34 (rational subsets of a complete affinoid are unchanged under sufficiently small perturbations of the defining functions) and Lemma 7.54 (open covers of quasi-compact opens of Spa(A, A⁺) have standard rational refinements), for A a K-affinoid algebra with A⁺ = A°.

(A) Layer 3.1–3.4: the rational localisation O(U) = (A⟨T/s⟩, A_U⁺) as a complete Huber pair with Spa(O(U)) ≅ U matching rational subsets and its universal property among complete Huber pairs (Huber 1994 Proposition 1.3); the category of complete separated topological rings (so that O_X(X) is a complete Hausdorff nonarchimedean ring with closed integrally closed subring O_X⁺(X)); the predicates `Huber.IsSheafyPair`, `Huber.IsSheafyRing`, `Huber.IsStablySheafyRing` (Wedhorn Definition 8.26: every complete Huber ring topologically of finite type over Â is sheafy for every ring of integral elements) with their invariance under completion and isomorphism. Also: the uncompleted rational localisation A(T/s) (the ring A_s with ring of definition A₀[T/s] and ideal of definition I·A₀[T/s], Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.locSubring`, `locIdeal`) and its completion 𝒪(R(T/s)) (Tau Ceti `completionLocObj`) as the structure presheaf on rational subsets, for Huber pairs that are not Tate; Huber 1994 Lemma 1.5 / (1.4): Spa 𝒪(U) ≅ U matches rational subsets of Spa 𝒪(U) with rational subsets of Spa A contained in U, compatibly with the rings 𝒪. (B) The category 𝒱^pre of pre-adic spaces containing the affinoid pre-adic spectra Spa(A, A⁺) of arbitrary complete Huber pairs (not necessarily sheafy), with restriction to rational subsets and Hom sets from such Spa(A, A⁺) into adic spaces; these are the test objects of Huber's infinitesimal lifting Definition 1.6.5. (C) The structure sheaf O_X on Spa(A, A⁺) as a sheaf of complete topological rings with O_X(Spa(A,A⁺)) ≅ A for a complete Hausdorff sheafy pair (Layer 3.5), and the universal property of rational localisation in its plus-ring form (Huber 1994 Lemma 3.5(i) for A⟨T⟩_M and rational subsets): a continuous map to a complete Huber pair sending the weighted variables into B⁺ carries the plus ring into B⁺. (D) The structure presheaf O on Spa(A, A⁺) with O(R(T/s)) = A⟨T/s⟩ and O⁺ (Layer 3.3), used to define λ_X: (d(X), O⁺) → (X, O_X) as a morphism of locally ringed spaces and to glue charts of admissible blow-ups. (E) The structure presheaf 𝒪_X on all opens of Spa(A, A⁺) with 𝒪_X(R(T/s)) = A⟨T/s⟩ independent of the presentation, restriction maps with identity/composition laws, and the identification of rational subsets of Spa(A⟨T/s⟩) with rational subsets of X contained in R(T/s) (so that a rational subset of a rational subset is rational with the same coordinate ring); 𝒪_X(X) ≅ A. The pinned tree has presentationLimitPresheaf, not identified with 𝒪_X. Also the sheafiness predicate `Huber.IsSheafyPair A A⁺` (Layer 3.4) and the basis sheaf criterion of Layer 3.5 (rational subsets are quasi-compact, and every open covering of a rational subset has a finite rational refinement). (F) For a K-affinoid algebra Â with A⁺ = Â° and f_1..f_m, g generating the unit ideal: the identification of the rational localisation Â⟨f/g⟩ (TauCeti completionLocalization) with the quotient Â⟨X_1..X_m⟩/(gX_i − f_i) of the Tate algebra, compatibly with the structure maps.

(A) Layer 4.1: for a complete Hausdorff strongly noetherian Tate ring A and any ring of integral elements, `Huber.IsSheafyPair` with all-degree Čech exactness on finite rational covers (Wedhorn Theorem 8.28(b)); completion preserves strong noetherianness; Corollary 8.35 (strongly noetherian Tate rings are stably sheafy) including its step that a Tate ring topologically of finite type (weighted presentation, Tau Ceti `IsTopologicallyFiniteType`) over a strongly noetherian Tate ring is strongly noetherian (Wedhorn Remark 6.37(1) with Proposition 6.34: over a Tate base topological finite type equals strict topological finite type). (B) Layer 4.2: the predicate `Huber.IsUniform` for Huber rings (Hansen–Kedlaya Definition 2.3: A° is bounded), invariant under isomorphisms of topological rings. R0 states with it that the spectral topology A_sp of a Tate ring, the uniformization (A^u, A^{u+}) and the uniform completed tensor product are uniform, and uses it as the hypothesis on the target of the uniformization's universal property (until the predicate exists, the ring-level condition `IsBounded (powerBoundedSubring A)` is used). (C) Sheafiness of Spa(A, A⁺) for complete strongly noetherian Tate A (Layer 4.1), so that Spa(A_K, A_K°) for a K-affinoid A_K and Spa(A(1/s), B) in Huber's condition (S)(b) are adic spaces. (D) Layer 4.1 for a complete Hausdorff strongly noetherian Tate ring A and any ring of integral elements A⁺: `Huber.IsSheafyPair A A⁺` and exactness in every degree of the augmented Čech complex of 𝒪 on every finite rational covering of every rational subset (neither is in the pinned Tau Ceti tree). Čech acyclicity for arbitrary sheafy Tate pairs (Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 2.4.23) is planned in AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-cech-acyclicity and is not part of this request. (E) Layer 4.2 objects missing from the pinned tree: uniform (A° bounded) and stably uniform complete Tate pairs (Hansen–Kedlaya Definitions 2.3, 3.13) and the Buzzard–Verberkmoes theorem that stably uniform pairs are sheafy. (F) The predicates Huber.IsUniform (Hansen-Kedlaya Definition 2.3: A° bounded) and stable uniformity of a complete Hausdorff Tate pair (every rational localisation uniform, Hansen-Kedlaya Definition 3.13), and the pair-level Buzzard-Verberkmoes theorem: a stably uniform complete Hausdorff Tate pair is sheafy (Layer 4.2).

(A) Layer 5: (a) the category of adic spaces (objects of 𝒱 locally Spa of sheafy pairs), open subspaces, gluing of adic spaces and of morphisms (morphisms form a sheaf, Wedhorn Remark 8.24), exposed as a category in which Mathlib's `HasPullback` can be stated; (b) Huber 1994 Proposition 2.1 / Wedhorn Proposition 8.25: for an adic space X and a complete sheafy Huber pair (R, R⁺), morphisms X → Spa R correspond naturally to morphisms of pairs (R, R⁺) → (O_X(X), O_X⁺(X)); (c) Layer 5.2: the plus ring of the weighted restricted series pair A⟨X⟩_M (integral closure of {∑ a_ν X^ν : a_ν ∈ M^ν·Â⁺}), its pair-level universal property (Huber 1994 Lemma 3.5(i)), quotient mappings, pair-level topologically-finite-type maps with composition and cancellation (Huber 1994 Lemma 3.3(iv), 3.5(iv); Wedhorn Propositions 6.33, 8.46), rational localisations topologically of finite type (Huber 1994 Corollary 3.4(i), Wedhorn Example 6.38), and morphisms locally of finite type with restriction to open subspaces (Wedhorn 8.50); (d) Layer 5.1: closed immersions affinoid-locally Spa(A/J) → Spa(A) for closed J with A/J sheafy, with independence of the affinoid cover (so closedness is local on the target) and open immersions. (B) The category of adic spaces (Huber's triples, sheafy affinoid pieces) with: morphisms and their stalk maps O_{Y,f(x)} → O_{X,x}; open adic subspaces with their universal property (morphisms into U are morphisms into X landing in U); quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphisms; gluing along open subspaces (used for P¹, the disc with doubled origin and disjoint unions in the tests); Hom(X, Spa(A, A⁺)) = Hom of Huber pairs (A, A⁺) → (O_X(X), O_X⁺(X)) (Huber 1994, Proposition 2.1(ii)); for every point y the completed residue affinoid field κ(y) = (k(y)^∧, k(y)⁺^∧) with its canonical morphism Spa κ(y) → Y; maximal (rank-one) points of analytic spaces and the statement that every point of an analytic adic space is a specialization of a unique maximal point. (C) The category of adic spaces with morphisms of adic spaces, open subspaces (open immersions), gluing of adic spaces and of morphisms along open covers, and closed immersions defined by closed ideals of sheafy quotient pairs (Layer 5.1–5.3); the analytification is glued from affinoid charts in this category. (D) The category of adic spaces with open immersions and gluing along open immersions (Layer 5.1, 5.3), and the open unit polydisc D^d_{<1} = ⋃_m {|T_i|^m ≤ |ϖ|} over an arbitrary complete rank-one K and arbitrary d as an adic space (Layer 5.4 constructs the one-dimensional disc over Q_p). (E) The category of adic spaces with 𝒪_X a sheaf of complete topological rings, open subspaces, affinoid opens, gluing of sheaves and spaces along open coverings, closed immersions for closed ideals with sheafy quotients, and continuous ring maps of complete affinoid rings ↔ morphisms of affinoid adic spaces (Huber 1994 Proposition 2.1). (F) The category of adic spaces (objects of Huber's 𝒱 covered by affinoid adic spaces), open adic subspaces and open immersions, restriction to open subsets, and gluing along open immersions (Layer 5.1 and 5.3), as the carrier on which A1's sites and R4's smooth pairs are defined. (G) Adic spaces (objects of 𝒱 covered by affinoid adic spaces Spa(A, A⁺) with (A, A⁺) sheafy), open subspaces, the adjunction Hom(T, Spa(A, A⁺)) = Hom((A, A⁺), (O_T(T), O_T⁺(T))) for complete sheafy (A, A⁺) (Huber 1994 Proposition 2.1(ii)), and gluing along open immersions (Layer 5.1, 5.3). (H) The category of adic spaces over Spa(K, O_K) (locally of finite type, quasi-separated) with structure sheaf as a sheaf and open subspaces, as the target of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor; F1 uses it to state the adic form of dagger spaces and of strict neighbourhoods (closure of a quasi-compact open).

(A) Coherent cohomology over a noetherian base ring, not only over a field: for a noetherian separated scheme Y (here projective over a noetherian ring C) — coherent O_Y-modules, with images of morphisms from coherent to quasi-coherent modules coherent; Hⁱ(U, F) = 0 for i > 0 for U affine and F quasi-coherent (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.Cohomology); and the Čech complex of a quasi-coherent F for a finite affine open covering of Y computes Hⁱ(Y, F), compatibly with the C-module structures. (B) Acyclicity of affines: for an affine scheme U and a quasi-coherent O_U-module F, H^i(U, F) = 0 for i > 0 (EGA III, 1.3.1), for TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.Cohomology.

Generalized elliptic curves with Γ(N)- (N ≥ 3) or Γ_1(N)- (N ≥ 5) structure and their proper, finitely presented moduli scheme M over Z[1/N] (Deligne–Rapoport, Conrad), with the formal group of the smooth locus along the identity section; used for the universal case of Conrad's Theorem 4.1.1.

The r-th Fitting ideal F_r(M) of a finitely presented module M over an arbitrary commutative ring A (the ideal generated by the (n − r)-minors of a presentation matrix A^m → A^n, equal to A when n ≤ r), with independence of the presentation, compatibility with base change F_r(M ⊗_A A') = F_r(M)A' and with localisation, monotonicity F_r ⊆ F_{r+1}, F_r(M)_p = A_p iff M_p is generated by r elements, and F_r(M) = A, F_{r−1}(M) = 0 for M locally free of rank r (Layer 0 lists Fitting ideals among its missing operations); R2 globalises it to coherent modules on formal schemes (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Definition 3.13) without any noetherian hypothesis.

(A) Coherence of the higher direct images Rⁱf_*F of a coherent sheaf along a proper morphism of locally noetherian schemes (EGA III 3.2.1; Stacks Tag 02O5), with Hⁱ(f⁻¹V, F) = Γ(V, Rⁱf_*F) for affine V (the same need AdicSpacesPartII:F0 records). (B) Coherent cohomology of proper morphisms over locally noetherian bases, for arbitrary coherent sheaves (no flatness assumption): (1) for f : X → Y proper with Y locally noetherian and F a coherent O_X-module, the higher direct images R^i f_*F (sheaf associated with V ↦ H^i(f⁻¹V, F), H^i = TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.Cohomology) are coherent (EGA III, 3.2.1; Stacks Tag 02O5); (2) for V ⊆ Y affine, H^i(f⁻¹(V), F) ≅ Γ(V, R^i f_*F) (EGA III, 1.4.11); (3) for X proper over a noetherian ring A, H^i(X, F) is a finite A-module for the A-module structure AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.cohomologyBaseModule; (4) for an affine morphism π : X′ → X and a quasi-coherent O_{X′}-module G, H^i(X, π_*G) ≅ H^i(X′, G), and relative Spec of a quasi-coherent O_X-algebra with the equivalence between quasi-coherent modules over the algebra and over its relative Spec.

On topological spaces with sheaves of modules: Cartan's criterion (vanishing higher Čech cohomology on a cofinal system of coverings of a basis closed under intersections gives vanishing sheaf cohomology, Stacks Tag 01EW), Leray's theorem that a covering with acyclic finite intersections computes sheaf cohomology, and Rᵠf_*F = sheafification of V ↦ Hᵠ(f⁻¹V, F).

The Gel'fand spectrum M(A) of a complete Tate Banach ring A (bounded multiplicative seminorms; not only algebras over a field), compact, functorial, with Berkovich's theorem that the spectral seminorm is max_{α∈M(A)} α(x) (Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 2.3.10).

(A) Chow's lemma for separated morphisms of finite type over a noetherian base (EGA II 5.6.1; Stacks Tag 0200), as already requested by AdicSpacesPartII:F0, in the form used to pass from projective to proper coherent GAGA (the package ComplexComparisonPartII:C3 imports from R09.2–R09.3). (B) Chow's lemma in the noetherian setting (EGA II, 5.6.1; Stacks Tag 0200): for a separated morphism of finite type X → S with S noetherian there are a proper surjective π : X′ → X and an immersion X′ → P^n_S such that π is an isomorphism over a dense open U ⊆ X; when X is proper over S, X′ is projective over S (the immersion is closed). The stage description of R09.2 already names this Chow-lemma/proper-modification package; the need here is the arbitrary noetherian base (a complete adic noetherian ring), not only fields.

Grothendieck's dévissage lemma for coherent sheaves on noetherian schemes (EGA III 3.1.2; SGA1 XII §4): a property of coherent sheaves that is exact-sequence stable and holds for the pushforwards needed after Chow's lemma holds for all coherent sheaves.
Effective faithfully flat descent for modules along a faithfully flat ring map (cocycle and uniqueness), and descent of finite projectivity.

(A) An explicit form of the erratum's corrected coverings for the pro-étale site of Scholze's Definition 3.9: a family of pro-étale morphisms (f_i: U_i -> U) with |U| = ∪ f_i(|U_i|) is a covering iff each f_i is a composite U_i -> W_i -> U of a transfinite composition U_i = lim_{μ<λ} U_μ -> W_i (U_0 = W_i, each U_μ -> U_{<μ} the pullback of a finite étale surjection) and an étale morphism W_i -> U. The wording of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-site-corrected ('the covering maps U_i -> U must be transfinite compositions ... of pullbacks of finite étale surjective maps') would exclude open and étale covers; the étale factor must be allowed. Also: stability of this class under base change and composition. (B) Étale and finite étale morphisms of (pre)adic spaces by local description (Kedlaya-Liu Definition 8.2.16: finite étale = affinoid-locally Spa(S, S⁺) -> Spa(R, R⁺) with R -> S finite étale and S⁺ the integral closure of R⁺; étale = locally open immersion, finite étale, open immersion), their base change along arbitrary morphisms when the pulled-back finite étale pieces are sheafy, the small étale site of a non-noetherian analytic adic space (Kedlaya-Liu Definition 8.2.19). (The comparison with Huber-étale on locally noetherian analytic adic spaces, Huber Lemma 2.2.8, is AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-local-open-finite-etale-factorisation.)

(a) For every perfectoid Tate ring R̃ in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1 (no perfectoid base field) and every n ≥ 0, the perfected Tate algebra R̃⟨T_1^{1/p^∞}, ..., T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩ (the ϖ-adic completion of R̃°[T_i^{1/p^∞}] with ϖ inverted) is a perfectoid Tate ring. (b) For K a finite extension of Q_p, the completion of K(μ_{p^∞}) is a perfectoid field.

Rational localisations of an arbitrary perfectoid Tate ring (ECD Definition 3.1, no perfectoid base field) are perfectoid (Berkeley Theorem 6.2.6; Hansen-Kedlaya Proposition 3.8; KL16 Theorem 3.3.18). The node PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids is stated for perfectoid affinoid algebras over a perfectoid field K, and a sousperfectoid ring's frame need not contain one.

Finite étale algebras over an arbitrary perfectoid Tate ring are perfectoid (ECD Theorem 6.1(i); Berkeley Theorem 7.4.5(1); Hansen-Kedlaya Proposition 2.15(a)). The node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-purity-theorem proves this over a perfectoid field and records the Tate-ring statement as not proved in its sources.

The affinoid criterion for tilde-limits: for affinoid X_n = Spa(A_n, A_n⁺) with adic transition maps and X = Spa(A, A⁺) with compatible maps such that colim A_n -> A has dense image and A⁺ is the closure of the integral closure of the image of colim A_n⁺, the map |X| -> lim |X_n| is a homeomorphism, so X ∼ lim X_n in Huber's sense (2.4.1-2.4.2).

Projective geometry over a noetherian base: (1) the projective bundle P(E) = Proj Sym E of a finite module E over a noetherian ring A with its universal property (S-morphisms X → P(E) ↔ invertible quotients of the pullback of E) and its compatibility with base change P(E) ×_S S_n = P(E/I^{n+1}E); (2) ample and very ample invertible sheaves relative to Spec A for X proper over A: some power of an ample sheaf is very ample; a very ample L with a finite generating module E ⊆ Γ(X, L) gives a closed immersion X → P(E) (EGA II, 4.4.3, 4.5.10); restriction of an ample sheaf to a closed subscheme is ample and pullback along an affine morphism is ample; a proper X with an ample invertible sheaf is projective over A; a scheme quasi-projective over A (immersion into P^n_A) admits an open immersion into a scheme projective over A; (3) Serre's theorems for X proper over a noetherian ring A with ample L and coherent F: F ⊗ L^n is globally generated and H^i(X, F ⊗ L^n) = 0 for i > 0 and n ≫ 0 (EGA II, 4.5.5; EGA III, 2.2.1).

Flat base change for higher direct images: for f : X → Y quasi-compact and quasi-separated, F quasi-coherent on X and a flat morphism g : Y′ → Y, the base change map g*R^i f_*F → R^i f′_*(g′*F) is an isomorphism (EGA III, 1.4.15); used with Y′ = Spec O_{Y,y}.

General sheaf cohomology on a topological space (for sheaves of abelian groups, Mathlib CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H on the Zariski site): Godement's canonical flasque resolution F → C^•(X, F), an exact functor with flasque terms whose restriction to an open U is the canonical resolution of F|_U (Godement II, 4.3); vanishing of Čech cohomology of a flasque sheaf on every open cover in positive degrees and the comparison of Čech and derived cohomology for flasque sheaves (Godement II, 5.2.3, 5.9.2).

coverage.note: R0 has four groups of declarations. R0.0: the classical affinoid algebras (Noether normalisation, residue fields and the Jacobson property, supremum seminorm and maximum modulus, power-boundedness, integrality of A°, reductions). R0a: rings of noetherian type, adic homomorphisms, sheafiness for rings with a noetherian ring of definition (Huber 1994 Theorem 2.2, Case I) and discrete pairs, the spectral seminorm and uniformisation, the completed tensor product of Huber pairs with its topology, plus ring, universal property and uniformisation, fibre products of adic spaces under Huber's hypotheses with their points and base change, adic morphisms and the finite-type classes compared with the anchor's locally-finite-type morphisms, locally noetherian adic spaces, closed adic subspaces and the diagonal. R0b: separated, universally closed, proper and partially proper morphisms with the valuative criteria and closure properties, finite and quasi-finite morphisms. R0c: continuous differentials, flat, unramified, smooth and étale morphisms, the Jacobian criterion, standard étale presentations, smooth morphisms as étale over polydiscs, and the local structure of étale morphisms. Every target of the RS-05 narrowing of R0 is realised by a node. The stage is source-decomposed: the proof inputs that were not read (Huber's 1996 book beyond the reviewed decomposition's transcriptions, his habilitation, Huber–Knebusch, Bosch–Güntzer–Remmert, and the propositions Huber asserts 'similarly as for schemes') are recorded gaps, the diagonal lemma carries its own proof, and the anchor's Layers 0–5 are requests.

Every target of the R1 stage text is realised: the analytification from affine charts with independence of presentation and gluing (Huber 1994 Proposition 3.8), its universal property, fibre products, open and closed immersions, finite, étale and smooth maps with converses for maps of finite type, the separatedness and properness comparison, Tate's rigid spaces with affinoid subdomains and Huber's rigid–adic comparison, analytic groups (finite locally free group schemes, abelian varieties, isogenies and quotient maps) with invariant differentials, and the rigid identity principle. Proper GAGA, the second half of the R1 stage text, is realised by AdicSpacesPartII:R3/proper-gaga and AdicSpacesPartII:R3/gaga-finite-covers, which list R1 in realises (restructure proposal). The stage is source-decomposed: the unread proof sources (BGR for the affinoid-subdomain theory, Huber 1994 Proposition 4.5(ii)–(iv), [Hu4]/[L1]) and the unpublished differential comparison are recorded gaps; the anchor's Layers 3–5 are requests.

Every target of the RS-05 narrowing of F0 is realised: Spf and formal schemes for adic rings with a finitely generated ideal of definition (with the noetherian theorems stated as such), independence of the ideal of definition, gluing, the equivalence with compatible systems of thickenings, functorial completion, coherent formal modules with the affine equivalence and the description by inverse systems, the theorem on formal functions, Grothendieck's existence theorem, full faithfulness, and algebraisation under the ample-line-bundle hypothesis (EGA I §10, EGA III §§4–5). The analytic paragraph of the F0 stage text (fibre products of analytic spaces, finite and étale stability, Jacobian criteria, formal-model comparisons) is realised by R0–R3 and has no F0 nodes. DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1 is not a prerequisite of any F0 node: its complete local coefficient rings are instances of AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring. F0 owns the completed tensor product of adic rings; R0's completed tensor product of Huber pairs agrees with it on adic rings (API item Huber.Pair.completedTensor_adicRing). The stage is source-decomposed: its prerequisite chains end in pinned Mathlib and Tau Ceti declarations, in nodes of this roadmap, and in the requests to the roadmaps that own coherent cohomology of schemes, projective geometry and Serre vanishing, Chow's lemma, flat base change, affine acyclicity and Godement resolutions.

Every target of R2 is realised: admissible formal O_K-schemes over an arbitrary complete rank-one valuation ring and their ring theory, formal schemes of type (S) and Conrad's FS_C, Huber's functors t and d, Raynaud's generic fibre and its affinoid formula, the specialisation map and tubes, rig-points, admissible blow-ups and their invariance, Raynaud's theorem, formal models of morphisms and their separatedness, flattening by admissible blow-up with its proof after Bosch–Lütkebohmert II §§1–4 and Raynaud–Gruson, quasi-finite formal models, Huber's formal/rigid properness comparison (1.3.18), the algebraic comparison 1.9.4–1.9.6 and the good-reduction locus with its properness converse, fibral finiteness and topological invariance of affinoids, smooth formal schemes, their étale sites and Frobenius lifts over the formal torus, residue discs, fractional valuation bounds, section domains and their formal models, Hasse domains with transition maps, and Conrad's Hasse loci. Requests addressed to R2 by RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0 and RF4 (analytic adic spaces, sheafiness, their étale site) are the anchor's and AdicEtaleGeometry A1's. The stage is source-decomposed: the unread imports (BGR, EGA I_new and IV, Bourbaki, Bass, Lazard, Bhatt's notes, Berthelot, Katz–Mazur, Conrad's [C3]) and the Nagata compactification over O_K needed for the general separated case of the good-reduction converse are recorded gaps; the anchor's Layers 0 and 2–5, Tau Ceti StableReduction Layer 0 (ring-level Fitting ideals) and ModularCurvesPartII R13.1 are requests.

Every target of the RS-05 narrowing of R3 is realised: the associated sheaf of a finite module with Tate acyclicity (Huber 1994 Theorem 2.5; Kedlaya–Liu 2.5.20), Kiehl's equivalence on affinoids and Theorems A and B on quasi-Stein spaces, coherent sheaves with their operations and coherent ideals, Čech acyclicity of 𝒪 for every sheafy Tate pair (Kedlaya–Liu 2.4.21–2.4.23), finite-projective gluing on sheafy Tate affinoids (Kedlaya–Liu 2.7.7), the splitting criterion for stable uniformity and spectral seminorms, Kiehl's proper mapping theorem with base-field extension and étale base change (Scholze 2013, 7.13 and 9.2), proper GAGA and finite covers, and the trace along finite locally free morphisms with base change, composition, the étale trace pairing, comparison with the algebraic trace and pull–identify–trace on correspondences. Structure-sheaf sheafiness and all-degree acyclicity for strongly noetherian Tate rings and Buzzard–Verberkmoes are the anchor's Layer 4. The stage is source-decomposed: the unread inputs (Kiehl for non-Tate noetherian affinoids, Huber 1996 Remark 1.3.17, Temkin, Köpf and Serre, BGR 2.7.1/4, Berkovich's spectral radius theorem, Huber 1996 Lemma 2.2.8) are recorded gaps, and the inputs from other roadmaps are requests.

Every target of the RS-05 narrowing of R4 is realised: AdicEtaleGeometry A1's étale and pro-étale sites are identified on the carriers of R0 and R1 (no second site is built), with functoriality along morphisms, slice sites of étale objects and open subspaces, Huber's comparison of the rigid and adic étale topoi, the morphism of sites for analytifications, geometric points, smooth pairs with their analytification, and the restriction to the boundary complement. The stage is source-decomposed: the anchor's Layer 5 carriers and A1's explicit corrected pro-étale covering condition are requests, and Huber 1996 Lemmas 2.1.2 (not public) and 2.2.8 are recorded gaps.

Every target of the RS-05 narrowing of R5 is realised: sousperfectoid rings (Berkeley 6.3.1) with their stability under rational localisation, finite étale and étale extensions and Tate algebras (6.3.3), stable uniformity and sheafiness (6.3.4), sousperfectoid adic spaces, products of perfectoid spaces with smooth rigid spaces over a perfectoid extension (BHW Corollary 3.4) and with polydiscs, CHJ's mixed completed tensor products and coefficient sheaves O_X ⊗̂ R with Tate acyclicity, flatness and Kiehl's theorem, and the rational/integral base change and local equalizer statements. Continuous torsor descent of modules is PerfectoidSpaces P9's. The stage is source-decomposed: the perfectoid inputs without a base field (PerfectoidSpaces P1–P3), the anchor's Layers 4–5, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H0 and AdicEtaleGeometry A1 are requests, and the unread imports (SGA 3 VII_B, Ardakov–Wadsley, de Jong's Berthelot generic fibre paper, Huber 2.2.8) are recorded gaps.

F1 decomposes Grosse-Klönne's dagger paper §§1–4 (all numbered results except 3.5 and 5.1), Grosse-Klönne's finiteness paper (Lemma 0.1, 1.10–1.18, 2.1, 2.4, 2.5, 3.3–3.6), the Monsky–Washnitzer weak completion and MW-type algebras (van der Put §2; Kedlaya), and the logarithmic and compactly supported de Rham complexes for smooth pairs, and serves the requests of PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.0, RD.3–RD.6 and ColemanIntegration L1. Grosse-Klönne's Theorems 3.5 and 5.1 are proved through Berthelot's j† on tubes, owned by PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.3, and belong with RD.4; they are outside F1. The stage is source-decomposed: the finiteness chain's use of Monsky–Washnitzer finiteness is a recorded gap with a rescope proposal, the other unread inputs are recorded gaps, and the anchor's Layers 0, 2, 3 and 5 are requests.

gaps.title: Huber 1996 Definition 1.2.1 and Corollary 1.2.3 are known only through the reviewed decomposition's paraphrase
gaps.detail: The book is not public. The definitions of locally +weakly finite type (integral closure of O_Y⁺(V)[E ∪ O_X(U)°°] for a finite E) and of locally of finite presentation (lft plus finite presentation when O_Y(V) is discrete) follow the decomposition's paraphrase of 1.2.1, and only part (d) of Corollary 1.2.3 is available verbatim. The paraphrase lists quasi-compactness and 'finite type' among properties preserved by base change in case (a); that is false when g is not adic (R0/fibre-product-along-finite-type: the base change of the quasi-compact Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) → Spa(ℤ_p) along Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧) → Spa(ℤ_p) is the open unit disc, not quasi-compact), so R0/base-change-stability asserts quasi-compactness only for adic g (Wedhorn Remark 8.57(2)). The exact wording of 1.2.1 and 1.2.3 must be checked against the book.

gaps.title: No read source proves that the diagonal of a morphism locally of weakly finite type is a locally closed embedding
gaps.detail: Huber 1996 §1.3 (not public) is the expected source; Zavyalov 2024 Corollary 5.11 cites [Zav24, Cor. B.7.4] only for separated morphisms, and Conrad's notes warn that for Berkovich spaces the diagonal need not have the immersion property. The node supplies a complete argument (multiplication C ⊗̂_A C → C is a quotient mapping with continuous section, closed immersions are local on the target); it should be checked against Huber 1996 §1.3 when available.

gaps.title: Huber 1996, Propositions 1.6.7-1.6.9 are asserted by analogy with schemes; locality of smoothness on the source is not automatic
gaps.detail: The source says 'can be proved similarly as for schemes (cf. [EGA], [I])'. The nodes transport the EGA IV §17 arguments; each is a proof obligation. For injectivity (unramified, étale) and for the examples (open embeddings, relative polydiscs, monomorphisms) the transport is direct. For locality of smoothness on the source (1.6.7), the scheme proof glues local lifts using vanishing of H¹ of a quasi-coherent module on an affine; the test objects Spa A of Definition 1.6.5 are affinoid pre-adic spaces of arbitrary complete Huber pairs, for which Čech acyclicity of M ⊗ O on rational covers is only known under noetherian hypotheses (Huber 1994 Theorem 2.5; anchor Layer 4). Next action: either prove the needed H¹-vanishing for the torsor of lifts (the module Hom(ḡ*Ω, I) with I square-zero) directly, or restrict the test objects in Definition 1.6.5 and prove equivalence with Huber's definition for locally noetherian X, Y.

gaps.title: Huber's habilitation [Hu4] imports for finite morphisms; the transcribed converse of (1.4.2) needs a hypothesis
gaps.detail: (a) Finiteness over every affinoid open ([Hu4, 3.6.20, 3.12.12]) is available publicly only for strongly noetherian Tate affinoids (Zavyalov, Quotients, Theorem B.2.18 and Remark B.2.19). (b) The converse of (1.4.2) ([Hu4, 3.12.10]) as transcribed asserts that every finite A-algebra with its natural topology is a complete affinoid ring; for A = K⟨X₁, X₂, …⟩ and J the algebraic ideal (X₁, X₂, …) the finite algebra A/J is not Hausdorff (see sourceIssues). R0/finite-algebra-over-affinoid is therefore stated for A noetherian Tate or with a noetherian ring of definition. (c) The transfer of properness from the adic fibre to the scheme map g in the proof of 1.4.7 is cited to [Hu4, 3.12.5]. Next action: obtain Huber, Bewertungsspektrum und rigide Geometrie (Regensburger Math. Schriften 23, 1993), §§3.6, 3.12.

gaps.title: Huber–Knebusch [HK] imports: 1.4.5(ii) over non-analytic bases and openness 1.7.9
gaps.detail: Finite ⇒ proper is proved here only for analytic targets (via the valuative criterion 1.3.9); Huber's general statement uses [HK, 2.1.2, 2.1.6]. Openness of Spv(f) for flat finitely presented adic A → B (1.7.9) uses [HK, 2.1.4]. Next action: read Huber–Knebusch, 'On valuation spectra' (Contemp. Math. 155, 1994), §2.1.

gaps.title: Huber 1996 Lemma 2.2.8 (étale = locally an open embedding followed by finite étale) is not public; its affinoid case over a field rests on de Jong–van der Put inputs that are cited, not decomposed
gaps.detail: (1) General case. For morphisms of locally noetherian analytic adic spaces, 'étale ⇒ locally an open embedding into a finite étale cover' is Huber 1996, Lemma 2.2.8; the book is not public and the lemma is not among the reviewed decomposition's excerpts. Its statement is known through Scholze–Weinstein (Berkeley Lecture 7, p. 55), Kedlaya–Liu (Definition 8.2.16; the proof of Lemma 8.2.17 reduces to classical affinoids and cites de Jong–van der Put) and Scholze 2013 (§5, proof of Lemma 5.2). R0/etale-local-open-finite-etale-factorisation uses it outside the case of spaces locally of finite type over a field, and R4/etale-site-on-analytic-carriers and R5/sousperfectoid-etale-base-change use it through that node. (2) Affinoids over a field. For étale morphisms of affinoid adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°) the statement is de Jong–van der Put, Étale cohomology of rigid analytic spaces, Documenta Math. 1 (1996), Proposition 3.1.4 (public; proof read), which R0/etale-affinoid-finite-etale-embedding follows. The inputs its proof takes from that paper are cited, not decomposed into nodes: the theory of analytic points and wide neighbourhoods of §2.1 (after Berkovich and Schneider), Lemma 2.1.1 with Remark 2.1.2 (henselian local rings at analytic points; finite separable extensions of F_a spread out to finite étale covers of wide neighbourhoods), Lemma 3.1.5 (an étale map inducing an isomorphism of completed residue fields is a local open immersion) and Lemma 3.1.6 (separation of fibres by wide neighbourhoods, via the Key Lemma of §2.3); their transcription from analytic points of rigid affinoids to rank-one points of Spa is not written out. Part (2) is what R0/smooth-toric-chart and R3/proper-coherent-base-change use. Next action: decompose dJvdP Lemmas 2.1.1, 3.1.5 and 3.1.6 into R0 lemma nodes in adic language; for (1), read Huber 1996 §2.2.

gaps.title: Huber Remark 1.2.6(iii) and the notion 'algebraically of finite type' for affinoid rings
gaps.detail: PadicHodgeTheory:P8 requests Corollary 1.7.3(iii) together with Remark 1.2.6(iii) (Scholze 2013 Lemma 6.12). R0/algebraically-finite-type-ring-map defines the notion as the polynomial analogue of Huber 1994's topologically-finite-type quotient mappings; with this definition the plus-ring statement (API exists_fg_plus) follows from the definition, but agreement with Huber's text of §1.2 (Remark 1.2.6) is unverified. Next action: read Huber 1996 §1.2 (1.2.4-1.2.6).

gaps.title: Preparatory points (1)-(3) of the proof of Huber 1.7.1 and the reference [B, III.4.4 Proposition 5]
gaps.detail: The reviewed decomposition records only outlines: an inverse-function statement for convergent power series with unit linear part over an f-adic ring (citing Bourbaki), perturbation of values, and 'small perturbations of topological generators define automorphisms, using a noetherian ring of definition or discreteness'. Their exact statements and hypotheses are needed to split them into lemma nodes. Next action: read Huber 1996 pp. 81-85.

gaps.title: Existence of the finite faithfully flat cover in the proof of Huber 1.5.5
gaps.detail: The proof of 1.5.5 chooses a finite faithfully flat affinoid W → V such that the residue fields of the points of f⁻¹(V) ×_V W over a point w are purely inseparable over k(w)^∧; the source asserts that such a W exists without giving a reference or construction. Next action: construct W over a rational neighbourhood of y (at least for V strongly noetherian Tate), or replace this step by an argument that does not need purely inseparable residue fields.

gaps.title: Exact form of Huber's Definition 1.3.5 (valuation rings of X, centres, topology on X_v)
gaps.detail: The node fixes X_v = {(x, A) : A ⊆ k(x)⁺ a valuation ring of k(x)}, centres as images of the closed point under extensions Spa(k(x)^∧, Â) → Z of Spa κ(x) → Z, and the subbasis D(U, h) = {x ∈ U, h(x) ∈ A}, reconstructed from the reviewed record (which states 1.3.6, 1.3.7-1.3.9 and 1.3.12 in these terms) and consistent with Huber 1.3.10. The book's definition and the explicit description (2) used in the proof of 1.3.12 are unread. Next action: compare with Huber 1996 pp. 52-56.

gaps.title: Huber [Hu1, 1.7.i] in the proof of 1.7.6
gaps.detail: Case (i) of 1.7.6 uses flatness of a completed algebra over A[X] from [Hu1] (Huber, Continuous valuations, Math. Z. 212 (1993)); unread. Next action: read Huber 1993 §1.

gaps.title: Huber 1996 Lemmas 1.3.14–1.3.16, Proposition 1.5.7 and Lemmas 1.5.8 and 1.5.10 are not public and are not decomposed
gaps.detail: These results of Huber's book (specialisation lemmas used in his §1.9 and Chapter 2, and comparisons of quasi-finite morphisms with the rigid setting) are not stage targets of R0; the reviewed decomposition does not transcribe them, so no node cites them as an input. R0/smooth-toric-chart mentions 1.5.10 only as the analytic Tate case of its statement and proves it from R0/smooth-local-structure. Huber's Lemma 1.5.9 is used through the reviewed decomposition (R1/proper-separated-comparisons) and Proposition 1.7.11 through AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-etale-comparison. Next action: read Huber 1996 §§1.3, 1.5 and add nodes if a consumer needs them.

gaps.title: Huber 1994 Proposition 4.5 (ii)–(iv): proofs not written in the source
gaps.detail: Huber writes '(i)-(iv) follow from the proof of (4.3) (cf. [H1, 4.6] for (i))'. The affinoid step (Huber 1993 Theorem 4.1, Corollaries 4.2–4.4) and the universal property of 4.3 were read; the global full faithfulness and the quasi-separated equivalence need a written gluing argument, supplied in the proof steps but not checked against a source.

gaps.title: [Hu4] (Huber, Bewertungsspektrum und rigide Geometrie, 1993) and [L1] (Lütkebohmert) behind Huber 1996 Remark 1.3.19
gaps.detail: Separatedness equivalence (i) and the converses in (ii)–(iii) (for discretely valued K) are delegated by the source to [Hu4, 3.11.21] and [L1]; [Hu4] has no public copy. R1's analytification theorems do not depend on this node: R1/analytification-separated-proper is proved directly on adic spaces (Chow's lemma, constructible closures).

gaps.title: No source states the comparison Ω_{X^ad/Y^ad} ≅ (Ω_{X/Y})^ad
gaps.detail: The node gives the complete chart argument (identical presentations of the continuous and algebraic differential modules, Huber 1996 (1.6.2), Mathlib's conormal sequence); it has not been checked against a published proof. The invariant-differential comparison inherits this.

gaps.title: Quotients of analytic groups: test objects outside Adic^lft_K and non-algebraic subgroups
gaps.detail: The coequalizer property of a finite locally free surjection is proved for test objects locally of finite type over Spa K (continuity and plus rings are automatic for maps of K-affinoid algebras). For arbitrary adic test objects, and for quotients of an analytic group by a finite flat analytic subgroup that is not the analytification of an algebraic one, no source was read and nothing is claimed; Conrad's rigid descent (Relative ampleness Cor 4.2.5) is the closest source.

gaps.title: Inputs of Conrad's Lemma 2.1.5 (equidimensionality of affinoid domains) that no node supplies
gaps.detail: Conrad's proof of Irreducible components of rigid spaces, Lemma 2.1.5 imports, besides Noether normalisation (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-noether-normalisation) and the finiteness of residue fields (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-residue-fields-finite), which the node cites: (2) factoriality of the Tate algebra T_n(K) (BGR 5.2.6/1), used only to get that T_n(K) is integrally closed; (4) equality of the Krull dimensions of a noetherian local ring and of its completion, which is not in Mathlib at the pinned commit. Items (2) and (4) have no node and no public proof was read.

gaps.title: Inputs of Conrad's Lemma 2.1.4 (rigid identity principle) that no node supplies
gaps.detail: The proof of Irreducible components of rigid spaces, Lemma 2.1.4, and the function case (iii) use, besides the completion isomorphism of local rings (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-local-ring-completion) and the Jacobson property (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-jacobson), which the node cites: (a) transfer of normality between A_m and O_{X,x}, for which Conrad uses the excellence of affinoid algebras (his Theorem 1.1.3, citing Kiehl); (b) the set-theoretic complement of an analytic subset is an admissible open, and a covering of X by an analytic subset that is a union of connected affinoids together with its complement is admissible (BGR 9.1.4, 9.5.2). Neither has a node, and no public proof was read.

gaps.title: Proof source BGR 5.2.6/3 not public: Tate algebras are Jacobson rings
gaps.detail: Bosch–Güntzer–Remmert, Non-Archimedean Analysis (Grundlehren 261, 1984) is not a public source and its proof was not read; the statement is taken from the public sources cited on the node. Next action: read the proof in Bosch, Lectures on Formal and Rigid Geometry (LNM 2105), §2.2, or prove it by induction on n with Weierstrass preparation (a nonzero element of K⟨X⟩ does not vanish at every point of the closed unit polydisc over the algebraic closure).

gaps.title: Proof source BGR 7.1.1/3 not public: maximal ideals of K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ are generated by polynomials
gaps.detail: Bosch–Güntzer–Remmert, Non-Archimedean Analysis (Grundlehren 261, 1984) is not a public source and its proof was not read; the statement is taken from the public sources cited on the node. The intended contrast is presumably for power-boundedness: x_1 ∈ W_n is power-bounded in the affinoid topology (|x_1|_sup = 1) but not power-bounded in any fringe algebra T_{n,ρ} (spectral norm ρ > 1).
sourceIssues.reason: In T_{n,ρ} the spectral norm of x_1 is ρ > 1, so x_1^m does not tend to 0; any fringe algebra B maps continuously to Â and |x_1|_sup ≥ 1 on the points of the unit polydisc.

sourceIssues.printed: Lemma 2.2.3 and Remark 2.3.9 (flatness of dagger algebra maps and of A_1 → A_1 ⊗̂ A_2) are stated without a reducedness hypothesis on A, B (resp. A_1, A_2).
sourceIssues.correction: A and B (resp. A_1, A_2) must be reduced, so that the flatness assertion can be lifted from the integral subrings.
sourceIssues.reason: The proof passes through A^int, B^int and needs A^int/πA^int = reduction, i.e. the reducedness used in the errata.

restructure.detail: Grosse-Klönne's finiteness theorem for de Rham cohomology of dagger spaces reduces, through semistable tubes, to the finite-dimensionality of Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology of smooth affine schemes over the residue field (Berthelot 1997, Mebkhout 1997). In the atlas that finiteness is owned by PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.5 (finiteness, duality and Künneth), and RD.0–RD.5 consume AdicSpacesPartII F1 (dagger algebras, fringe topology, dagger spaces, de Rham complexes). Citing RD.5 from F1 would create the stage cycle F1 → RD.5 → F1, so six F1 nodes currently rest on the gap 'Finiteness of Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology … cannot be a prerequisite of F1': AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-semistable-tube-finiteness (uses MW finiteness directly for H_dR(Sp B), B = D† ⊗ K), AdicSpacesPartII:F1/quasi-algebraic-affinoid-finiteness (uses it through the semistable tubes of a de Jong alteration), AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-de-rham-finiteness-and-base-change (Grosse-Klönne Theorems 3.6/4.4/4.9, via the previous node), AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-strict-differentials (the Stein case closes only with finite-dimensional H^{i+1}_dR, and the affinoid case reduces to the Stein interiors X_ρ, whose finiteness is the previous node), AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-de-rham-kunneth and AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-poincare-duality (both assume or use the finiteness and the strictness). No other F1 node depends on them (checked on the prerequisite graph).
restructure.proposal: Move these six nodes, unchanged in statement, to PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.5 as applications of MW finiteness to dagger spaces: AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-semistable-tube-finiteness, AdicSpacesPartII:F1/quasi-algebraic-affinoid-finiteness, AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-de-rham-finiteness-and-base-change, AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-strict-differentials, AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-de-rham-kunneth, AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-poincare-duality. F1 keeps every input they use that does not need finiteness (dagger-semistable-tube-invariance, dagger-polyannulus-de-rham-cohomology, de-rham-cohomology-with-supports, dagger-local-cohomology-comparison, dagger-resolution-lemma, dagger-finite-etale-trace, dagger-proper-modification-sequence, dagger-de-rham-finite-field-extension, dagger-serre-duality, compact-support-de-rham, fringe-topology), so the moved nodes depend on F1 and on RD.5's MW finiteness, and the order F1 → RD.5 stays acyclic. F1's stage text 'Prove local acyclicity/base-change statements with convergence and finiteness hypotheses explicit' is then met with finiteness as an explicit hypothesis, and RD.5's description gains 'finite-dimensionality, Künneth and Poincaré duality for the de Rham cohomology of smooth dagger spaces (Grosse-Klönne, Finiteness §§3–4)'. AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.4, which uses F1/dagger-de-rham-finiteness-and-base-change, gains a link RD.5 → AG2.4. The F1 gap on MW finiteness is then deleted.

restructure.detail: R1's description ends its first paragraph with 'Establish the properness comparison and the proper GAGA results required for algebraic coefficient sheaves.' Proper GAGA needs coherent sheaves on adic spaces, Kiehl's theorem on affinoids and the proper mapping theorem, which are R3's (R3 depends on R0–R2 and R2 on R1), so R1 cannot prove it. The packet realises it by AdicSpacesPartII:R3/proper-gaga, AdicSpacesPartII:R3/proper-gaga-coherent-equivalence and AdicSpacesPartII:R3/gaga-finite-covers (the PerfectoidSpaces P8 request), whose realises lists name R1 as well as R3, and by AdicSpacesPartII:R3/analytification-coherent (coherence of F^an).
restructure.proposal: Move the target 'proper GAGA' from R1 to R3. R1 keeps: 'Establish the properness comparison (X proper ⇔ X^ad proper) and the analytification of coherent modules as sheaves of O_{X^ad}-modules (exactness, tensor and pullback compatibility).' R3 gains: 'Prove proper GAGA over an affinoid base: coherence of F^an, the comparison (R^i f_* F)^an ≅ R^i f^an_* F^an for proper f, the equivalence of coherent sheaves on proper X and X^an, and the algebraicity of finite analytic covers of X^an for proper X.' The realises lists of R3/proper-gaga and R3/gaga-finite-covers then name R3 only, and the link R1 → R3 (already implied by R1 → R2 → R3) carries R1/analytification-of-modules, R1/analytification-separated-proper and R1/analytification-reflects-finite-closed-immersion.

restructure.detail: Layer R0 has 121 nodes (PROTOCOL §14: a layer too broad to read as one star may be divided). Its nodes fall into four groups: the classical affinoid algebras (Noether normalisation, residue fields, supremum seminorm, integrality of A°, reductions); with a clear dependency order: affinoid products and fibre products (the ring-level inputs, Huber 1994 Theorem 2.2 Case I, uniformization, completed tensor products, fibre products, adic and finite-type classes, closed subspaces); separated, proper, finite and quasi-finite morphisms (Huber 1996 §§1.3–1.5); differentials, smooth and étale morphisms (Huber 1996 §§1.6–1.7). The R0 planets fall 0 / 2 / 2 / 2.

restructure.detail: Owners fixed by this reconciliation, which the stage descriptions do not yet state. (1) Huber 1994 Theorem 2.2, Case I (sheafiness of complete Huber pairs with a noetherian ring of definition, and the discrete case, Wedhorn 8.28(c)) had no owner: the anchor's Layer 4 covers only strongly noetherian Tate rings and Buzzard–Verberkmoes. It is now planned in R0 (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-sheafy, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/discrete-huber-pair-sheafy and their lemmas, including Huber's (1.3) for finite modules, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-laurent-cech-strict, moved from R3). (2) Uniformization of completed tensor products (AdicEtaleGeometry A0's supplier contract; consumed by PerfectoidSpaces P2) is planned in R0 (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-seminorm, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product). (3) Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 2.4.23 (Čech acyclicity of O for every sheafy Tate pair) extends the anchor's Layer 4 and is planned in R3 (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-cech-acyclicity); RS-05's narrowing of R3 ('import anchor structure-sheaf acyclicity') assumed the anchor states it, which it does only for strongly noetherian rings. (4) Classical affinoid-algebra theory had no owner: its algebraic half (Noether normalisation, Nullstellensatz and the Jacobson property, supremum seminorm and maximum modulus, power-boundedness, integrality of A°, reductions) is planned in R0 (section R0.0), which uses it in Huber 1.5.2; affinoid subdomains, Gerritzen–Grauert, Tate acyclicity for affinoid coverings and the rigid local rings are planned in R1 (section R1.0). (6) EGA 0_I (7.3.1), noetherianity of adic completions, is owned by F0 (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-completion-noetherian); AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-adic-completion keeps only its Huber-ring consequence. (5) The local structure of étale morphisms (de Jong–van der Put 3.1.4; Huber 1996 Lemma 2.2.8) is R0's (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-affinoid-finite-etale-embedding, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-local-open-finite-etale-factorisation); R4 and R5 cite R0, not AdicEtaleGeometry A1.
